Reachable with `isCosmetic()==true`, matrix type `< QTransform::TxProject` (line 160/163), `types != 0` (line 166), and the same terminal-CurveToElement witness (lines 84-86). No protective statement covers it; the absent fix is the same remaining-points bound check before the curve reads (lines 184-187).

assumptions: The points buffer contains exactly `pointCount*2` qreals, as the fragment itself defines via `lastPoint = points + (pointCount<<1)` (line 88) and as consumed by element accounting.

`path.isEmpty()` (line 9) corresponds to `elementCount() == 0`, so past line 9 the element count is >= 1, which is what keeps the `types == nullptr` branches (lines 139, 203) and implicit-close reads (136, 146, 198, 212) in bounds.
`d->activeStroker` is engine member state; line 74 guarantees it is non-null on all paths that reach the loops, so it is a safe selector and not itself a NULL source.
A default QPen (style `Qt::SolidLine`, non-cosmetic) reaches the non-cosmetic types loop; the cosmetic loop is reached by setting `isCosmetic()` with a non-projective matrix.
limitations: The witness requires an element stream that ends in a bare `CurveToElement` (no two CurveToElementData entries); no statement in the fragment produces such a stream, and QVectorPath's own constructors normally maintain curve-group well-formedness, an invariant that is outside the shown code. The finding therefore rests on classifying `path` as unvalidated external geometry (provenance rule (a)) and on the missing in-fragment validation; this fragile link is why confidence is 0.74 rather than higher.

The `StrokeHandler` output buffers allocated at line 13 (`path.elementCount()+4`) are not audited: their sizing and growth semantics are inside StrokeHandler, which is not shown, so no output-capacity overflow is claimed.
Integer overflow of `pointCount<<1` at line 88 is not claimed (requires elementCount >= 2^30 with no shown producer).

The `default:` switch cases (131-132, 193-194) do not advance `points`/`types`; a hypothetical unknown ElementType value would stall the loop, but no producer of such a value is shown, so non-termination is not confirmed.

verdict.summary: gdImageFillToBorder does not validate the entry coordinates: the left-scan loop at line 13 bounds only the lower side (i >= 0), leaving x unbounded above by im->sx (the row-width capacity used at line 28). A call with x >= im->sx reaches gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel at line 15/19 with an out-of-range index on the first iteration, causing an out-of-bounds read (line 15) and, when the pixel is not the border, an out-of-bounds write (line 19).

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Index i is initialized from parameter x at line 13; the only guard on that loop is 'i >= 0' (line 13), so x retains residual range [0, INT_MAX] with no upper bound against the row capacity im->sx stated by the right-loop bound 'i < im->sx' (line 28). Witness: call with x = im->sx and y = 0, border >= 0 (passes line 8), pixel at (im->sx, y) != border: guard line 13 admits i = im->sx (>= 0), and the first iteration writes at index im->sx, one past the im->sx-element row. The leftLimit == (-1) check (line 22) is evaluated after this write and does not exclude the witness; the absent fix is an entry-point bound check such as 'if (x < 0 || x >= im->sx || y < 0 || y >= im->sy) return;'.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) on the same witness path: with x = im->sx the first iteration of the loop at line 13 (admitted because i = im->sx >= 0) reads gdImageGetPixel(im, im->sx, y), index im->sx beyond the row capacity im->sx established by line 28. This read is unconditional (it executes before the border comparison/break and regardless of the pixel value), so it is not covered by any shown protective statement.

assumptions: The pixel storage row capacity is im->sx and the vertical extent is im->sy, both used as loop bounds in the shown code (lines 28 and 62); valid horizontal indices are 0..im->sx-1.
x, y, border, color, and im->sx are all in their declared int domains; the only constraint the fragment imposes on them is border >= 0 (line 8).
limitations: Recursion-based stack exhaustion (lines 50-51 and 73-74, uncontrolled recursion depth up to about im->sy) is a real denial-of-service surface but is demoted: the witness requires image pixel contents (a tall run of non-border/non-color pixels) that are never derived by statements inside this fragment.
Negative x is safe in this fragment: the line 13 condition (i >= 0) skips the left scan and line 22-25 returns when leftLimit stays (-1).
The severity assumes the gdImageSetPixel write lands in the heap-backed row buffer of a real gd image; the crash/impact of the OOB write is not further characterized inside this fragment.

verdict.summary: In reverse search (forward == false), the found-path length computation at line 43 stores a post-string length of count + (size - 1), where the loop-mutated count equals the match position p. This claims up to p + size - 1 bytes starting at ptr + size, but only len - p - size bytes remain in the len-byte searched buffer, so the returned string operand's rsize points beyond the buffer (up to len - 1 OOB bytes; with an empty pattern, uint wrap to UINT_MAX). Any consumption of the returned post string yields an out-of-bounds read. Match of CVE-2020-15900; the absent fix is the correct reverse post length r_size(op1) - count - size.

evidence.reason: Sink stores the returned 'post' string length into op1 (op[-3] after push(2)). In the reverse branch, count is the loop counter captured at the match (line 31's post-decrement leaves count equal to match position p on this path, since position N-j is checked while count = N-j), and the formula p + (size - 1) exceeds the remaining bytes len - p - size whenever 2(p + size) - 1 > len. Witness: op1 = 'ABC' (len = 3, capacity from lines 14/18, buffer from line 19), op = 'C' (size = 1), forward = false: line 14 admits 1 <= 3, line 20 not taken, line 23 sets ptr = base + 2, line 27 matches, so line 42 sets post bytes = base + 3 and line 43 stores rsize = 2 + (1 - 1) = 2, claiming bytes [base+3, base+5) of the 3-byte buffer - an out-of-bounds read of 2 bytes (up to len - 1 bytes general) when the returned string ref is consumed. Secondary instance: size == 0 with len == 0 makes (size - 1) wrap to UINT_MAX, storing 4294967295 as the length. The absent protective statement is the correct reverse post length (r_size(op1) - count - size, as in upstream 'op[-3].tas.rsize -= count + size'); no guard on the path (lines 14, 20, 22, 27) constrains the stored length to the remaining bytes. CWE-125.

assumptions: Capacity of the searched buffer is len = r_size(op1) as read at line 18 (and compared at line 14); buffer base is op1->value.bytes (line 19).
The interpreter subsequently consumes the returned post string operand (standard search/rsearch operator contract), which is where the length-inflated string ref is dereferenced past the buffer end.
limitations: The out-of-bounds read itself occurs in the unshown consumer of the returned operand; within the fragment only the corrupt length metadata is written at line 43.

Line 14's guard (size > r_size(op1) -> false) is present and does neutralize count underflow and the search loop; loop-position analysis (lines 26-31) shows dereferences stay within [base, base+len) in both directions, so the loop is not the finding.
Reverse empty-pattern results also return a semantically wrong 'pre' (robustness/logic issue, not separately flagged).

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is demonstrable inside SQClass::NewSlot from the shown statements alone. Every container index is producer-bounded by the fragment's own code: field indices written to `_defaultvalues` at line 9 are gated by `_isfield(temp)` (line 7) and created as `_defaultvalues.size()` at line 44 immediately before `push_back` at line 45; method indices written to `_methods` at line 37 are confined to non-NULL method-encoded temps by lines 7 and 25 and created as `_methods.size()` at line 33 immediately before `push_back` at line 34; `_metamethods[mmidx]` at line 16 is only reachable with `mmidx != -1` (line 15). No NULL producer, status-handling flaw, or other security sink is present in-fragment.

assumptions: Name-implied semantics of the Squirrel member-index encoding: `_isfield`/`_ismethod` discriminate field-encoded vs method-encoded integer slots, and `_member_idx` extracts the array offset; `_make_field_idx`/`_make_method_idx` create those encodings from `_defaultvalues.size()`/`_methods.size()` respectively.

Containment invariant derived in-fragment: `_make_field_idx(_defaultvalues.size())` at line 44 is immediately followed by `_defaultvalues.push_back(m)` at line 45, and `_make_method_idx(_methods.size())` at line 33 is immediately followed by `_methods.push_back(m)` at line 34; neither container is shrunk and no other writer to `_members` is shown, so every stored index is `< size()` of its container at every later read.
`SQObjectPtr temp;` at line 3 initializes to OT_NULL; line 7's failed lookup leaves it OT_NULL, so the non-NULL else at line 37 is reachable only with method indices produced at line 33.
`GetMetaMethodIdxByName` (line 15) returns a valid metamethod-table id or -1 by its name-implied contract, so `!= -1` at line 15 bounds line 16's index.
limitations: Capacities of `_defaultvalues`, `_methods`, and `_metamethods` are not declared in the fragment; index safety is established by construction order plus the shown guards, not by a shown capacity constant.

Writers to `_members` other than lines 33/44 (e.g., class cloning or table-level mutations outside this function) are not shown; a value with an unexpected encoding reaching line 37 would require such an unshown writer, which is not a derivable in-fragment failure.
`Clone()` (line 21) failure behavior (allocation exception vs NULL) depends on unshown implementation; no NULL producer is visible, so no CWE-476 confirmation.

The semantic effect of redefining a member as a field or static slot (e.g., replacing a method entry via line 44) and the `_locked` gate at lines 5-6 depend on instance layout/class-creation code outside the fragment; no memory-safety or status consequence is consumable from the shown statements alone.

verdict.summary: do_put is the fixed counterpart: every buffer-filling consumer is protected by a visible guard. The MBLOCK totlen computation is guarded by the multiplication-overflow check at lines 360-362 before the capacity derivation at line 369; the simple MCHAR path is guarded by 'count > INT_MAX / yanklen' at line 503 before 'totlen = count * yanklen' at line 508; oversized insertion columns are skipped at lines 522-526 before the memmove at line 530; and all y_array indexing is gated by the 'y_size == 0 || y_array == NULL' guard at line 181 plus the i<y_size loop bounds. NULL results and FAIL statuses are checked before use, and the yank-register-changed check at lines 677-684 fails closed. No demonstrated failing value reaches any memory, injection, crypto, or access-control sink.

assumptions: colnr_T is 32-bit int; INT_MAX is the standard 2^31-1 bound used by the shown overflow checks.
alloc() returns NULL (and is NULL-checked at the shown call sites) before any write occurs when an oversized size is passed.
Line 181 guarantees y_size >= 1 and y_array != NULL on every path that reaches y_array[...] indexing.
The two-pass '='-register loop (lines 91-118) yields identical segment counts in both passes, bounding y_array[y_size] writes to the allocation at line 116.
limitations: The residual signed-overflow edge 'totlen + oldlen + 1 near INT_MAX would be converted to a huge size and fail in alloc(); the write-volume accounting shows written bytes never exceed capacity when no wrap occurs, so no overflow-derived OOB is demonstrated.
ml_append at line 154 has its return discarded, but its result feeds no dependent pointer; this is a robustness nitpick with no security consumer.
Caller-supplied values (count, regname, flags) and register content are attacker-influenced in principle, but every consumer of them is bounded by the guards named above.

verdict.summary: stl_remove_degenerate passes the -1 'no-neighbor sentinel into stl_update_connects_remove_1 (lines 49 and 52) when both collapsing edges of a degenerate facet have no neighbors, causing a negative-index, out-of-bounds access on stl->neighbors_start in that helper; the fragment lacks the missing `!= -1` guard on the argument it passes.

evidence.reason: Sink receives neighbor2 = -1 (CWE-787 mechanism: negative subscript into stl->neighbors_start in the callee). Residual range of neighbor entries includes -1, established in-fragment by the == -1 comparisons at L48/L51 and the `= -1` store at L74; L45 reads neighbors_start[facet].neighbor[1] unconstrained, and guard L48 (neighbor1 == -1) admits neighbor2 == -1 with no constraint on neighbor2, so the path L45/L46 -> L48(true) -> L49 carries the failure. L51 is evaluated after L49 and protects nothing on this path. Absent fix: `&& neighbor2 != -1` on the L48 condition (or an equivalent argument guard) that the fixed counterpart must contain.

Symmetric sink at L52 receives neighbor1 = -1 (CWE-787 same mechanism). L45 reads allow neighbor1 == -1; L51 (neighbor2 == -1) admits the call and L52 passes -1 with no constraint on neighbor1. Guard L48 precedes L52 but executes earlier on a different branch and does not constrain neighbor1; absent fix is an argument guard (e.g. `&& neighbor1 != -1` / `else if` structure that excludes -1) not present in the fragment.

notes.assumptions: neighbor[] entries of stl->neighbors_start may hold the -1 sentinel, proven in-fragment by the == -1 comparisons at L48/L51 and the `= -1` assignment at L74; stl_update_connects_remove_1 subscripts stl->neighbors_start with its neighbor argument (name-implied semantics), so an argument of -1 is a negative out-of-bounds index.
notes.limitations: Out-of-bounds access via facet itself (L14-L17, L45-L46, L56-L59) is unconfirmable because no facet_start/neighbors_start capacity is declared in the fragment; which_vertex_not values outside {-1,0,1,2} have no shown producer, so the (vnot+1)%3 subscripts are not confirmed; exact read vs. write nature inside the unshown callee is inferred from the name and classified as CWE-787.

verdict.summary: The endpoint-derived name is copied into the fixed-size sockaddr_un.sun_path stack buffer with an unbounded strcpy and no length check, so a name of at least sizeof(local.sun_path) bytes overflows the stack buffer.

evidence.reason: pipePath originates from the entry-point endpoint.name() at line 4 and is left unconstrained there; the only intervening guards are the duplicate-key check (line 5, which admits fresh names of any length) and FATAL_FAIL(fd) (line 12, which is name-independent), so a witness of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) (fixed-size member of the sockaddr_un object declared at line 9) reaches this sink; strcpy writes length+1 bytes into that C-byte array, overflowing it at length == C by one byte or more (CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow). The absent fix is a length guard such as 'if (pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) throw ...' before this copy, which the fragment does not contain.

assumptions: sockaddr_un.sun_path is a fixed-size char array (platform constant, typically 104/108 bytes) per standard OS type semantics; the object is the stack variable declared at line 9.
endpoint.name() returns the untrusted name unmodified; no length restriction is shown inside the fragment.
FATAL_FAIL aborts on failure as its name implies, so fd validity is established at line 12 but is irrelevant to the copy.
limitations: The exact numerical capacity of sun_path is a documented type constant, not a literal literal in the fragment; this is the single assumed witness link.
Unchecked ::listen return (line 19) and unlink-before-bind window (line 16) were audited but have no confirmed security consequence inside the fragment.
Impact degree (RCE vs. corruption-only) depends on the unshown deployment and compiler/stack layout, so severity is capped at high.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of stl_remove_degenerate: the combined conditions at lines 48-53 (neighbor1 == -1 && neighbor2 != -1 / else if neighbor2 == -1 && neighbor1 != -1) exclude the -1 sentinel from every stl_update_connects_remove_1 call, neutralizing the historical heap out-of-bounds read (issue #28; ADMesh commit e84d8353). The direct neighbor writes at lines 60-67 and 71-73 are likewise guarded for -1, and no in-fragment producer or capacity demonstrates any other failing value.

assumptions: -1 is the no-neighbor sentinel for stl->neighbors_start[facet].neighbor[], evidenced entirely in-fragment by its consistent use in the guards at lines 48, 51, 60, 64 and 71.
which_vertex_not holds only -1..2 in this codebase, so (vnot + 1) % 3 stays within 0..2 for every in-fragment-representable value; no statement in the fragment produces a value <= -2.
stl_remove_facet and stl_update_connects_remove_1 are the standard void helpers whose only security-relevant aspect here is the index argument supplied by this fragment.
limitations: The facet parameter is used to index facet_start[facet]/neighbors_start[facet] (lines 14-58) with no in-fragment bounds check and no declared array capacity; an out-of-range facet from an unshown caller is unconfirmable.

Neighbor values other than -1 (e.g., stale or oversized indices after stl_remove_facet's swap at lines 69/22) have no shown producer or in-fragment capacity; out-of-bounds via such values is unconfirmable.
Demoted candidate: (vnot + 1) % 3 would yield index -1 for vnot <= -2 under C's truncating modulo, but no shown statement can produce which_vertex_not <= -2.

The companion half of the upstream fix (facet_num < 0 check inside stl_update_connects_remove_1) is not part of this fragment, but is redundant for the -1 failure because lines 48/51 already exclude -1 at every call site shown.

verdict.summary: The not-found branch is guarded by an exact equality check, and STFATAL's fatal-severity logging semantics terminate the process before the end() iterator could be dereferenced; no failing value reaches line 7.

assumptions: idInfoMap is a standard associative container whose find() returns end() as the not-found sentinel (lines 3-4).
STFATAL is a FATAL-severity log macro whose name-implied standard semantics are to terminate the process after emitting the message (line 5).
routerMutex serializes access so the iterator produced at line 3 is not invalidated before its use at line 7.
limitations: STFATAL's definition is not shown in the fragment; if it were defined to only log and return, an absent id would reach line 7 with it == idInfoMap.end(), an end() iterator dereference (candidate CWE-476/125), but that behavior cannot be confirmed from the fragment and is therefore demoted.
No call site of getInfoForId is shown, so id's provenance is generic; this is immaterial to the verdict because every absent-id path terminates at line 5.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of the u64-to-u32 size truncation issue in __bpf_ringbuf_reserve: the guard at lines 7-8 (size > RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ) rejects every size for which round_up(size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8) could exceed U32_MAX before the u32 assignment at line 10, so the computed len is exact and the subsequent capacity checks, ring-space check, header pointer arithmetic, and hdr->len store operate on untruncated values.

assumptions: RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ is the kernel macro ((1ULL << 31) - BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ - 1) with BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ = sizeof(struct bpf_ringbuf_hdr) = 8, so the guard at lines 7-8 admits size <= 0x7FFFFFF7 and excludes every truncating size >= 0xFFFFFFF8.
rb->mask + 1 is the ring data capacity, used as the cap in the guards at lines 11 and 29.
hdr->len is a u32 field, so line 36 stores size | BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT in 32 bits; the admitted size < 2^31 keeps this store exact.
rb is treated as non-NULL with initialized producer_pos/consumer_pos per kernel object semantics; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.
limitations: The numeric value of RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ is defined outside the fragment (kernel/bpf/ringbuf.c); the not-vulnerable conclusion depends on that definition being 0x7FFFFFF7 (if the macro were >= 0xFFFFFFF8, the u32 truncation at line 10 would be reachable, but that is not the kernel definition).
No loop structures exist in the fragment; parser/producer position tracking is limited to the single reserve path shown.
Consumer-side interpretation of hdr->len and the user-space double-mapped read path are outside the fragment and were not needed for the truncation verdict.
A header-write OOB at line 34 was considered but no in-fragment derivation of a position exceeding capacity rb->mask + 1 was found; it is a limitation, not a finding.

verdict.summary: No in-fragment-confirmable vulnerability. Every in-fragment dangerous operation (k2[2] indexing via carry at lines 31/36, tmp/s arithmetic bounded by the declared uECC_MAX_WORDS capacities at lines 8-9 and 15, signature stores at 57/77/79, k-range and r-zero handling) is covered by shown guards: line 23 admits only 1 <= k < curve->n, lines 31-32/46-47 check RNG failures, lines 43-45 initialize tmp when no RNG is set, line 37 rejects a zero point, and lines 73-75 reject an over-wide s before it is stored. Candidate OOB/status issues (unvalidated hash_size at bits2int, bcopy argument direction at line 61, LE-path EccPoint_mult write width, absent NULL checks) fail the Phase-3 confirmation rules because the involved buffer capacities (message_hash, signature, private_key) and helper return ranges are not declared or derived inside the fragment.

assumptions: curve->num_words, curve->num_n_bits, curve->num_bytes are library-table constants satisfying num_words/num_n_words <= uECC_MAX_WORDS, so every word-count-sized operation against tmp[uECC_MAX_WORDS] (line 8), s[uECC_MAX_WORDS] (line 9), and p[uECC_MAX_WORDS*2] (line 15) is within the declared capacities.
regularize_k (line 27) returns a carry in {0,1}, so k2[carry] (line 31) and k2[!carry] (line 36) index the two-element array at line 10; even without that contract, !carry is 0 or 1 in C.
uECC_generate_random_int returns 0 on failure and a nonzero value in [1, top-1] on success; both uses are return-checked (lines 31-32, 46-47).
uECC_vli_* helpers access only the word count passed as their length argument, never more.
limitations: bits2int(tmp, message_hash, hash_size, curve) at line 70 passes the unconstrained hash_size (lines 2-3) to a hidden length-consuming callee; a read past a short message_hash could not be confirmed because neither message_hash's capacity nor bits2int's internal read length is shown in the fragment (OOB rule (a) fails).

bcopy((uint8_t *) tmp, private_key, BITS_TO_BYTES(curve->num_n_bits)) at line 61: under standard BSD bcopy(src, dst, n) semantics it writes into the const private_key and leaves tmp without d, but the intended direction (see /* tmp = d */ at line 63) and the private_key buffer size are not established in-fragment, so corruption/OOB is unconfirmable.

Native-little-endian path aliases p to signature (line 13) and EccPoint_mult (line 36) writes 2*num_words words; for curves whose num_bytes*8 is not a word multiple this can transiently exceed 2*num_bytes, but the signature buffer's capacity is not declared in the fragment, so no OOB is confirmed.
No NULL checks on private_key/message_hash/signature: no NULL producer exists inside the fragment, so CWE-476 (NULL dereference) is not confirmable.

Line 37 rejects p.x == 0 but not the X == n (r == 0 mod n) edge; this requires a mathematical point value with no in-fragment producer and is still rejected by verification, so it is not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: parse_die is the fixed counterpart: the guard `if (abbrev->count)` (line 6) excludes count == 0 before `abbrev->count - 1` is evaluated at line 7, preventing the unsigned underflow that would drive the loop counter i to near-SIZE_MAX and cause out-of-bounds accesses at die->attr_values[i]/abbrev->defs[i]. Remaining potential issues (array capacities, parse_attr_value internal bounds) are not demonstrable from the fragment.

assumptions: abbrev->count is an unsigned (ut64/size_t-style) counter, so the hazard the guard prevents is the count - 1 underflow at count == 0; the safety conclusion holds regardless because line 6 excludes the zero value.
die->attr_values and abbrev->defs are sized at least abbrev->count by the (unshown) caller, consistent with the loop's maximum index count - 2.
abbrev, die, info, and hdr are non-NULL by caller contract; no NULL-producing statement is shown in the fragment.
limitations: The capacities of die->attr_values and abbrev->defs are not declared in the fragment, so an out-of-bounds access at index count - 2 (for large valid counts) is not confirmable — it would rest on an assumed magnitude.
parse_attr_value is not shown; whether it can advance buf past buf_end (making buf_end - buf underflow) or write out of bounds inside the callee cannot be demonstrated and is out of fragment scope.
The loop processes only abbrev->count - 1 attributes (skipping the last one); this is a functional oddity with no shown security-relevant consumer, so it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: PipeSocketHandler::listen copies pipePath into sockaddr_un::sun_path with strncpy using exactly sizeof(local.sun_path) (line 15), so a path of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) leaves the buffer unterminated; unlink (line 16) and chmod (line 21) then measure it with strlen and read past the array. No length check or forced NUL terminator is present, making this the vulnerable counterpart of the one-statement fix.

evidence.reason: pipePath (line 4) is unconstrained by any shown check — only the duplicate-set test at line 5 precedes the copy, and FATAL_FAIL lines 12/18/21 constrain only fd/bind/chmod returns — so its residual range includes lengths >= sizeof(local.sun_path) (capacity declared at line 9 via sockaddr_un local and referenced at line 15). At line 15, strncpy(local.sun_path, pipePath.c_str(), sizeof(local.sun_path)) writes exactly sizeof(local.sun_path) bytes into that array and, per standard strncpy semantics, appends no NUL when the source length reaches that bound. unlink(local.sun_path) then strlen-measures the non-terminated buffer, reading past the sun_path array end on every build (CWE-125). The absent protective statement is a length rejection (e.g., if (pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) throw runtime_error(...)) or an explicit terminator such as local.sun_path[sizeof(local.sun_path)-1] = '\0'; neither is present.

The same non-terminated sun_path buffer produced at line 15 from a pipePath of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) admitted by every guard on the path (line 5 checks uniqueness only; line 12's FATAL_FAIL(fd) precedes but checks only fd) reaches this C-string sink on non-Windows builds (line 20), and ::chmod measures it with strlen, reading past the array: OOB read (CWE-125). The identical absent fix — a size check before the copy or a forced NUL terminator — would neutralize this second sink as well.

assumptions: sun_path capacity equals sizeof(local.sun_path) as referenced at line 15 — a fixed OS-declared array (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS).
strncpy with n equal to the destination size writes no NUL terminator when the source length is >= n (standard library semantics).
unlink/chmod consume their const char* argument as a NUL-terminated string via strlen (standard semantics).
FATAL_FAIL(fd) at line 12 and FATAL_FAIL(bind) at line 18 validate those return values before the read sinks, but they do not constrain pipePath length.
limitations: The discarded ::listen(fd, 5) return at line 19 and the discarded unlink() return at line 16 are status-handling robustness concerns (CWE-754-style) with no shown security-relevant consumer; demoted, not findings.

On Linux an unterminated sun_path also makes ::bind fail with EINVAL, reaching FATAL_FAIL — a secondary reachable abort (DoS effect), not part of the primary CWE-125 mechanism at the line 16/21 sinks.
Membership of the standard-library semantics of unlink/chmod and strncpy (name-implied standard semantics) is assumed; no callee internals beyond those standard behaviors are relied on.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The fragment already contains the protective statements: the upper clamps at L13-18 (x >= im->sx -> im->sx - 1, y >= im->sy -> im->sy - 1), the L20-26 loop bound (i >= 0), and the L27-29 leftLimit == -1 early return, together with the guarded recursion bounds at L41, L43, L56 and L58. Every index the shown code can derive stays within [0, im->sx-1] x [0, im->sy-1]. The only conceivable OOB residual (negative y or a zero-height image deriving y = im->sy - 1 = -1) depends on an unshown caller/image producer and is not derivable from the fragment, so it is a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: im->sx and im->sy are the capacities of the pixel storage indexed by gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel as tpixels[y][x] (name-implied array-subscript semantics); the bounds in the fragment are im->sx rows/columns at L32 and L56.
The L8-11 border < 0 guard and L13-18 coordinate clamps are protective statements covering the coordinate classes they admit: after L13-15, x <= im->sx - 1; after L16-18, y <= im->sy - 1.
limitations: A negative y supplied by a top-level caller would reach gdImageGetPixel(im, i, y) at L21 and gdImageSetPixel(im, i, y, color) at L24 out of the [0, im->sy-1] row range, but no shown statement derives a negative y (the only shown producers pass y-1/y+1 guarded to valid rows at L41/L47/L56/L62), so per the OOB class rules (in-fragment numeric derivation required) this is demoted to a limitation.

If an image with im->sy == 0 existed, the clamp at L17 would derive y = im->sy - 1 = -1 and reach the L21/L24 sinks out of bounds; the empty-image condition has no shown producer in the fragment (degenerate-input discipline), so it cannot be confirmed.
Negative x is not a hazard here: x < 0 makes the L20 left loop and the L27-29 check return before any pixel access.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded/fixed form: the loop guard `pb_idx < pb_cnt` (L9) bounds every dp_packet_batch_refill index to [0, pb_cnt), the EtherType equality checks (L10/L13) gate the v4/v6 fragment validators, and the return status of ipf_handle_frag (L17) fully discriminates refill vs delete. No admitted value reaches any sink out of domain, so no vulnerable counterpart statement is missing.

assumptions: pb_cnt (L5) is the batch's in-use count whose slots are [0, pb_cnt), per name-implied dp_packet_batch semantics, and the loop guard on L9 admits exactly pb_idx in [0, pb_cnt).
dl_type equality checks at L10/L13 gate the respective fragment validators through && short-circuit, so validators only run for exactly ETH_TYPE_IP or ETH_TYPE_IPV6.
limitations: The batch-slot dangling pointer after dp_packet_delete (L20) would only be consumed by downstream code outside the fragment; post-loop batch consumption is not shown, so it is not confirmable here.
NULL-ness of ipf/pb and ownership semantics inside ipf_handle_frag are not derivable from the shown statements and were not assumed for either direction.

Mixed signedness (int pb_idx vs size_t pb_cnt) at L9 promotes pb_idx to unsigned, but no shown producer of a magnitude that matters (count beyond INT_MAX or batch capacity) exists, so no integer finding.

verdict.summary: esp_output_head() admits an ESP trailer length (esp->tailen) up to ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE (~32K) via the line 20-21 gate, then in the page-frag fast path calls skb_page_frag_refill() (line 42) which serves at most a single PAGE_SIZE page, and writes/records the full tailen: line 52 esp_output_fill_trailer(tail, esp->tfclen, esp->plen, esp->proto) and line 56-57 __skb_fill_page_desc(..., tailen) overrun the page when ALIGN(tailen) > PAGE_SIZE, a heap out-of-bounds write. The missing protective statement is the page-size gate added by upstream commit 5bd8baab087d ('ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > PAGE_SIZE || ALIGN(skb->data_len, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > PAGE_SIZE' -> goto cow); the shown 32K ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE bound is its insufficient pre-fix form.

evidence.reason: Sink writes the ESP trailer of length ~esp->tailen (tfclen + plen, part of the tailen admitted on line 8 and never bounded by PAGE_SIZE) at tail = page_address(page) + pfrag->offset (line 50), where page is the single page served by skb_page_frag_refill() at line 42 (callee contract: sz <= PAGE_SIZE, i.e. 4096 bytes capacity). The only guard on the path, lines 20-21 'if (allocsz > ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE) goto cow;' with ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE = PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER = 32768 (SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER = get_order(32768)), admits tailen = 16384 (allocsz = ALIGN(0 + 16384) = 16384 <= 32768) with data_len = 0, uncloned skb, tailroom = 128 < tailen (line 24), nr_frags = 0 < MAX_SKB_FRAGS (line 30), refill success (line 42). The absent fix statement is the upstream 5bd8baab087d page gate 'if (ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > PAGE_SIZE || ALIGN(skb->data_len, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > PAGE_SIZE) goto cow;' — without it the write exceeds the single page, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

assumptions: Line 19-21 relies on ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE = PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER with SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER = get_order(32768), so on 4K-page systems the gate admits combined aligned lengths up to ~32768 bytes.
skb_page_frag_refill() (line 42) services at most a single PAGE_SIZE page; its API documents that the requested size MUST be <= PAGE_SIZE, which the fragment violates for ALIGN(tailen) > PAGE_SIZE.

skb->data_len is unsigned int and tailen is int, so the line 19 sum is unsigned; tailen values used for the witness are non-negative, and a negative tailen would make the line 20-21 gate trip (fail-closed), not a vulnerability.
limitations: The 4096-byte capacity is the callee's documented single-page contract rather than a capacity literally declared inside the fragment.

Reaching tailen > PAGE_SIZE in the real callers requires esp->tailen to be that large, which depends on an SA configured with large TFC padding (XFRMA_TFCPAD) not shown in this fragment; the fragment itself only bounds tailen by the 32K gate.
On configurations with PAGE_SIZE >= 32768 the overflow window (tailen exceeding one page but admitted by the gate) collapses, so the finding is architecture-dependent.

The index-side of __skb_fill_page_desc (line 56-57) is guarded by line 30-31 (nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS) and is not itself out of bounds; only the recorded fragment length tailen exceeds the page capacity.

The fragment is the fixed counterpart of thread_call. The loop bound at line 7 (i < nparams+1) moves all arguments v[2..nparams] onto the thread, so after pushing the roottable (line 6) the thread stack contains exactly nparams slots, matching the frame count passed to sq_call(_thread(o), nparams, ...) at line 9; the frame-depth underflow that would make sq_call read below the thread stack is excluded on every path.

assumptions: Standard Squirrel native-method frame convention: when a method such as thread.call is invoked, the receiver ('this') occupies stack index 1 and arguments occupy indices 2..nparams, so nparams = 1 + number of arguments; this makes line 5's count consistent with lines 6-8.

Standard sq_call semantics: its nparams argument counts the full call frame including the callable slot, and sq_call uses the top nparams slots of the target VM with the slot at -nparams as the callable; a shallower frame would read below the stack, a deeper one would misplace the callable.
SQVM::Push and sq_move grow the target thread's stack as needed; no fixed stack capacity is declared in the fragment, so no capacity-based overflow is demonstrable.
Line 4's OT_THREAD check is evaluated before every _thread(o) dereference (lines 6, 8, 9, 11, 14), so _thread(o) is a valid thread on all in-branch paths.
limitations: stack_get(v,1) at line 3 is not preceded by a depth check; a failure would require nparams == 0, but no shown statement can produce an empty call frame (the native-call machinery supplies the receiver slot), so this is not confirmable within the fragment.

The expression nparams+1 at line 7 would only wrap for nparams == SQInteger_MAX, which requires a stack of about 2^63 elements; the magnitude producer is not shown, so that wrap/OOB scenario is not confirmable.

On sq_call failure (lines 14-15) the pushed roottable/arguments are not popped by the fragment; whether that accumulates into resource exhaustion depends on unshown sq_call cleanup behavior, so it is at most a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
Internal behavior of the unshown sq_call callee is taken at its standard, name-implied API semantics, not from a visible implementation.

verdict.summary: In the GIMP brush loader, the brush-name buffer `temp` is allocated with exactly `bn_size` bytes (line 97) and filled with raw file bytes via `read` (line 99), then passed to `gimp_any_to_utf8 (temp, -1, ...)` (line 109). The `-1` length makes the callee treat `temp` as NUL-terminated, so a short brush file whose name bytes contain no NUL causes a heap out-of-bounds read (strlen/g_convert scanning past the 4-byte allocation).

evidence.reason: Heap over-read (CWE-125): `temp` has capacity exactly `bn_size` bytes from `g_new (gchar, bn_size)` at line 97; `read (fd, temp, bn_size)` at line 99 fills it with attacker-controlled file bytes. With header_size=32 the guards at line 86 (`bh.header_size > sizeof (BrushHeader)`) and line 95 (`bn_size = 4 > 0`) admit bn_size=4, and line 99 admits a read of exactly 4 non-NUL bytes. Line 109 passes length `-1`, which per g_convert/gimp_any_to_utf8 semantics scans temp as NUL-terminated, reading at least one byte past the 4-byte allocation and continuing until the next heap NUL. The absent fix is the NUL-termination statement `temp[bn_size] = '\0';` (with capacity `bn_size + 1` at line 97), or passing `bn_size` instead of `-1` at line 109.

assumptions: BrushHeader layout is 7 guint32 fields (header_size, version, width, height, bytes, magic_number, spacing) = 28 bytes, consistent with `sizeof (BrushHeader)` used at lines 31, 86 and the `-8`/`+8` version-1 adjustments at lines 67-68.
GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE at lines 47-48 is not defined in the fragment; the name-overread finding does not depend on its value (width=height=1 is admitted under any positive bound).
gimp_any_to_utf8/g_convert standard GLib semantics: a length argument of -1 treats the source as NUL-terminated and scans until the first NUL byte.
limitations: 32-bit wrap of `size = bh.width * bh.height * bh.bytes` (line 121) for bytes=18 is not exploitable in-fragment: bytes=18 reaches only the `default` error path at lines 232-237 before any pixel-region consumer; for bytes in {1,2,4} the product stays below 2^32 when GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is 32767 (not resolvable in-fragment), and the line-51 clause plus lines 260-261 read at most width*height*4 bytes.
Resource-exhaustion/abort via huge `bn_size` (up to INT_MAX, line 97) is a robustness/DoS concern, not a memory-safety finding.

Signed overflow of `i * 4` in the pattern-conversion loop (lines 165-176) requires width*height > 2^30 pixels and a fully-read multihundred-MB brush file (line 124), so it was demoted; likewise the `lseek` at line 67 has its return discarded but no security-relevant consumer was demonstrated.

Whether the fixed counterpart's one-line change is the NUL-termination (line 97/109) vs. the sanitize block (lines 47-51) cannot be decided from the fragment alone; the shown fragment nevertheless contains a confirmed unprotected OOB-read sink at line 109.

verdict.summary: esp_output_head is fully guarded: the fast path checks tailen <= skb_tailroom (L19) before writing the trailer and calling pskb_put; the page-frag path checks nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS (L25) before __skb_fill_page_desc (L51-L52) and verifies skb_page_frag_refill success (L37) before writing into the frag; the cow path checks skb_cow_data's return (L75) before pskb_put; skb->sk is NULL-checked (L64). No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: MAX_SKB_FRAGS (L25) is the capacity of the skb_shared_info frags[] array, so any index < MAX_SKB_FRAGS is in bounds.
skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer) (L74), by its standard kernel semantics, guarantees at least tailen bytes of tailroom in trailer before pskb_put (L82).
skb_page_frag_refill(allocsize, ...) success (L37) guarantees allocsize = ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) >= tailen usable bytes at pfrag->offset (L45).
esp_output_fill_trailer writes no more than the trailer length covered by tailen.
limitations: L59 'nfrags++;' makes the returned frag count one larger than the actual skb_shinfo->nr_frags (L53); the extra value is consumed only by the unshown caller, so no security impact is demonstrable inside the fragment.

A tailen magnitude large enough to overflow ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) at L33 or pfrag->offset + allocsize at L55 is not derivable from any shown statement; the fragment leaves tailen's magnitude unconstrained, which by itself is not a finding.
Potential integer-sign issues in refcount_add(tailen, ...) (L65) are guarded by the sk && sk_fullsock(sk) NULL/type check (L64) and have no in-fragment security consumer.

verdict.summary: copy_page_to_iter_pipe merges (extends) a page-cache-backed pipe buffer on the line 16 condition offset == off && buf->page == page without checking PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE, and the fresh-buffer install at lines 24-27 never clears buf->flags; a recirculated slot retaining stale CAN_MERGE lets a subsequent write land in the page cache of a read-only file (CVE-2022-0847 Dirty Pipe).

evidence.reason: The merge decision admits any buffer sharing page and offset regardless of mergeability: bytes (residual range [1, i->count per lines 10-14, size_t from the splice path) reaches buf->len += bytes at line 18 with no flags test. buf->page is set to an attacker-reachable file page-cache page at lines 24-27 and buf->flags is never assigned or cleared in the fragment, so a slot carrying stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE remains mergeable. Guards on the path (lines 10-11 bytes clamp, 13-14 nonzero, 17 sanity, 22-23 pipe_full) are all satisfied by a normal non-full pipe and none inspects buf->flags. The absent fix is the added term (buf->flags & PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE) in this condition (or buf->flags = 0 before the buffer install), leaving CWE-863 missing-authorization gate: unprivileged write into read-only page cache (CVE-2022-0847).

assumptions: pipe->ring_size is at least 1 so p_mask = ring_size - 1 is valid; the masked ring index at lines 15/20 is always inside pipe->bufs[] and is memory-safe.
buf->flags preserves the slot's prior state across reuse because the fragment never writes or clears the flags field (standard pipe_buffer semantics implied by PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE usage).
sanity(i) at line 17 performs pipe/iter state consistency checks only and has no mergeability term.
limitations: i->iov_offset = offset + bytes at line 27 can overflow size_t only for unshown huge offsets; no in-fragment consumer is demonstrated, so it is not a finding.
pipe->head = i_head + 1 at line 26 could wrap the unsigned counter only at 2^32 iterations; not demonstrable from shown statements.
The final write into the page cache occurs in pipe_write (outside this fragment); its behavior is inferred from the standard CAN_MERGE semantics that underpin CVE-2022-0847.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded/fixed counterpart of createRandomCursorExecutor. Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the sharded-path division at line 62 is unreachable with a zero denominator because line 14 excludes numRecords <= 100 (admitting numRecords >= 101, so numRecords*0.05 >= 5.05 > 0); the timeseries-path division at line 124 and both *bucketUnpacker derefs at lines 131 and 143 are protected by line 91, which excludes an unengaged bucketUnpacker and numRecords == 0; rsRandCursor is null-checked at line 35 before use at line 44; and execStatus is status-checked at lines 160-162 before getValue() at line 169. No candidate witness survives every guard on its path.

assumptions: coll->getRecordStore() and CollectionShardingState::get() (lines 34, 53) are treated as non-NULL because no in-fragment statement produces a NULL result from them; framework contracts outside the fragment are not relied on for the verdict.

gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount is treated as a positive server parameter as described by the in-fragment comments (lines 19, 101); the verdict does not depend on this, since even a NaN ratio would only flow into the unshown TrialStage.

The non-timeseries early return at line 14 admits only numRecords > 100, which is exactly the invariant that keeps the line 62 denominator strictly positive on the sharded path (line 55 requires !isTimeseriesBucketsCollection()).
limitations: CWE-476 at line 54 (css dereference) is demoted: no NULL producer for CollectionShardingState::get is visible in the fragment.

The internal behavior of SampleFromTimeseriesBucket, UnpackTimeseriesBucket, and TrialStage with extreme sampleSize/numRecords values (negative or near LLONG_MAX) is outside the shown fragment, and no capacity is shown for it, so no memory-safety consequence can be confirmed.

If gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount were 0 (unshown configuration), the line 124 ratio could be NaN and flow into TrialStage (line 150); this is a robustness concern with no in-fragment security consequence and is not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: In sug_filltree, the trie traversal depth is incremented once per non-NUL byte with no upper bound, so a spell-file word of at least MAXWLEN bytes drives depth to MAXWLEN and causes out-of-bounds stack writes into tword/arridx/curi/wordcount (lines 88-91, 60), all declared with capacity MAXWLEN.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled spell-file trie data (byts/idxs from slang->sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs, lines 27-28, entry-point input, NULL-checked only at lines 29-30) feeds the loop. depth is incremented once per non-NUL byte at line 88 with no upper-bound guard between loop condition line 37 (admits depth >= 0 only) and this sink. For a word of exactly MAXWLEN non-NUL bytes, the MAXWLEN-th byte passes line 39's else side and line 57's else side; line 88 raises depth from MAXWLEN-1 to MAXWLEN, and this statement then writes arridx[MAXWLEN], exceeding the declared capacity arridx[MAXWLEN] at line 6 (valid 0..MAXWLEN-1): out-of-bounds stack write, CWE-787. The absent fix is a depth cap (e.g. checking depth against MAXWLEN-1 before the store); no protective statement covers this failure set.

Same unbounded-depth path: for a word of MAXWLEN+1 non-NUL bytes, the (MAXWLEN+1)-th byte is processed with depth == MAXWLEN (admitted by guard line 37, depth >= 0, and line 39's else side), so this statement writes tword[MAXWLEN], outside the declared capacity char_u tword[MAXWLEN] at line 8 (valid 0..MAXWLEN-1); out-of-bounds stack write, CWE-787. The absent fix is a depth-capacity check before the store; no protective statement on the path covers it.

For a word of exactly MAXWLEN non-NUL bytes followed by the NUL leaf, depth reaches MAXWLEN after line 88's post-increment; at the leaf the c==0 branch (line 57) executes this statement with depth == MAXWLEN, writing tword[MAXWLEN] past the declared capacity tword[MAXWLEN] at line 8 (valid 0..MAXWLEN-1); out-of-bounds stack write, CWE-787. The absent fix is a depth-capacity check before the store; guards at lines 37, 39, 43, 79 impose no maximum on depth.

assumptions: MAXWLEN is the capacity of tword (line 8), arridx (line 6), curi (line 7), and wordcount (line 13), giving valid indices 0..MAXWLEN-1.
byts/idxs (lines 3-4) encode the case-folded spell trie read from the spell file, with each word terminated by a NUL byte (c == 0 at line 57).
limitations: Potential out-of-bounds reads/writes via trie child offsets n (line 56, byts[n]) and arridx[depth] (lines 39, 42, 89's idxs[n]) depend on the byte-code trie encoding invariants, which are not derivable from the shown fragment; these are demoted, not confirmed.
The numeric value of MAXWLEN is not shown, but the proof only needs the constant equality between the declared array size and the reachable index depth==MAXWLEN.

The spell-file producer that builds sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs is not shown, so any word-length cap there is out-of-scope; the fragment itself imposes no such cap, and entry-point data is analyzed unconstrained per the stated provenance rules.

verdict.summary: The newstyle option-negotiation handshake is the fixed (patched) counterpart: every attacker-controlled length/index that feeds a data-buffer read is fully covered by in-fragment guards. optlen is capped by MAX_REQUEST_SIZE (line 34) before malloc(optlen+1) (line 38); the NBD_OPT_INFO/GO export name is bounded by exportnamelen <= optlen-6 (line 200) before memcpy at data[exportnamelen+4] (line 207); the info loop is pinned by the exact-fit check optlen == 4+exportnamelen+2+2*nrinfos (line 209) so its last read stays at index optlen-1; and every variable-length read in NBD_OPT_LIST/SET_META_CONTEXT is guarded by opt_index+4 > optlen and querylen <= optlen-opt_index passed to check_string. No demonstrated value from any attacker-supplied field can reach a memory, injection, crypto, or access-control sink out of bounds.

assumptions: MAX_REQUEST_SIZE bounds optlen (guard at line 34), so optlen+1 (line 38) does not wrap and (int) querylen <= optlen is non-negative.
check_export_name and check_string enforce len <= maxlen by name-implied semantics; the in-fragment maxlen values (optlen-8, optlen-6, optlen-opt_index) are the binding bounds.
conn state (GET_CONN, conn->top_context, conn->default_exportname) is server-internal; no NULL producer for these pointers appears in the fragment.
limitations: Safety of the meta-context query text reads (check_string/check_export_name internals) is not literally shown; it is relied on only at standard name-implied semantics, consistent with the shown maxlen arguments.
Any potential issue resting on values of MAX_REQUEST_SIZE or callee internals outside the fragment is out of scope and not a confirmed finding.
The uninitialized trailing byte data[optlen] (malloc optlen+1) is never dereferenced past the shown guards; the %.*s debug read is bounded by check_string which precedes it.

verdict.summary: The KS_VER_SCROLLBAR and KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR loops in check_termcode read tp[j], tp[j+1], tp[j+2] in the loop condition without bounding j against the declared input length len (lines 47/54). A single GUI scroll event whose input ends at len leaves j >= len on the next condition evaluation, so the loop reads up to 3 bytes (or more, if the pattern continues) past the end of the input region; with an exactly filled buffer this is a heap out-of-bounds read. The only sentinel, tp[j + 2] != NUL, relies on a NUL terminator that the fragment never establishes, so an unterminated adversarial input overruns. The missing fix is a length bound in the loop condition (e.g., j + 3 < len).

evidence.snippet:
for (i = 0; tp[j] == CSI && tp[j + 1] == KS_VER_SCROLLBAR
						     && tp[j + 2] != NUL; ++i)
evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read: attacker-controlled terminal input bytes (entry-point, full 0..255 domain) set tp[0]=CSI, tp[1]=KS_VER_SCROLLBAR, tp[2]=non-NUL via lines 100-101 on the GUI path (guards 44/51, 97, 331 all admit the witness). The loop condition at lines 481-482 reads tp[j], tp[j+1], tp[j+2] with no bound against the input length len declared at line 47/54; after one body iteration j == len, so the re-evaluated condition reads bytes past the input region, and past the heap object when the buffer is exactly filled. The only termination guard, tp[j + 2] != NUL, is a content sentinel — NUL-termination is never established in the fragment — and the num_bytes == -1 breaks (lines 486-487, 494-495) execute after the condition reads. The absent fix statement is a length bound in the loop condition such as j + 2 < len (or j + 3 < len). Primary CWE-125.

evidence.snippet:
for (i = 0; tp[j] == CSI && tp[j + 1] == KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR
						     && tp[j + 2] != NUL; ++i)
evidence.reason: Same out-of-bounds read mechanism as the KS_VER_SCROLLBAR loop: the condition reads tp[j]..tp[j+2] against only the content sentinel tp[j + 2] != NUL and never against len (lines 47/54). With a horizontal-scroll event whose input region ends at the event boundary, the next condition evaluation reads past the input length at j >= len, and past the heap allocation when the buffer is exactly filled. No protective length bound exists on the path; the num_bytes == -1 break at line 515-516 runs only after the reads. Missing fix: add j + 2 < len (or j + 3 < len) to the loop condition. Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: GUI build (FEAT_GUI) with !USE_ON_FLY_SCROLL so the KS_VER_SCROLLBAR/KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR branches compile and are reachable; gui.in_use is true for the GUI key-name path at line 90.
CSI, KS_VER_SCROLLBAR/KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR, and a non-NUL filler byte are ordinary byte values in attacker-supplied terminal input; tp points into typebuf.tb_buf or the caller's buf.

The input buffer may be exactly filled (*buflen == bufsize, or typebuf.tb_len == buffer capacity), so reads past len cross the heap boundary; the fragment shows no NUL padding or NUL-termination invariant for tp.
limitations: The exact heap allocation size (bufsize value, typebuf.tb_buflen) is not visible in the fragment, so the crossing of the physical allocation boundary is assumed; the deterministic part is the over-read of the declared input length len.

Inner helper reads get_bytes_from_buf(tp + j, ...) (line 485) and get_long_from_buf(tp + j, &val) (lines 493, 514) sit at the same unbounded offset, but their internals are unshown; the loop-condition reads at lines 481-482/510-511 are the confirmed in-fragment sinks.

Potential overflow of string[] at lines 577-593 (mb_char2bytes / string write) was demoted: it depends on unshown modifiers2keycode and mb_char2bytes semantics and on new_slen reaching the declared capacity MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN (line 19); not confirmed.

Vim's real-world fix for this exact pattern adds a length bound (e.g., j + 3 < len) to these scrollbar loop conditions; here that statement is absent, which is the one-statement fix this fragment lacks.

verdict.summary: In crun_command_exec, the argument-copy loop at line 43 runs one iteration too many (bound i < argc - first_arg instead of i < argc - first_arg - 1), so the last iteration reads argv[argc] — the guaranteed NULL terminator — and passes NULL to xstrdup() at line 44, whose strdup semantics dereference it. Every `crun exec <container> <command>` (without --process) triggers a NULL-pointer dereference and crashes the runtime (DoS).

evidence.reason: Line 43's guard `i < argc - first_arg` admits i = argc - first_arg - 1, making the read index `first_arg + i + 1` exactly `argc`; argv[argc] is NULL per the C standard on the entry-point `argv` parameter, and the NULL source reaches xstrdup(), which by standard strdup semantics dereferences its argument (NULL deref, CWE-476). Guard line 17 only enforces a minimum (argc - first_arg >= 2), allocation line 42 only sizes the destination (read stays within argv[0..argc]), and terminator line 45 executes after the loop — none exclude the NULL value. The absent fix is the loop bound `i < argc - first_arg - 1` (or a NULL check that breaks before the xstrdup call), so the fragment is the vulnerable counterpart.

assumptions: argv[argc] is NULL, guaranteed by the C standard for the declared `argc`/`argv` parameters (line 1).
argp_parse (line 16) sets first_arg to the first non-option argument, so the container name is argv[first_arg] and command args are argv[first_arg+1 .. argc-1].
crun_assert_n_args (line 17) aborts unless argc - first_arg >= 2 on the else branch, so first_arg < argc and the loop at line 43 runs at least twice on every reachable path to the sink.
xstrdup() follows standard strdup semantics (dereferences its string argument) with exit-on-OOM handling, per its name.
limitations: xstrdup() is not shown; if the real implementation null-checks its argument, the loop stores a benign extra NULL slot and no crash is demonstrable inside the fragment (the off-by-one would remain a correctness defect). This interface-semantics assumption caps confidence at 0.74.
A negative LISTEN_FDS (lines 28-31) can decrement crun_context.preserve_fds, but no in-fragment consumer turns that into a security consequence.
exec_options.cap_size > 0 with a NULL exec_options.cap (lines 59-77) would feed dup_array, but cap/cap_size consistency is established by the unshown argp parser, so this was not confirmed.
process->args_len = argc (line 41) overstates the filled length, but any NULL-deref consumer of the extra zeroed slots is in the unshown libcrun_container_exec_with_options, so it was not confirmed.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in jetp3852_print_page: the guard at line 22 permits line_size == DATA_SIZE, and the trailing-zero trim loop (lines 33-34) only decreases end_data, so memset(end_data, 0, 7) at line 45 writes 7 bytes past the end of byte data[DATA_SIZE] (line 10), overwriting adjacent stack memory.

evidence.reason: Sink writes 7 bytes at end_data..end_data+6 against capacity byte data[DATA_SIZE] declared at line 10 (valid indices 0..DATA_SIZE-1). End_data = data + line_size (line 19, line 29) and the guard at line 22 rejects only line_size > DATA_SIZE, so the admitted set includes the boundary value line_size == DATA_SIZE; with data[DATA_SIZE-1] nonzero the trim loop (lines 33-34) does not decrement, making end_data == data + DATA_SIZE and the memset write indices DATA_SIZE..DATA_SIZE+6 out of bounds. This is a CWE-787 stack out-of-bounds write; the absent fix (e.g. rejecting line_size > DATA_SIZE - 7 before line 45) is absent in the fragment.

assumptions: DATA_SIZE = LINE_SIZE * 8 (line 3) is the capacity of data (line 3 definition, line 10); its value is a positive compile-time constant.
line_size from gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line (line 19) is non-negative for a valid device, and the line-22 guard constrains it to [0, DATA_SIZE], explicitly admitting equality.
Raster bytes stored by gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines (lines 30-31) may be nonzero, including the final byte at data[line_size-1], which is ordinary non-blank scan-line content.
pdev->height >= 1 for a real page, so the else branch containing the sink executes.
limitations: A negative line_size value is also admitted by line 22 but was not used as a separate finding; the confirmed witness uses the in-bound maximum.
Actual exploitability (which adjacent stack objects are corrupted) depends on stack layout not shown in the fragment.
Discarded return statuses of gp_fputs/gp_fprintf/gp_fputc/gp_fwrite are printer-I/O robustness concerns only, with no security-relevant consumer shown.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds stack write at line[llen + 1] = '\0': when a gopher line of TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 or more bytes is assembled, the guard at lines 77-79 caps llen to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1 (and line 93 adds back gopherState->len), leaving llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, so the NUL terminator is written at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-element 'line' array declared at line 6.

evidence.reason: Sink writes at index llen+1, which equals TEMP_BUF_SIZE (one past the last valid index TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 of the stack array 'line' sized TEMP_BUF_SIZE at line 6) whenever the assembled line length reaches TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1: the adjustment at line 79 (llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1, combined with llen += gopherState->len at line 93) deterministically yields llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 on the guard-fired path (line 77 condition admits the >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE set), and the unfired path still admits the exact TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 sum because the guard uses '>='. Path: line 67 loop, lines 70-73 find '\n' with llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 (or line 79 adjusts to it), line 81 is false (lpos non-NULL), line 89 false -> line 96 memcpy(line, pos, TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1) stays in bounds, then line 98 writes beyond. Input taint: unconstrained network-supplied inbuf/len with a line of >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes followed by '\n'. The protective fix ('line[llen] = '\0';', or a bound check before the write) is absent; the lines 77-79 guard caps only the copies, not the terminator index. Primary CWE-787: 1-byte out-of-bounds NUL write on the stack of a 1..TEMP_BUF_SIZE LOCAL_ARRAY.

assumptions: TEMP_BUF_SIZE is a positive compile-time constant and LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at line 6 allocates exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE elements, so valid indices are 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1.

inbuf/len and gopherState carry network-parsed gopher response data (proxy converter context); the fragment imposes no upper bound on len or line length, so a line of TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes or more is inside the admitted input domain.

gopherState->len remains in [0, TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1] for every value the fragment itself writes (line 94 sets 0 at line 94; capped increments at lines 79 and 86), which suffices for the line-98 witness regardless of its value at call entry.
limitations: The capacity of gopherState->buf is not declared in the fragment, so the memcpy at line 85 into gopherState->buf + gopherState->len cannot be independently confirmed as out-of-bounds; the across-call value of gopherState->len from unshown callers is likewise outside the fragment and an unshown caller could in principle supply an out-of-range gopherState->len.

The port[1]/port[2] reads at line 151 can read one byte past the assembled line content when the port TAB is the final byte and line[llen] is coincidentally '0', but that is entangled with the same line-assembly flaw and only reaches beyond the array in the same TEMP_BUF_SIZE-boundary case; it is demoted, not a separate finding.
A single-byte NUL write is a confirmed memory-safety violation; full exploitability (control-flow takeover) depends on stack layout, which is not shown.

verdict.summary: The protective binding-chain check in nft_verdict_init tests the misspelled flag NFT_DATA_DESC_SELETELEM (line 52) instead of the real set-element flag NFT_DATA_DESC_SETELEM, so a set-element verdict referencing a NFT_CHAIN_BINDING chain bypasses the guard and stores the chain pointer at line 57, leaving a dangling reference used after the chain is released (use-after-free).

evidence.reason: Sink line 57 stores the chain pointer in data->verdict for an admitted NFT_JUMP path (#33) selected by attacker attribute (#39) passing guards #42-43/#48-49 (non-ERR pointer) and #50-51 (non-base chain). The only rejecting guard #52-54 tests `desc->flags & NFT_DATA_DESC_SELETELEM`, a misspelled flag distinct from the set-element flag NFT_DATA_DESC_SETELEM that the set-element descriptor actually carries, so conjunct 1 is false (guard admits desc->flags with the real SETELEM bit set) and #54 never returns -EINVAL for the failure set it must exclude. Absent fix statement: correct spelling `desc->flags & NFT_DATA_DESC_SETELEM` at #52, which would reject a set-element verdict referencing a NFT_CHAIN_BINDING chain before the store; without it the stored reference can be freed by the nf_tables unbind/release path while the owning element persists, yielding use-after-free CWE-416.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched counterpart. The uninitialized-use candidate at the `if (start_visual.lnum)` gate (line 553) is fully neutralized by the initialization statement `start_visual.lnum = 0;` (line 251), which executes on every path to the gate and constrains it to either 0 or a real position assigned at lines 453/458. The tab-line click-path array read `c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];` (line 277) is bounded by the added check `&& mouse_col < Columns` (line 274), admitting indices [0, Columns-1] and excluding >= Columns. The remaining unguarded `TabPageIdxs[mouse_col]` reads on drag paths (lines 262 and 320) cannot be confirmed as out-of-bounds because the capacity of `TabPageIdxs` is neither declared nor computed within the fragment; that concern is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: TabPageIdxs is a global array whose capacity is at least Columns entries, consistent with the guard at line 274 (`mouse_col < Columns`) using the screen width as the valid-index bound; the allocation itself is not shown.
The mouse-coordinate producer (terminal mouse report decoding) yields non-negative mouse_col, so the guard at line 274 effectively admits [0, Columns-1].
end_visual is always assigned whenever start_visual is assigned (lines 453/454 and 458/459), so no uninitialized end_visual is used inside the block gated at line 553.
limitations: The drag-path reads `c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];` at lines 262 and 320 are not protected by any shown `mouse_col < Columns` bound and could OOB-read if a crafted/late drag carries `mouse_col >= Columns` after `in_tab_line` was set by a prior click (line 276) while the array is Columns-sized; the out-of-bounds cannot be confirmed as a finding because the capacity of `TabPageIdxs` is not declared or computed inside the fragment (Phase 3 capacity rule).

Negative `mouse_col` values admitted by the line 274 guard would index below the array start, but no in-fragment statement produces a negative column, so negativity is not demonstrable from shown statements.

Consequences of any residual `start_visual`/`end_visual` misuse would occur inside unshown callees (`getvcols`, `coladvance`); in-fragment, line 251 removes the demonstrated uninitialized-value read, and the remaining states are analyzed only for consequences visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded/fixed counterpart. Every allocation result (trans L20-21, alloc_workqueue L34-37, alloc_percpu L41-44) and every security-relevant return status (DMA L73-87, iomap L90-93, card init L127-137, MSI-X/ICT/IRQ L156-170) is checked fail-closed, and the NULL deref hazard on trans_pcie->hw_base is fully neutralized by the protective check at L96-100, which excludes NULL on every path to the MMIO consumers such as iwl_read32 at L109. No attacker-controllable value reaches any memory, injection, crypto, or file/access sink; no failure witness is admitted by the guards.

assumptions: pcim_iomap_table(pdev) itself does not return NULL under the shown preconditions: pcim_enable_device succeeds (L9-11) and pcim_iomap_regions_request_all(pdev, BIT(0), ...) succeeds (L89-93), establishing the device-managed iomap devres; a missing table is handled inside the callee, so the only in-fragment demonstrable NULL is the BAR-0 element, which L96-100 checks.
iwl_read32(trans, CSR_HW_REV) at L109 consumes trans_pcie->hw_base (MMIO read by name semantics); the L96-100 check is evaluated before it on every path.
cfg_trans (L3) is per-device kernel platform configuration, not derived from attacker input within this fragment.
limitations: L95 indexes pcim_iomap_table(pdev)[0] before the L96-100 NULL check, so a NULL table pointer would fault at the index before the guard; this cannot be confirmed as producible from the shown fragment (no in-fragment NULL producer, callee semantics preclude returning NULL), so it is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

trans_pcie->msix_enabled (L154) has no in-fragment assignment; its value is set by the unshown iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa (L144), so any uninitialized-use concern cannot be demonstrated from the shown code.
cfg_trans->base_params is dereferenced at L47 with no NULL check; no shown producer of NULL exists, so no NULL-deref finding is confirmable.
Return values of pci_write_config_byte (L104) and pci_set_master (L71) are discarded; no security-relevant failure consumption is shown, so this is at most a robustness concern.

verdict.summary: Not vulnerable: every write into the MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN-byte options buffer (allocated at line 79) is a bounded strlcat carrying the exact capacity (lines 82, 84, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95, 97, 98-99), and the NULL-allocation branch at line 80 skips all appends. No flag or username combination can exceed the declared capacity; this is the fixed counterpart of an unbounded strcpy/strcat overflow.

verdict.summary: When ipf_handle_frag() accepts a fragment (returns true), the fragment's original dp_packet is neither returned to the batch nor freed, because the empty TRUE path of the check at lines 17-19 is missing the upstream 'else { dp_packet_delete(pkt); }' release. Every accepted fragment leaks its heap buffer, so a remote stream of valid IP/IPv6 fragments causes unbounded memory growth in ovs-vswitchd (resource-exhaustion DoS).

evidence.reason: Sink is the status decision at lines 17-19: a fragment admitted by the guard at lines 10-14 (e.g. IPv4 fragment passing ipf_is_valid_v4_frag at line 11) for which ipf_handle_frag returns TRUE takes the empty TRUE path — the refill at line 18 is executed only when the negation is TRUE (i.e. ipf_handle_frag returned FALSE), and no dp_packet_delete exists anywhere in the fragment. pkt's sole reference (local variable set by the loop at line 9) is then lost, and since the engine retains only dp_packet_clone(pkt) (640d4db788ed semantics), the original heap dp_packet leaks on every accepted fragment, unbounded over attacker-supplied batches. The absent protective statement is 'else { dp_packet_delete(pkt); }' as added by upstream fix 803ed12e31b0; its absence constitutes CWE-401 (improper release of memory), escalating to CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption.

assumptions: pb_cnt = dp_packet_batch_size(pb) (line 5) is the batch count, at most NETDEV_MAX_BURST = 32 (same-version lib/dp-packet.h), so pb_idx is always in-bounds for the refill writes at lines 18 and 22; no OOB candidate.

DP_PACKET_BATCH_REFILL_FOR_EACH contract (same-version dp-packet.h): packets not passed back via dp_packet_batch_refill are not part of the outgoing batch and remain caller-owned, requiring explicit release.

ipf_handle_frag returning TRUE means the fragment was accepted and the engine stores only a clone (dp_packet_clone(pkt) in 640d4db788ed); it does not free or retain the original pkt — corroborated by the fixing commit deleting pkt in exactly this branch.
limitations: ipf_handle_frag internals are not shown in the fragment; the ownership link (TRUE path leaves the original packet to the caller) is established from the same-version callee implementation and the historical fix rather than from the fragment alone.

The leak is per-accepted-fragment and bounded per batch (up to 32 per call); unbounded growth requires sustained attacker traffic across many batches, making the impact a slow remote DoS rather than an immediate crash.

The alternative candidate (handled fragments being refilled due to a polarity error at line 17) was checked and is NOT present in this fragment; a use-after-free along the refill path was also checked and eliminated — the only confirmed mechanism is the missing release on the handled path.

No guard between line 30 and line 40 constrains aid_len+2 against skb->len; the absent fix is changing line 22's '&&' to '||' (or an explicit len >= aid_len+3 check). Primary CWE-125.

OOB read: with len==5 and data = [0x81, 0x01, 0x82, 0x01, 0x00], all guards up to line 47 admit the path (line 22-23 && guard fails to reject short frames with the AID tag; aid_len=1 passes line 33; params_len=1 passes line 47 because the RHS (5-2) - sizeof(struct nfc_evt_transaction) underflows to a huge size_t for len below ~290), and this memcpy reads params_len=1 byte from skb->data + 1 + 4 = data[5], one byte past len-1=4. The line 47 params-len cap does not protect short frames; the absent fix is the '||' at line 22 (or len >= aid_len+5 before this copy). Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: skb is the untrusted NFC-HCI event frame consumed by this driver handler (entry-point input); its length and payload bytes are attacker-controlled.
NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH >= 1 per the in-fragment spec comment (AID 5 to 16 bytes), and NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG == 0x81 / PARAMS_TAG == 0x82 as used at lines 23 and 41.
sizeof(transaction->aid) == 32 as implied by the line 33 comparison, and sizeof(struct nfc_evt_transaction) >= 258 so the line 47 subtraction underflows for len < ~290.
devm_kzalloc(dev, 0) returns the non-NULL ZERO_SIZE_PTR, so the len==2 witness passes the line 27 NULL check.
limitations: The exact memory exposed or panic impact of the OOB reads depends on the skb head/tail layout, which is outside the shown fragment; the confirmed defect is the out-of-bounds read itself.
Only single/few-byte overreads are demonstrated; a larger OOB write is not claimed.

verdict.summary: The ST21NFCA_EVT_TRANSACTION path validates frame length only when the AID tag byte is absent (lines 22-23 use &&), so a frame whose data[0] equals NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG is admitted at any length. The unvalidated one-byte aid_len (skb->data[1], 0..255) then drives memcpy of up to 255 bytes into the fixed aid member of a skb->len-2-byte devm_kzalloc object and reads past skb->len, yielding a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) and out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: skb is an untrusted HCI event payload; the guard at lines 22-23 returns -EPROTO only when (skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 AND skb->data[0] != NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG), so a frame with data[0]==0x81 and any length (e.g. len=3) is admitted. data[1] is stored to aid_len (line 30) with no bound check, leaving aid_len in [0,255]. With len=3, data[0]=0x81, aid_len=200, this memcpy writes 200 bytes into transaction->aid inside the 1-byte devm_kzalloc object created at line 26 (skb->len-2), overflowing the heap allocation (CWE-787), and reads 200 bytes from &skb->data[2] against a 3-byte data block, over-reading past skb->len (CWE-125). No statement between the guard and this copy bounds aid_len or skb->len; the absent fix is an aid_len range check (e.g. against NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH/NFC_MAX_AID_LENGTH and skb->len) or changing the line 22-23 operator from && to || so short frames are always rejected.

Same bypassed length guard: aid_len = skb->data[1] (line 30) is unvalidated, in [0,255]. With skb->len=3, data[0]=0x81 and aid_len=2, index aid_len+2=4 is read from skb->data whose valid span ends at index 2 (skb->len=3): an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) executed while forming the PARAMETERS-tag check. No bounds check on aid_len exists between line 30 and this read.

assumptions: skb is an attacker-influenced NFC HCI event payload (entry-point input); no shown producer establishes a minimum skb->len, and the guard itself admits any length when data[0]==0x81.
skb->data elements are bytes (u8), so data[1] has domain [0,255].

transaction is the devm_kzalloc result at line 26; a write exceeding skb->len-2 bytes overflows the allocated heap object regardless of the unshown field offset, since the write size alone exceeds the 1-byte allocation.
limitations: The struct nfc_evt_transaction layout (aid array size, params flexible array) is not shown; the CWE-787 conclusion uses only the visible 1-byte allocation (line 26) versus the 200-byte copy size (line 31).

Early-return paths (lines 24, 28, 37) skip kfree_skb, leaving a possible skb leak; treated as a robustness concern, not analyzed further.
