verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: snprintf into mfn (char mfn[MAXPATHLEN], line 34) is bounded and its <0 return checked (line 42); filearr growth (files >= maxfiles, maxfiles = (maxfiles + 1) * 2, lines 52-54) guarantees capacity above the write index used at line 64 on every path; the estrndup length is capped at sizeof(mfn)-1 (line 64), so no over-read of mfn can occur even under snprintf truncation; ecalloc/erealloc/opendir failures are checked (lines 19, 37, 56); mset[j].me[i] accesses are bounded by mset[j].count (line 80). The discarded-status and NULL-base concerns (qsort with 0 files, NULL mset[j].me[i].mp, maxfiles*sizeof overflow) are not demonstrable from the shown statements and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: mfn is char[MAXPATHLEN] (line 34) and snprintf(mfn, sizeof(mfn), ...) at line 42 writes at most sizeof(mfn)-1 characters plus NUL, so strlen(mfn) <= MAXPATHLEN-1 (standard snprintf truncation semantics).

On truncation (mflen >= sizeof(mfn)), strlen(mfn) == sizeof(mfn)-1 exactly, and otherwise mflen == strlen(mfn); hence n = min(mflen, sizeof(mfn)-1) at line 64 never exceeds the string length actually stored in mfn.
estrndup copies exactly n bytes and NUL-terminates (name-implied PHP allocator semantics); efree(NULL) is a no-op.
php_stream_readdir (line 41) yields valid directory entries with NUL-terminated d_name; php_sys_stat/stat success (lines 32, 49) makes st valid.
mset and map are zero-initialized (memset line 15; ecalloc line 19), so mset[j].count and map->magic[j] start at 0/NULL and `if (map->magic[j])` at line 110 is safe.
limitations: qsort(filearr, files, sizeof(*filearr), cmpstrp) at line 67 is called with filearr == NULL when the directory yields no regular files (lines 5-6, 41, 49-50); no dereference or crash is demonstrated in-fragment, and behavior is libc/implementation-dependent.
mset[j].me[i].mp at line 81 could be NULL only if load_1 (lines 69/74) produced an entry with NULL mp for count > 0; no such NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so CWE-476 cannot be confirmed.
Integer overflow of maxfiles = (maxfiles + 1) * 2 and mlen = maxfiles * sizeof(*filearr) (lines 54-55) requires more than 2^63 regular directory entries, which the shown code cannot derive.
set_text_binary returning i unchanged (line 85) could in principle loop forever, but its semantics are unshown; the cont_level != 0 branch at lines 81-84 does advance i.
The FIXME at lines 30-31 (unsorted directory reads) is a determinism/robustness concern, not a demonstrated security flaw.
coalesce_entries/set_last_default/magic_entry_free internals (lines 87-106) are unshown; only their call-site arguments (count, me) are visible, and those are bounded by mset[j].count.

verdict.summary: No failure is demonstrable from the shown statements alone. Every path to the sinks is covered: the fast-path fit check (L11-12) admits only req_size that fits the existing buffer, and the growth path (L14 with L16-23) rejects any req_size that cannot fit (L17-20) or clamps to MAX only when it fits (L22). The memcpy at L29, the actions_len increment at L36, and the returned write pointer at L37 are therefore all backed by an adequate capacity for every value the fragment can reach; the remaining theoretical size_t-to-int truncation at L14 would need an actions_len near 2^31+, which no shown statement can produce (limitation, not a finding).

assumptions: Invariant maintained by the fragment: after every completed call, next_offset + req_size <= ksize(*sfa), so actions_len never grows past the allocated capacity on any path (L11-12 fast path; L14/L16-23 growth path).

nla_alloc_flow_actions(new_acts_size) returns either a valid buffer of at least new_acts_size bytes or an ERR_PTR (kernel allocation convention); the failure case is handled at L26-27, and no shown statement can make *sfa NULL.
MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE is a positive compile-time constant; its numeric value is not shown, but L16-23 bounds every allocation by it.
limitations: A size_t-to-int truncation of new_acts_size at L14 (which could in theory produce an undersized allocation consumed by the memcpy at L29) requires actions_len + req_size >= 2^31 with a small low-32-bit result; there is no in-fragment producer of actions_len near 2^31 (L36 only adds req_size while the guards keep actions_len within capacity), so no witness is derivable inside the shown code.

Negative attr_len values produce via NLA_ALIGN at L7 either 0..8 or a huge size_t; every huge req_size is rejected at L17-20 before reaching the reallocation, and the fragment shows no path where it reaches the memcpy at L29.
The entry values of (*sfa)->actions_len and ksize(*sfa) are not established by any shown statement; the safety argument holds for any starting state consistent with a buffer of ksize(*sfa) bytes.
Any verdict about behavior outside this function (e.g., a caller supplying an already-oversized *sfa, or MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE >= 2^31) is unconfirmable from the shown code and was not used.

verdict.summary: No confirmed in-fragment vulnerability. MAXCOL bounds in-domain column values, so bot.col + 1 at line 55 cannot wrap for any in-domain bot.col; no shown statement produces a bot.col above MAXCOL.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in mbfl_filt_conv_big5_wchar: the search loop over cp950_pua_tbl (lines 51-55) can exit without a match, leaving k equal to the table row count, and line 57 then indexes cp950_pua_tbl[k][2] with no post-loop bounds check, reading one row past the end of the table. An attacker-controlled CP950 byte pair such as lead byte 0x81 followed by 0x40 reaches the sink: line 31 admits c=0x40, line 33 computes w=-5024, line 40 normalizes w=0, lines 45-49 admit (0x81,0x40), and any c2 not covered by a table row drives k to the row count at line 57. The missing fix is a post-loop bound/equality check before the table access.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125) at line 57: k is the loop counter of lines 51-55 whose only bound is the loop condition, so after a non-matching scan k == nrows, where nrows = sizeof(cp950_pua_tbl)/(sizeof(unsigned short)*4) (line 51) is the table's row capacity and valid indices are 0..nrows-1. The residual range of k at the sink therefore includes nrows, admitted by every guard on the path: lines 31 (c=0x40 in (0x39,0x7f)), 37/40 (w=-5024 at line 33 is normalized to 0), 45 (w<=0), 46-48 (c1=0x81 in [0x81,0x8d] and c=0x40 in (0x39,0x7f)), 50 (c2=0x8140), and line 52 (no row matches, so no break). The fix form that would neutralize the failure, a post-loop 'if (k < nrows)' or 'if (k == nrows)' check before line 57, is absent from the fragment.

assumptions: cp950_pua_tbl is a file-scope array whose row count is the in-fragment expression sizeof(cp950_pua_tbl)/(sizeof(unsigned short)*4) used as the loop bound at line 51; valid row indices are 0..nrows-1.
filter->from->no_encoding can equal mbfl_no_encoding_cp950 (line 43) for the CP950 PUA branch to be reached; line 8 uses the same comparison for the lead-byte threshold.
The filter is fed bytes of an untrusted stream in sequence, so the witness byte pair (lead byte then second byte) is attacker-controlled input.
limitations: The concrete c2 value(s) not covered by any cp950_pua_tbl row cannot be enumerated from the fragment because the table's contents are not shown; the witness is a range (e.g., c1 in [0x81,0x8d] with c in [0x40,0x7e]) and the OOB requires at least one admitted c2 that no row covers.
big5_ucs_table contents are also unshown, but the w==0 derivation for c1 < 0xa1 (line 33/35 producing a negative w, forced to 0 by lines 37/40) does not depend on those contents.
The output_function callbacks and the CK macro are treated as non-NULL / error-aborting per the framework's non-NULL convention; no NULL-derivation flaw is claimed.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The heap record buffer rr is allocated (line 45) with exact worst-case capacity rrlen = strlen(provider_name) + 15 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2 (lines 40-44), and every snprintf size is capped at rrlen - 1 - strlen(rr) (lines 50, 54, 56, 65), bounding the final written byte to absolute index rrlen-2, so no certificate content derivable from shown statements can overflow the allocation. assumptions: rr is a 1-byte-per-char buffer whose maximum content length is strlen(provider_name) + 15 (prefix, line 50) + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) (4-char escapes, line 56) + 1 (closing quote, line 65), and every snprintf call NUL-terminates when its size argument is >= 1.

Capacity at lines 40-45 (rrlen = P + 15 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 1 + 1) exactly covers the worst-case content plus NUL, and the loop bound j < sizeof(struct SignedCert) (line 51) matches the 4*sizeof budget (line 42).
sizeof(struct SignedCert) >= 1, so the escape budget 4*sizeof >= the loop iteration count.
limitations: uint16_t rrlen (line 19) truncates the size_t sum at lines 40-44; an overflow (rrlen wrapping to 0/1 so that rrlen-1 becomes SIZE_MAX) would require strlen(provider_name) ≈ 65518-65519 - 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert), a ~64 KB provider name whose value no shown statement derives — provenance class (c), unconfirmable, so not a finding.
Indexing of dnscenv->signed_certs[i] (line 21) and dnscenv->rotated_certs[j] (line 24) has no shown array capacity, so any out-of-bounds read there is unconfirmable.
strdup results (lines 6, 7, 66) are unchecked and are consumed only inside the unshown cfg_str2list_insert, whose NULL handling is not shown.

In the all-non-printable worst case the closing quote (line 65) is truncated (snprintf size becomes 1), producing a malformed-but-safe TXT string; this is a functional robustness issue, not a memory-safety finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart: every memory sink (nrinfos/info copies, strndup, meta nr_queries/querylen copies, index arithmetic) is covered by in-fragment bounds guards — L203 `exportnamelen > optlen-6`, L212 exact-layout equality, L392 `optlen < 8`, L406 maxlen-validated export name, L427/L457 `opt_index+4 > optlen`, and L463 check_string maxlen — with declared capacity `malloc(optlen+1)` at L38. verdict.summary: Fragment is the fixed counterpart of cgroup1_parse_param: the Opt_name path bounds param->size to [1, MAX_CGROUP_ROOT_NAMELEN-1] via the empty check (line 65) and length check (line 67), so the validation loop (lines 70-77) only reads param->string[0..size-1] strictly inside the size-byte buffer; the -ENOPARAM/-ENOPARAM status flow is fail-closed, and the source/release_agent/name pointer stores are each preceded by a uniqueness guard. Downstream consumers of ctx->name / ctx->release_agent / fc->source are not shown; NUL-termination and later strlen/copy safety rely on the fs_parameter contract, not on fragment-visible statements.

Opt_name and Opt_release_agent lack an explicit `param->type == fs_value_is_string` check (contrast with line 11); framework semantics make this a hardening concern (flag => size 0 rejected at line 65; blob => size-byte buffer keeps line 71 in-bounds), not a demonstrable vulnerability.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart. The one-statement protective guard at line 12 (`task_completed_or_cancelled (data->task)`) excludes every completed/cancelled-task state before any body sink touches `data->task` or `data`, so no use-after-free or other confirmed failure reaches a sink on any shown path. Remaining concerns (double-unref at lines 48-56, NULL `protocol`) depend on invariants established only by unshown producers and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: `attempt` and `data` (lines 5-6) are non-NULL: no NULL producer exists anywhere in the shown statements, and all derefs at lines 6, 12, 14-15, 19-22, 28-33, 38-39, 45-56, 58-62, 66, 75-100, 105-111 proceed from these without a NULL check.

After line 12 admits a path, `data->task` is neither completed nor cancelled, so `data` and `data->task` remain live through the body (lines 14-112); this is the protective invariant making all body derefs safe.
`proxy` is non-NULL whenever the line-92 branch executes because the assignment-in-condition only admits non-NULL results.
limitations: A double-unref/use-after-free at lines 48-56 would require showing from unshown code (`connection_attempt_new`, `connection_attempt_remove`) that the successful `attempt` is still a member of `data->connection_attempts` at line 48 and that the list holds its final reference; neither is derivable from the fragment, so it is not confirmable.

`protocol` (line 70) could be NULL if `g_proxy_address_get_protocol` returned NULL, but no NULL producer is shown; its only consumers are a hash lookup (line 86), a NULL-checked factory (line 92), and value-position `%s` formatting (line 109), none of which is an exploitable sink on an admitted path.
The `G_SOCKET_CONNECTION (source)` cast at line 25 relies on the unshown async-callback contract; no type-confusion or memory-safety consequence is demonstrable from shown statements.

Cancellation/completion interleaving between the line-12 check and later uses (e.g., line 98) would require threading/re-entrancy that is not present in the fragment, so race-based use-after-free is out of scope.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The only directly reachable dangerous call, expr->ops->offload(ctx, flow, expr) at line 39, is fully guarded on every path by the NULL target check at lines 35-38 (excluded bound: ops->offload == NULL) and by the fail-closed return check at lines 40-41. The flow-rule capacity (num_actions at line 20) is derived from the same counter at lines 11-12, and no shown statement produces an index or count exceeding it; any out-of-bounds write would require unshown offload-callee behavior and is recorded as a limitation. num_actions == 0 (lines 17-18) and the allocation NULL checks (lines 21-22, 27-30) are all present, and every err_out path assigns err before line 55 reads it.

assumptions: nft_expr_first / nft_expr_more / nft_expr_next (lines 9-10, 14, 24, 34, 43) follow their name-implied nf_tables iterator semantics: they enumerate exactly the rule's own expression array without returning NULL or running past its end; no in-fragment statement can derive a degenerate or out-of-range expr.
nft_flow_rule_alloc(num_actions) (line 20) allocates an action-array capacity of num_actions entries, matching the counter built at lines 11-12.
kfree(NULL) is a no-op under the kernel's standard semantic, so the err_out path entered from line 29 with ctx == NULL is safe.

Each expression flagged NFT_OFFLOAD_F_ACTION corresponds to exactly one action slot written by its offload handler; this invariant is NOT visible in the fragment, which is why the OOB hypothesis cannot be confirmed or categorically refuted here.
limitations: An out-of-bounds write into flow->rule->data via expr->ops->offload (line 39) or nft_flow_rule_transfer_vlan (line 45) would require offload handlers to write more actions than the line-20 capacity; those callee bodies are unshown, and no in-fragment numeric derivation (index or count) exceeds num_actions, so this candidate is demoted to a limitation, not a finding.
err (line 6) is declared without an initializer, but every err_out predecessor assigns it (lines 28, 36, 39) before line 55 reads it; no uninitialized-use (CWE-457) path is derivable.
flow->proto = ctx->dep.l3num (line 47) can yield proto == 0 if no L3 expression set the dependency, which is a correctness concern without a shown security consequence.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of the XBM parser. Every attacker-controlled magnitude is bounded before reaching a memory sink: width/height must be > 0 (lines 41/46) and non-zero (line 83); the allocation product is validated against overflow by `size / bytes_per_line != hh` (lines 94-95); and in the v10 path `bytes_per_line` is always even (line 86 gates padding to ww%16 in 1..8, and lines 91), so the byte-pair loop writes exactly `size` (padding=0) or `size - hh` (padding=1) bytes, never past `g_malloc(size)` at line 96. The v8 loop writes exactly `size` bytes (line 113-116). Unbounded `%s` into `name_and_type[MAX_SIZE]` is capped by `fgets` (line 30) and the line-length guard (line 31), and even unguarded the token+NUL cannot exceed the array capacity. All `next_int`/parse statuses are checked (lines 103/114 and sscanf arity tests). No demonstrated failing value reaches a sink.

assumptions: MAX_SIZE is a positive compile-time constant declared outside the fragment (the array capacities at lines 9 and 11 depend on it).
int and guint are 32-bit with two's-complement wrap semantics, matching the code's own overflow-check idiom at lines 94-95.
g_malloc never returns NULL and g_free(NULL) is safe (GLib semantics), so the `if (!bits)` test at line 122 is redundant, not a producer of NULL.
Output parameters width/height/data are treated as non-NULL per the plain-parameter rule; they are only written at lines 125-127 after all parsing succeeds.
limitations: next_int's definition is not shown; its failure convention (negative return) is inferred from the `< 0` checks at lines 103/114 and is handled on both call paths.
`initialized` and `init_hex_table()` are external and their status is discarded, but no input-derived data flows into them and no security consequence is visible.
The 'hot' value is stored without validation, but hx/hy are consumed only as output ints; no security-relevant consumer is shown.

A divide-by-zero at line 94 would require `bytes_per_line == 0`, which needs `ww+7` to wrap (ww > UINT_MAX-7); the `value <= 0` guards at lines 41/46 restrict ww to [1, INT_MAX], excluding this - demoted, not a finding.

The unbounded `%s` in the sscanf calls is conventionally dangerous, but the token length is bounded by the fgets cap and the line-length guard such that token+NUL never exceeds the declared `name_and_type` capacity - demoted.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability: the fragment already contains the protective statements — the maywrite authorization gate (L36-39) excluding maywrite==0 before all quota and write sinks, the NULL-userid rejection for live-value writes (L83), the identical-value early-out with zero-length memcmp guard (L33), and the sized key buffer (L12 with sizeof(key) passed at L26). The quota diff at L44 uses unsigned wrap for negative deltas; any wrap only causes a fail-closed quota denial, so it is a robustness concern, not a vulnerability.
Unshown callers' contracts for value, entry, userid, and maywrite are not assumed; nothing in the fragment derives a failing value from them.

Line 3 dereferences the parameter sock without a shown NULL guard; sock is a plain parameter so NULL is not demonstrable in-fragment.

Only the shown fragment is analyzed; the external lifecycle invariant that ax25->ax25_dev can become NULL (device removal) is not visible in this fragment and was treated strictly per the shown-code rule.

verdict.summary: No demonstrated failing value reaches a dangerous operation. The quickfix-chain traversal is protected by the visible NULL check `if (qfp == NULL) break;` (lines 72-73), which excludes qfp==NULL from every subsequent dereference at lines 66, 69, and 71; the qftf-list traversal (lines 58, 75), the tv_get_string_chk NULL result (lines 61-62), the call_qftf_func NULL result (lines 48-49), the qfl!=NULL gate (line 23), and the qf_buf_add_line FAIL status (lines 66-67) are all guarded on every path. limitations: A NULL qfl->qf_start with qf_count > 0 (line 34 feeding lines 66/69/71) is not producible inside the fragment; no NULL producer is shown, so this is an unconfirmable caller-state hypothesis, not a finding.
buf is dereferenced at line 43 with no NULL check on the old_last != NULL path; a NULL buf would require an unshown caller, so this is a limitation.

ml_delete(lnum + 1) at line 81 has no visible bound guard, but the buffer's line-count capacity is never declared in the fragment and ml_delete's standard failure mode is an internal-error/FAIL, not memory corruption; demoted to robustness.
(long)(lnum + 1) at line 46 could only overflow with an lnum near the type maximum, a magnitude not derivable from the shown statements.
The line-18 delete loop could only fail to terminate under an ML_EMPTY invariant violation that the fragment cannot produce.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. All dereferences of priv/ndev/nfc_dev (lines 3, 6) occur before the only shown frees (nci_free_device line 14, kfree line 15); no statement in the fragment produces NULL or frees ndev/nfc_dev before line 6, and nci_unregister_device (line 5) is name-implied as unregister-only, paired with the explicit nci_free_device. priv->ndev (line 3) is non-NULL and equals the local ndev; nothing in the fragment reassigns or frees it before its last use at lines 6/14.

NULL-deref behavior inside the unshown helpers nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_abort (line 7) and nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_deinit (line 9) (e.g., unguarded priv->fw_dnld) is out of scope; the fragment shows no producer of NULL for their arguments.
A possible race with a concurrent firmware-download completion is not demonstrable from the shown statements (no synchronization or freed-object producer is visible).
The unconditional nfcmrvl_fw_dnld_deinit(priv) after the flag-gated abort (lines 6-9) is at most duplicate-cleanup robustness, with no in-fragment security consequence.

verdict.summary: In the connect-failure branch, `data` (from `attempt->data` at L6, which the fragment itself can set to NULL at L55 and treats as nullable at L12-L13) is dereferenced at L31 (`data->connectable`) whenever the guard at L29 admits `!g_cancellable_is_cancelled(...)`. The only NULL guards — L13 and L37 — do not cover L31: L13 short-circuits FALSE exactly when `data == NULL`, and L37 is evaluated only after the dereference. The absent protective statement is a `data &&` NULL check on the L29 condition (or an `if (data)` guard before L31), so a NULL `GSocketClientAsyncConnectData *` reaches the dereference, causing a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: Sink dereferences `data->connectable` while `data` may be NULL. NULL provenance: `data = attempt->data` (L6); `data` is a NULL-admitted value per the in-fragment producer `attempt_entry->data = NULL` (L55), the comment at L12, and the guards at L13/L37. Path and guard order: L13 passes because `data && g_task_return_error_if_cancelled(...)` short-circuits to FALSE when `data == NULL`; L26 admits connect_finish failure; L29 admits `not cancelled` and constrains only `attempt->cancellable`, never `data`; L37 (`if (data)`) is evaluated after L31 and protects only L39-41. The admitted set {data==NULL, not cancelled, failure} is non-empty, so the failure set reaches the sink. Absent fix (Fix-Scan): `data &&` added to the condition at L29, or an `if (data)` wrapping L31-32 — no visible statement covers the failure set. Mechanism: loading `->connectable` from a NULL `GSocketClientAsyncConnectData *` is a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476), yielding a crash/DoS in the GLib GSocketClient connect flow.

assumptions: The fragment's own comment at L12 ('data is NULL once the task is completed') is taken as in-fragment evidence that a NULL `data` state is an expected, reachable state.
`g_socket_connection_connect_finish` may return FALSE (failure), and `g_cancellable_is_cancelled` may return FALSE; both outcome arms are explicitly written at L26-29.
GSList iteration at L51-57 is NULL-safe (`l = g_slist_next(l)`) and the list is not mutated during iteration (freed at L58).
limitations: The NULL write candidates at L48-49 (and later `data` derefs at L62-66) are not confirmed: reaching them requires `g_socket_connection_connect_finish` to succeed while `data == NULL`, which the shown statements do not derive.

The suspected double-unref of `attempt` at L56/L60 (loop unrefs entries, then `connection_attempt_unref (attempt)` at L60) depends on the current attempt being a member of `data->connection_attempts` and on refcount semantics not shown in the fragment; not confirmed.

The confirmed NULL-deref witness rests on the co-occurrence of `data == NULL` with `not cancelled` (the fragment's own producer at L54-55 correlates cancellation with NULL for other attempts); the safe correlation 'NULL implies cancelled' cannot be assumed from outside the fragment, and this is the link that limits confidence.
The `%s` format at L111-113 uses a literal format string; `protocol` is not attacker-controlled, so no format-string injection is present.
If `protocol` could be NULL, the `%s` at L113 would be separately unsafe, but no NULL producer for it is shown; not a finding.

verdict.summary: On the sp->source_from_buf path, after line 31 appends a NUL and increments ga.ga_len, line 40 computes STRLEN(buf + ga.ga_len) starting one byte past that NUL. For an attacker-controlled sourced-buffer line of length ga.ga_maxlen - 1, ga.ga_len equals ga.ga_maxlen and STRLEN reads the first byte past the ga_maxlen-byte ga.ga_data allocation, a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) whose resulting len then feeds further OOB buf[len-1] accesses.

evidence.reason: The STRLEN at line 40 reads from buf + ga.ga_len on the buffer-branch path where line 31 (buf[ga.ga_len++] = NUL;) has already advanced ga.ga_len past the NUL appended after the line copied by ga_concat (line 26); the byte at index ga.ga_len has no in-fragment guarantee of NUL termination. The ga.ga_data object has ga.ga_maxlen bytes, the capacity this code itself uses at lines 36 and 57. For an entry-point buffer line of length ga.ga_maxlen - 1 (line length L is unconstrained by any guard; with the line-20 ga_grow setting ga_maxlen = 120, a 119-byte line suffices), ga.ga_len == ga.ga_maxlen after line 31, so STRLEN's first byte read is at index ga_maxlen, past the allocation: heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Guards on the path (lines 20, 24, 28) are all admitted: line 24 bounds only sp->buf_lnum, line 28 only guarantees room for the line-31 NUL write and actually produces the exact-fit case. The absent protective statement is 'len = ga.ga_len;' inside the if (sp->source_from_buf) block, keeping the STRLEN-based length computation solely in the fgets branch; without it, the indeterminate len also drives OOB buf[len-1] reads at lines 57 and 60.

assumptions: ga_grow(&ga, n) guarantees ga.ga_maxlen >= ga.ga_len + n and returns FAIL only on allocation failure — the semantics the fragment itself relies on for the writes at lines 31 and 36.
ga_concat(&ga, s) copies strlen(s) bytes and advances ga.ga_len by strlen(s) without appending a NUL, as confirmed by the explicit NUL write at line 31.
When sp->source_from_buf is true, the line at line 26 is entry-point data (script text held in a Vim buffer) whose content and length are attacker-controlled and unconstrained by the shown fragment.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in the octet-counting digit phase: the write at line 42 stores each count digit into pThis->pMsg[pThis->iMsg] with no iMsg bound. iMsg can already equal iMaxLine (reached via the bounded stuffing writes at lines 102-103 and preserved across the delimiter transition at lines 90-96, which never resets iMsg), so a crafted digit then writes at index iMaxLine, one past the iMaxLine-element message buffer, with further digits overflowing past it.

evidence.reason: Sink: heap write at index pThis->iMsg of the iMaxLine-element buffer pThis->pMsg (capacity model: every other write is bounded by iMaxLine, lines 102 and 109-115). iMsg reaches iMaxLine via iMaxLine non-delimiter chars admitted by line 102 (iMsg < iMaxLine) and written at line 103, then a '\n' at lines 90-96 transitions to eAtStrtFram without resetting iMsg (the only reset, line 64, is in the octet-count terminator branch, not on this path). A following digit '5' is admitted by lines 13-14 (bSuppOctetFram, isdigit), 32 (isdigit), and 33 (iOctetsRemain=0 <= 200000000), reaching line 42 with iMsg == iMaxLine, so the write lands at index iMaxLine and subsequent digits at iMaxLine+1, +2, ... (the count cap at line 33 bounds the arithmetic, not the index; the too-large branch at lines 35-40 changes state only after the current digit's write). Absent fix: an 'if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine)' guard around this write (exactly as present for the identical write at line 103). Primary CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write of attacker-controlled digit bytes.

assumptions: pThis->pMsg is the iMaxLine-element message buffer; this capacity is derivable from the fragment's own guards (lines 102, 109-115) which treat iMaxLine as the exclusive maximum index for both other writers.
Octet-counting framing support must be enabled on the session (pThis->bSuppOctetFram true, line 14) for the eInOctetCnt path to be reachable.
iMaxLine is positive (it is used as the message-size bound throughout the fragment); the attacker sends iMaxLine bytes to set iMsg == iMaxLine.
limitations: The pMsg allocation itself is not shown in the fragment; capacity is inferred from the iMaxLine-based guard model rather than a literal declaration line.
isdigit(c) at line 32 with a negative char value (high-bit bytes) is undefined behavior but is not the confirmed finding.
Post-overflow heap layout/exploitability beyond the first out-of-bounds byte cannot be assessed from the fragment.

verdict.summary: In the CP950 PUA branch, the row-search loop over cp950_pua_tbl can run to exhaustion leaving k equal to the table row count (line 47); the subsequent unconditional cp950_pua_tbl[k] reads at lines 53-57 then dereference one row past the table (out-of-bounds read). Row capacity of cp950_pua_tbl is the in-fragment expression sizeof(cp950_pua_tbl)/(sizeof(unsigned short)*4) at line 47, and a for-loop with condition k < N exits with k == N when no break occurs.
The PUA conversion block is reached only for cp950 (line 43) with w == 0 (line 45), which the shown arithmetic admits for lead bytes 0x81..0xa0 and valid second bytes.
limitations: Reachability of the no-match case depends on is_in_cp950_pua(c1, c) (line 45) returning nonzero for a byte pair that matches no cp950_pua_tbl row; the predicate's body is not shown, so its admitted set vs. the loop's match set cannot be fully resolved from the fragment (this is the exact historical bug state, later fixed by adding a k < row_count guard).

verdict.summary: Fixed counterpart: the exact-length guard at line 27 (`if (ticklen + 6 != n)`) forces ticklen == n - 6 on the only path reaching the malloc (line 36), memcpy (line 41), and EVP_Digest (lines 54-57) sinks, so every network-derived ticket length is exactly equal to both the allocation size and the remaining message bytes, leaving no out-of-bounds or overflow path.

n2s (line 25) reads exactly two bytes and yields ticklen in [0, 65535], never negative, so the int arithmetic `ticklen + 6` cannot overflow and cannot corrupt the line-27 comparison.
s->init_msg (line 23) holds the n-byte received message, so p advanced 6 bytes points to exactly n - 6 readable bytes.

verdict.summary: addBinding's int len can wrap from INT_MAX to INT_MIN at the namespace-separator increment (line 64); on the reusable-binding path (line 67 false) the wrapped value reaches memcpy(b->uri, uri, len * sizeof(XML_Char)) (line 119) and b->uri[len-1] (line 121) with no intervening guard, causing a heap out-of-bounds write. The only near guards (lines 69/97) run after the overflow and admit INT_MIN, and they are skipped entirely on the reuse path. The upstream fix — if (len == INT_MAX) return XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY; before len++ — is absent.

evidence.reason: Sink: memcpy size is len * sizeof(XML_Char) with len = INT_MIN. Phase 1: uri (entry-point attacker-controlled namespace URI, no length cap in the fragment) yields len == INT_MAX from the sentinel loop at line 45; the separator branch at lines 63-64 wraps int len to INT_MIN (INT_MAX + 1). The free-list path condition at line 67 (len > b->uriAlloc) is false for INT_MIN, so the overflow guards at lines 69 and 77-81 are skipped, and the wrapped value reaches this copy with a size of ~2^64 - 2^33 bytes (XML_Char 4 bytes) against b->uri whose capacity is the small prior uriAlloc set at lines 88/116. Guards at lines 69/97 admit INT_MIN (INT_MIN > INT_MAX - EXPAND_SPARE is false) and line 69 is not evaluated on this path. Absent fix: if (len == INT_MAX) return XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY; before len++ at line 64 (and at loop head line 45). Mechanism: heap out-of-bounds write, CWE-787, from CWE-190 signed wrap.

Sink: index len - 1 with len = INT_MIN (wrapped at lines 63-64 from a uri of length INT_MAX as derived by the line 45 loop) computes a massively negative offset into b->uri (capacity uriAlloc from lines 88/116), i.e. an out-of-bounds write of the separator byte. The same path analysis as the line 119 memcpy applies: line 67 excludes the only guards (lines 69, 77-81) because INT_MIN > b->uriAlloc is false, and no pre-increment INT_MAX check exists. Absent fix: if (len == INT_MAX) return XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY; before len++. Primary CWE-787 OOB write; secondary CWE-190.

assumptions: uri is a NUL-terminated XML_Char string; the loop at line 45 establishes uri[len] == '\0' at loop exit (capacity of the string object includes the terminator).
parser->m_namespaceSeparator is treated as possibly non-zero because no constraint on it appears in the fragment (line 63).
parser->m_freeBindingList non-NULL is an admitted state: the fragment itself reads and relinks it (lines 66, 90); b->uriAlloc >= 0 on such a reused binding.
EXPAND_SPARE is a positive build-time constant (not defined in the fragment).
limitations: The failing witness requires uri length exactly INT_MAX (about 2^31 XML_Chars); that magnitude is not produced by a shown statement but is permitted by the fragment, which caps nothing (range/boundary witness, hence confidence 0.74).
The INT_MAX -> INT_MIN wrap is signed-overflow UB in ISO C, though two's-complement wrap is universal on supported targets.

On 32-bit size_t builds, the memcpy byte count (size_t)INT_MIN * sizeof(XML_Char) may wrap to 0; the line 121 OOB write remains the demonstrable sink there, and the line 78/105 SIZE_MAX guards apply only inside the realloc/malloc branches.
Reachability of the free-list path assumes a binding previously parked in parser->m_freeBindingList by unshown unbinding code; the branch is in-fragment-admitted but its population is external.

verdict.summary: tipc_crypto_key_rcv copies attacker-controlled key material into a kmalloc(size) buffer (line 17) whose size (line 6, u16) and key length (line 24, u32 from ntohl) are never bounded relative to each other before the memcpy at lines 26-27; the only size sanity check (line 30) runs after the copy, so keylen > size - TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME - sizeof(__be32) yields a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: The sink copies skey->keylen bytes (Phase 1 residual range [0, 2^32-1], sourced from ntohl of message data at line 24) into the object allocated at line 17 (capacity exactly `size`, u16 range [0,65535] from line 6). Neither magnitude is constrained before this memcpy: guards at line 10 (existing-key path) and line 18 (kmalloc NULL) admit the witness, and the only size check at line 30 executes after the sink (guard order 30 > 27) so it cannot protect the write. Witness size=64, keylen=65535 reaches offset TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME+4+65535 > 64, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the absent fix is a pre-copy validation bounding keylen against size (e.g., moving the line-30 sanity check before line 25).

assumptions: sizeof(__be32) == 4 and TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME is a positive compile-time constant (the witness is insensitive to its exact value since 65535 > 64 - TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME - 4 for any such constant).
kmalloc(size) returns an object of at least `size` usable bytes and may return NULL; its NULL branch is checked at line 18.
limitations: Out-of-bounds reads of the message payload (line 24 source read and the source sides of the memcpys at lines 25-27) are not confirmed because the capacity of the buffer `data` points into is not declared in the shown fragment.
Dereference of tx->wq at line 46 is not a confirmed NULL deref because no in-fragment statement can produce NULL for tipc_net(rx->net)->crypto_tx.
No integer-overflow (CWE-190) finding: keylen is not truncated and the failure is a direct capacity-exceeding write, correctly attributed to CWE-787.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart. verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The strchr result is NULL-checked (L11-12) before use in http_hdr_flags (L13), and the http_hdr_flags result is NULL-checked (L14) before f->flag is dereferenced. The only remaining candidate, an out-of-bounds read of fm->hdf[u]/fm->hd[u] for large u, cannot be confirmed because the capacity of these arrays is not declared or computed anywhere in the fragment and no caller is shown.

verdict.summary: NOT vulnerable: the fragment is the fixed counterpart. The register-cursor advance is NUL-guarded at L140-141 (advance admitted only when **arg != NUL, excluding the NUL position), curly-name alias use is NULL-guarded at L198-199, non-positive name lengths are rejected at L201-202, and leader/name paths keep all cursor advances at-or-before the NUL. assumptions: *arg points into a NUL-terminated expression buffer and the NUL is the terminal boundary, evidenced in-fragment by L129 IS_WHITE_OR_NUL(**arg) and L140 **arg != NUL.
get_name_len's standard contract: returned len is the byte length of the name and any alias it allocates holds len+1 bytes; used only to show STRNCMP/eval_* consume within the (s,len) pair.
eval_leader stops at the first non-leader byte (its loop is unshown).
limitations: handle_subscript receives name_start which may point to the alias freed at L257 (assigned at L245); the fragment never dereferences name_start and the callee's use is unshown, so CWE-416 is unconfirmable.

rettv->vval.v_partial->pt_func (L154) and ufunc->uf_ret_type (L159) are dereferenced under ret == OK after the unshown get_lambda_tv; no NULL producer is visible in the fragment, so CWE-476 is unconfirmable.

Non-vim9 input '@\0' reaches get_reg_contents(NUL, ...); the callee's handling is unshown.
The fragment declares no array/object capacity, so OOB claims (CWE-121/122/125/787) that require a shown capacity are unsupportable.

verdict.summary: In octet-counting framing, the octet count is accumulated into a signed int (line 33) with no digit-count or overflow cap and with only a log-only validity check (lines 40-44) that does not stop processing (line 54 still runs). A 10-digit count such as '2147483648 ' wraps iOctetsRemain to INT_MIN, which the buffLen clamp (lines 100-102) and the iMaxLine clamp (lines 103-105) both fail to bound because both comparisons are false for negative values; the negative int is then widened to a huge size_t at memcpy (line 108), causing a heap buffer overflow on pMsg plus an out-of-bounds read from *buff.

evidence.reason: octatesToCopy (int) inherits iOctetsRemain from line 98; iOctetsRemain is accumulated from network digits at line 33 (pThis->iOctetsRemain = pThis->iOctetsRemain * 10 + c - '0') with no shown digit-count or overflow cap, so 10 digits '2147483648' wrap the accumulator to INT_MIN (-2147483648). The only validity check, line 40 if(pThis->iOctetsRemain < 1), merely logs (lines 42-44) and line 54 still sets inputState = eInMsg, so the negative count survives. The clamps at lines 100-102 and 103-105 admit the negative value because both comparisons (buffLen < octatesToCopy and octatesToCopy + pThis->iMsg > iMaxLine) are false for negatives, so the memcpy at line 108 receives INT_MIN as its length; converting the negative int to size_t yields an enormous length, overflowing the iMaxLine-capacity pMsg (capacity implied by the truncation bounds at lines 92 and 103-105) and reading out of bounds from *buff. Primary CWE-787 heap overflow; secondary CWE-190 from the line-33 signed overflow. The absent small fix is a guard/clamp rejecting octatesToCopy < 1 on the path to line 108 (or FINALIZE after the line-40 diagnostic).

assumptions: pMsg is allocated to iMaxLine bytes, as implied by the fragment's consistent use of iMaxLine to cap every pMsg write (lines 92-93, 103-105).
pThis->iMsg stays within [0, iMaxLine] because the only shown increments (lines 93 and 109) are bounded by the guards at lines 92 and 103-105.
buffLen reflects the actual size of *buff and is >= 1 on every executed path because line 10 dereferences **buff.
The caller (rcvData loop) advances *buff by exactly one byte per call, consistent with the '- 1' pointer adjustment at line 111.

int is 32-bit two's complement and signed overflow wraps in the build (default GCC/Clang -O2 behavior); with -ftrapv or UBSan the same input causes an abort instead of a wrap, still attacker-triggerable.
Octet-counting framing is enabled (bSuppOctetFram), which is the attacker-facing configuration gate at line 14.
limitations: Signed overflow at line 33 is formally undefined behavior in ISO C; the negative-value witness relies on the standard two's-complement wrap behavior of the target build.
The one-byte-per-call caller advance convention is inferred from the shown '- 1' at line 111 and is not itself displayed.
The zero-octet-count case (TODO at line 41) is a robustness/framing logic concern only and was not escalated.
The emergency-flush scan (lines 64-70) is bounded by buffLen and was analyzed and cleared, not flagged.
No literal allocation line for pMsg appears in the fragment; its capacity is derived from the shown iMaxLine bounds.

Every dangerous operation is covered by a protective statement visible in the fragment: the resource bound check at L7-8 admits only 0..RLIM_NLIMITS-1 before the L13 index and L35 store; cur<=max is enforced at L11-12; hard-limit raises are capability-gated at L14-16; RLIMIT_NOFILE is capped at NR_OPEN at L17-18; the security hook status is checked at L20-22; and RLIMIT_CPU zero/infinity values are neutralized at L24-31 and L47-48. assumptions: current->signal->rlim is an array of RLIM_NLIMITS rlimit entries; this capacity is evidenced by the guard at L7 using the same constant RLIM_NLIMITS that bounds the index used at L13 and L35.
old_rlim derived at L13 is non-NULL because it is in-bounds arithmetic within the rlim array after the L7 check; no statement in the fragment can produce NULL.
copy_from_user returning nonzero (including a NULL user pointer) is fully handled by the -EFAULT return at L9-10.
limitations: A hypothetical 32-bit overflow of secs_to_cputime(rlim_cur) at L55 cannot be confirmed: the pre-conversion magnitudes, HZ, and cputime_t width are not shown in the fragment, and no security-relevant consumer of a possibly corrupted value is demonstrated.

The RLIMIT_CPU timer path at L50-58 is only reachable for resource == RLIMIT_CPU after L38-39; any residual functional concern there (e.g., the documented long-standing error-code behavior in the comment at L41-46) is out of scope of the memory/injection/authz focus and does not constitute a finding.
Only RLIMIT_NOFILE is explicitly capped at NR_OPEN; other resources rely on the old-limit and capability gates, which are all present in the fragment.

verdict.summary: krb5_sname_to_principal() at lines 30-32 can fail leaving princ NULL (initialized at line 6), but the return status is never checked before princ is passed to krb5_kt_get_entry() at lines 34-38, which dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference / denial of service. The absent fix is a 'if (krb5rc) goto exit;' check after the sname_to_principal call (the only NULL guard, line 50, protects only the later free).

evidence.snippet:
krb5rc = krb5_kt_get_entry(krb5context, krb5keytab, 
                                princ,
                                0 /* IGNORE_VNO */,
                                0 /* IGNORE_ENCTYPE */,
                                &entry);
evidence.reason: princ is NULL-initialized at line 6 and is only updated by krb5_sname_to_principal at lines 30-32, whose nonzero krb5_error_code return is discarded (overwritten at line 34). On any such failure princ stays NULL and is passed as the third argument here at line 35 with no equality/NULL check between line 32 and this call; the only NULL guard, 'if (princ)' at line 50, runs after this sink and guards only krb5_free_principal. The absent protective statement is 'if (krb5rc) goto exit;' following line 32 (or 'if (!princ) goto exit;' before line 34). krb5_kt_get_entry dereferences the principal per standard Kerberos semantics, so the NULL principal triggers CWE-476; the unchecked return of krb5_sname_to_principal is the enabling CWE-252 status-handling flaw.

assumptions: krb5_init_context success yields a valid non-NULL krb5context (line 10-11 guards failure).
After passing the checks at lines 19/25, krb5keytab is a valid resolved/default keytab.
The ternary at line 31 guarantees sname is non-NULL, so a NULL princ can only come from a failing krb5_sname_to_principal leaving the line-6 NULL initialization intact.
krb5_kt_get_entry dereferences its principal argument, per standard MIT Kerberos krb5_kt_get_entry semantics (principal realm/name components are read).
limitations: The exact error values produced by krb5_sname_to_principal (e.g., ENOMEM, invalid/empty service name) are not shown; the witness is a range of nonzero returns and depends on environment/config conditions.
The dereference of the NULL principal occurs inside unshown krb5 library code and is inferred from name-implied semantics.

The NOTFOUND branch (lines 39-41) sets rc=1 while the success path also sets rc=1 (line 46), which appears logically inverted, but no shown consumer of the function's return value is present, so that logic issue is unconfirmed.
Whether an attacker can directly force krb5_sname_to_principal to fail depends on unshown callers/config; the in-fragment finding is a DoS on the checked keytab-availability path.

verdict.summary: The mkdir return status is captured (line 15) and fully guarded by `if (rv != 0) SCM_SYSERROR;` (lines 16-17), so every failure raises an error and the success path cannot silently continue. The mode value from `scm_to_uint` (line 13) is caller-chosen, bounded to [0, UINT_MAX], and only influences permission bits that umask and kernel masking additionally constrain, with the caller owning the created directory; no memory-safety, injection, or access-control failure is demonstrable within the fragment.

assumptions: `scm_to_uint` signals an out-of-range error for negative values and values greater than UINT_MAX, bounding `c_mode` to [0, UINT_MAX] (standard Guile conversion semantics).
`STRING_SYSCALL` asserts that `path` is a string, converts it to a NUL-terminated locale buffer, and frees it after the syscall (standard Guile macro semantics).
`SCM_SYSERROR` raises a Scheme error using the saved errno, so an `rv != 0` result cannot pass silently.
`mkdir`'s standard semantics apply the process umask and use only permission/flag bits of the mode.
limitations: If `mode_t` is narrower than 32 bits (e.g. 16-bit `unsigned short` on some platforms), a mode value above the type's maximum truncates; the worst outcome is a caller-supplied permission set on a directory the caller owns, so no CWE is confirmable and this is treated as robustness only.

A `path` containing embedded NUL bytes would be truncated at the first NUL by `mkdir`, but the fragment neither shows a protective statement for it nor demonstrates a crossed security boundary, since the path is supplied by the calling Scheme program in the same trust domain.
No memory-copy, index, format-string, crypto, or injection sinks exist in the fragment; there are no further confirmed or candidate vulnerabilities.

Lines 148-152: dump_header(s, name, iter->second) writes attr name/value into an HTTP header with no visible CR/LF sanitization, but attrs provenance (attacker control and any ingestion-time sanitization) and dump_header semantics are outside the shown fragment; CWE-117 cannot be confirmed.
Line 54 total_len += metadata_bl.length(): signed/unsigned overflow requires impractical values not derivable from the shown code, with no demonstrated security-relevant consumer.
Lines 106-122 are safe because of the is_anonymous() rejection at 112-114; anonymous response-header manipulation is not admitted.

The KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND branch (lines 42-44) sets rc=1 ("available") even though the host-key entry is missing. No caller or security decision is shown consuming this value, so it is a robustness/semantic observation, not a confirmed finding.
Return statuses of the cleanup calls krb5_kt_close/krb5_free_principal/krb5_free_context (lines 52-54) are discarded; this is resource-cleanup-only and not security-relevant within the fragment.

verdict.summary: Line 7's guard `if (p > end) return 0;` admits `p == end`, so `len = *p++;` at line 10 dereferences one byte past the end-exclusive input region when the remaining stream is empty (a state the fragment itself produces via line 17 when a record exactly consumes the remainder); the neutralizing fix `if (p >= end) return 0;` (or a `p + 1 > end` remaining-bytes probe) is absent.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read: `p` retains the value `p == end` after the line 7 guard `if (p > end) return 0;` (admitted set `p <= end`, so `>` excludes only pointers beyond `end`); `*data == end` is derived in-fragment — line 17 `*data += 1 + len;` yields `end` exactly when the record ends at the boundary admitted by line 11's `p + len > end` check — and then line 10 `len = *p++;` dereferences `end`, one byte outside the `[.., end)` region the fragment's own guards (lines 7 and 11) define. The absent fix statement is `if (p >= end) return 0;` (or an equivalent `p + 1 > end` / `end - p < 1` pre-read probe); the later guard at line 11 is evaluated only after the read and cannot protect it. Primary CWE-125 (OOB read).

assumptions: `end` is treated as an exclusive upper bound of the readable input region, as evidenced by line 7 (`p > end`) and line 11 (`p + len > end`, which admits `p + len == end`).
`p_malloc` is treated per pool/g_malloc convention as non-failing (no NULL producer is shown), so its unchecked result at line 14 is not a demonstrated NULL dereference.
limitations: The capacity is conveyed by the `end` pointer rather than a declared array, so the failure is proven relative to the end-exclusive region the fragment's own guards define, not a named declaration.

Reaching line 10 with `p == end` requires either a caller-supplied exhausted-stream entry state or a prior invocation whose record exactly consumed the remainder (line 17 sets `*data == end`) followed by another invocation; that re-invocation is not shown in the fragment.
Line 17 can form the one-past pointer `end + 1`, which is legal pointer formation and was not treated as a finding.
The line 15 `memcpy` copy is fully covered by the line 11 guard (`p + len <= end` admitted, boundary equality safe) and was demoted.

All ratio arithmetic (L14, L62, L114) coerces `long long` operands to `double`, so no integer overflow/truncation occurs; `kMaxPresampleSize + 5` (L125) is size_t literal addition.
`CollectionShardingState::get` (L53), `coll`, and `coll->getRecordStore()` (L34) are non-NULL by framework contract; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: A guest-controlled, unvalidated RTAS nargs field is used at line 28 to index args.args, so args.rets can be set to a pointer outside the stack-resident rtas_args object; the handler invoked at line 35 then writes results through it, causing an out-of-bounds stack write (guest-to-host memory corruption or crash).

evidence.reason: args.nargs is guest-controlled data copied by kvm_read_guest at line 16 (entry-point input) whose residual range remains 0..2^32-1: the only guard on the path, `if (rc) goto fail;` (lines 18-19), constrains the read status, not the index, and no other statement (e.g., a `be32_to_cpu(args.nargs) >= ARRAY_SIZE(args.args)` bound check) exists. The object args is a fixed-size automatic struct declared at line 4 with sizeof(args) used at lines 16 and 45, so args.args has a finite element count; a witness nargs = 16 (or any value >= that count) passes line 18 (rc == 0) and line 34 (token match), then line 28 forms a one-past/out-of-bounds pointer stored into args.rets, which is passed at line 35 to the handler that stores result words through it, yielding an out-of-bounds stack write (CWE-787). The absent fix statement, which the vulnerable fragment is missing, is `if (be32_to_cpu(args.nargs) >= ARRAY_SIZE(args.args)) goto fail;` placed before line 28.

assumptions: args is a fixed-size automatic struct (line 4), so the member array args.args has a finite compile-time element count and sizeof(args) is a constant used at lines 16 and 45.
The comment at lines 21-26 establishes the in-fragment contract that args.rets is fixed up to point into the local args copy specifically so handlers can access argument/result slots through it.
limitations: The numeric element count of args.args (ARRAY_SIZE(args.args), 16 in the upstream definition) is not displayed in the fragment; the finding rests on the guaranteed finiteness of the member array versus an unconstrained u32 index rather than on the exact constant.

The actual 4-byte out-of-bounds store happens inside the handler invoked at line 35, whose body is not shown in the fragment; the confirmed in-fragment operation is the unchecked index consumed by the pointer arithmetic at line 28.

No other candidate (status handling, guest-address validation, write-back) was confirmed: kvm_read_guest/kvm_write_guest statuses are checked at lines 18-19 and 46-47, and the write-back at line 45 stays within sizeof(args).

The buffer's only derivable capacity is its original content: 5+len+1 bytes, last valid index len+5 (from lines 17/24/336). For the witness "'<,'>silent", len=6 and indexes 0..11 are valid; STRCPY writes indexes 6..12, so index 12 is one past the buffer: a 1-byte heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). No shown guard bounds len or the destination capacity; the absent fix is a capacity-one-larger allocation/check or a bounded copy before this STRCPY.

assumptions: Ex-mode precondition: exmode_active, an ex-mode getline (getexmodeline/getexline), and cursor line count below buffer line count (lines 42-45) are required to set use_plus_cmd; the comment at line 41 documents this ex-mode path.
The command buffer orig_cmd is sized to its content, i.e. the original "'<,'>"+cmd_start string of 5+len+1 bytes (lines 17/24/336); no slack beyond the input length is visible in the fragment.
limitations: If the caller's command buffer carries unused allocation slack beyond strlen+1, the 1-byte write at index len+6 would land inside the allocation and not corrupt memory; the fragment shows no capacity guarantee in either direction.

verdict.summary: In the FLX_FRAME_TYPE branch, flxfh.size (attacker-controlled, copied at line 98) is only checked against avail (lines 105-106), which admits values smaller than FlxFrameChunkSize. The subtraction flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize at line 112 then underflows to a huge unsigned length passed to gst_adapter_take (line 111), causing an oversized read/allocation from the adapter or a NULL result dereferenced at line 113. The missing protective statement is a lower-bound check (flxfh.size < FlxFrameChunkSize) before the take.

evidence.reason: flxfh.size is entry-point file data (memcpy at line 98 from the adapter map of line 97, endianness-fixed at line 99). The only guard on the path, `if (avail < flxfh.size) goto need_more_data;` (lines 105-106), admits flxfh.size <= avail and does not exclude flxfh.size < FlxFrameChunkSize; the loop guard `avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize` (line 90) likewise does not constrain flxfh.size. Witness: avail = 6, flxfh.size = 1 passes line 90 then line 105 and reaches line 112, where 1 - FlxFrameChunkSize underflows (guint32: 0xFFFFFFFB = 4294967291), and that wrapped value is consumed as the length of gst_adapter_take at line 111. Per the take's standard semantics this is an oversized memory read/allocation (CWE-125 consequence) and, if the take returns NULL, an immediate NULL dereference at line 113. Primary mechanism is unsigned integer underflow (CWE-191) feeding a memory-size consumer. The absent fix is a single lower-bound check, e.g. `if (flxfh.size < FlxFrameChunkSize) goto wrong_length;`, placed after line 105 before the subtraction; no such protective statement is present.

assumptions: FlxFrameChunkSize is the size of the two-field chunk header (id + size) and is referenced consistently as the header-read length at lines 90, 97-98, 109 and as the subtractive constant at line 112; standard FLI/FLX value is 6, and it is at least 1 by construction, so flxfh.size values in [0, FlxFrameChunkSize-1] always underflow.

gst_adapter_take follows its documented semantics: it returns/copies a freshly allocated buffer of the requested nbytes, so a request far larger than the adapter's available data is an oversized memory operation or returns NULL.

Reachability of the PLAYING branch is established in-fragment by the state machine: header parse sets state = GST_FLXDEC_PLAYING at line 84 in an earlier invocation, and the else-if at line 86 enters chunk processing on later invocations.
limitations: The exact downstream failure mode inside gst_adapter_take (out-of-bounds read/huge allocation vs. NULL return followed by the line-113 dereference) is not visible in the fragment; both outcomes are failures of the same confirmed underflowed length.

flxdec->size = width*height (line 78) and flxdec->size * 4 (line 124) could permit huge allocations/aborts depending on the unshown FlxHeader width/height field widths; not counted as a separate finding.

flx_decode_chunks (lines 127-129) is an unshown callee; a chunk whose body is shorter than FlxFrameTypeSize could be over-read there, but this depends on callee internals and is not the confirmed sink.

The default branch (lines 149-155) with a zero-size chunk flushes nothing (line 154), leaving avail unchanged (line 160) and can spin the line-90 loop forever (CWE-835-style DoS); secondary concern, not part of the primary verdict.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the canonical Nettle ecc_256_modp reduction. Every array access — initial reads rp[2*p->size-1] and rp[2*p->size-2] (lines 7-8), in-loop read rp[n-2] (line 39), writes via mpn_submul_1/cnd_sub_n/cnd_add_n at rp+n-4..n-2 (lines 35-36, 44), and final stores rp[2]/rp[3] (lines 47-48) — is bounded by the loop guard 'n >= p->size' (line 11) together with the initialization 'n = 2*p->size; u1 = rp[--n]' (lines 6-7), which admit only n in [p->size, 2*p->size-1] and keep every index inside [0, 2*p->size-1] for the fixed 4-limb P-256 modulus. The arithmetic uses 64-bit-specific idioms (u1 << 32, & 0xffffffff); a 32-bit-limb build is not shown to be selected or guarded, a portability concern outside the shown control flow.

Primary mechanism: stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) / out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

The OOB witness relies on the fully-consumed state p == end; because the fragment shows no producer guaranteeing p < end, the witness is valid, but the degenerate empty-input edge caps confidence at 0.74.

verdict.summary: chacha20_poly1305_ctrl dereferences actx (obtained from aead_data(ctx)) without a NULL check in the EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_IVLEN, SET_IV_FIXED, SET_TAG, GET_TAG and TLS1_AAD cases. The fragment's own EVP_CTRL_INIT branch treats actx == NULL as a real, handled state (line 8), and EVP_CTRL_COPY guards actx on line 26, but every other case dereferences it unconditionally. Invoking those controls on a context whose cipher_data/aead data is unallocated (e.g., aead_data returns NULL) crashes with a NULL-pointer read/write. The absent protection is the single upstream fix: a NULL check on ctx->cipher_data (or actx) at the top of the ctrl handler.

evidence.reason: actx is NULL: line 4 derives actx from aead_data(ctx), whose NULL result is a state the fragment itself handles only in the INIT case (line 8, 'if (actx == NULL)') and in COPY (line 26); no guard on the SET_IVLEN path checks actx or ctx->cipher_data. The guard at lines 38-40 ('if (arg <= 0 || arg > CHACHA_CTR_SIZE) return 0;') admits arg=12 and validates only arg, so the witness (actx==NULL, arg==12) reaches line 41, which writes through a NULL pointer. The absent fix is a NULL check on ctx->cipher_data/actx at the function entry; without it this is a NULL-pointer write (CWE-476), reachable before EVP_CTRL_INIT has allocated cipher_data.

On the EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD path with actx==NULL (same origin as above: line 4 result left unguarded outside INIT/COPY), the guard at lines 70-72 ('if (arg != EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN) return 0;') admits arg==13 and bounds only the source size; it does not constrain actx. The witness (actx==NULL, arg==13) therefore reaches this memcpy whose destination actx->tls_aad is invalid, causing a NULL-pointer write (CWE-476). The absent fix is the single top-of-function NULL check on ctx->cipher_data/actx that the INIT and COPY cases already assume; the denial of service (library crash) follows directly from the shown control flow.

assumptions: aead_data(ctx) returns NULL when the AEAD context data (ctx->cipher_data) is not yet allocated; this is the premise that the fragment's own line 8 'if (actx == NULL)' branch treats as a legitimate state, and it is not contradicted anywhere in the shown code.

A caller can invoke this ctrl handler with type values such as EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_IVLEN (or EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD) before EVP_CTRL_INIT has run, so that actx is still NULL; the fragment itself contains no ordering requirement that establishes the opposite.
limitations: The body of aead_data() is not shown, so the exact condition under which it returns NULL is inferred from the fragment's own NULL handling in the INIT case rather than quoted from the fragment.

The SET_TAG, GET_TAG and SET_IV_FIXED branches share the same NULL-actx dereference but were not given separate evidence items; they are covered by the same root cause and the same absent fix statement.

All size/argument-bounded operations (tag/AAD copies capped by arg, the 12-byte fixed-IV reads, and the guarded len -= POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE discount) were audited and are protected by shown guards; no OOB CWE-125/787/190 and no injection issues are confirmed.

The exact overflow mechanics of the vulnerable counterpart (CVE-2022-2061, absent this guard) are not reconstructed here; no positive verdict is made.

verdict.summary: fix_dl_name reads out of bounds when dl->length is smaller than the shared-object extension length: dl->length - so_ext_len at line 4 wraps under size_t arithmetic, and my_strcasecmp dereferences dl->str plus the wrapped offset with no lower-bound guard on dl->length.

The only conditional in the function is this sink's own condition, so no guard precedes the read on any path; the absent one-line fix is a lower-bound check such as 'dl->length >= so_ext_len &&' before the subtraction, or an early return for dl->length < so_ext_len.

assumptions: dl->length is an unsigned size-compatible field (it participates in size_t arithmetic at lines 4, 7, 11) with full declared domain [0, SIZE_MAX]; the fragment imposes no constraint on it.
dl->str is a buffer holding at least dl->length readable bytes, evidenced by the in-fragment memcpy(s, dl->str, dl->length) at line 8.
SO_EXT is the standard nonempty shared-object extension suffix, so so_ext_len = sizeof(SO_EXT) - 1 >= 1 (typically 3 for ".so").
limitations: SO_EXT's literal value is not shown in the fragment; the verdict requires only so_ext_len >= 1, not its exact value.

No call site for fix_dl_name is shown, so the concrete in-program trigger (a caller passing a name shorter than the extension) is not demonstrated; reachability rests on the parameter's unconstrained declared domain.
Unchecked alloc_root result (potential NULL dereference at lines 8-9) is demoted: NULL-return/OOM semantics of alloc_root are not visible in the fragment.
Allocation-size wraparound at line 7 (dl->length + so_ext_len + 1) with the consequent memcpy at line 8 would require dl->length near SIZE_MAX, a magnitude no shown statement produces.

verdict.summary: Heap-stack out-of-bounds write in compileRule's macro-expansion substitution copy: tmpFile.line accumulates definition literal characters up to the MAXSTRING limit admitted by the guard at line 157, and the argument copy at line 170 then writes arg.length characters with no bound check, storing past the end of tmpFile.line (capacity MAXSTRING) when linelen + arg.length exceeds MAXSTRING.

evidence.reason: The store at line 170 writes to tmpFile.line with index tmpFile.linelen, where linelen was 0-initialized at line 125, incremented at line 164, and is NOT re-bounded on this path. The only bound check in the expansion loop, line 157 (tmpFile.linelen >= MAXSTRING -> error), is inside the definition-character branch of while (i < next) at lines 144-164 and therefore admits linelen values up to MAXSTRING-1 (and linelen == MAXSTRING after the admitted write at index MAXSTRING-1). On the substitution branch (lines 166-174), the copy bound is only j < arg.length (line 169), and arg.length is attacker-controlled table-file token data read at lines 130-131 without any shown cap. Witness: definition literal run of MAXSTRING-1 characters followed by a substitution of an argument of length 2 yields writes at indices MAXSTRING-1 (admitted) and MAXSTRING (one past the capacity MAXSTRING established by line 157), i.e. an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) into the stack-local FileInfo tmpFile declared at line 117. The absent fix is the missing check `if (tmpFile.linelen + arg.length > MAXSTRING) { compileError(file, "Line exceeds %d characters (post macro expansion)", MAXSTRING); return 0; }` before the copy loop at lines 169-170.

assumptions: MAXSTRING is the capacity of tmpFile.line, established by the fragment's own guard at line 157 which uses MAXSTRING as the exclusive index limit for writes at line 164.
Table-file contents are attacker-controlled entry-point input consumed by getToken (lines 15, 49, 130), getOpcode (line 28), and compileMacro (line 37).
The macro-expansion path is compiled and active (ENABLE_MACROS), matching the shown macro-invocation consumption code at lines 107-191.
limitations: malloc(m->argument_count * sizeof(CharsString)) at line 128 is not null-checked before the store at line 131; a NULL deref requires allocation failure (environmental) and is not the primary finding.

The CTO_Replace memmove (&ruleDots.chars[1], ruleDots.length-- * CHARSIZE) performs a one-element read past the logical token end and reaches a physical OOB index only when the token length equals the array capacity, which is not declared in the fragment; demoted.
putChar/getChar return values in CTO_Attribute/CTO_Base are dereferenced without null checks; the callee NULL contract is not shown in the fragment.

Length accumulations in CTO_SeqAfterExpression, CTO_MultInd (ruleChars.chars[ruleChars.length++]) and CTO_RepEndWord have no visible capacity declaration for the target arrays; missing-bound claims without a shown capacity were not confirmed.
Integrity of m->substitutions argument numbers (indexing arguments[] at line 168) is assumed to be enforced by the unshown compileMacro producer.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability: every sink whose failure is demonstrable from the shown statements is protected by a visible guard (line 78 NULL check, line 132 MAXWLEN cap/NUL termination, line 133 length-sign guard, line 189 selection bounds, line 215 alloc NULL check, and IOSIZE-bounded vim_snprintf calls); the remaining OOB concerns on the wcopy offset and the replacement geometry depend on magnitudes produced by the unshown spell_find_suggest and are recorded as limitations.

vim_strncpy(to, from, len) copies at most len bytes and writes the terminating NUL at to[len] (standard Vim semantics), so line 132 always terminates wcopy within its capacity.
vim_snprintf(IObuff, IOSIZE, ...) bounds both output and, via precision '%.*s'/'%s', the source reads used here.
alloc() returns NULL on failure and that NULL is checked at line 215; vim_strsave() NULL is checked at line 78.
SUG(sug.su_ga, i) indexes the ga_data array of suggest_T with i; the loop (line 126) admits i in [0, ga_len-1].
STRLEN(line) returns size_t, so line 214 arithmetic is unsigned and an oversized st_orglen would only enlarge the request (alloc fails, guarded at line 215).
limitations: Sink at lines 134-136: an out-of-bounds write into wcopy cannot be confirmed because stp->st_wordlen, sug.su_badlen and stp->st_orglen are produced by the unshown spell_find_suggest (called at lines 87-88); no shown statement derives a value with st_wordlen + (su_badlen - st_orglen) > MAXWLEN + 1, so this rests on an assumed magnitude (OOB class rule (b) unsatisfied).

The '%.*s' precision reads at lines 150-151 and 201-203 and the STRCAT/AppendToRedobuffLit geometry (lines 220, 226) could over-read or over-write only if st_orglen exceeded the remaining line length (su_badptr + st_orglen past the line NUL), which depends on unshown spell_find_suggest invariants.

The negative-length (int-to-size_t) failure of the line 134 strncpy is excluded by the guard at line 133 (admitted su_badlen - st_orglen >= 1; excluded <= 0); if that guard were absent the fragment would be vulnerable (CWE-195/787), but it is present.
p_verbose/sps_flags paths and prompt_for_number's mouse_used output are not shown to have security impact in-fragment; they only influence message text and the guarded selected value.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The output_port index cannot be demonstrated out of bounds because no output-array capacity or in-fragment derivation of an out-of-range port is visible.

qh_find_handler returns NULL on no-match, and line 23 (if (qh == NULL)) is evaluated before the qh->handler dereference at line 27.

The handler registered under the name "help" is qh_help itself (the contract evidenced by the literal argument "help", 4 at line 27); this is the registration fact that makes the historical recursion bug real, and it matches upstream fix commit 239d82a.
The format strings passed to nsock_printf/nsock_printf_nul are all literals; buf/name/description are value arguments only.
limitations: NULL buf would crash at line 5 (!*buf), strcmp calls and %s reads, but no statement in the fragment can produce NULL buf; a NULL value could only come from an unshown caller, so it is not confirmable as a finding.
An unterminated buf would cause unbounded reads at lines 5/12/22/25/29; no producer of an unterminated buffer is shown and len is never used, so no out-of-bounds read can be demonstrated in-fragment.

The comparison > 200 at line 27 is odd (it only controls which help message is printed) but its semantics are not shown and no security-relevant consumer is affected; it is at most a robustness/logic concern.

The recursion vulnerability is excluded by line 5; the reasoning that qh_help is registered as "help" relies on the handler table outside the fragment (verified against the real upstream fix) and therefore caps confidence below the top safe band.

verdict.summary: In release builds the debug-only DCHECK at line 41 is compiled out, so the attacker-controlled index ix (edge->src_output() stored at line 17, read at line 40) is passed unvalidated to node_t.args(ix) at line 45, causing a heap out-of-bounds read whenever ix >= node_t.args_size().

evidence.reason: ix is attacker-controlled: edge->src_output() (entry-point graph data) is stored into input_idx.at(i) at line 17 and read as `int ix = input_idx[i]` at line 40, with no always-on constraint on its residual int range. The only guard before the sink is `DCHECK(ix < node_t.args_size())` at line 41, which is compiled out under NDEBUG, so in release the admitted set is the full int domain including ix == args_size() (capacity computed at line 41/43). Witness: a non-control edge with dst_input()==0 and src_output()==args_size() passes lines 11, 14, 24-30, 35, 37, 39, 41 and reaches `node_t.args(ix)` on line 45, reading one or more FullTypeDef elements past the args array (heap OOB read, CWE-125). The absent fix is an always-on bounds check (e.g., `if (ix < 0 || ix >= node_t.args_size()) { ClearTypeInfo(); return; }`) inserted before line 45; the debug-only DCHECK does not cover the release-build failure set.

assumptions: DCHECK compiles to no-op under NDEBUG (standard TensorFlow/C++ assertion semantics), making line 41 non-protective in release builds.
node_t.args(ix) indexes the repeated args field whose capacity is node_t.args_size() (computed at line 41), and the accessor performs no always-on bounds check.
props_->input_types.size() >= 1 so that loop C (line 35) executes and the sink is reachable.
limitations: The exception generated by input_nodes.at(i)/input_idx.at(i) for out-of-range dst_input() (lines 16-17) is a robustness concern (uncaught exception aborts the process) but not a memory-safety flaw.
