Under strict signedness, a ue value >= 2^31 would truncate to a negative s32 pps_id and bypass the `> 255` check at line 11; this depends entirely on unshown gf_bs_read_ue_log internals (no shown producer of such a magnitude), so it is unconfirmable, not a finding.

Line 17 (si->sps = &avc->sps[si->pps->sps_id + GF_SVC_SSPS_ID_SHIFT]) has no in-fragment upper-bound check on sps_id, and line 18 is only a post-deref validity check, not a bounds check; however sps_id's producer (the PPS parser) and the sps array size are unshown, so no in-fragment witness of an out-of-range index exists.
The discarded return of the first gf_bs_read_ue_log (line 6) has no security consequence in the shown code because no resource or decision depends on it.

verdict.summary: No security-relevant failure is demonstrable from the shown statements alone. `rank` (L2) is an unvalidated dimension of input 0 and flows into `Matrix`/`Vector` (L4, L6), but the fragment declares no capacity or proportional allocation and shows no downstream consumer, and `Dim`'s out-of-range behavior is not visible; the missing rank/input validation is a robustness limitation, not a confirmed finding.

`c->input(0)` is a valid handle for op input 0; the fragment itself shows no constraint on its shape.

`return Status::OK()` (L7) is returned without validating the rank/input shape, but no security-relevant consumer of the malformed shape state is visible in the fragment, so this is a robustness/fail-open concern only.
A NULL dereference of `rank` inside `Matrix`/`Vector` is not confirmable: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.

The fragment contains no protective statement and no demonstrated failure, so it cannot be positively classified as either the patched counterpart (no fix visible) or the vulnerable counterpart (no reversible failure); verdict rests on absence of a demonstrable danger.

verdict.summary: In the session-refresh branch of callback_glewlwyd_user_auth, session_uid from get_session_id(config, request) is passed unguarded to get_users_for_session at line 50. get_session_id is shown (lines 20-22, 81-83, 114-116) to return NULL when no session cookie is present, and no guard on the path (lines 14, 15, 16, 17, 46) constrains it, so a cookie-less request with a username but no password reaches get_users_for_session with a NULL session id, yielding a NULL-pointer dereference inside the session lookup.

evidence.reason: session_uid is assigned at line 49 from get_session_id(config, request), whose NULL outcome is proven in-fragment by the identical NULL-handling guards at lines 20-22, 81-83 and 114-116 (get_session_id(...) == NULL -> generate_session_id()) and by the '!= NULL &&' gate at line 37. Guards on the path - j_param != NULL (line 14), non-empty username string (line 15), absent scheme_type/password (lines 16, 17, 46) - all admit a request with no session cookie, and none checks session_uid. Witness: POST {"username":"victim"} with no password field and no session cookie passes lines 14, 15, 16, 17, 46 in order, then line 49 yields NULL, reaching this sink unguarded; get_users_for_session consumes the session id as a required string key (name-implied dereference). The absent fix is a NULL/status check before line 50 mirroring lines 20-22/37/114-116 (e.g. if (session_uid == NULL) { response->status = 401; } else { ... }). Primary mechanism: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476), remotely triggerable denial of service.

assumptions: get_session_id returns NULL when no session cookie is present; this is derived from the fragment's own NULL-handling guards at lines 20-22, 81-83, 114-116 and the '!= NULL &&' gate at line 37.
get_users_for_session treats its session-id argument as a required non-NULL string key (name-implied semantics); its internal NULL handling is not shown.
Jansson json_object_get/json_string_value/json_string_length/json_decref are NULL/non-string safe as standard library semantics.
o_free is NULL-safe (orcania helper semantics), so o_free(session_uid) with NULL is not a fault.
expires[129] (line 6) with strftime size 128 (line 13) caps output below capacity.
limitations: Unvalidated j_result["username"] at lines 117/122: whether auth_check_identify_scheme can return G_OK with a missing or non-string username is not derivable from the fragment.
u_map_get(request->map_cookie, config->session_key) at line 53 may return NULL; its consumption by user_session_update is inside an unshown callee.
Line 16 passes json_string_value(scheme_type) which is NULL for a non-string scheme_type into o_strcmp; o_strcmp's NULL-safety is not shown in the fragment.

Log sinks at lines 28/35/74/89 receive unescaped attacker-controlled username (log injection shape), demoted because the primary confirmed mechanism is the NULL session-id dereference and the log backend's interpretation is unshown.
gmtime_r failure (line 12) could leave ts uninitialized for strftime (line 13); the time source is not attacker-controllable.
Line 57 would only set a NULL cookie if get_users_for_session returned G_OK for a NULL session id; that degenerate combination is not derivable and was rejected.

verdict.summary: main() dereferences the OS-provided envp (and argv) at lines 48 (and 47) without any NULL or emptiness check. As entry-point input, envp's residual range is unconstrained by the fragment and includes NULL; under an environment/launcher that passes NULL envp, `*envp` is a NULL pointer dereference causing an immediate crash (CWE-476). The neutralizing fix (an added `envp`/`*envp` guard) is absent from the fragment.

evidence.reason: envp is entry-point input (argv/environment per Phase 1(a)) with no shown constraint, so its residual range includes NULL. No guard on any path excludes envp==NULL before the dereference at line 48; the guards at lines 44-45, 54-56, and 60-62 test unrelated values. Fix-Scan: the neutralizing statement (a NULL/emptiness check, e.g. `if (envp && *envp) cmdline_end = *envp;`) is absent, so line 48 is the unguarded sink of the NULL dereference, CWE-476 (process crash/DoS). Confidence is capped because the NULL-envp premise is host-dependent and not produced by any shown statement.

argv is unconstrained entry-point input with NULL in its residual range, and line 47 dereferences argv[0] with no preceding guard (Fix-Scan: no `argc > 0` / `argv != NULL` check exists in the fragment). Under an argc==0/NULL-argv launch, `*argv` is a NULL pointer dereference, CWE-476. Same class and absent-fix form as line 48; reachability rests on the same fragile host/launcher premise.

assumptions: envp and argv are OS/runtime-provided entry-point inputs; the fragment imposes no constraint on them, leaving NULL inside their residual ranges (Phase 1(a)).
The getopt loop, the `if (!tmate_settings->tmate_host)` branch, and the mkdir/chmod status guards at lines 44-45, 54-56, 60-62 do not touch envp or argv and therefore do not constrain the witness.
limitations: NULL envp/argv is not produced by any shown statement; on Linux, `execve` with NULL envp fails with EFAULT, so on common hosts the deref may be unreachable — impact is confirmed only under the NULL-envp/argv premise (fragile boundary, confidence capped at 0.67).

The standard-conforming empty-environment case (envp[0]==NULL) only assigns NULL to cmdline_end at line 48 with no in-fragment dereference; any downstream crash/over-read would occur in unshown callees and is not confirmable.

atoi-based ports (lines 17, 20, 26) accept negative/zero values without validation; the only in-fragment consequence is fail-closed (bind failure) with no confirmed security consumer, so this is robustness only.
mkdir/chmod use the fixed macro TMATE_WORKDIR whose value is unshown; potential symlink/TOCTOU issues on the workdir cannot be confirmed from the fragment.
get_full_hostname() (line 45) is unchecked; a NULL return would only matter in unshown consumers.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment is covered by a protective statement present in the shown code: the N_big bound (line 22) makes the cast at line 27 lossless, the params.shape[0] bound (line 29) keeps the row count in Index range, the N > 0 guard (line 41) prevents the division by N at line 63, the StartsWith prefix check (line 58) makes num_updates an exact multiple of N so the shaped view fits the buffer, and the bad_i < 0 checks (lines 50, 68) reject any out-of-range index before the scatter functors write. No failing value was demonstrated to reach any sink.

assumptions: Index is instantiated as a signed integer type (int32 or int64) by kernel registration, so std::numeric_limits<Index>::max() at lines 22 and 29 bounds the cast at line 27 and the params row count.

The scatter functors (lines 48-49, 66-67) follow their name-implied bounds-check contract: they scan every index position, return the first position whose value is outside [0, params_flat.dimension(0)), and perform no writes before such a position is reported, which the kernel rejects at lines 50/68.
TensorShapeUtils::StartsWith at line 58 requires the leading dimensions of updates.shape() to equal indices.shape(), which makes num_updates an exact multiple of N in the else branch.
indices and updates tensors are dtype/rank-validated by kernel registration outside this fragment.
limitations: Updates' trailing dimensions are not compared to params.shape[1:]; an inner-dimension mismatch (e.g., updates {2,5} vs params {3,4}) is unvalidated, but any resulting misbehavior would occur inside the unshown functor and cannot be confirmed from the shown statements.
The DIV zero-validation at lines 36-39 is skipped on GPU devices; division-by-zero there is a robustness/NaN concern with no shown memory-unsafe sink.
If Index is int32 and inner-dimension element counts exceed 2^31-1, any overflow would occur in the unshown functor's arithmetic, not in a derivation visible in this fragment.
The exact internal write loop lengths of ScatterScalarFunctor/ScatterFunctor are not shown; their safety is taken from their name-implied bounds-check semantics.

assumptions: gf_list_count (line 11) returns the element count of movie->moov->trackList, and gf_isom_get_track (line 13) follows its name-implied standard semantics: 1-based track number returning NULL only for trackNum 0 or trackNum > gf_list_count(trackList).

limitations: If an untrusted MP4 could yield NULL for trak->Media, information, sampleTable, SampleSize, TimeToSample, or ChunkOffset, the dereferences at lines 19-20, 31-34, 42, 49, 52, and 57 would be NULL derefs; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so this is not confirmable.

Lines 41 and 47 return GF_OUT_OF_MEM directly, bypassing the CleanWriters(writers) cleanup performed at label exit (lines 70-72), leaking already-added writers on allocation failure; this is OOM-only with no shown attacker control or downstream consumer, so it is a robustness concern rather than a confirmed finding.

The constant_size/constant_dur computation (lines 31-38) keeps values only when sampleSize is in [1,9] and there is exactly one time-to-sample entry with delta 1; any downstream misuse of these values occurs outside the fragment and cannot be demonstrated here.

No format-string, path, allocation-size, or arithmetic sink exists in the fragment; the attacker-controlled `name` is consumed only as a container key whose failure is status-handled.

verdict.summary: No in-fragment vulnerability: every tagstack index is bounded (full-stack shift with --tagstackidx at 141/147; `>=` guards at 196 and 261; clamps at 268 and 297-298; empty-stack check at 171), and every matches[] access is bounded by the num_matches clamp at 536/550 plus the selection check at 519. verdict.summary: No demonstrated vulnerability. The fragment is the fail-closed/fixed form: the retry loop at L6-L9 (while (rInv.IsZero())) excludes every non-invertible blinding factor, all intermediate arithmetic operates on reduced arbitrary-precision Integer residues with no fixed buffers or indexing, and the final check at L32-L33 (if (ApplyFunction(y) != x) throw) excludes every incorrect internal computation and every out-of-range x before any value is returned. No memory, injection, file, or authz sink exists in the shown code.

assumptions: Integer is Crypto++'s arbitrary-precision type, so no fixed-width overflow occurs in the shown arithmetic.
m_n = m_p * m_q with odd primes, validated by the unshown DoQuickSanityCheck() call at L3; only needed for residue bounds [0, p-1], [0, q-1], [0, n-1].
MultiplicativeInverse returns 0 exactly when no inverse exists (the fragment's own L9 check relies on this standard semantics).
ModularSquareRoot and CRT return reduced representatives mod p/q/n per their standard semantics.
limitations: ApplyFunction's body is not shown; the protective claim at L32-L33 assumes standard semantics (y^2 mod n or the RW forward function consistent with the twist), making the equality check an exact verification.

ModularSquareRoot's exact behavior on a non-residue argument is not shown; its output stays within a reduced residue class and any error is contained by L32-L33, but the precise failure range cannot be computed in-fragment.

x = 0 returns y = 0 without throwing (a fixed point of the squaring map); this is inherent to the scheme, provides no key-dependent forgery advantage per the shown code, and is recorded as a robustness note, not a finding.
The retry loop L6-L9 terminates probabilistically and assumes the RNG produces coprime values; a hostile/degenerate RNG could stall signing, but no in-fragment control over rng is shown.

The loop at line 16 would fail to terminate only if m_ucCount could exceed the UBYTE counter range; no shown type declaration or producer derives such a value.

DownsamplerBase::CreateDownsampler (line 22) receives sx/sy/width/height without shown validation of degenerate values (e.g., sx=0), and its internal behavior is not shown; no failing argument is derivable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: dequeue_node is declared without initialization at line 79; when train_nodes contains no dequeue op, the loop at lines 80-85 never assigns it, and the indeterminate pointer is read at line 88 and dereferenced at lines 89-90, causing undefined behavior, a crash, or an arbitrary-memory read.

evidence.reason: dequeue_node (declared at line 79 without an initializer) is only assigned inside the loop at lines 81-82 when IsDequeueOp(*train_node) holds. Nothing in the fragment guarantees a dequeue op exists in train_nodes (built at line 76 from item.fetch/graph_), so on the admitted path where the loop completes without a break, line 88 reads an indeterminate pointer value. The guard cannot protect anything because it tests the indeterminate value itself; the absent fix is an initialization (`const NodeDef* dequeue_node = nullptr;`) or an explicit null check after the loop. Confirmed CWE-457 uninitialized-variable use.

Reachable only when the indeterminate dequeue_node from line 79 reads non-NULL at line 88; dereferencing the uninitialized pointer here (and again in ComputeTransitiveFanin at line 90) yields undefined behavior, a likely crash, or reading from an arbitrary address. No protective NULL/initialization statement exists between line 79 and this sink, so the vulnerable counterpart is missing the one-statement fix (initialization of dequeue_node to nullptr). Primary CWE-457; the dereference is the impact of the uninitialized read.

assumptions: train_nodes may contain no dequeue op: no shown statement forces any node to satisfy IsDequeueOp at line 81, and graph contents are unconstrained beyond the non-empty fetch/variable checks at lines 7 and 11.
NodeDef::input(i) / mutable_input(i) are the standard protobuf repeated-field accessors whose valid index domain is [0, input_size()).
Return values of AddNodeDivConst() and AddNodeDiv() are treated as non-NULL; no NULL producer is shown.

gradient_pos[apply_gradients_op] at line 67 cannot insert a default key because apply_gradients_nodes_ is populated only for ops listed in apply_gradients_ops (lines 27-37, 41-43), all of which are keys of gradient_pos (lines 50-60).
The magnitude/exploitability of the arbitrary-memory read at line 89 depends on the indeterminate pointer value landing in mapped memory; the core confirmed flaw is the uninitialized read itself.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only arithmetic candidates (u64 wrap in num_devices - 1 at lines 14 and 111) require the device counters to be 0, which the shown fragment never derives from btrfs_num_devices()/btrfs_super_num_devices(), and even then the line 15-16 fail-open decision has no consuming effect because the line 18 device lookup cannot succeed when no devices exist. The device->name dereference at lines 121-122 (and 32) has no in-fragment NULL producer, and the WRITEABLE guard at line 120 excludes the bdev-less/missing-device paths. All other candidates (rw_devices counter guards on different devices objects, unbalanced reada undo, seed-path counter mismatch) depend on state produced outside the fragment.

assumptions: Line 20's IS_ERR(device) guard is taken to establish device is valid-or-ERR_PTR; no NULL-producing call is visible in-fragment.

Line 120's test_bit(BTRFS_DEV_STATE_WRITEABLE, &device->dev_state) guard is the only gate before btrfs_scratch_superblocks at lines 121-122; a missing/bdev-less device is excluded from reaching the device->name->str dereference.
Lines 42-43 guard (fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices == 1) protects the line 51 decrement only when device->fs_devices == fs_info->fs_devices, matching the non-seed path described at lines 85-89.
num_devices at lines 12 and 111 is internal fs-derived state with no shown minimum; each sink analysis treats the full u64 domain but rejects the 0 witness as underived (degenerate-input discipline).
limitations: u64 wrap of num_devices - 1 at line 14 into btrfs_check_raid_min_devices requires num_devices == 0; no shown statement derives 0, and the fail-open check result has no demonstrated downstream effect since the line 18 lookup cannot return a device with zero devices in the list (CWE-190/191 demoted as undemonstrated).
u64 wrap of btrfs_super_num_devices(fs_info->super_copy) - 1 at lines 111-112 requires super_copy->num_devices == 0, also not derived by any shown statement; demoted.

NULL dereference of device->name at lines 121-122 (and line 32 via rcu_str_deref) requires a NULL name producer; none is shown, and the WRITEABLE guard at line 120 excludes missing/bdev-less devices; reaching the sink requires a writable opened device, whose name state is unshown (CWE-476 demoted as unconfirmed).

The only-writable check at lines 42-43 reads fs_info->fs_devices->rw_devices while the decrement at line 51 uses device->fs_devices->rw_devices; for seed devices these differ, but the consequence (counter underflow or policy bypass) depends on seed fs state not visible in the fragment.

On a failed btrfs_shrink_device (line 60), error_undo at line 139 runs btrfs_reada_undo_remove_dev although line 58's btrfs_reada_remove_dev was skipped; balance impact is inside an unshown callee with no shown memory-safety effect (CWE-754 robustness concern only).

A hypothetical NULL return from btrfs_find_device_by_devspec would escape the IS_ERR-only check at line 20 and be dereferenced at line 29, but no shown statement produces NULL from that helper; classified as caller/callee-dependent limitation, not a finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of PQconnectPoll: every dangerous length/path operation is covered by a visible protective statement. Overlong Unix-domain socket paths are rejected by `if (strlen(portstr) >= UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN)` (lines 174-181) before `portstr` reaches `pg_getaddrinfo_all` (line 187), admitting only NUL-terminated paths with `strlen(portstr) <= UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN - 1`. All other sinks (snprintf of the bounded port, peer-credential auth decision, startup-packet NULL check) are likewise guarded. No witness admitted by every guard reaches a security-relevant failure.

assumptions: `char portstr[MAXPGPATH]` (line 84) is the shown buffer written by `UNIXSOCK_PATH` (line 173) and re-read at line 187; the guard at line 174 keys on the same `UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN` bound referenced by the macro name.

`msgLength` is a signed 4-byte big-endian network value; guard lines 1055/1063 make negative and oversized values unreachable at lines 1092/1101/1205.

`memcpy(&conn->raddr.addr, addr_cur->ai_addr, addr_cur->ai_addrlen)` (lines 278-279): `conn->raddr.addr` capacity is not declared in the fragment, and `ai_addrlen` is OS-provided; no shown-capacity OOB is derivable, so no finding.

The internal processing of `pg_fe_sendauth(areq, msgLength, conn)` (line 1205) is unshown; the degenerate `msgLength == 0` after line 1196 is admitted by the guards, but no failure can be demonstrated from the shown code.
`strdup` failure at line 293 is deliberately ignored per the comment; the result is never dereferenced in the fragment, so no NULL-deref candidate is confirmable.

verdict.summary: gopherToHTML terminates each parsed line with line[llen + 1] = '\0'; when the combined line length (gopherState->len + llen) reaches TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1, llen + 1 equals TEMP_BUF_SIZE and the write lands one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-element local array `line`, an out-of-bounds stack write driven by attacker-controlled Gopher response data.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled inbuf/len (entry-point Gopher payload) positions a '\n' so that llen = lpos - pos (line 71) is TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1. Guard 75 admits combined lengths up to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 because it fires only at '>= TEMP_BUF_SIZE' (75-77); with gopherState->len == 0 and a TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 byte line, execution takes the else copy at 95 and reaches 97 with llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1, so line[llen + 1] indexes TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one past the array declared at line 6 (LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE), valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1). The guard also fails when it fires: line 77 sets llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1, which after line 92 is again TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 -> line[TEMP_BUF_SIZE]. No shown statement caps the combined llen at TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 2; the absent protective fix is replacing line 97 with `line[llen] = '\0';`. One-byte out-of-bounds stack write, CWE-787.

assumptions: TEMP_BUF_SIZE is the element count of `line` at line 6 (LOCAL_ARRAY), so valid indices are 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1.
gopherState->len is 0 on a first call and is capped at TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 on in-fragment leftover paths (lines 77, 85).
inbuf/len are entry-point Gopher response data: arbitrary byte content and selectable length.
limitations: gopherState->len's initial value originates from unshown caller state; the witness is k-parametric (satisfiable for every k in 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1), so this affects only the first-call illustration, not the finding.

The GOPHER_WWW branch (lines 240-241) passes three arguments for five format conversions in outbuf.appendf (undefined vararg reads); demoted as a separate UB concern, not the one-statement-fix target.
Capacity of gopherState->buf is not declared in the fragment, so the memcpy at line 84 cannot be confirmed as an OOB; its size is only bounded by TEMP_BUF_SIZE arithmetic.
strtok/atoi edge cases (s_code/s_recno NULL) coincide with result == NULL checked at lines 271/296, so no NULL-atoi path is confirmed.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of BinaryBroadcastFiveFold. verdict.summary: In ReadOneMNGImage, the CLIP chunk handler iterates attacker-controlled object IDs (first_object/last_object, 0..65535) over mng_info->exists/frozen/object_clip with no bound relative to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS, while the sibling MOVE handler contains exactly that check (line 891). A crafted MNG CLIP chunk (e.g., first=0, last=65535) drives i to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS and beyond, producing a heap out-of-bounds read (line 812) and, when length >= 22 and the OOB-read byte is nonzero, an out-of-bounds write of object_clip[i] (lines 819-820). The DEFI chunk handler additionally admits object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS (line 384 uses '>' not '>=' and clamps to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS at 392), indexing the same tables one past their shown domain.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read of mng_info->exists[i] at i admitted by loop line 810 ('for (i=(int) first_object; i <= (int) last_object; i++)') with last_object decoded from file bytes at line 807 ((p[2] << 8) | p[3]) giving residual range [0,65535]; guards 168, 174, 182, 188, 232, 804 all admit a CLIP chunk of length 4 carrying 00 00 FF FF, and no guard on this path bounds i against MNG_MAX_OBJECTS. The valid index domain is shown by the fragment's own init loops lines 114-118 and 326-327 ('for (i=0; i < MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; i++) mng_info->object_clip[i]=...'), i.e., [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS); i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS (e.g., 256..65535) dereferences outside the array. The protective statement that would neutralize this (if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;) exists only in the MOVE loop at line 891 and is absent on this CLIP path — the missing one-line fix. Primary CWE-125 (heap OOB read).

Out-of-bounds write to mng_info->object_clip[i] with the same uncontrolled i from the CLIP loop (lines 806-810, residual [0,65535]); the guard at line 818 ('(p-chunk) < (ssize_t) (length-17)', with p-chunk fixed at 4 since p advances once at 808 and never inside the loop) admits the write for any length >= 22; the value branch at 812 then depends on the already out-of-bounds read of exists[i]/frozen[i]. For i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS (outside the domain shown at lines 114-118/326-327) this writes heap memory past the object_clip table. The absent fix is the same index bound as line 891 applied in this loop. Secondary CWE-787 (heap OOB write).

Out-of-bounds write of mng_info->exists[object_id] when object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS: object_id is decoded at line 377 ((p[0] << 8) | p[1], residual [0,65535]); the guard at line 384 ('if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)') excludes only values strictly greater than MNG_MAX_OBJECTS, so the boundary value passes unchecked, and values greater than the limit are clamped at line 392 to object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS — the exclusive bound of the tables per init loops 114-118/326-327. The read at line 395 (if (mng_info->exists[object_id])) is already out of bounds for this index; when it reads zero, the write at 406 executes one past the array. Absent fix: change the operator and clamp ('if (object_id >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS) object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1;'). CWE-787 (heap OOB write).

assumptions: The MngInfo object tables (exists, frozen, viewable, invisible, x_off, y_off, object_clip) each have MNG_MAX_OBJECTS elements, with valid indices [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS), as inferred from the fragment's own initialization loops bounded at line 114-118 and 326-327.

MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is smaller than the 16-bit object-ID space (<= 65535), as evidenced inside the fragment by the MOVE bound check at line 891 and the DEFI 'object id too large' clamp at 384-393; with the historical limit 256, the CLIP out-of-bounds range starts at index 256.

AcquireQuantumMemory at lines 185-186 returns an allocation of length+MagickPathExtent bytes and a non-NULL pointer on the admitted path (NULL checked at 188); ReadBlob fills up to length bytes unless EOF.
limitations: The exact numeric value of MNG_MAX_OBJECTS and the MngInfo struct declaration are not shown in the fragment; if the constant were >= 65536, the CLIP/DEFI indices would remain in-bounds. The fragment's own guard/clamp machinery (lines 384-393, 891) contradicts such a reading, but the magnitude itself is an assumption.

The out-of-bounds WRITES (evidence items 2 and 3) additionally require the out-of-bounds byte read of exists[i]/exists[object_id] to take the corresponding branch (nonzero for the CLIP write, zero for the DEFI write), so they are conditional on heap contents; the out-of-bounds READ at line 812 (and 395) is unconditional on the admitted path.
DISC/SEEK pass raw 16-bit object IDs to MngInfoDiscardObject(mng_info,i) at lines 862-865; the callee body is not shown, so an internal bound cannot be confirmed or excluded.

LOOP/ENDL index loop_active/loop_jump/loop_count/loop_iteration with loop_level = chunk[0] in [0,255] (lines 921-922, 937-938, 941, 951, 961, 967-970, 1003-1005); array capacities are not shown in the fragment.

Chunk-padding reads (TERM at 343-344, FRAM name scan at 651-654 and 663-724) can read uninitialized bytes but stay inside the length+MagickPathExtent allocation (185-186); they are not out-of-bounds of the allocation and are not confirmed as security-relevant.

verdict.summary: The loop at line 42 iterates i over [0, depth-1] with depth = input_max.NumElements() (line 6), while transposed_input's dimension-0 extent is only the product of input's non-leading dims (lines 21/29). No shown statement constrains depth against input's shape, so an attacker can supply input_max with more elements than that extent; the guards at lines 8/12 only bound input_min/input_max sizes and are satisfied, letting i reach chip<0>(i) beyond the extent and cause a heap out-of-bounds read at lines 44/46.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125): index i retains residual range [0, depth-1] from the line 42 loop bound with depth = input_max.NumElements() (line 6), unconstrained by guards at line 8 (input_min.dim_size(0) == depth) and line 12 (input_max.dim_size(0) == depth); both admit the witness input_min=[100,1], input_max=[100,1] (depth=100), while transposed_input's dim-0 extent is 2 for the witness input=[1,1,1,2] (dim-0 extent derived from flat_inner_dims at line 21 and shuffle at line 29). i=2..99 passes every guard in order (8, 12, 42) and reaches chip<0>(i), reading beyond the stated capacity; the absent fix is an added input-validation statement tying depth to input's channel extent (e.g., an OP_REQUIRES that depth equals input.dim_size(input.dims()-1)).

Same heap OOB read (CWE-125) as line 44 for the same loop index i in [0, depth-1] (line 42, depth from line 6): the witness input=[1,1,1,2], input_min=[100,1], input_max=[100,1] satisfies guards at lines 8 and 12, so i=2..99 reaches chip<0>(i) against a dim-0 extent of 2 (lines 21/29), and no protective statement relating depth to input's shape exists on the path; the absent fix is the same added depth-vs-input extent validation.

assumptions: input.flat_inner_dims<qint32>() (line 21) yields [input.dim_size(0), product(remaining dims)], and shuffle({1,0}) (line 29) makes transposed_input's dimension 0 have extent equal to the product of input's dims 1..(rank-1) (standard Tensor/Eigen semantics implied by the shown calls).
Op inputs are graph-supplied tensors (entry-point), so tensor shapes and dtypes are attacker-controlled subject only to shown checks.
Lines 8 and 12 guarantee input_max is effectively 1-D with exactly depth elements, so the input_max_data[i] read at line 52 is within bounds.
limitations: A degenerate input_min shaped [depth, 0] passes line 8 with zero elements and would over-read at line 52; not used as the primary finding because the degenerate shape is not derived in-fragment (degenerate-input discipline).
std::abs(INT32_MIN) at line 50 is undefined behavior but affects only float scale computation, not a security-relevant consumer.
Depth values beyond INT64_MAX are impractical given TensorFlow tensor limits and were not analyzed.

verdict.summary: setup_config dereferences `local` at line 31 after an inverted return-status check: `!find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1)` treats only return 0 as failure, but find_site_by_name returns 0 on success and a negative (nonzero) error on failure, so any failed lookup bypasses the error branch and reaches `local->local = 1` with `local` unwritten (NULL), causing a NULL-pointer dereference / daemon crash. The fix would be the corrected comparison `find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1) < 0` at line 26.

evidence.reason: NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476) at the sink line 31. `local` is a file-scope booth_site_t* written only through the out-parameter of the line 26 call; a failed lookup returns negative (nonzero) under the codebase's own 0-on-success/negative-on-failure convention shown at lines 6, 11, and 37 and leaves *site unwritten. Guard line 25 (DAEMON, nonempty cl.site) is passed by the witness; guard line 26 admits every nonzero return to line 31 (`!x` is true only for ret==0), so the failure value -1 flows to the sink with `local` still NULL. The protective statement that would cover the whole failure set, `find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1) < 0`, is absent; the present `!` check protects only the ret==0 case (and misroutes success 0 into `return -EINVAL` at line 29, confirming the inversion, CWE-754). Result: write to a NULL `local` and daemon crash (availability DoS).

assumptions: `local` is a file-scope global `booth_site_t *` initialized to NULL and assigned nowhere else in the fragment. (Declaration is outside the shown code.)

`find_site_by_name` follows the fragment's visible status convention: returns 0 on success and negative on failure, and does not write `*site` on failure — consistent with the `< 0` checks used for read_config (line 6), read_authkey (line 11), and check_config (line 37), and with standard lookup/out-parameter semantics implied by the name.
`cl.lockfile` is a fixed char array with sizeof >= 2, and `booth_conf` is non-NULL after `read_config` succeeds (lines 5-7).
limitations: The exact failure-return convention of `find_site_by_name` is not textually shown in the fragment; if it in fact returns nonzero on success and 0 on not-found, the line 26 guard would be correct and the fragment safe. This unshown callee contract is the main reason confidence is 0.74 rather than higher.

`local`'s NULL initial value is not visible in the fragment; if a producer elsewhere guaranteed a non-NULL prior `local`, the crash would not occur (absent such guarantee, the failed lookup leaves it unchanged).

The `snprintf(cl.lockfile, sizeof(cl.lockfile)-1, ...)` at line 44 is memory-safe under standard snprintf semantics (always NUL-terminated, bounded write); the `-1` is at most a truncation-robustness nit, not a vulnerability.
`find_myself`'s return at line 33 is ignored per the line 24 comment, but no shown statement dereferences `local` on that path, so no in-fragment consequence is confirmable.

verdict.summary: Heap-buffer-overflow write in mpgviddmx_process: line 139 copies an 8-byte start-code window into ctx->hdr_store, whose capacity (ctx->hdr_store_alloc, set at lines 69/299/343) is never guaranteed to be >= 8, while ctx->bytes_in_header ∈ {1..4} (set at lines 130/199/433) is admitted; a small accumulated store (capacity 5..7) combined with a persisted bytes_in_header overruns the gf_realloc'd buffer.

The absent protective statement is the capacity check `if (ctx->hdr_store_alloc < 8) { ctx->hdr_store_alloc = 8; ctx->hdr_store = gf_realloc(ctx->hdr_store, sizeof(char)*ctx->hdr_store_alloc); }` before this memcpy.

assumptions: ctx->hdr_store_alloc is the byte capacity of the gf_realloc'd ctx->hdr_store buffer (sizeof(char)=1), changed only at lines 69, 299, 343.

ctx fields (hdr_store_size, hdr_store_alloc, bytes_in_header) persist across filter invocations; bytes_in_header is reset only at lines 163/170, while the staging branches exit via break at lines 131/219/526.
limitations: The exact attacker byte sequence steering the unshown callees (gf_m4v_parse_config returning GF_EOS/GF_OK, gf_m4v_get_object_start's obj_size) is not enumerated; the witness uses the residual ranges the fragment itself admits, so it is a relational/range witness rather than a single exact-value witness.

Impact is process-abort availability only; no memory-corruption or code-execution mechanism is exercised.

verdict.summary: HttpFileImpl::saveAs writes uploaded content to an attacker-influenced path: the L5-7 anchor guard checks only is_absolute(), has_parent_path(), and the first path component (begin()), so a fileName such as "a/../../evil.txt" passes the guard, is joined to the upload path at L11, and when saved at L25 resolves (via OS '..' handling) to a location outside the upload directory — an arbitrary-file-write path traversal (CWE-22).

("a/../../evil.txt").

verdict.summary: TransposeShapeFn indexes the input shape's dimension array (capacity = rank, established by WithRank at line 33) with attacker-controlled perm entries; the only guard, `if (in_idx >= rank)` at line 51, excludes values at or above rank but admits negative values, so a perm entry such as -1 reaches c->Dim(input, in_idx) at line 55 as a negative subscript, causing an out-of-bounds heap read.

verdict.summary: publish() can overflow the 64-entry triggeredTopics buffer: the only drain guard (line 3) fires once per call and only when numTriggeredTopics is exactly 64, but a single call adds up to two topics (line 30 for a terminating wildcard child, line 54 for the exact match), so a pre-call count of 63 yields a write at index 64 (CWE-787). The per-write drain bound that would neutralize this is absent.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): with numTriggeredTopics == 63 at entry (admitted by the line 3 guard `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64)`), a publish of topic "a" with an untriggered terminatingWildcardChild T and exact child "a" adds T at line 30 (valid index 63, counter becomes 64) and then reaches this sink at index 64, one past the 64-entry buffer whose capacity is stated by line 2 and line 3. No drain/bound check exists between line 30 and this write; the absent fix is a per-write `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) drain();` immediately before line 54, as the fixed upstream variant adds.

Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): in the recursion frame entered via line 37 (which re-checks line 3 at count 63, so no drain), publishing "a/b/c" with terminating wildcard children at two successive levels writes index 63 for segment "b" and then index 64 for segment "c" here, exceeding the 64-entry triggeredTopics capacity expressed by lines 2-3. The per-write drain check that would neutralize this is absent; the top-of-function drain (line 3) only covers the first add of each call.

assumptions: triggeredTopics is the fixed 64-entry buffer whose capacity is stated by line 2 and the line 3 `== 64` bound (valid indices 0..63).
numTriggeredTopics is a counter whose in-fragment constraint is only line 3, so 63 is an admitted pre-call state.
A trie node may legitimately hold both a terminatingWildcardChild and exact children simultaneously (lines 25 and 40 handle them as independent fields); nodes start untriggered.
Publish topics are entry-point (attacker-supplied) data; both single- and multi-segment topics are handled by the shown loop.
limitations: The declaration of triggeredTopics' capacity is not inside this fragment; it is inferred from the visible 64-bound at lines 2-3 (corroborated upstream by the real `Topic *triggeredTopics[64]` declaration).
The pre-call value of numTriggeredTopics is caller state; the fragment constrains only the value 64 at line 3, and the demonstration requires 63.
The wildcard filter (lines 18-22) and the top-of-function drain (lines 3-5) do not mitigate this failure; only a drain immediately before each triggeredTopics write closes it.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. MqttPacket_Read returns bytes read on success (capped by rx_buf_len) and negative on error, so rc >= 1 after the `rc <= 0` guard at line 94.

The multithread recv-lock ownership in the READ case (line 124) assumes the library's state-machine invariant that entering with MQTT_MSG_WAIT implies lockRecv held; not fully derivable from the shown statements.

verdict.summary: HttpFileImpl::save builds the file destination from the unconstrained path parameter and the fileName_ member without canonicalizing or checking containment against the upload root. A path argument whose first component is '..' is routed around the upload-path anchoring by the guard at lines 7-9, and a fileName_ such as '../../escape.bin' is appended unchanged at line 27, so the uploaded content is written outside the upload directory (arbitrary file write via relative-path escape). The fragment lacks the canonicalize-plus-containment check that the patched version adds before saveTo.

evidence.reason: Sink L27 writes at fsPath / fsFileName with no containment check. fileName_ has residual range 'any non-empty string' (only L4 constrains it to non-empty), so the witness fileName_='../../escape.bin' with path='files' is admitted by G1 (L4), anchored at L13 to <uploadRoot>/files, then appended unmodified, yielding <uploadRoot>/files/../../escape.bin which the OS resolves outside the upload root obtained at L12. The guard at L7-9 also admits '..'-prefixed path values (condition false when begin()=='..'), passing them unanchored to L27. The absent fix, present in the patched upstream version, is weakly_canonical + a std::equal prefix-containment check before saveTo; no protective statement exists on the L3->L27 path, confirming CWE-22 arbitrary file write outside the upload directory.

assumptions: The upload root returned by HttpAppFrameworkImpl::instance().getUploadPath() (L12) is the intended confinement boundary for saved files.
saveTo(path) has the name-implied semantics of writing the uploaded file content to the given path (upstream implements it with std::ofstream).
filesystem::path operator/ does not normalize '..' components; resolution to the escaped location happens at OS call time.
limitations: The attacker provenance of fileName_ (set from the HTTP multipart Content-Disposition filename in the full framework) is not visible inside this fragment; the demonstrated failing value relies on a '..'-bearing value being supplied through path or fileName_.

An empty path reaching fsPath.begin()->string() at L9 would be an end-iterator dereference, but only in release builds where the L3 assert is compiled out; this depends on an unshown NDEBUG setting and was not treated as a finding.

A caller may deliberately pass absolute or '..'-prefixed paths since save() is a general-purpose API; the vulnerability materializes when untrusted request data (filename or user-chosen path) is forwarded into save().
TOCTOU between the exists() check at L16 and create_directories() at L20 is benign because the error_code status is checked at L21.

verdict.summary: The release callback recovers the enclosing rtrs_clt_sess via container_of and frees it. The fragment contains no conditional, loop, arithmetic, capacity, or NULL-producing statement, so no failing value can be shown to reach kfree(clt). No confirmed vulnerability is derivable from the shown code.

Use-after-free or double-free cannot be confirmed: no in-fragment path or reference-count logic can free clt twice; it depends on unshown callers.
An out-of-bounds or wrong-pointer free cannot be confirmed because no capacity or numeric derivation is shown and the struct layout is not visible.
Caller-side invariants (dev being live and properly embedded) are not verifiable from the fragment in either direction.

verdict.summary: FractionalAvgPoolGrad Compute reads attacker-controlled row/col pooling-sequence values without validating them; a negative in_row_start/in_col_start is admitted by the pooling loops and yields a negative in_index, causing an out-of-bounds write through in_backprop_tensor_temp_mat.coeffRef.

evidence.reason: Sink write: in_index is derived at L103 as (b * in_rows + in_r) * in_cols + in_c, where in_r starts at in_row_start = row_seq_tensor_flat(r) (L86) and in_c at in_col_start = col_seq_tensor_flat(c) (L91). row_seq_tensor/col_seq_tensor are entry-point inputs with int64 values left fully unconstrained: guards L38/L44 bound only NumElements (element count), and clamps L89/L94 cap only the loop ENDS. Witness: orig_input_tensor_shape=[1,3,2,1] (in_batch=1, in_rows=3, in_cols=2, in_depth=1), row_seq=[-1,5], col_seq=[0,2], out_backprop=[1,1,1,1], overlapping_=false. All guards pass in order: L38 (2>1), L44 (2>1), L84/L85/L90, L89 (end clamped to 2), L94, L101 (in_r=-1 <= 2 admitted), L102 (in_c=0), L105 (d=0 < out_depth=1); at L103 in_index=(0-1)*2+0 = -2. The capacity declared at L74-76 is in_depth=1 row x in_cols*in_rows*in_batch=6 cols (valid flat index 0..5), so in_index=-2 yields coeffRef(0,-2) referencing memory before the buffer; the write in_backprop_ref += ... (L110-111) performs a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The absent fix is a lower-bound clamp/validation of in_row_start/in_col_start (e.g., in_row_start = std::max(in_row_start, 0);) or validation that seq elements lie in [0, in_rows]/[0, in_cols].

assumptions: Tensor op inputs (orig_input_tensor_shape, out_backprop, row_seq_tensor, col_seq_tensor) are entry-point, attacker-controlled data (L23-31).
Eigen Map::coeffRef performs unchecked raw element access with the matrix dimensions declared at L74-79.
OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK correctly abort on allocation or shape errors (L24, L38, L44, L69, L121).
limitations: The same sink is also reachable when out_depth > in_depth (d overruns the in_depth rows at L75/L105) or out_batch > in_batch (column overflow), since no shape-consistency guard is shown; these are secondary drivers of the same finding, not used in the primary witness.
Potential int64 overflow in in_cols*in_rows*in_batch (L76) or in the index arithmetic for extreme shape values was not pursued; TF size limits and allocation failure paths would normally abort first.
Degenerate/zero or negative entries in orig_input_tensor_shape (L55-58) were not used as the primary witness; TensorShape/allocator failure semantics there are not fully shown.
Seq-read guards at L38/L44 and end-clamps at L89/L94 were verified protective for their own operations (reads of seq(r+1)/seq(c+1) and upper-bound overflow) and are not demoted.

verdict.summary: In the decrypt branch (lines 59-63), ilen = aes->src_len - authsize is an unsigned subtraction with no underflow check: for src_len < authsize (e.g., src_len=0, authsize=16, both admitted by the shown guards, and 0-length input explicitly allowed by the comment at lines 50-51), ilen wraps to 4294967280 and is consumed as the scatterlist advance length (line 62), the DMA/loop size (lines 148-151, 167-186) and the tag-source position (line 249), causing out-of-bounds reads/NULL SG walks and non-termination in kernel memory. The absent protective statement is an underflow check such as 'if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;' between lines 61 and 62.

evidence.reason: Unsigned underflow at line 61: aes->src_len (entry-point request field, no shown lower bound; comment at lines 50-51 permits 0-length input) minus authsize (admitted as 16 by the switch at lines 34-45) wraps for src_len=0 to ilen=4294967280 (u32). The wrapped value passes every guard on the decrypt path (lines 21, 24-27, 29, 33-45, 56 else-branch, 116, 144 'if (ilen > 0)', 167 'while (src.sg_wa.bytes_left)') and is consumed as the SG-advance length at line 62, as the DMA/loop size at lines 148-151 and 167-186 over a 0-byte input SG, as the GHASH length at line 217, and as the tag fetch position at line 249 (ccp_set_dm_area(&tag, 0, p_tag, 0, authsize) reads 16 bytes ~4 GiB beyond the input), yielding an out-of-bounds read / NULL SG walk / hang in kernel memory (CWE-125). The absent fix is the single protective statement 'if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;' (or 'if (ilen > aes->src_len) return -EINVAL;') between lines 61 and 62; its absence leaves the CWE-191 wrap feeding every listed consumer.

assumptions: authsize is restricted to {4,8,12,13,14,15,16} by the switch at lines 33-45; the value 16 is admitted (line 35) either from aes->authsize or the AES_BLOCK_SIZE default at line 33.
ilen and authsize are unsigned 32-bit (ilen declared 'unsigned int' at line 11); aes->src_len participates in this unsigned arithmetic with no shown minimum.
aes->iv and aes->key are non-NULL after the checks at lines 21-22 and 29-30; aes->key_len is in {128,192,256} after lines 24-27.
The ctx workarea has capacity CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES (lines 97-99); the key workarea has capacity CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES (lines 76-78).
limitations: The internal behavior of the unshown callees (scatterwalk_ffwd, ccp_init_data, ccp_set_dm_area) - OOB read vs NULL dereference vs clean -EINVAL rejection - is not displayed; the finding relies on the standard name-implied semantics that an ~4 GiB advance/length over a finite (0-byte) scatterlist walks past the end. Even if a callee rejects it, the wrapped value still drives the GCTR loop bound (lines 167-186) and the GHASH length (line 217).
No in-fragment capacity for aes->src is shown; the OOB-read impact rests on ilen=4294967280 vastly exceeding any realistic SG byte count rather than a literal displayed capacity.

Demoted candidate: the dm_offset wrap at line 103 (ccp_set_dm_area(&ctx, dm_offset, aes->iv, 0, aes->iv_len) for aes->iv_len > CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES) is not confirmed because ccp_set_dm_area's internal bounds validation is not shown and the GCM IV-length contract of the caller (crypto AEAD framework) is outside the fragment.
The aad_len-driven scatterwalk_ffwd calls at lines 54-55 were not confirmed from the fragment because the actual byte counts of aes->src/aes->dst SGs are caller-provided and unshown.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every security-relevant sink is protected: getaddrinfo/socket/setsockopt/bind/getsockname return codes are checked (lines 24, 36, 41, 45, 52, 57, 74) before use, and the only failure set that could reach the naddr consumers (net_port_get at line 85, net_address_get at line 86) is a truncated/oversized getsockname result, which is excluded by the bound check 'else if (naddr_len > sizeof(naddr))' at line 79 that exits to error before consumption. getaddrinfo returns a non-NULL result list on success (ret >= 0), so servinfo/ptr are valid inside the loop; each addrinfo node's ai_addr/ai_addrlen/ai_next fields are well-formed per POSIX.
net_address_get caps its output at the passed size argument (inet_ntop-style name-implied semantics), so addr is bounded when reached after the line 79 check.
bind/socket/setsockopt return negative on failure, which the loop's continue/break structure uses correctly.
fd is initialized to -1 at line 30, so no uninitialized descriptor is used; close(fd) at line 93 is harmless when fd == -1.
limitations: Reading ptr at line 65 after freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 63 is technically a value read of a freed pointer (UB), but ptr is never dereferenced or otherwise consumed after that point, so no use-after-free sink is demonstrable inside the fragment.

Behavior of the unshown helpers (cfg_getsec/cfg_getstr/cfg_getbool, net_port_get, net_address_get) is not verified beyond name-implied semantics; no shown producer supplies NULL or out-of-domain values to them that would create a failure.

Without the line 79 check, interpretation of a truncated sockaddr would depend on OS truncation behavior for the downstream consumers; that hypothetical is not reachable in this fragment because the check is present.

The attacker-controlled extension tokens from g_strsplit can be arbitrarily long, but no write path exceeds the declared capacity, so the fragment is the fixed counterpart of an unbounded-append overflow.

g_strsplit at line 13 returns a NULL-terminated token array for a non-NULL input, making the sentinel loop at line 17 well-bounded.
g_strlcat with sizeof(buffer) never writes past the destination and always NUL-terminates, bounding the result to 255 chars.

limitations: A NULL extensions_str argument at line 13 would make g_strsplit return NULL and the loop at line 17 dereference NULL; no in-fragment statement produces that NULL, so this depends on an unshown caller and is not confirmed.
tags_data->timestamp at lines 11 and 51 assumes a non-NULL tags_data; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.
The return of tcp_sendf at line 52 is discarded; a failed send has no shown security-relevant consequence.
The vulnerable counterpart would have used unbounded strcat/sprintf for the appends at lines 29, 37, and 38; those protective g_strlcat bounds are present here.

verdict.summary: rtrs_clt_dev_release is a straight-line device release: container_of, two mutex_destroy calls, and one kfree. No attacker-controlled input, branch, loop, capacity, or index exists in the fragment, and no shown statement produces NULL or a double free, so no failure witness is derivable. All dangerous-operation scenarios (NULL dev, uninitialized mutex, use-after-free/double-free of clt) depend on unshown caller/device-core contracts and are therefore not confirmable.

assumptions: container_of(dev, struct rtrs_clt_sess, dev) (lines 4-5) implies dev is the address of the embedded dev member of a live rtrs_clt_sess, so clt is non-NULL whenever dev is non-NULL.
kfree(clt) at line 11 frees the containing object exactly once under the standard driver-core release-once-refcount-zero contract.
limitations: NULL-dev dereference via container_of and mutex_destroy (lines 4-10) is not confirmable: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, and a NULL release pointer would have to come from an unshown caller/device-core path.
Use-after-free or double-free of clt (line 11) is not confirmable: it depends on unshown path/session lifetime and refcount logic in rtrs_clt callers, which the analysis rules forbid assuming.

mutex_destroy on uninitialized or in-use mutexes (lines 9-10) cannot be established from the fragment because mutex initialization and locking are not shown; this is a robustness/contract concern, not a demonstrated flaw.

verdict.summary: In the VNC_MSG_CLIENT_CUT_TEXT case, when the handler is invoked with a partial message (len > 8 but less than 8 + dlen), the fragment calls client_cut_text(vs, read_u32(data,4), data + 8) with an unvalidated, attacker-controlled length. The only dlen check (line 66) is nested under 'if (len == 8)' (line 64) and never runs on this path, so dlen can exceed the len - 8 valid bytes behind data + 8, causing a heap out-of-bounds read and remote denial of service.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled dlen = read_u32(data,4) (residual range 0..UINT32_MAX from the entry-point VNC wire buffer, Phase 1) reaches the sink on the partial-message path: witness len=9, dlen=65535 (data[4..7]=0x0000FFFF, data[0]=CUT_TEXT). Guards in order: L7 (3>3 false), L11->L60, L61 (9==1 false), L64 (9==8 false, so the only dlen guard L66 never executes), then L70. The fragment's own layout arithmetic (L62 'return 8;', L67 'return 8 + dlen;') establishes the valid payload capacity behind data+8 as len-8 = 1 byte, so dlen=65535 > 1 exceeds it; the cut-text callee consumes/copies dlen bytes from data+8 (call-site confirmation), yielding a heap over-read (CWE-125). The len==8-only check at L64-L66 covers only the exact-header sub-path and does not cover this failure set; the absent protective statement is the partial-message bound check 'if (dlen > len - 8) return 8 + dlen;' before the sink.

assumptions: data points to the transport input buffer whose valid prefix is len bytes; the fragment's own return-value protocol (L62 'return 8;', L67 'return 8 + dlen;') fixes the 8-byte CUT_TEXT header and dlen-byte payload layout.
The unshown callee client_cut_text consumes/copies dlen bytes from data+8 per its name-implied semantics, so dlen must not exceed len-8.

The transport may invoke the handler with len larger than the minimum, including partial CUT_TEXT payloads (the fragment's re-arm protocol via vnc_read_when(...,1) at L138 implies partial-message handling).
limitations: The heap allocation capacity of data is not declared in the fragment; the over-read magnitude beyond the allocation assumes the transport buffers at most the received prefix (plus slack). The in-fragment derivation dlen > len-8 remains the confirmed out-of-domain argument regardless.

SET_ENCODINGS loop reads/writes (L33-36) and set_encodings(data+4, limit) (L38), plus reads at offsets 4..16 in SET_PIXEL_FORMAT / QEMU audio (L16-20, L110, L117, L120) may read past len, but their backing capacity is not shown; demoted.
Unsigned wrap of '8 + dlen' (L67) and '4 + (limit * 4)' (L29) affects only the unshown caller's re-arm logic; no in-fragment consumer is shown.
len==0 would make data[0] (L7) an OOB read, but no shown producer guarantees len>=1 from the transport; demoted.

verdict.summary: In the decryption branch, ilen = aes->src_len - authsize (line 61) underflows to 0xFFFFFFF0 when src_len < authsize (e.g., src_len=0, authsize=16), and the wrapped length is then consumed as a byte offset in scatterwalk_ffwd (line 62) and as a size by ccp_init_data (lines 148/158) and the loop at line 167, causing an out-of-bounds read/write over the undersized source scatterlist. The absent fix is a src_len >= authsize bound check before the subtraction.

evidence.snippet:
ret = ccp_init_data(&src, cmd_q, p_inp, ilen,
				    AES_BLOCK_SIZE,
				    in_place ? DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL
					     : DMA_TO_DEVICE);
evidence.reason: ilen is derived at line 61 as aes->src_len - authsize with u32 semantics: for the admitted decrypt witness src_len=0 (allowed by the lines 50-51 comment) and authsize=16 (line 33 default, admitted by the switch at lines 34-45), ilen wraps to 0xFFFFFFF0. The guard at line 144 (ilen > 0) admits it, and it is passed as the copy length to ccp_init_data, which by its standard semantics commits ilen bytes from p_inp (an SGL describing src_len=0 bytes), yielding an OOB read/Possibly-corrupting DMA (CWE-191 underflow consumed as a size, CWE-125 OOB read). No statement bounds src_len against authsize; the missing fix is 'if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;' before line 61.

On the same decrypt path and witness, ilen=0xFFFFFFF0 is used as a byte offset to walk p_inp forward; p_inp represents the source SGL of only src_len=0 bytes, so scatterwalk_ffwd advances ~2^32 bytes, reading SG descriptors/pages beyond the list end or dereferencing NULL at the chain end — an OOB read caused by the unguarded u32 underflow at line 61. This sink executes with no intervening guard after line 61.

assumptions: aes->src_len and aes->authsize are 32-bit unsigned fields (ilen is declared unsigned int at line 11); even if src_len were signed, src_len=0 - 16 converts to the same 0xFFFFFFF0 value.
AES_BLOCK_SIZE == 16 and CCP_AES_ACTION_ENCRYPT identifies the encrypt branch (line 56), so any other action takes the decrypt path.
p_inp describes at most aes->src_len bytes of source data (per the length semantics used at lines 57 and 61).
Lines 50-51 explicitly admit zero-length input, grounding the src_len=0 witness in the fragment itself.
Sink semantics are taken from the function names per the task rules: scatterwalk_ffwd advances by the given byte count, ccp_init_data processes the given length from the scatterlist.
limitations: The aes->iv_len-derived dm_offset at lines 103-104 is demoted: the fragment's own comment (lines 93-95) fixes the IV at 16 bytes, and no shown statement derives iv_len > CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES.

The exact post-wrap behavior of ccp_init_data/scatterwalk_ffwd (immediate error return vs. actual OOB commit) is callee-internal; the confirmed point is the oversized length/offset reaching the copy/DMA sink.

aad_len-based offsets (lines 54-55) were not audited for overlap with src_len, and the precise crash mode (OOB descriptor read vs. NULL deref) at line 62 depends on SGL termination details not shown in the fragment.
Subsequent sinks (lines 158, 167, 217, 249) all inherit the same wrapped ilen but are downstream of failure at lines 62/148 and are not given separate evidence items.

verdict.summary: Use-after-free: freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 frees the entire addrinfo chain, after which the successful-bind path dereferences the freed node via ptr->ai_addr / &ptr->ai_addrlen in getsockname (line 70) and ptr->ai_addr in net_port_get/net_address_get (lines 77-78).

evidence.reason: ptr aliases the addrinfo node selected by break at line 58; freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 frees that node and its ai_addr storage before this dereference. On the admitted success path (getaddrinfo ret==0, socket/setsockopt/bind ret==0, break, !ptr false at line 63) no statement between line 61 and line 70 copies or revalidates ptr, so ptr->ai_addr is a freed-pointer read and the kernel writes the socket name into freed heap while &ptr->ai_addrlen writes through the freed node. The absent protective statement is deferring freeaddrinfo until after line 78 (or saving ptr->ai_addr/ai_addrlen before line 61). Primary CWE-416 use-after-free.

Reads the freed sockaddr buffer through ptr->ai_addr after freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 freed the chain on the admitted successful-bind path; same CWE-416 use-after-free as line 70, with no intervening copy or revalidation.

Reads the freed sockaddr buffer through ptr->ai_addr after freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 on the admitted successful-bind path; size is bounded by sizeof(addr), so the flaw is the freed-pointer read (CWE-416), not a buffer overflow.

assumptions: getaddrinfo success returns a non-NULL, NULL-terminated addrinfo list (POSIX).
freeaddrinfo frees the whole chain including each node's ai_addr and ai_addrlen storage (POSIX).
net_address_get(addr, sizeof(addr), ...) is a size-capped formatter for the INET6_ADDRSTRLEN buffer declared at line 7.
limitations: Line 22 checks getaddrinfo with 'ret < 0'; whether positive EAI error codes exist depends on the platform's EAI sign convention, which is not shown, so a failure-treated-as-success path consuming uninitialized servinfo (lines 28, 61) cannot be confirmed from the fragment (CWE-754/697 candidate only).
Exploitation of the freed heap depends on allocator reuse; the memory-safety violation itself is confirmed by the shown statements.
close(fd) at line 85 with fd == -1 is a harmless EBADF no-op; not reported.
NULL provenance of cfgaddr/log_service_name from unshown config is handled by the shown ternaries; no finding.

verdict.summary: No security-relevant failure can be demonstrated from the shown statements. The type gate at line 3 constrains only input1->type, and no tensor buffer capacity, NULL producer, or callee contract is visible in the fragment, so the suspected type-mismatch OOB, the ignored QuantizeMultiplier status with uninitialized shift/multiplier variables, and the INT32_MIN negation cannot be confirmed as findings. All dangerous operations were inventoried and all guards audited, but no protective statement decisively covers them, leaving this a complete-audit default verdict.

assumptions: The tensor pointers input1, input2, and output are treated as non-NULL because no shown statement can produce NULL for them (plain parameters; GetTensorShape/GetTensorData are accessors).
input_dtype and opname are template parameters of the enclosing kernel and are assumed consistent with the branch taken, since their values are not shown.
limitations: Type mismatch: line 3 checks only input1->type (kTfLiteUInt8/kTfLiteInt8), so an input2 of a different type reaches input2->params.zero_point (line 5), input2->params.scale (line 13), and GetTensorData<input_dtype>(input2) (lines 26, 31). A CWE-125/type-confusion claim is unconfirmable because no buffer capacity for input2 is declared or computed in the fragment and the mismatch itself requires an unshown caller.

Status handling: the return values of QuantizeMultiplier (lines 12-13) are discarded and input1_multiplier/input1_shift/input2_multiplier/input2_shift (declared lines 8-11) are never initialized before use at lines 18-19 and 21-22; whether the callee can fail on an admitted scale and what the downstream kernels do with the values is not shown, so no CWE-754/CWE-457 finding is confirmable.

Integer: -input1->params.zero_point (line 4) and -input2->params.zero_point (line 5) overflow int32 only for zero_point == INT32_MIN, a value no shown statement can produce, so the witness is invalid under the degenerate-input discipline.
No capacity for the output or input data buffers is visible in the fragment, so none of the comparison kernel accesses (lines 24-27, 29-32) can be proven out-of-bounds from shown statements.

verdict.summary: Fixed counterpart: passwd1_sum and passwd2_sum occupy disjoint hash_len-sized regions (lines 22, 26), the PBKDF2 compare is bounded by keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN (line 41), and stored-hash read failures are fail-closed (line 35). No reachable memory-safety, injection, crypto, or authz failure is demonstrable from the shown statements.

assumptions: PBKDF2_LENGTH and PBKDF2_SALT_LEN are build-time constants; the fragment's own layout (key = passwd2_sum + PBKDF2_SALT_LEN at line 39, compared for keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN at line 41) implies PBKDF2_LENGTH >= PBKDF2_SALT_LEN and keylen <= hash_len.
calloc at line 22 returns 2*hash_len bytes when hash_len > 0; hash_len derives from the constant PBKDF2_LENGTH (line 10) or digest_length(d) of a valid digest (line 19).
read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd fill at most hash_len bytes per the size argument at lines 29/31 (name-implied decode semantics).
digest_length(d) equals the byte count digest_digest writes into passwd1_sum (lines 19, 51).
limitations: Negative keylen (PBKDF2_SALT_LEN > PBKDF2_LENGTH) cannot be derived from shown statements; it depends on unshown config constants.
digest_free(d) with d == NULL in the PBKDF2 error path (line 62): NULL is produced in-fragment (line 3), but the dereference behavior is inside the unshown callee, so it is demoted.
hash_len * 2 at line 22 has no attacker-controlled magnitude that could overflow int; digest_length results and PBKDF2_LENGTH are trusted constants.
Exact return-value semantics of the read helpers are unshown; a non-negative short fill only affects comparison success/failure against calloc-zeroed bytes, not memory safety.

verdict.summary: Stack-based buffer overflow in inbound_cap_ls: the server-supplied CAP LS parameter is split into an unbounded token count (g_strsplit with max_tokens=0, line 15) and each recognized token appends a fixed literal to char buffer[256] (line 4) via strcat with no accumulated-length check, so 20+ duplicate tokens overflow the stack buffer.

evidence.reason: Sink writes 13 bytes + NUL into buffer declared at line 4 as char buffer[256]. extensions_str is entry-point IRC-server data split at line 15 into an unlimited token count; the loop at line 19 admits any number of tokens and the guard at line 23 admits every duplicate of "identify-msg". After 19 appends strlen(buffer)=255 (NUL at index 255, the last valid index); the 20th strcat writes through index 268, exceeding the 256-byte capacity. No length/capacity check exists on any path; the absent fix is a bound check such as 'if (strlen(buffer) + 14 >= sizeof(buffer)) break;' before each strcat. Primary CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow.

assumptions: g_strsplit with max_tokens=0 (line 15) returns a NULL-terminated array of all space-separated tokens with no count limit, per standard GLib semantics.
Each matching literal is appended verbatim at a fixed size: "identify-msg " is 13 chars, "znc.in/server-time-iso " is 23 chars.
buffer[256] (line 4) is the only sink object; strcpy at line 17 is safe (9 bytes).
limitations: The other strcat sinks (lines 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 59, 64, 70, 79) exhibit the identical unbounded-append failure; the witness is shown for line 25 only.
tags_data and nick are consumed only by EMIT_SIGNAL_TIMESTAMP and were not analyzed for NULL/format issues because no such sink is visible inside the fragment.

verdict.summary: xfrm_migrate() stores found/migrated states into fixed-capacity stack arrays x_cur[XFRM_MAX_DEPTH] and x_new[XFRM_MAX_DEPTH] with counters nx_cur/nx_new that are incremented per loop iteration and never bounds-checked; an unvalidated num_migrate > XFRM_MAX_DEPTH drives an out-of-bounds stack write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: OOB write at the confirmed sink: num_migrate (int parameter, no shown bound — L14 only checks the unshown callee's return value) drives the loop at L29; each iteration admitted by the L30 non-NULL branch increments nx_cur at L32, so after XFRM_MAX_DEPTH+1 admitted iterations nx_cur == XFRM_MAX_DEPTH and L31 writes x_cur[XFRM_MAX_DEPTH], one past the capacity declared at L9 (valid indices 0..XFRM_MAX_DEPTH-1). The absent fix statement is a bound check rejecting num_migrate > XFRM_MAX_DEPTH or guarding nx_cur < XFRM_MAX_DEPTH; the L34/L38 status branch runs after the L31 store and cannot protect it. Primary CWE-787 stack out-of-bounds write.

Second OOB write at the confirmed sink: on the same path, each L34 non-NULL xc admission increments nx_new at L36; with num_migrate = XFRM_MAX_DEPTH+1 and xc non-NULL for those iterations, L35 writes x_new[XFRM_MAX_DEPTH], one past the capacity declared at L10. Same absent fix (no num_migrate/nx_new bound check anywhere in the fragment); primary CWE-787.

assumptions: XFRM_MAX_DEPTH is the compile-time element count of both arrays declared at L9-L10, so valid indices are 0..XFRM_MAX_DEPTH-1.
For the witness, xfrm_migrate_policy_find (L23) and xfrm_migrate_state_find (L30) succeed for the supplied entries; the shown code explicitly admits the non-NULL branches.
xfrm_migrate_check (L14) returns >= 0 for the witnessed num_migrate; the fragment shows no constraint tying its return to the magnitude of num_migrate.
limitations: The numeric value of XFRM_MAX_DEPTH and the concrete netlink origin of num_migrate are defined outside the shown fragment.
The witness is a relational/range witness (num_migrate > XFRM_MAX_DEPTH) whose full exploitability depends on the unshown lookup/migration callees succeeding for the attacker-supplied entries.
The restore_state paths at L66-L69 would additionally pass the oversized nx_cur/nx_new to xfrm_states_put/delete, but this is secondary to the confirmed L31/L35 write sinks.

Every server-supplied length is bounded before use: msgLength is restricted to [8,2000] for 'R' (L1032) and [8,30000] for 'E' (L1040), kept non-negative (L1069, L1173), and gated by the avail < msgLength / pqCheckInBufferSpace check (L1070-1082) so parsing, pqGetErrorNotice3, and pg_fe_sendauth only run on complete, validated messages. connhost[] indexing (L117) is bounded by the whichhost guard (L86-106); Unix socket path length is checked (L174); errorMessage indexing is guarded (L1057-1058). No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: conn->raddr.addr (sockaddr_storage) is at least as large as any ai_addrlen returned by getaddrinfo (OS invariant, not declared in the fragment).
Option strings sslmode/gssencmode/requirepeer/appname are non-NULL; they originate from conninfo parsing before this function.
UNIXSOCK_PATH is a bounded-output (snprintf-based) helper, so the post-write strlen check at L174 does not race an unbounded write into portstr.
getHostaddr, pg_getaddrinfo_all, pqGets_append, pqGetErrorNotice3, PQgetResult, and pg_fe_sendauth follow their standard bounded semantics for the validated lengths passed.
strdup failure for conn->connip is intentionally ignored per the in-fragment comment (non-security).
limitations: Demoted: PQgetvalue(res,0,0) in CONNECTION_CHECK_WRITABLE/CONNECTION_CHECK_STANDBY is used in strncmp without a NULL/PQnfields guard; the NULL deref only materializes if a malicious server sends a 1-tuple 0-column result, which no shown statement derives or excludes, and which stock libpq also tolerates.

Demoted: memcpy(&conn->raddr.addr, addr_cur->ai_addr, addr_cur->ai_addrlen) — the destination capacity (sockaddr_storage) is not declared in the fragment, so no in-fragment capacity failure can be demonstrated.
Demoted: server-controlled message bodies inside pqGetErrorNotice3 / pg_fe_sendauth are not analyzed; only the in-fragment length validation is assessed.

The mismatch between flat_segment_id.size() and relative_offset_set.size() cannot be resolved without the helpers' bodies; the safe verdict relies on their standard contracts listed in assumptions.

verdict.summary: SetupWriters dereferences stbl->TimeToSample without a NULL check: the guard at line 17 validates SampleSize, ChunkOffset, and SampleToChunk but omits TimeToSample, so a crafted MP4 track whose sample table lacks the stts box reaches line 39 with TimeToSample == NULL and crashes.

evidence.reason: stbl->TimeToSample is entry-point-derived at line 16 (trak->Media->information->sampleTable) and remains NULL when the file track has no stts box. The guard at line 17 admits this state: it returns only when stbl, SampleSize, ChunkOffset, or SampleToChunk is NULL, and the lines in between (22, 25, 36-38) impose no constraint on TimeToSample. On a track supplying stsz/stco/stsc but no stts, the path L16 -> L17(pass) -> L22(pass) -> L39 dereferences NULL, causing CWE-476 NULL-pointer dereference. The absent fix is adding `!stbl->TimeToSample` to the guard at line 17 (or an equivalent independent check before line 39).

assumptions: gf_isom_get_track returns a valid track for indices 1..trackCount, consistent with the loop bound at lines 11-12.

Sample-table sub-box members of the file-parsed stbl are nullable when the corresponding box is absent; this is supported in-fragment by the NULL checks on SampleSize, ChunkOffset, and SampleToChunk at line 17 and by the entry-point (file-content) provenance of stbl at line 16.
limitations: `trak->Media->mediaHeader` is dereferenced at line 26 with no visible NULL-producer or in-fragment nullable-model for mediaHeader, so that candidate was demoted.
`mw` and `writers` are used unguarded; their non-NULL status depends on the unshown caller.
`mw->total_samples += writer->stbl->SampleSize->sampleCount` (line 58) is a potential u32 arithmetic concern but has no shown security-relevant consumer.
No out-of-bounds or injection sink is demonstrated; entries[0] at line 40 is covered by the nb_entries==1 condition at line 39.

RemapVectorToMap (lines 13-14, 47-48, helper not shown) resizes row_id_present/col_id_present to the input tensor sizes, keeping line 213 accesses in-bounds.

verdict.summary: No attacker-reachable failure is demonstrable from the shown statements alone. The rank guard at lines 15-16 (params_dense_values_in.dims() > 0) fully protects the dim_size(0) read at line 17 on every path, and the remaining candidates (empty nested-splits list at line 12, negative num_params at line 13, unshown callee behavior in MakeSplits/WriteSplits/WriteValues) lack a capacity or producer inside the fragment that demonstrates a failure.

The bodies of ValidateIndices, MakeSplits, WriteSplits, and WriteValues are not shown; no out-of-bounds behavior is assumed for their arguments beyond name-implied standard semantics.

assumptions: safeRead(packed, index, size) bounds index within size, consistent with its name and the loop guard at line 305.

Capacities of smp[], instr[] (including instr[i].snum[120]), phead[], and header->tracker are not shown, so indexing at lines 143-206, 363, and 412 cannot be confirmed as out-of-bounds.
