verdict.summary: The 'i2c md' command parses argv[3] into 'uint length' with no bound (L48), assigns it to 'int nbytes' (L65), where a value >= 0x80000000 wraps negative; the line clamp at L70 caps only positive nbytes and forwards the negative value as 'linebytes', so an attacker-controlled negative byte count reaches the read sink dm_i2c_read/i2c_read (L73/L75) as the size of a read into the 16-byte stack buffer linebuf (L67). No protective statement (length bound/equality check or unsigned width) is present; the missing one-statement fix is a length cap such as 'if (length > INT_MAX) return CMD_RET_USAGE;'.

evidence.reason: Sink consumes an attacker-controlled size: 'length = hextoul(argv[3], NULL)' (L48) is unconstrained (full uint 0..0xFFFFFFFF); 'nbytes = length' (L65) into 'int nbytes' (L7) wraps values >= 0x80000000 to negative (witness 0x80000000 -> -2147483648); 'linebytes = (nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN) ? DISP_LINE_LEN : nbytes' (L70) admits the negative value unchanged because the clamp only caps positive nbytes; guards L77 and L98 are evaluated after the call and cannot exclude it, so linebytes = -2147483648 reaches dm_i2c_read as the read length into linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] (capacity declared L67). Absent fix: a bound/equality check on length (or unsigned nbytes/linebytes). Primary CWE-681: unsigned->signed conversion corrupts an attacker-controlled magnitude that is then consumed as a memory read size.

evidence.snippet: ret = i2c_read(chip, addr, alen, linebuf, linebytes);
evidence.reason: Same confirmed chain as the DM sink (compiled only when DM_I2C is disabled): length from argv[3] (L48) wraps negative at 'nbytes = length' (L65), is re-selected by the positive-only clamp (L70), and reaches i2c_read as a negative byte count for linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] (L67). No in-fragment guard excludes the witness length = 0x80000000 on this path; the absent fix is the same length bound/equality check (or unsigned nbytes/linebytes). Primary CWE-681.

assumptions: DISP_LINE_LEN is the compile-time line-buffer capacity (16) used by linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] at L67; the positive-length safety of the clamp at L70 depends on it.
The uint->int conversion at L65 for values > INT_MAX is implementation-defined but wraps in two's-complement on all real U-Boot targets (ARM/x86/RISC-V).
i2c_dp_last_chip/addr/alen/length are persistent globals; the repeat path (L19) reuses a stored, unvalidated length.
limitations: Whether the negative 'linebytes' causes an actual stack OOB write (CWE-787) depends on the unshown callee loop form: a 'while (len-- > 0)' or width-promoting driver overruns linebuf, while a 'for (j = 0; j < len; j++)' driver silently reads nothing and returns success (then misreported at L77-78); the in-fragment confirmed mechanism is the invalid negative size from the numeric conversion.
The OOB-write path was therefore not independently confirmed; CWE-787 is not listed as a secondary CWE.
Line 75 sink exists only in non-DM_I2C builds; line 73 only in DM_I2C builds.
get_alen and DISP_LINE_LEN definitions are outside the fragment; get_alen was assumed to return 1/2/4/default so that the L40 guard admits alen in {1,2,3}.
The alen>3 check (L40) was audited: alen only feeds offset-length setting (L54) with no shown buffer sized by it, so it is not an independent finding.
A degenerate zero length (L65 -> linebytes=0) is harmless here and was not used as a witness.

verdict.summary: The dangerous in-loop operation is fully protected: line 14 'if (offset >= sz) { break; }' excludes every offset >= sz before line 17 consumes 'buffer + offset' with length 'sz - offset', so neither an out-of-bounds read nor a ut64 underflow is reachable; the 'offset += bsm->size' advance (line 19) has no unguarded consumption. The header read at line 9 (offset 6) has no in-fragment size guard, but confirming an OOB read there requires r_bin_java_default_attr_new (line 5) to return non-NULL for sz < 8, which the fragment does not demonstrate, so it is a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: sz (line 1) is the byte capacity of buffer, established by its use as the total size in 'sz - offset' at line 17.
R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT (line 9) reads exactly two bytes starting at the given offset (standard macro semantics).
num_bootstrap_methods (line 9) is a 16-bit quantity, bounding the loop at 65535 iterations.
limitations: Line 9 reads buffer[6..7] with no in-fragment check that 8 <= sz; a confirmed CWE-125 read requires the unshown r_bin_java_default_attr_new to return non-NULL on an input with sz < 8, and any caller-side size invariant is outside the fragment.
The magnitude and type of bsm->size (line 19) are produced inside the unshown r_bin_java_bootstrap_method_new; the advance cannot be fully quantified, but no unguarded sink consumes it.
r_list_newf (line 11) is not NULL-checked before r_list_append (line 20); NULL-on-allocation-failure semantics are framework-internal and not shown.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of ReadMATImageV4: every input-derived magnitude is constrained by a visible protective statement before reaching a sink (ldblk <= 9999 at L55, imagf in {0,1} at L81, nameLen <= 0xFFFF at L83, non-zero dimensions at L103, SetImageExtent status at L116, quantum_info NULL check at L121, count == -1 at L164/L191, q NULL check at L168). No shown capacity is exceeded and no demonstrated witness survives the guards; remaining concerns (quantum-buffer capacity unshown, short-read handling, ping seek, discarded SetQuantum* statuses) are limitations/robustness, not confirmed vulnerabilities.

assumptions: HDR fields are fully assigned on both the LSB (L67-70) and MSB (L75-78) branches, so no uninitialized use occurs.
ReadBlobLSBLong/ReadBlobMSBLong return an unsigned 32-bit value, so the `ldblk < 0` term in L55 is dead and `ldblk <= 9999` bounds every Type digit to 0..9.
depth is restricted by the switch L123-149 to the set {64, 32, 16, 16, 8}, so depth/8 in {1,2,4,8}.
image->columns/image->rows are admitted only when both are non-zero (L103) and only after SetImageExtent succeeds (L115-117).
limitations: The capacity of the `pixels` buffer returned by GetQuantumPixels (L157) is configured inside unshown quantum.c (SetQuantumFormat/SetQuantumDepth/GetQuantumPixels), so the equality between `depth/8*image->columns` (L163/L190) and the buffer size cannot be fully re-derived from the fragment; an overflow of that buffer is therefore a limitation, not a confirmed finding.
`count == -1` (L164/L191) does not detect short reads (0..length-1); partially stale/uninitialized row data may be converted, which is a robustness concern without a shown security-relevant consumer.
The statuses of SetQuantumFormat/SetQuantumDepth/SetQuantumEndian (L153-155) are overwritten/discarded; a failure inside those unshown calls is not confirmed by a shown NULL producer.

The ping-mode seek `SeekBlob(image, HDR.nCols*ldblk, SEEK_CUR)` (L109) uses ldblk == the M digit (0/1) after extraction, which is a functional quirk of ping parsing with no shown memory-safety impact.
`(int) image->columns` at L173 is a truncation concern only for widths SetImageExtent would already have rejected, so it is not reachable with a failing value.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation in set_fflags_platform is reachable with a failing value: the open result is checked (L42-43, myfd < 0 -> return) before any ioctl, the GETFLAGS result is checked (L52-59) before oldflags is consumed at L62, both SETFLAGS results are checked (L63-70, L78-85), the fallback is gated to errno == EPERM (L71-72), ret is initialized at L49, and cleanup closes only self-opened fds (L93-94). The fragment is the fixed counterpart.

assumptions: ioctl(FS_IOC_GETFLAGS/FS_IOC_SETFLAGS) that return >= 0 are assumed to have written/read oldflags/newflags per the standard kernel ioctl contract; the macro transfer widths are system-header properties not visible in the fragment.
The mode check at L33-34 admits only regular files and directories, so set/clear are never applied to other file types.
ret is initialized at L49 before any success path can return it.
limitations: If Linux FS_IOC_GETFLAGS/FS_IOC_SETFLAGS transfer sizeof(long) into the int objects declared at L6, a 4-byte stack overwrite would occur on LP64; the transfer width is not shown in the fragment and the declarations are identical in both counterpart versions, so this cannot be confirmed or used as the discriminating fix.

The assignment at L62 can truncate the unsigned long set/clear into int newflags, but no in-fragment consumer demonstrably fails on the truncated value and no producer of an out-of-range bit pattern is shown.

The EPERM fallback at L75-85 can report ARCHIVE_OK when only a no-op subset was applied (e.g., an unprivileged attempt to clear a root-only flag); this is a robustness/status nuance of the intended partial-set retry, depends on unshown caller and kernel semantics, and is not one of the listed one-statement fix forms.
NULL a or name, and caller-supplied fd values other than those handled by L37/L42/L93, depend on unshown callers and are not confirmable from the fragment.
__archive_ensure_cloexec_flag at L40 may receive -1 when open fails (checked afterward at L42); fcntl on -1 fails benignly with EBADF and has no security impact.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched counterpart of __tipc_sendmsg. ua is either validated by tipc_uaddr_valid (lines 20-21) or replaced by the non-NULL &tsk->peer fallback (lines 38-43), atype is initialized on every path before any read (lines 22, 42), skaddr is fully determined before use (lines 61-66), dlen is capped at line 16-17, and every security-relevant return status (lines 63-64, 74-75, 96-97, 98-100, 106-110) is checked. No demonstrated failing value reaches a dangerous sink.

assumptions: m->msg_name may be NULL (the fragment explicitly tests it at lines 19 and 27/38), and a non-NULL m->msg_name points into the kernel-copied address buffer whose length m->msg_namelen is validated by the shown gate at line 20-21.
tipc_uaddr_valid(ua, m->msg_namelen) is the shown input-validation gate: its name implies it rejects invalid/undersized TIPC addresses, and all user-ua field reads are gated on it.
tipc_nametbl_lookup_anycast fills skaddr on success; the fragment returns -EHOSTUNREACH on the failure branch (lines 63-64), so only a successfully filled skaddr reaches lines 72-79.
ua = (struct tipc_uaddr *)&tsk->peer (line 39) points into the containing tipc_sock object, so the cast cannot escape the object and is never NULL.
tipc_node_get_mtu returns a positive MTU and tipc_msg_build returns the built length or a negative error, consistent with the fragment's rc != dlen check (lines 95-97).
limitations: Bodies of unshown callees (tipc_uaddr_valid, tipc_msg_build, tipc_node_get_mtu, tipc_nametbl_lookup_anycast, tipc_sendmcast, tipc_send_group_*) were not audited; however, no in-fragment numeric derivation or pointer value demonstrates a failing argument reaching them.

The 'uninitialized atype' candidate is fix-eliminated: the fragment contains both initializations (line 22 for the user-ua path, line 42 for the NULL-ua path), and every read of atype (lines 29-33, 52, 58) is dominated by one of them.
The reuse of timeout (line 115: msecs_to_jiffies on a value already in jiffies) is a timing/robustness oddity with no demonstrated security consequence.
A zero-length dlen with an empty pkts queue reaching the trace at line 104 is a robustness consideration only; no security impact is shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Fixed counterpart: the home-replaced heap copy p is never returned (line 20 assigns match = name, not p), so vim_free(p) at line 21 cannot cause a use-after-free at line 25; the NULL-producing home_replace_save result is guarded by 'p != NULL' short-circuit at line 19, and name derefs are guarded by line 9.

assumptions: rmp is a non-NULL parameter: no shown statement in the fragment can produce NULL for it (plain parameter, per rules).
vim_free tolerates NULL, so freeing p when home_replace_save failed (line 18 -> line 21) is safe.
line 6 initializes match to NULL, so the name==NULL path (line 9 else) returns NULL without dereferencing anything.
p_fic is a read-only global ('fileignorecase'); only its truthiness is consumed at line 12.
limitations: A NULL rmp->regprog reaching the first vim_regexec at line 13 would require an unshown caller; no NULL producer for regprog exists inside the fragment, so this is unconfirmable and not a finding.

The vulnerability class this fragment is fixed against is the use-after-free of the home-replaced copy; the neutralizing statement (line 20, match = name instead of the freed match = p) is present, so no CWE-416 witness exists here.
The semantic choice of returning the original name rather than the '~'-replaced string (line 20) has no security consequence unless a shown consumer relied on it; no such consumer is shown.
name's unchecked length is not a finding because no size/capacity sink in the fragment consumes it.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded/fixed form: the geometry boundary check at lines 98-99 (admitted set offset_x+width <= gif->width and offset_y+height <= gif->height) bounds every frame-buffer write in both the decode path (line 283) and the clear path (lines 307-313) to the gif->width x gif->height image whose capacity is evidenced by the memsets at lines 197 and 232, while the gif_bytes minimum checks (49, 67, 117, 150, 177), the frame range check (30), the NULL checks on bitmap_get_buffer results (164, 241), and the LZW status checks (253, 289) cover their respective sinks. Suspected OOB reads on gif->frames[] and the colour tables are not confirmable because the fragment never declares those allocations, and the LZW stack semantics are outside the fragment.

assumptions: The frame image returned by bitmap_get_buffer has at least gif->width * gif->height unsigned-int capacity; this is the only in-fragment capacity evidence, via the memsets at lines 197 and 232 that write exactly gif->width*gif->height*sizeof(int) bytes.
The frame-range guard at line 30 (frame > gif->frame_count_partial) admits only frame in [0, frame_count_partial]; the actual allocation size of gif->frames[] is not shown.
gif_interlaced_line(height, y) returns a scanline in [0, height-1] per GIF interlace semantics, so decode_y at line 260 stays within [offset_y, offset_y+height-1].
offset_x, offset_y, width, height are 16-bit fields assembled at lines 90-93, so the unsigned sums at lines 98-99, 264, and 305 cannot wrap 32-bit arithmetic.
limitations: gif->frames[frame].display is dereferenced at line 25 before the frame-range check at line 30, and gif->frames[frame].frame_pointer at line 41 follows that check; a failing OOB witness requires the frames[] allocation size, which is not declared in the fragment, so this candidate is unconfirmable.

colour_table[colour] at line 283 uses colour in [0,255] (unsigned char from line 279) while only colour_table_size in [2,256] entries are populated at lines 123-140; whether colour >= colour_table_size reads past the allocation is not derivable because gif->local_colour_table / gif->global_colour_table sizes are not declared, and LZW output bounds live in the unshown lzw.c.

burst_bytes = (stack_pos - stack_base) at line 272 converts a signed difference to unsigned; a negative delta would underflow the stack, but stack_pos >= stack_base is an unshown lzw.c invariant with no in-fragment producer of the negative state.
gif_data[0] (LZW minimum code size) at line 252 is not validated to [2,8]; all consequences are inside the unshown LZW implementation.

Early returns at lines 165 and 242 (GIF_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY) and at 254/294 skip the buffer-position restore and exit-path bitmap callbacks; this is a robustness/state concern with no shown security consumer.

verdict.summary: The allocation-failure cleanup path in _gdContributionsAlloc decrements the unsigned loop counter u into the wrap region and then tests while (u >= 0), which is always true for unsigned int. Entering the failure branch with u == 0 (e.g., line_length=1 and windows_size >= 2^29, admitted by the unconstrained unsigned int parameter and setting overflow_error at line 24) wraps u to UINT_MAX, so line 31 reads res->ContribRow[UINT_MAX].Weights out of bounds relative to the line_length-element allocation at line 17 (CWE-125) and the loop at lines 30-33 never terminates (CWE-835), making the intended return NULL at line 34 unreachable. No protective statement bounds u or checks u == 0 before the decrement.

evidence.reason: Capacity: res->ContribRow is allocated at line 17 with exactly line_length elements (line_length passes the line 13 overflow check and is at least 1). With line_length=1 and windows_size=2^29 (unconstrained unsigned int parameter; line 23 overflow2 returns nonzero, overflow_error=1 at line 24), line 28 admits the failure branch; line 29 decrements unsigned u from 0 to UINT_MAX; the guard at line 30 (while (u >= 0)) admits every unsigned value including UINT_MAX, so line 31 reads ContribRow[UINT_MAX].Weights — out of bounds for any line_length <= UINT_MAX — then line 32 wraps again and the loop never exits, so line 34 is unreachable. The absent fix is an equality/bound guard (u == 0) before the decrement at line 29 or a cleanup loop bounded to [0, line_length-1]. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read; secondary CWE-835 non-termination (denial of service, garbage-pointer free).

assumptions: u is declared unsigned int at line 3, so u-- from 0 wraps to UINT_MAX and u >= 0 at line 30 is always true (standard C semantics).
overflow2(a, b) returns nonzero iff a*b overflows the internal width (name-implied semantics); with sizeof(double)=8, windows_size >= 2^29 makes line 23 true (2^29*8 == 2^32).
The line 17 allocation provides exactly line_length elements, so index UINT_MAX is out of bounds for every admissible line_length (line_length <= UINT_MAX).
limitations: The exact prototype/implementation of overflow2 is not shown in the fragment; the trigger threshold relies on its name-implied overflow semantics.
No caller is shown, so the concrete attacker path (e.g., image-dimension-derived windows_size) is outside the fragment; the witness uses only the fragment's unconstrained parameter domain.
The gdMalloc-NULL trigger (line 7/17/26) depends on allocator/OS behavior and is not required for the deterministic overflow trigger at line 23.

verdict.summary: No confirmed security-relevant failure inside the fragment. All reads of sp are bounded by the NUL terminator the fragment itself handles (case '\0' at line 17 with len=1, NUL-aware len at lines 33 and 47, and the octal loop condition isdigit(UChar(*sp)) at line 26 which admits only ASCII digits and excludes NUL). The octal loop wraps via UChar (line 27) and feeds only bounded printable output (lines 50-62); its unbounded returned len and the '^'-at-end-of-string len=2 are consumed only by unshown callers, so no in-fragment sink can fail.

assumptions: sp points into a NUL-terminated string: the fragment itself compares *sp to '\0' (lines 17, 33, 47, 54) and terminates the octal loop on isdigit('\0')==0 (line 26), so the invariant is visible in-fragment.
UChar(x) is an unsigned-char cast applied to every read (lines 14, 18, 26-27, 32, 38, 46), keeping c in 0..255.
isdigit/isgraph are called with values representable as unsigned char (UChar results), so their behavior is defined.
save_string/save_char append to a managed (growable) buffer as their names imply; their capacity and failure mode are not shown in the fragment.
limitations: The octal-escape loop (lines 26-29) accepts digits '8' and '9' via isdigit (line 26) as if octal and has no cap on the number of digits, so the returned len (line 63) can be arbitrarily large; a caller that advances its input pointer by len could over-read, but that consumer is unshown and no in-fragment sink sizes an index/pointer/array by len -> CWE-125 not confirmable.
For input "^\0" (lines 37-44), the branch returns len=2 with c=0, so an unshown caller advancing by 2 would pass the NUL; the advance happens outside the fragment.
dp buffer capacity and save_string/save_char NULL/overflow behavior are not shown; heap overflow or NULL dereference there is not derivable from the fragment.

sp == NULL would fault at line 7, and an unterminated buffer would overrun at line 26, but no shown statement can produce either value (plain parameter; NUL-termination is the fragment's own invariant) -> CWE-476/125 not confirmable.

verdict.summary: The write path is bounded: line 17 rejects words >= PXA3XX_GCU_BATCH_WORDS, so the copy_from_user size at line 37 and the end-command write at line 49 stay within the batch buffer (last word reserved), and the negative-words truncation path cannot reach the indexed sink because line 38 catches the failed copy and returns -EFAULT.

assumptions: PXA3XX_GCU_BATCH_WORDS is a positive compile-time constant, and each batch buffer holds BATCH_WORDS words with the last word reserved for the end command, as encoded by the line 16 comment and the line 17 guard boundary.
to_pxa3xx_gcu_priv(file) yields a valid priv (standard container_of).
copy_from_user has standard usercopy semantics: a size that fails access_ok/range checks returns a nonzero uncopied count and leaves the destination intact.
limitations: The allocation size of buffer->ptr is not declared in this fragment; the in-bounds verdict for index BATCH_WORDS-1 depends on the (unshown) batch allocation holding at least BATCH_WORDS words.

If pxa3xx_gcu_wait_free could return 0 while priv->free is still NULL, line 32 would NULL-dereference; the callee's behavior is outside the fragment, so no in-fragment NULL producer exists and this is demoted.

The int narrowing at line 9 (count/4) can yield negative words for gigantic counts, but those paths fail copy_from_user and exit at line 43 before reaching the line 49 sink; treated as robustness, not a finding.
num_words counter at line 14 could be skewed by wrapped words values; it is statistics-only with no security consumer shown.

verdict.summary: In lprn_is_black, y0 is computed at line 11 as (r + h - bh) % maxY with no clamp for a negative dividend. When r + h < bh, C's truncating modulo yields a negative y0, which flows into the ImageBuf index at line 13, forming a pointer before the buffer; the p[x] read at line 15 is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: p is formed at line 13 as &lprn->ImageBuf[(y0 + y) * bpl + bx * lprn->nBw]. y0 comes from line 11, (r + h - bh) % maxY, where r and h are unconstrained int parameters (full domain): the witness r=0, h=1, bh=16, maxY=16 (line 9 with BlockLine=nBh=16) gives dividend -15, and C99 truncating modulo yields y0 = -15. Loop guard line 12 admits y=0, so the index is -15*bpl + bx*nBw < 0 for bpl >= 1, placing p before lprn->ImageBuf; the guard at line 14 admits x=0 and line 15 reads p[0] out of bounds (CWE-125). No protective clamp such as 'if (y0 < 0) y0 = 0;' exists between line 11 and the sink; the loop guards only bound y and x and do not exclude this witness.

assumptions: lprn->ImageBuf (line 13) is a byte array whose valid index range starts at 0; a negative byte offset is out of bounds for any capacity, so no size magnitude is assumed.
bpl = gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line(pdev) (line 6) is non-negative and at least 1 for an active raster, making the line 13 index negative when y0 is negative.
maxY (line 9) is positive and a multiple of nBh when BlockLine >= nBh >= 1, so the modulo at line 11 is defined and can return negative residues.
limitations: Division-by-zero at line 9 (nBh == 0) and modulo-by-zero at line 11 (maxY == 0 when BlockLine < nBh) cannot be confirmed because no in-fragment validation or producer establishes those field values.
An upper-bound OOB read past the end of lprn->ImageBuf cannot be confirmed because the buffer capacity is not declared in the fragment.
Caller provenance of r, h, and bx is not shown; the analysis relies on their unconstrained int residual ranges per Phase 1.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched counterpart: every in-fragment memory operation is covered by a visible protective statement. FSCTL_SET_SPARSE guards in_data[0] with in_len >= 1 (L21); FSCTL_GET_SHADOW_COPY_DATA validates max_out_len (L96), rejects undersized replies (L137), and zero-initializes the reply buffer (L144); FSCTL_FIND_FILES_BY_SID bounds sid_len (L198, L203); FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES validates in_len/max_out_len and rejects 64-bit wraparound (L257, L263, L272). No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: talloc_array/talloc_zero_array success is verified immediately after each allocation (L50-52, L106-110, L144-148, L284-288).
fsp and fsp->conn/fsp->fsp_name are framework-provided non-NULL state with no NULL producer in the fragment.
SMB_VFS_GET_SHADOW_COPY_DATA fills shadow_data->num_volumes/labels without any shown bound on num_volumes.
limitations: FSCTL_GET_SHADOW_COPY_DATA: labels_data_count (uint32, L128-129) and *out_len (L134) could wrap if num_volumes >= 2^32/(2*sizeof(SHADOW_COPY_LABEL)); no shown producer can demonstrably yield such a value, so the heap-overflow witness rests on an unshown magnitude (recorded here, not a finding).

FSCTL_CREATE_OR_GET_OBJECT_ID: bytes 48..63 of the 64-byte talloc_array buffer (L49, L55-57) are uninitialized, and *out_len can be 64 (L47); whether those bytes are disclosed depends on an unshown reply path transmitting all *out_len bytes and on heap content, so it is not confirmable from the fragment.

FSCTL_FIND_FILES_BY_SID: sid_to_uid failure sets uid = -1 and the function still returns NT_STATUS_OK (L213-218, L242), but no in-fragment consumer of uid performs a security decision, so there is no reachable security consequence in the shown code.

verdict.summary: The BYE reason copy is fully bounded: line 8 (if (size > 8)) guarantees size >= 9 so the length-byte read at offset 8 and the size-9 subtraction are valid, line 14 caps reason.slen at sizeof(sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_), and line 16 additionally caps it at size-9 (the bytes actually remaining after offset 9), so the memcpy at lines 18-19 can neither over-read the packet nor over-write the destination buffer. This is the fixed counterpart; the protective statements are present.

assumptions: pj_size_t is an unsigned size type, so line 8's size > 8 guarantees size - 9 >= 0 and that offsets 8 and 9 are inside the size-byte packet.
The destination buffer capacity is exactly sizeof(sess->stat.peer_sdes_buf_), the same expression used as the cap at line 14.

verdict.summary: virtbt_rx_handle reads *((__u8 *)skb->data) at line 5 and calls skb_pull(skb, 1) at line 6 with no check on skb->len; an empty virtio RX buffer (skb->len == 0) reaches the read, causing a 1-byte out-of-bounds read whose value is used as the HCI packet type, and an unsigned underflow of skb->len before the skb is handed to hci_recv_frame at line 14.

evidence.reason: skb is entry-point input from the virtio RX queue and the fragment imposes no constraint on skb->len (no conditional exists between entry at line 1 and this read), so its residual range is 0..UINT_MAX. The payload capacity of skb->data is skb->len; the admitted degenerate witness skb->len == 0 reaches this 1-byte read at offset 0, exceeding that capacity (CWE-125 OOB read). The same witness also makes skb_pull(skb, 1) at line 6 underflow skb->len before the skb is consumed by hci_recv_frame at line 14. The absent fix statement is an input/bound check such as 'if (skb->len < 1) { kfree_skb(skb); return; }' placed before line 5.

assumptions: skb arrives from the virtio RX vq as externally controlled packet data, so skb->len is attacker-controllable with no shown minimum.
The readable payload region addressed by skb->data has exactly skb->len bytes (kernel sk_buff invariant); this capacity is not literally declared in the fragment.
vbt->hdev is non-NULL (no NULL producer shown in the fragment).
limitations: The downstream effect of the skb_pull(skb, 1) length underflow inside hci_recv_frame is not shown, so any memory-corruption escalation beyond the line-5 OOB read is unconfirmed.
The missing 'default:' case leaks the skb for unrecognized pkt_type values (resource leak) but no security consequence is confirmed within a single invocation.
If an unshown caller guaranteed skb->len >= 1 the read would be safe; no such invariant is derivable from the shown fragment.

Line 67's unsigned subtraction can wrap to a huge mtu when be32_to_cpu(info) < offset, and line 68 clamps only the low side; this is a robustness/upper-clamp concern with no shown security-relevant consequence, not a confirmed vulnerability.

verdict.summary: snd_pcm_oss_sync derives width from user-controlled OSS format state (runtime->oss.format via snd_pcm_oss_format_from / snd_pcm_format_physical_width) and divides by it at lines 30 and 44 without validating that the width is positive/non-zero. evidence.reason: The divisor width at line 30 is derived solely from the unconstrained entry-point value runtime->oss.format (line 24 -> line 25) with no in-fragment bound check; guards at lines 12, 14, 17, 20 and 26 (buffer_used > 0) admit a path with width == 0, so the unsigned division at this sink performs a divide-by-zero (kernel SIGFPE/oops, DoS). The absent protective statement is a width validation such as 'if (width <= 0) goto unlock;' inserted between line 25 and line 26, which the Fix-Scan confirms is missing; primary CWE-369 at the sink.

The same unvalidated, user-derived width from lines 24-25 is used as the divisor here on the else-if path: guards line 26 (buffer_used == 0) and line 37 (period_ptr > 0) admit width == 0, so line 44's 'size * 8 / width' performs a divide-by-zero fed as the sample count to snd_pcm_format_set_silence (kernel SIGFPE/oops, DoS). No width bound check exists between line 25 and this sink; the absent fix 'if (width <= 0) goto unlock;' would exclude the witness; primary CWE-369 at the sink.

assumptions: runtime->oss.format, oss.period_bytes, oss.buffer_used, oss.period_ptr and runtime->period_size are user-settable OSS runtime state (entry-point provenance) and receive no constraint anywhere in the shown fragment.
The playback block only runs when pcm_oss_file->streams[SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_PLAYBACK] is non-NULL (line 12), and the capture block only when streams[SNDRV_PCM_STREAM_CAPTURE] is non-NULL (line 82).
All return-status checks shown (lines 17, 20, 35, 46, 64, 74, 84, 88) are correct; no security-relevant status is mishandled.
limitations: Producing exactly width == 0 depends on the unshown return-value distribution of snd_pcm_format_physical_width: under its standard semantics invalid formats yield a negative int, which stored into unsigned long width becomes a huge divisor making the division yield 0 (harmless); the zero-valued witness is therefore the fragile link in the chain (reflected in the 0.74 confidence).

An out-of-bounds write inside snd_pcm_format_set_silence (lines 31-33, 42-44) is not confirmable: the capacity of runtime->oss.buffer and the invariant buffer_used <= period_bytes / period_ptr <= period_bytes are not declared or derived in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Device-controlled fw.len (u16, residual 1..0xFFFE after the 0xFFFF retry guard at L24/L29) is used unvalidated as the download length: (fw.len + sizeof(u32) - sizeof(u8)) / sizeof(u32) dwords, up to 16384 dwords (~64 KB), are written into the fixed-size self->rpc member (L34-L40: &self->rpc), an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787). The sibling sw.len value (0..0xFFFF) is passed unvalidated to hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call at L25, causing a matching out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The upstream fix (commit b922f622592a) adds exactly the missing checks 'if (fw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))' and 'if (sw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))', which are absent from this fragment.

evidence.snippet:
err =
			hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords(self,
						      self->rpc_addr,
						      (u32 *)(void *)
						      &self->rpc,
						      (fw.len + sizeof(u32) -
						       sizeof(u8)) /

evidence.reason: Sink B: fw.len originates from device MMIO (u16, via aq_hw_read_reg at L9 and the rpc_state_get poll at L13-L16). Guards in order admit it: L17/L21 only require err == 0; L24 excludes exactly fw.len == 0xFFFF; L29 (loop exit) excludes only 0xFFFF; L31 admits non-NULL rpc; L32 (if (fw.len)) admits 1..0xFFFE. No upper-bound check exists, so (fw.len+3)/4 dwords — up to (0xFFFE+3)/4 = 16384 dwords = 65536 bytes — are written into the fixed-size self->rpc member (&self->rpc at L37), exceeding its capacity sizeof(self->rpc) (the bound the upstream fix compares against). This is an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787). The absent protective statement is 'if (fw.len > sizeof(self->rpc)) { err = -EINVAL; goto err_exit; }' before this call, which is precisely what upstream commit b922f622592af76b57cbc566eaeccda0b31a3496 adds.

Sink A: sw.len is a u16 field read from the device control register at L9 with no constraint anywhere in the fragment (residual 0..0xFFFF). When fw.len == 0xFFFF (admitted by L24), sw.len is passed to hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call, whose size argument is transformed inside the callee to (sw.len+3)/4 dwords read from &self->rpc — up to 16384 dwords (~64 KB) from a fixed-size struct member, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) confirmed by the KASAN report in the fixing commit. The absent protective statement is 'if (sw.len > sizeof(self->rpc)) { err = -EINVAL; goto err_exit; }' before the call, added by upstream commit b922f622592a.

assumptions: fw.len and sw.len are u16 fields of struct aq_hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_tid_s (union { u32 val; struct { u16 tid; u16 len; }; }), read directly from device MMIO HW_ATL_RPC_CONTROL_ADR — device/firmware-controlled entry-point data.

self->rpc is a fixed-size struct member (struct hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc: u32 msg_id plus a small packed union of message structs); the upstream fix's bound sizeof(self->rpc) is the capacity, and it is far below the in-fragment maximum write of 65536 bytes.

hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords(self, addr, p, cnt) decodes cnt dwords from the device into buffer p (write of 4*cnt bytes), and hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call forwards its rpc_size as the upload length read from &self->rpc.
Downstream callers can pass a non-NULL rpc for response fetches (the L31 branch exists precisely for that mode).

The out-of-bounds read through hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call (L25) depends on the unshown callee body (hw_atl_write_fwcfg_dwords reading (sw.len+3)/4 dwords); it is corroborated by the fixing commit's own sw.len sanity check and KASAN trace, but is secondary to the fully visible write sink.

For sink B, reachability requires at least one caller passing rpc != NULL; no call site is shown in the fragment (the NULL-rpc init path skips the download block). The sink is nonetheless reached on the function's response-fetch usage, which the fix commit targets.

verdict.summary: No in-fragment sink or demonstrated failure: the only data forwarded are `p = current` (line 3) and `int user_tick` (line 1); no shown statement can produce a NULL pointer, an out-of-range index/size, or any failing value, and the guarded calls at lines 10-11 and 14-15 pass no fragment-supplied arguments.

verdict.summary: get_complex_object leaks heap allocations on the second-string failure paths: when the n2 length read fails, the overflow guard trips, or the s2/s1 mallocs fail, the bare 'return NULL;' statements at lines 39, 23, and 43 return without freeing ret (line 7) and s1 (line 21). A truncated .pyc (e.g. magic<=62061, bytes 0x02 'A' 'B' then EOF) drives get_ut8 to set error=true, is admitted by every prior guard (8, 17, 22, 26, 38), and reaches line 39 with both allocations still live.

evidence.reason: Leak sink at line 39: on the n2 failure path, guard at line 38 admits error==true (get_ut8 at line 34 sets error on EOF; buffer is entry-point .pyc data) and the overflow value 0xFFFFFFFF is also excluded here without cleanup. The return at line 39 abandons ret (allocated, RZ_NEW0, line 7) and s1 (allocated, malloc(n1+1), line 21), both still live. No protective statement on this path frees them; the absent fix is RZ_FREE(s1); RZ_FREE(ret); before this return. Confirmed witness: magic_int&0xffff<=62061, buffer bytes 0x02 'A' 'B' then EOF, passing guards at lines 8, 17, 22, 26 in order. Primary CWE-401: memory not released before last reference is dropped on an attacker-triggerable error path.

Leak sink at line 23: when malloc at line 21 returns NULL, guard line 22 admits s1==NULL and this return abandons ret (line 7). Absent fix: RZ_FREE(ret); before returning. Distinct from the primary sink; trigger depends on allocator failure (environment condition) rather than an attacker value. CWE-401.

Leak sink at line 43: when malloc at line 41 returns NULL, guard line 42 admits s2==NULL and this return abandons ret (line 7) and s1 (line 21), both still live. Absent fix: RZ_FREE(s1); RZ_FREE(ret); before returning. Trigger depends on allocator failure. CWE-401.

assumptions: UT32_ADD_OVFCHK(a, b) is the standard radare2 overflow macro; with b=1 it admits n in [0, 0xFFFFFFFE] and excludes n==0xFFFFFFFF, so malloc(n+1) sizes at lines 21 and 41 never wrap (if checks at lines 17 and 38 are the protective statements for the integer-overflow failure set).
get_ut8/get_st32 read from buffer and set *error on short read/EOF; the fragment's own pattern of checking error after every get_* call (lines 17, 38) confirms this contract.
buffer carries attacker-controlled .pyc file contents (entry-point input); RZ_NEW0 at line 7 allocates and zero-initializes a pyc_object and is NULL-checked at line 8.
s1[n1] (line 31) and s2[n2] (line 52) are safely in-bounds because the malloc capacity is n+1 and the exact-read checks at lines 26/46 bound n by the bytes actually read.
limitations: The leak's denial-of-service impact (memory exhaustion) requires repeated parsing of malformed files in a long-lived process by callers not shown here; the per-call leaked amount is bounded by the n1 bytes already read, so there is no in-fragment amplification. This is why severity is low and no CWE-400 secondary is asserted.

The line 23 and line 43 leaks depend on the allocator failing, which is a system condition rather than an attacker-controlled value; they are reported as confirmed but lower-weight secondary leak sinks.

No memory-safety (CWE-787/125/476/416), injection, crypto/entropy, file/access-control, authz, or status-handling flaw was found: the overflow checks at lines 17/38 exclude the only wrap-inducing length values, all reads are exactly length-checked, and the format string at line 55 is a literal.
The error/'overflow' guard branches at lines 17 and 38 are fail-closed for lengths; the only defect is that the line 38 branch does not release the already-allocated objects before returning.

assumptions: this_cpu_add(net_rand_state.s1, ...) writes a single fixed-size machine word at net_rand_state plus the offset of member s1 (offset 0), so the write width cannot vary with any input (name-implied semantics; no pointer arithmetic shown).

The exact per-CPU object size of net_rand_state and the resolved address semantics of this_cpu_add are not shown in the fragment; only the fixed-width, fixed-offset nature of the write is relied on.

Behavior inside unshown callees (account_process_tick, run_local_timers, rcu_sched_clock_irq, scheduler_tick, run_posix_cpu_timers) is out of scope; no in-fragment argument to them exceeds a shown bound.

verdict.summary: add_slot_store copies up to MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1 bytes into drc_name (line 11) without initializing a terminator, then scans the unterminated buffer with strchr (line 13); with an all-'a' input of length MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1 the scan reads past the stack array, and the subsequent *end = '\0' (line 16) can write out of bounds. The fix `drc_name[nbytes] = '\0';` before strchr (or memchr bounded by nbytes) is absent.

evidence.reason: strchr (line 13) scans drc_name, whose capacity is declared at line 4 (`char drc_name[MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN];`), but the guard at lines 8-9 only caps nbytes to [0, MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1] and line 11 copies the entry-point buf without writing any terminator; the only buffer initialization, `*end = '\0'` at line 16, executes after the scan. For the admitted witness nbytes = MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1 with all-admitted 'a' bytes (no '\n'/'\0' in the copied data, tail bytes [MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1..] uninitialized), strchr's scan loop reads past index MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1, an out-of-bounds stack read (CWE-125). The absent protective statement is `drc_name[nbytes] = '\0';` before line 13 (or replacing strchr with memchr(drc_name, '\n', nbytes)); without it, an in-bounds termination of the scan is never guaranteed.

assumptions: MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN is a positive compile-time constant (a name-length macro), making `drc_name[nbytes]` with nbytes = MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1 a valid index.
buf/nbytes are entry-point input (sysfs store payload), so buf contents are attacker-controlled up to the shown guard at lines 8-9.
dlpar_add_slot's return (line 18) is properly checked at lines 19-20, so no status-handling flaw is present.
limitations: The exact extent of the over-read (how many bytes past drc_name) depends on indeterminate stack contents, so the boundary crossing is demonstrated as a range witness, not an exact index.

The out-of-bounds write at line 16 (`*end = '\0'` via a non-NULL OOB end pointer, CWE-787) requires strchr to encounter a '\n' beyond the object; that byte is not attacker-controlled and is not deterministically present, so it is not independently confirmed as a separate finding.
The nbytes = 0 path (fully uninitialized buffer scanned by strchr) is also unsafe but was not used as the primary witness.
The sysfs attribute's required write permissions are outside the fragment and were not factored into severity.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of extract_arg: the backward '0x' scan at line 38 carries the added bound check `addr >= esil_buf + 1`, which stops the loop at the buffer start so every addr[0]/addr[1] read stays inside the strdup'd buffer (guaranteed >= 6 bytes by the non-NULL strstr of the >=5-char pattern at lines 30-31). A `SIZE_MAX` index passed to `r_type_func_args_type` at line 116 (loop wrap at line 115 when `stack_rev` and `to == 0`) cannot be confirmed as OOB: the callee's internal bounds are not shown and the in-fragment `if (!tp) break;` at lines 117-119 implies out-of-range lookups return NULL.
`R_ABS` on the minimum `st64` value at lines 14/67 is signed-overflow UB, but no in-range failure is shown: the magnitude guards at lines 90 and 156 reject the resulting values.
Whether callers can pass NULL `sign` (dereferenced at lines 13 and 81) or an unbounded/empty `reg` is not derivable from the fragment; no shown producer establishes such values.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The guard at line 2 establishes bf and bf->o as non-NULL, but the fragment contains no NULL producer for qo = bf->o->bin_obj, so the qo->fixups dereference at line 4 cannot be shown to fail from the shown statements alone.

verdict.summary: The fragment is an inert allocation wrapper: it forwards an unsigned long size unmodified to kvmalloc and returns the result. verdict.summary: Use-after-free: `mixer` is deleted at line 4 when `mixer != NULL`, then dereferenced at line 8 (`mixer->isActive()` / `mixer->isDeviceRemoved(player)`) on every path where `player != NULL`, with no intervening check or reordering.

No statement between line 4 and line 8 re-validates `mixer`; the only guard on the path is the `player` check at line 6, which imposes no constraint on `mixer`. The absent fix is relocation of `if (mixer) delete mixer;` to after the player block (or a validity check recognizing the prior delete), confirming use-after-free with capacity/object lifetime established by line 3-4 and primary CWE-416.

assumptions: `mixer` and `player` may be non-NULL simultaneously; both line 3 and line 6 guards admit their non-NULL values and the fragment shows no correlation between them.
A non-NULL `delete` (line 4) ends the pointed-to object's lifetime, making subsequent dereference a use-after-free.
limitations: The `(mixer == NULL, player != NULL)` path would be a NULL dereference at the same sink, but the fragment contains no in-fragment NULL producer for `mixer`, so CWE-476 is not raised as a separate finding.

Member initialization (whether the destructor can run with both pointers non-NULL) occurs outside the fragment; the guards' independent checks are the only shown evidence, which is why confidence is 0.83 rather than higher.

verdict.summary: ip6gre_err dereferences the GRE header before the packet-length validation and computes the GRE key with an index that extends beyond the pskb_may_pull-verified window: `flags = p[0]` at line 10 executes before the only length gate (lines 22-23), and the line 28-29 key read `*(((__be32 *)p) + (grehlen / 4) - 1)` with p = skb->data + offset and grehlen = offset + 4 + extras reads up to offset bytes past the grehlen bytes guaranteed by line 22. Crafted short ICMPv6 error packets reaching this handler cause out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled entry-point inputs `offset` and the packet length reach this sink unconstrained: line 5 sets p = (__be16 *)(skb->data + offset) and no statement before line 10 bounds offset or skb->len. The only length guarantee in the fragment, `if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, grehlen)) return;` with grehlen = offset + 4 computed at lines 6/15/17, is evaluated at line 22, after this dereference, so it protects nothing on this path (use at line 10 precedes guard at line 22). Witness: offset = 8, skb->len = 8 passes the assignment statements at lines 3-9 and reads bytes [8,10), a 2-byte out-of-bounds read. The absent protective statement is a length check such as `if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, offset + 4)) return;` placed before line 10; primary mechanism is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

Line 22 guarantees only bytes [0, grehlen) of skb->data after pskb_may_pull(skb, grehlen). With the admitted witness offset = 8 and GRE_KEY set (line 14), grehlen = offset + 4 + 4 = 16 (lines 6, 15); flags with VERSION/ROUTING/CSUM clear pass guards at lines 11-16; line 22 admits skb->len = 16. p is reassigned to skb->data + offset at line 25, so index grehlen/4 - 1 = 3 makes the read span bytes [20,24), exceeding the [0,16) window by 8 bytes — an out-of-bounds read for every offset >= 4 because the index is anchored at p while grehlen counts bytes from data base. The absent fix is a header-relative index (e.g., (grehlen - offset)/4 - 1) or a larger pull; the confirmed mechanism is CWE-125.

assumptions: skb, offset, type, code, and info are entry-point network/ICMPv6-derived inputs; no in-fragment constraint bounds offset or skb->len.
pskb_may_pull(skb, grehlen) at line 22 is the fragment's only packet-length guarantee; after success, bytes [0, grehlen) of skb->data are valid linear data (standard name-implied semantics).
ip6gre_tunnel_lookup dereferences the daddr/saddr addresses it is given (standard name-implied semantics for a tunnel lookup).
limitations: skb->len is not literally declared in the fragment; the confirmations calibrate the failing reads against the fragment's own computed grehlen/may_pull window rather than a literal buffer-size declaration.

The daddr/saddr reads at line 27 occur inside the unshown callee and would also overrun the [0, grehlen) window on short packets with offset < 36; treated as a weaker secondary manifestation of the same length-validation gap.

The line 65-68 PKT_TOOBIG path (`mtu = be32_to_cpu(info) - offset`) can underflow to a huge unsigned value when info < offset, bypassing the line 66-67 IPV6_MIN_MTU clamp before the line 68 store; demoted to a robustness concern because no in-fragment security decision or memory-safety consumer uses the stored device MTU.

verdict.summary: seq_buf_alloc bounds the allocation size with the line-3 guard (size > MAX_RW_COUNT returns NULL) before kvmalloc at line 6, so no oversized-size witness can reach the allocation sink; the fragment is the fixed counterpart.

assumptions: kvmalloc returns a pointer to at least 'size' bytes on success and NULL on failure (standard allocator contract); a NULL return is not consumed inside the fragment.
MAX_RW_COUNT is a positive compile-time constant; the guard at line 3 establishes the admitted range [0, MAX_RW_COUNT] for the allocation path regardless of its literal value.
limitations: The numeric value of MAX_RW_COUNT is not displayed in the fragment, so the concrete cap magnitude is assumed rather than shown.
No call site is shown, so downstream use of the returned allocation (checking the NULL result, using the allocation size) cannot be analyzed; out of scope for this fragment.
kvmalloc internal behavior beyond NULL-on-failure is not shown and was not relied upon for any verdict.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_wait (upstream commit b922f622, 'atlantic: Fix OOB read and write in hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_wait'). Both device-controlled 16-bit lengths are bounded to sizeof(self->rpc) before use: sw.len is checked at line 25 before hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call (line 30) and fw.len is checked at line 38 before hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords (lines 43-50). No demonstrated failing value reaches either sink.

assumptions: sizeof(self->rpc) is the byte capacity of the destination object at &self->rpc, by the semantics of sizeof/address-of on the member expression used at lines 25, 38, and 47; the fragment itself therefore shows the guard bound equal to the destination capacity.

sw.tid/sw.len and fw.tid/fw.len are 16-bit decoded fields of the 32-bit register values read at lines 9 and 13-16; the comparsion fw.len == 0xFFFFU at line 24 and the sentinel loop at line 34 are consistent with a 16-bit len field, giving the unguarded domain [0, 0xFFFF].
limitations: The download count (fw.len + sizeof(u32) - sizeof(u8)) / sizeof(u32) rounds up to a whole dword; exact fit at the maximum admitted fw.len == sizeof(self->rpc) requires sizeof(self->rpc) to be a multiple of 4, which the fragment alone cannot prove (external header confirms the real object is 88 bytes, 4-aligned). A non-4-aligned size would create at most a 3-byte write past the object at the exact boundary value; this is not a demonstrated failure within the fragment and is superseded by the confirmed upstream fix.

The behavior of the hidden callees hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call and hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords is taken by name-implied semantics (upload/download of count dwords from/to the passed buffer); no callee behavior beyond that standard semantics is assumed.
A negative verdict itself (not vulnerability) rests on the two protective bounds checks at lines 25-29 and 38-42; any future caller-side guarantee is not relied upon.

A NULL goresc would be a limitation requiring an unshown caller contract, not a finding.

verdict.summary: udf_expand_file_adinicb writes out of bounds of the page-cache page because iinfo->i_lenAlloc (an on-disk, attacker-controlled __u32) is never bounded above by PAGE_SIZE: at line 33, PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc underflows to a huge size when i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE, and the memset starts past the page end; the same oversized i_lenAlloc is also copied into the page at lines 34-35.

evidence.reason: iinfo->i_lenAlloc is a __u32 whose only in-fragment constraint is L9 (if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)), admitting [1, 2^32-1] on this path; guards L27 and L30 impose no upper bound. With i_lenAlloc = 4097 (any value in [4097, 2^32-1]), PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc (L33, unsigned long arithmetic) wraps to 2^64-1 and the write begins at kaddr + 4097, past the PAGE_SIZE-capacity page obtained at L26/L31. No protective statement (bound check or saturated length) exists, so the absent fix is a check such as 'if (iinfo->i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE) return -EFSCORRUPTED;' before line 32; this is a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

The same unconstrained iinfo->i_lenAlloc (residual [1, 2^32-1] after L9; guards L27/L30 impose no bound) is used as the memcpy length into kaddr, whose capacity is the PAGE_SIZE page from L26/L31. For any i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE (e.g. 4097) the copy writes past the page, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) covered by the same absent upper-bound check as the line 32-33 sink.

assumptions: Page-cache pages returned by find_or_create_page (L26) have capacity PAGE_SIZE, and kmap_atomic (L31) maps exactly one page; PAGE_SIZE appears as the capacity constant at L33.

iinfo->i_lenAlloc, iinfo->i_lenEAttr and inode->i_size are loaded from the on-disk UDF inode (filesystem image), i.e., entry-point-derived attacker-controlled values; the fragment itself imposes no upper bound on them.
A freshly created page at index 0 is not PageUptodate, so the L30 branch containing the sinks is the normal path.
limitations: The magnitude producer for i_lenAlloc (the UDF inode loader reading the image) is not part of this fragment, so the witness is a range ([PAGE_SIZE+1, 2^32-1]) rather than a single value with a shown textual derivation; this caps confidence at 0.74.

Source-side out-of-bounds read at L34-35 (iinfo->i_data + i_lenEAttr) and the writable spans of L41-42 and L59 (iinfo->i_data destination) cannot be confirmed because i_data's capacity is declared outside the fragment.
Sink L59 additionally requires filemap_fdatawrite to fail (L54) and an unbounded inode->i_size; it was demoted for the same missing-capacity reason.
UDF inode data is normally read under i_data_sem; lock-ordering and concurrency are outside the shown fragment and unused for the verdict.

verdict.summary: Fixed counterpart: the buf accumulation loop (lines 35-38) is protected by the termcode-length guard at lines 12-13, which nulls 'end' when STRLEN(end) >= NUMBUFLEN, capping any persistent idx below NUMBUFLEN and resetting idx each iteration when end is NULL; PASTE_EX copy is guarded by ga_grow(gap, idx+1) == OK.

assumptions: buf capacity is NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES as declared at line 4.
mb_char2bytes writes at most MB_MAXBYTES bytes and returns the count written (name-implied standard semantics).
STRNCMP is strncmp-like and stops at the first NUL, so a persistent prefix match cannot advance idx past STRLEN(end) with non-NUL bytes.
The 'PE' termcode returned by find_termcode is NUL-terminated; its length is bounded below NUMBUFLEN by lines 12-13.
Appended bytes are non-NUL: line 29 breaks on c == NUL, and multibyte lead/trail bytes are nonzero for the encodings Vim uses.
ga_grow(gap, idx + 1) == OK at line 55 guarantees room for the idx-byte mch_memmove at lines 57-58.
limitations: No call sites are shown for mode/drop/gap, so their residual domains are only analyzed for in-fragment consequences.

The end[idx] read at line 41 would be an OOB read only if a multibyte char could contain a NUL byte at the exact boundary; that is not reachable under standard Vim multibyte encodings and was not confirmed, so it is demoted.
Behavior of unshown callees (put_on_cmdline, ins_char_bytes, AppendToRedobuffLit, mb_ptr2char) beyond their name-implied semantics was not analyzed.
In the vulnerable counterpart (without lines 12-13) an over-long termcode would allow unbounded idx growth and a heap/stack-buffer overflow; that counterpart is not the code shown here.

verdict.summary: This is the fixed counterpart of ins_bs. Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the ml_get_cursor()-1 reads at L210-211 and L248 are guarded by curwin->w_cursor.col > 0 at L209 and L247 respectively (excluding col==0/underflow); the ptr[len-1] truncation at L128 is guarded by len > 0 at L127 (excluding the empty line); cpc[MAX_MCO] at L14 matches utfc_ptr2char's MAX_MCO fill bound; and the do-while deletion loop cannot drive the cursor below column 0 because mincol is initialized at L179 and the loop bound at L352 requires col > mincol (mincol >= 0). Failure of the USB core to enforce endpoint-count consistency before probing (which would make the line 61-63 loop unsafe) is a framework invariant violated only outside the shown fragment, so no in-fragment witness exists.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled DXF group code 90 value is converted to int maxVertices (line 4) with no upper bound (line 5 admits up to INT_MAX). For maxVertices = 2^30, the size arithmetic 4*maxVertices at line 9 wraps a 32-bit int to 0, allocating a 0-element double array, and the init loop at lines 10-14 immediately writes vertices[0..3] out of bounds (heap OOB write). At line 9 the int expression 4*maxVertices wraps to 0, so vertices is a 0-element array (capacity declared at line 9). Loop line 10 admits i=0, and line 11 writes vertices[0] (and lines 12-14 vertices[1..3]) beyond the 0-capacity object: heap out-of-bounds write, CWE-787, enabled by the CWE-190 signed wrap at line 9. No upper-bound/input-validation check on maxVertices exists between the origin and the sink; the absent fix is a bound check such as maxVertices <= INT_MAX/4 before allocation.

assumptions: maxVertices, vertexIndex and groupCode are 32-bit signed ints: inferred from `maxVertices = toInt(groupValue)` (line 4) with toInt's standard int-returning atoi behavior, `for (int i=0; i<maxVertices; ++i)` (line 10), and signed `vertexIndex>=0` comparisons (lines 30, 33).
groupValue/groupCode are attacker-controlled DXF entity data (entry-point); toInt performs no clamping over the int domain.
vertices may initially be NULL; the fragment reallocates whenever the most recent groupCode==90 carried maxVertices>0 (lines 5-9).
limitations: The fragment does not show the member declarations; if maxVertices were wider than 32-bit int, the 2^30 witness degenerates to an oversized-allocation failure (bad_alloc/DoS) rather than a wrapped-capacity OOB.

The coordinate/bulge sinks (lines 31, 34) are protected by the increment cap (line 25) and write guards (lines 30, 33); the classic vertexIndex==maxVertices OOB is unreachable as shown and only coalesces with the same capacity-wrap scenario, so it is not a separate finding.
A NULL/dangling-vertices dereference at lines 31/34 without any groupCode==90 would require unshown caller state and is demoted to a limitation.

The only guard on the path, IS_ERR(lp->base_addr) at line 35, is evaluated after line 34 and cannot protect the call's NULL argument; the absent fix is an if (!res) { rc = -ENXIO; goto error; } check after line 33 mirroring lines 25-29.

netdev_priv(ndev) at line 20 is non-NULL because ndev passed the alloc_etherdev() check at lines 13-15.

lp->phy_node from of_parse_phandle() at line 62 is unchecked, but it is only consumed inside the unshown xemaclite_mdio_setup(); no dereference is demonstrated in this fragment.
The internal behavior of devm_ioremap_resource() on a NULL resource is not shown; the verdict relies on its name-implied semantics rather than a displayed callee body.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the protected/fixed form of cmdline_insert_reg: the cursor-position writes (L58/L60) are confined to [0, ccline.cmdlen] by the new_cmdpos >= 0 filter (L54) and the new_cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen clamp (L57-L58) after the new_cmdpos = -1 reset (L25), the paste sink is gated by c != ESC (L38) and aborted on error (L45), and no NULL producer exists for *gotesc (L47). limitations: Whether cmdline_paste (L40) is safe for every non-ESC character value c cannot be established from this fragment: the callee body and the command-buffer capacity are not shown, and no in-fragment numeric derivation produces an out-of-range index/size.

Downstream consumers of ccline.cmdpos are outside the fragment; only the value written here (clamped to [0, cmdlen]) is verifiable.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability: every write to src (lines 12, 24) is bounded by the null-terminator search (lines 8-9, 22); every write to dst (lines 15-16) lands at or before the position of dst's own terminating null under the layout the q/r offsets assume, and no dst capacity or NULL producer is declared or computed in the fragment, so an out-of-bounds verdict cannot be formed from the shown code. stat/mkdir/chmod statuses are checked (lines 14, 17, 19); no injection, crypto, or authz sink exists.

Out-of-bounds read/write on src would require src_prefix_len + 1 > strlen(src) or an unterminated src — a caller-provided degenerate value with no in-fragment producer; rejected as caller-dependent.

Duplicate-slash components are skipped (line 11), which can fail to create intermediate directories and can shorten the dst path passed to mkdir; this is a semantic/robustness concern with no memory-safety or security-decision impact shown.

errExit (lines 18, 20) aborts the process only on genuine filesystem failures — standard error handling, not an attacker-reachable finding.

verdict.summary: In the '-write' branch of CLINoImageOperator, arg1 is derived from the entry-point CLI argument arg1n with no non-NULL constraint (line 26; NULL is an admitted value per the fragment's own guards at lines 23/34/41). When '-write' is processed with an empty image list, line 133 admits the path and line 134 dereferences arg1 via LocaleCompare(arg1,"null:") while arg1 is NULL, crashing the process; a NULL arg1 also reaches the exception formatter at line 136 and the file-name consumers at lines 139/143. With an empty image list the guard at line 133 admits the path, and at line 134 LocaleCompare(NULL,"null:") dereferences NULL under standard string-comparison semantics (and even if it tolerated NULL, line 136 formats the same NULL arg1 via CLIWandExceptArgBreak). No protective statement (absent fix: an added NULL/equality check on arg1 before line 134) covers the failure set on this path, yielding a NULL-pointer dereference / process crash — CWE-476.

option, arg1n, arg2n are NUL-terminated when non-NULL; LocaleCompare follows standard string-comparison (dereferencing) semantics; FormatLocaleString is size-capped (snprintf-like) for key[MagickPathExtent] at lines 124/139.

Identical unguarded NULL-argument dereferences exist at line 266 (FormatLocaleFile(stdout,"%s",arg1) for '-print'), line 278 (InterpretImageProperties(...,arg1n,...) for '-set'), line 360 (IsSceneGeometry(arg1,...) for '-clone'), and line 391 (ParseCommandOption(...,arg1) for '-list'); these share the same root cause and absent-fix pattern but were not selected as separate findings.

The +clone branch (line 359) overwrites a possibly allocated arg1 with AcquireString("-1"), leaking the earlier interpretation result; classified as a robustness/leak concern, not a memory-safety finding.

Discarded return statuses (WriteImages line 143, SetImageRegistry line 297, SetImageOption line 322, SetImageProperty lines 345/347) surface errors only through _exception and show no in-fragment failure-state consumption, so no CWE-754 status-handling finding is confirmed.

verdict.summary: add_interrupt_randomness() calls get_reg(fast_pool, regs) at line 14 with a regs that the fragment itself treats as nullable (line 5 get_irq_regs(); line 19 ternary). On the cycles == 0 path (line 13) the call is unguarded, so get_reg dereferences a NULL pt_regs pointer, causing a kernel NULL-pointer oops. The only visible NULL guard (line 19) protects instruction_pointer(), not this call.

Line 13 admits cycles == 0, so the witness (cycles=0, regs=NULL) reaches line 14 with no guard excluding it. get_reg (by name-implied semantics) reads a register from the passed struct pt_regs* and dereferences the pointer, so a NULL argument causes a NULL-pointer oops (CWE-476). The absent fix is a NULL/regs check before the call (e.g., 'cycles = regs ? get_reg(fast_pool, regs) : 0;'); the line 19 ternary guards only instruction_pointer() and is evaluated after this sink.

get_irq_regs() and random_get_entropy() are OS-provided channels; NULL and 0 respectively are admitted by the fragment itself (line 19 ternary; line 13 branch) and excluded by no shown constraint.

The capacity of fast_pool->pool is not shown, so the constant-index writes at lines 17, 18, 20, 21 are not assessed for out-of-bounds.
The conjunction (cycles==0, regs==NULL) is architecture/context-dependent; the fragment admits both values independently with no shown constraint between them, which caps confidence below 0.91.
instruction_pointer(regs) at line 19 is protected by the ternary and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in SetGrayscaleImage for PseudoClass images: when the entry colormap has at most 65534 entries, colormap_index is allocated with MagickMax(image->colors+1, MaxMap) = 65535 entries (valid indices 0..65534), but the second pixel pass indexes it with ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(image,q)), whose residual range reaches MaxMap = 65535, reading one element past the end. The missing fix is the one-larger capacity (MagickMax(image->colors+1, MaxMap+1)) or an explicit bound on the scaled index.

evidence.reason: For a PseudoClass image with entry colors <= 65534, lines 26-27 allocate colormap_index with MagickMax(colors+1, MaxMap) = MaxMap = 65535 elements, whose largest valid index is 65534. At line 148 the sink reads colormap_index[ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(image,q))], and GetPixelIndex (line 149) returns the attacker-controlled pixel-index channel with no shown bound, so the scaled index retains residual range [0, MaxMap] = [0, 65535]. Guards 138 (status), 141 (q non-NULL), and 146 (x < columns) admit the pixel without constraining the index value. A pixel whose index maps to MaxMap yields subscript 65535 on the 65535-element array, a one-element heap over-read whose value is then stored as the pixel index. The absent protective statement is the one-larger capacity MagickMax(image->colors+1, MaxMap+1) at lines 26-27; without it the failure set {index == MaxMap} reaches the sink, giving CWE-125 heap out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: MaxMap = 65535 and MaxColormapSize = 65536 (documented ImageMagick constants referenced at lines 26-30, 36, 38).
ScaleQuantumToMap maps a Quantum in [0, QuantumRange] onto [0, MaxMap]; a raw index of QuantumRange therefore maps to MaxMap.
GetPixelIndex returns the pixel index channel value without any cap shown inside the fragment for the PseudoClass path.
For a PseudoClass image, image->colormap holds image->colors entries (standard ImageMagick invariant used by lines 99-103 and 111).
limitations: The trigger requires a malformed input pixel index value that maps to MaxMap while the colormap holds at most 65534 entries; no statement inside the fragment produces that value, it is admitted only because the fragment leaves the index channel unconstrained (entry-point data).

The first-pass write image->colormap[image->colors] (lines 82/84/86) is safe only by an exact-fit margin (MaxMap+1 == MaxColormapSize distinct intensities vs 65536-entry colormap); converted to a limitation, not a finding.

A possible NULL dereference of image->colormap[0] at line 111 for a degenerate PseudoClass image with colors == 0 and a NULL colormap is not confirmable: no in-fragment statement can produce that NULL.

verdict.summary: The NULL check at lines 3-5 excludes block == NULL before any dereference, fully covering the only in-fragment failure value for the sinks (QLIST_REMOVE_RCU at line 11 and reclaim_ramblock at line 16). No other dangerous operation has a failure demonstrable from the shown statements.

RAMBlock 'block' is a current member of the uc->ram_list list when passed, so QLIST_REMOVE_RCU at line 11 operates on valid le_prev/le_next link fields.
