A NULL uc pointer would crash at line 12, but no shown statement can set uc to NULL.

verdict.summary: In the refresh-cleanup loop, L11 frees using `*mdev_types[i]`, which (due to precedence) indexes the out-parameter variable `mdev_types` itself instead of the array `(*mdev_types)[i]`. When the caller supplies `*nmdev_types >= 2` on a refresh, iteration i=1 reads one pointer-width past the single `*mdev_types` object, dereferences the garbage address, and passes the result to virMediatedDeviceTypeFree, causing an out-of-bounds read and invalid free.

evidence.reason: Sink at L11: `*mdev_types[i]` parses as `*(mdev_types[i])` (postfix `[]` binds tighter than unary `*`), so for i=1 it indexes the out-parameter pointer variable `mdev_types` rather than the types array. The loop guard at L10 (`i < *nmdev_types`) admits i=1 when the caller's refresh count `*nmdev_types >= 2` (entry value unconstrained by the fragment), and no shown guard re-bases the index. The indexed object's capacity is one pointer element, as established in-fragment by the single-pointer uses at L12 `VIR_FREE(*mdev_types);` and L18 `*mdev_types = g_steal_pointer(&types);`. The absent protective fix is the parenthesized indexing `(*mdev_types)[i]`. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read of the pointer object; secondary CWE-590 free of an invalid/non-owned pointer after the garbage dereference.

assumptions: `*mdev_types` is a single pointer object (capacity 1), evidenced by the fragment's own single-pointer writes at L12 and L18.
The L9 comment 'this could be a refresh' and L19 (`*nmdev_types = ntypes`) establish that a caller can legitimately pass a prior non-zero `*nmdev_types` entry value.
limitations: The exact magnitude `*nmdev_types >= 2` is a caller-provided refresh count; no statement inside the fragment itself produces a value >= 2 before the loop, so the witness is a range (any count >= 2) rather than a single derived constant.

The address reached by the garbage dereference at i>=1 is determined by caller stack layout and is not shown, so the invalid-free target is not attacker-shaped by the fragment; impact assessed as crash/abort (DoS).
Only i=0 is accidentally correct (`*mdev_types[0] == (*mdev_types)[0]`); the failure requires a second or later element, which is presupposed by the loop's own semantics.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the output-buffer sizing at line 46: data_len is an attacker-controlled int string length with no upper-bound check in the fragment. With data_len == INT_MAX and a cipher with block size 1 (e.g. "rc4"), data_len + EVP_CIPHER_block_size(cipher_type) wraps negative, and emalloc(outlen + 1) at line 47 converts it to an enormous size_t, causing an unsatifiable allocation and a fatal out-of-memory abort (reachable DoS). The absent protective statement is an overflow guard (e.g. if (outlen < data_len)) between lines 46 and 47.

evidence.reason: CWE-190 at the sizing computation: data_len is an entry-point int produced by zend_parse_parameters (line 14, "s" specifier) and no shown guard (lines 18, 24, 29, 36) bounds it, so its residual range is [0, INT_MAX]. EVP_CIPHER_block_size(cipher_type) is >= 1 for any valid cipher ("rc4" passes the line 23 lookup with block size 1). Witness data_len = INT_MAX wraps the int addition to INT_MIN; outlen + 1 is then negative and converts to a ~2^64 size_t consumed by emalloc at line 47, which cannot be satisfied, aborting the request with an OOM fatal (reachable DoS). Fix-Scan: no protective statement covers this failure set; the absent fix is an overflow guard (e.g. if (outlen < data_len) { php_error_docref(...); RETURN_FALSE; }) placed between line 46 and the emalloc at line 47.

assumptions: EVP_get_cipherbyname("rc4") resolves to a cipher with EVP_CIPHER_block_size() == 1 (standard OpenSSL semantics); any block size >= 1 suffices to trigger the wrap (data_len = INT_MAX - block_size + 1).
PHP string arguments reach this function with length at most INT_MAX because the engine stores string lengths as int, so data_len = INT_MAX is within the admitted domain.
emalloc of a negative int converted to size_t requests an enormous allocation that the Zend memory manager cannot back, producing a fatal out-of-memory abort.
limitations: The demonstrated failure is the failed-allocation abort, not a small-buffer write overrun: if the huge allocation were ever satisfied (pathological overcommit), EVP_DecryptUpdate at line 54 would write into a comparably huge mapping, so no OOB evidence item is placed at line 54.

The EVP_DecryptInit/DecryptUpdate/DecryptFinal return values (lines 49-56) are discarded; an uninitialized i reaching outbuf[outlen] at line 58 could not be confirmed because OpenSSL's name-implied behavior initializes *outl on failure, so this is recorded only as a status-handling robustness concern.

The base64 branch (lines 30-32) reassigns data_len = base64_str_len and data = base64_str without checking decode failure; a NULL result reaching EVP_DecryptUpdate would require callee semantics not shown in the fragment, so it is not confirmed.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every tile-decoder sink is bounded in-fragment: tile clamps at lines 12/16 and loop conditions at 10/14 keep t.area() <= 64*64 = 4096 matching buf at line 8; both RLE paths throw when a run exceeds remaining capacity (lines 87-89, 110-112); packed and run palette indices are masked to 0..127 (lines 65, 115) against palette[128] (line 21); palette fill is capped by palSize = mode & 127 (line 20). The only sink lacking a protective statement, the readU32-to-int length at lines 5-6, has no demonstrated in-fragment failure and is demoted.

assumptions: PIXEL_T buf[64 * 64] at line 8 is exactly 4096 elements; the min-clamps at lines 12 and 16 combined with loop conditions at lines 10 and 14 bound every tile's width and height to [1, 64], so t.area() <= 4096.
palSize = mode & 127 at line 20 is at most 127, so the palette fill loop at lines 23-25 writes at most 127 entries into palette[128] at line 21.

In the non-CPIXEL raw path at line 43, sizeof(PIXEL_T) >= BPP/8 is assumed so that t.area() * (BPP / 8) does not exceed the byte capacity of buf; this is a compile-time pixel-type invariant not visible in the fragment.
limitations: int length = is->readU32() at line 5 becomes negative for values >= 2^31 and is passed to zis->setUnderlying at line 6, but no shown statement turns that into a memory-safety failure and the callee's internals are not shown, so this candidate cannot be confirmed.

Palette entries palSize..127 are uninitialized and can be read at lines 66 and 117 when a decoded index is >= palSize; reads stay within the 128-element array, so this is a garbage-pixel/uninitialized-value concern rather than a confirmed security finding.

len accumulation at lines 85 and 107 can overflow int on pathological streams; in every wrap interpretation the guards at 87-89 and 110-112 or the zero-iteration write loop prevent writes past end (UB robustness concern only).

Tile arithmetic t.tl.x + 64 at line 16 and t.tl.y + 64 at line 12 can overflow for caller-supplied coordinates near INT_MAX; no shown producer of such rectangles exists and no confirmed failure follows in the fragment.

verdict.summary: bracketed_paste is the fixed counterpart: the guard at lines 12-13 (if (end != NULL && STRLEN(end) >= NUMBUFLEN) end = NULL;) caps the end-code length below NUMBUFLEN, so the prefix-accumulation path (continue at line 43) can never grow idx past NUMBUFLEN-1; every write into buf (capacity NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES, line 4) stays in bounds, and when end == NULL the per-iteration reset at line 87 limits idx to one character. No confirmed vulnerability.

assumptions: NUMBUFLEN and MB_MAXBYTES are positive constants, so buf at line 4 has capacity C = NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES with valid indices 0..C-1.
find_termcode at line 6 returns either NULL or a NUL-terminated string; NULL is explicitly admitted by the end != NULL branch at line 12.
mb_char2bytes at line 35 returns the number of bytes written, in 1..MB_MAXBYTES.
STRNCMP at line 39 stops comparison at a NUL byte in either operand, so end[L] == NUL forces a mismatch once idx > L.
limitations: Reads of uninitialized bytes within buf (e.g., mb_ptr2char at line 80 on a truncated multibyte char) stay inside the array object and are at most an uninitialized-read robustness concern, not an OOB.
Whether bracketed paste can be entered for a given terminal configuration is determined outside this fragment; the safety of the shown code holds on every path that does execute.
The discarded return of set_option_value (lines 19, 93) affects only the 'paste' editor toggle, with no security-relevant consequence visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The destructor's dereferencing operations are NULL- and state-guarded (line 4 for player, line 6 for the mixer call, line 11 for mixer deletion), and the unguarded delete[]/delete of audioDriverName (line 14) and listener (line 16) are NULL-safe under standard C++ semantics; no in-fragment producer can make those pointers invalid (non-new[]-owned or dangling), so no memory-safety, logic, or status failure is demonstrable from the shown statements.

assumptions: Standard C++ semantics apply: delete/delete[] of a NULL pointer is a well-defined no-op ([expr.delete]).
The destructor is invoked exactly once per object (no explicit double-invocation is shown).
player, mixer, listener, and audioDriverName are plain owned member pointers; audioDriverName is array-typed (delete[]) and the others scalar-typed, consistent with the delete forms used.
limitations: Whether mixer->removeDevice/isDeviceRemoved free the player object, making delete player at line 8 a double-free when the line 6 guard is false, depends on the unshown mixer contract — not confirmable from this fragment.

Whether audioDriverName or listener could hold non-NULL pointers not allocated with new[]/new (invalid delete at lines 14 and 16) is not derivable because no setter, allocation, or assignment appears in the fragment.
The discarded return of mixer->removeDevice(player) at line 7 has no shown security consequence (no status-dependent follow-up operation).
NULL guards on the delete expressions themselves (e.g., 'if (audioDriverName)') would be behavior-neutral defensive hardening here, not a vulnerability fix.

verdict.summary: In the -write branch, write_info is produced by CloneImageInfo at line 142 and passed to WriteImages at line 144 with no NULL check; on an allocation failure of CloneImageInfo (the sibling CloneImageList result is NULL-guarded at line 143, but write_info is not), WriteImages dereferences a NULL ImageInfo pointer, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

evidence.reason: NULL-pointer dereference sink: write_info is assigned from CloneImageInfo(_image_info) at line 142, an allocation-family call whose NULL-on-failure residual range is unconstrained here (the twin result CloneImageList is NULL-guarded at line 143, but line 143 tests write_images only). The path to line 144 passes guard line 133 (requires _images != NULL) and guard line 143 (requires write_images != NULL) in that order, and no statement between lines 141 and 144 checks write_info; when CloneImageInfo returns NULL while CloneImageList returned non-NULL, the call at line 144 passes a NULL ImageInfo to WriteImages, which dereferences it by standard semantics. The absent fix statement is a NULL/return-status check on write_info before the call, e.g. an if (write_info == (ImageInfo *) NULL) guard; primary CWE-476.

assumptions: CloneImageInfo returns NULL on allocation failure (standard allocation-family semantics, corroborated in-fragment by the NULL guard on the sibling CloneImageList result at line 143).
WriteImages dereferences its ImageInfo argument per its name-implied standard semantics.
ExpandFilenames on MagickTrue returns a valid argc/argv pair, making the line 104 loop bounded.
AppendImageToList treats a NULL image argument as a no-op per name semantics.
limitations: The confirmed write_info NULL witness requires an unchecked environment failure (allocation failure at exactly CloneImageInfo line 142 while CloneImageList at line 141 succeeded), so confidence is 0.67 and triggerability is not directly attacker-controlled.

arg1n/arg2n possibly NULL passed to InterpretImageProperties in the set branch (lines 279, 292, 318, 338) is not confirmable because the callee may return NULL, which is already handled by the surrounding checks.
arg1=AcquireString("-1") at line 360 may leak a previously percent-interpreted arg1 (robustness/leak, not memory safety).
WriteImages return status at line 144 is discarded, but no security decision depends on it.

No out-of-bounds, injection, crypto, or authz finding was confirmed in the other branches; all remaining guards (stack depth, NULL checks, prefix compares, FormatLocaleString bound) fully cover their sinks.

verdict.summary: Fragment is the fixed counterpart of the r_core_anal_esil scan loop. The heap buffer read at line 205 (buf + i, iend - i) is fully protected by the bound check at line 201 (if (i > iend) goto repeat;), which admits only i <= iend; at the admitted boundary i == iend the pointer buf + iend is still inside the iend + 2 byte allocation (line 79) and the iend - i length is 0. The iend + 1 byte read at line 85 fits the iend + 2 capacity. No attacker-controlled value reaches a memory or injection sink unguarded.

assumptions: buf capacity is exactly (size_t)iend + 2 bytes per line 79, with iend bounded 0 <= iend <= MAX_SCAN_SIZE by lines 72 and 75.
r_anal_op reads at most len (iend - i) bytes from data (buf + i) per its standard name-implied semantics.
On the non-'f' path i starts at 0 because start == addr (lines 14-15); increments of i occur only before the guard at line 201 reevaluates.
limitations: get_next_i is an internal helper without a shown call site; any overstep it produces is still caught by the guard at line 201 before the sink at line 205.

The return value of r_io_read_at (line 85) is discarded, so a short read can leave bytes of buf uninitialized when fed to r_anal_op; this is bounded by len and has no shown security consequence, so it is not a finding.

Conversion of ut64 end - start to int at line 71 is implementation-defined for out-of-range values, but both the iend < 0 guard (line 72) and the iend > MAX_SCAN_SIZE guard (line 75) fail closed, and the line 201 guard remains protective for the read sink.

verdict.summary: The output buffer is allocated one element larger than the worst-case ciphertext (data_len + block_size + 1), which exactly covers EVP_EncryptUpdate's block-aligned output, EVP_EncryptFinal's single padding block, and the NUL terminator write at outbuf[outlen] when outlen == data_len + block_size. All other memory operations are guarded (key padding check) or depend on unshown callee behavior that cannot be confirmed as a failure.

assumptions: emalloc(0) never fails/returns NULL in PHP Zend semantics (no NULL check is idiomatic here).
EVP_EncryptUpdate/EncryptFinal follow standard OpenSSL semantics: Update emits only complete cipher blocks (at most data_len bytes on a fresh context), Final emits at most one block_size.
zend_parse_parameters 's' yields non-negative lengths for data_len, password_len, iv_len.
Line 37's '+1' is exactly the one-element-larger capacity fix: capacity = data_len + block_size + 1, so index data_len + block_size (line 49 NUL write) is the last valid byte.
limitations: EVP_EncryptUpdate's return value (line 44) is discarded and int i (line 8) is uninitialized; if Update failed without setting *outl, i would be garbage at lines 45-46 — but no shown input/guard path can demonstrate Update failure, so this is unconfirmable.

EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_key_length(&cipher_ctx, password_len) at line 41 is reached for any password_len > keylen without an in-fragment bound; a very large password_len could stress OpenSSL's internal key buffer, but the receiving capacity lives inside EVP_CIPHER_CTX (line 7) and is not declared in the fragment, so no OOB can be confirmed.

The empty-IV path (lines 31-33 warns and continues) relies on php_openssl_validate_iv (line 34) to pad/normalize iv before EVP_EncryptInit_ex (line 43); the callee is not shown, so no undersized-IV OOB read can be confirmed from the fragment.

data_len + EVP_CIPHER_block_size on line 36 could overflow int only for data_len within 16 of INT_MAX (a >2 GB PHP string); no shown derivation establishes such a value, and the realistic string-length limit makes this a robustness concern only.
The empty-IV advisory warning (line 32) is informational; both the vulnerable and fixed counterparts emit it, and it does not gate any security decision here.

verdict.summary: raptor_xml_writer_start_element_common heap-overflows the nspace_declarations buffer: each attribute adds up to two entries (its namespace declaration at 58-64 plus its mandatory entry at 70-76) while the allocation at 21-22 is sized attribute_count+1 at line 15, so a single attribute with an out-of-scope namespace writes nspace_declarations[2] of a 2-element allocation; additionally the inner dedupe loop at 51-52 indexes element->attributes[j] with j bounded only by nspace_declarations_count, producing an out-of-bounds read when count exceeds attribute_count.

evidence.reason: With attribute_count=1 (admitted by loop 40: i=0 < 1), name->nspace N0 out of scope (declared at index 0, count=1 via line 35) and attributes[0]->nspace N1 non-NULL, out of scope and != N0 (admitted by 42 and 45), the declaration entry is written at index 1 (58) and count becomes 2 (64); this unconditional write then indexes nspace_declarations[2] of an array allocated with capacity nspace_max_count=attribute_count+1=2 (lines 15, 21-22, valid indices 0..1) and writes again at line 75, followed by count=3 at 76. No statement on the path (guards 14,27,28,39,40,42,44-45,51,57 admit the witness; 81 and 108 are skipped) compares nspace_declarations_count with nspace_max_count, and the Fix-Scan found no protective guard, only the absent fix of raising line 15 to attribute_count*2+1 or adding a count-vs-capacity check before each count-indexed write. This is a one-past-end heap write of a struct nsd (CWE-787).

nspace_declarations_count reaches 3 (name declaration at 35, first attribute's declaration at 64 and mandatory entry at 76) before the second attribute (i=1 admitted by loop 40 with attribute_count=2, and attributes[1]->nspace N2 admitted by guards 42 and 45). The inner loop at 51 admits j in [0,3), and at j=2 this line reads element->attributes[2], outside the [0, attribute_count)=[0,2) range that the fragment's own loop at 40 demonstrates for that array; guards 51 and 44-45 do not restrict j to attribute_count. The absent fix is element->attributes[i] instead of element->attributes[j] at line 52 (or bounding j by attribute_count). This is a heap-buffer-over-read of an 8-byte pointer (CWE-125); its array capacity is inferred from the line-40 access pattern since the struct declaration is not shown.

assumptions: nstack is non-NULL so that the guarded nspace_declarations path (lines 14-25) executes, matching the fragment's own branch structure.
raptor_namespace_format_as_xml and raptor_qname_format_as_xml succeed (return non-NULL) on the witness path, so execution does not take goto error before the sink.
element->name->nspace and each attribute's nspace satisfy the fragment's own in-scope/equality checks (lines 28, 44-45) exactly as chosen for the witnesses.
element->attribute_count is positive (1 or 2), which is the non-degenerate range the loop at line 40 admits.
The valid index range of element->attributes is [0, attribute_count), evidenced by the fragment's own loop at line 40.
limitations: The xml:lang escape block (lines 111-122) may overflow if raptor_xml_escape_string does not enforce buf_length for heavily escaped language strings; the callee's bound behavior is not shown, so it is not confirmed.
RAPTOR_MALLOC at line 112 is dereferenced by memcpy at line 116 without a NULL check; that is an OOM robustness concern, not an attacker-witnessed failure.
raptor_sequence_get_at (line 84) is dereferenced at line 90 with no shown NULL producer; not a confirmed NULL dereference.
Negative element->attribute_count would under-size the allocation (lines 15, 21-22), but such a value is not derived by any shown statement, so it is excluded by the degenerate-input discipline.

The read at line 52 is confirmed only against the [0, attribute_count) range evidenced by line 40; the declared size of element->attributes is outside the fragment, slightly lowering confidence for the secondary finding.

The name-nspace declaration must actually be out of scope for the minimal write witness (otherwise count would be 0 entering the attribute loop); the code's own branch at lines 27-28 permits this state.

verdict.summary: UINT32 width and height are unvalidated, so width * height * 4 at the BufferPool_Take allocation can wrap (e.g. 65536*65536*4 == 0 mod 2^32), allocating an undersized/zero surface buffer that is then bound to a width x height x 4-byte surface at line 34, enabling heap overflow when the surface is filled.

evidence.reason: width and height retain their full UINT32 domain (0..4294967295): no guard between lines 1-2 and this statement constrains them, and NULL checks at lines 6/13/21 do not affect them. Witness width=65536, height=65536: 65536*65536*4 = 2^34 wraps to 0 in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and is consumed as the allocation size of BufferPool_Take, while the intended backing store is 2^34 bytes as evidenced by the same expression and by createSurface(video, ret->surfaceData, x, y, 65536, 65536) at line 34. The check at line 28 tests only the allocation result and runs after the wrapped size is consumed. The absent fix is an overflow/upper-bound check on width*height*4 (e.g. rejecting width==0||height==0 and width > UINT32_MAX/4/height) before line 27. Primary mechanism: CWE-190 integer overflow feeding an undersized allocation.

assumptions: width, height, x, y are UINT32, so width * height * 4 is computed modulo 2^32 as shown in the declared types.
BufferPool_Take(pool, size) provides a buffer sized from its `size` argument (allocation/pool semantics implied by its name and use at line 27).
createSurface at line 34 binds surfaceData as the backing store for a width x height surface at 4 bytes/pixel, the '4' being the per-pixel byte count at line 27.
limitations: The overflowing surface-fill write is not shown in the fragment; the confirmed in-fragment mechanism is the wrapped size consumed by the allocation at line 27, so CWE-122 is not independently confirmed.

No call site of PresentationContext_new is shown; exact attacker control of width/height is not demonstrated in-fragment, though the parameters are dimension fields expected to be entry-point (protocol) derived.
Dimension handling inside h264_context_reset (line 18) and yuv_context_reset (line 48) is unshown and was not evaluated as a sink.
video->priv dereference at line 4 has no shown NULL producer and was treated as non-NULL per framework.

verdict.summary: tgs_build_reply() discards the return status of _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal() at three sites (L93 u2u additional-ticket name, L144 request server name, L149 TGT client name). When the conversion fails on an attacker-supplied principal, the resulting NULL (or, for L93, uninitialized) krb5_principal is passed on the very next statement into krb5_unparse_name(), which dereferences it, crashing the KDC via NULL/invalid-pointer dereference (CVE-2019-12098 class). The absent fix is a return-status check right after each conversion.

evidence.reason: p comes from the unchecked conversion at L93 of the attacker-supplied additional-ticket name; the only guards on the path (L75-76, L85) bound the ticket list and its krbtgt shape but not conversion success, and p is uninitialized at L70, so on a conversion error p is NULL/indeterminate and is dereferenced here by krb5_unparse_name (name-implied pointer dereference). The `if (ret) goto out` at L95-96 tests only unparse_name's own status; the in-fragment S4U2Self and constrained-delegation conversion sites do check this callee's return. Absent fix: `ret = _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal(context, &p, t->sname, t->realm); if (ret) goto out;` at L93. Primary CWE-476 NULL/invalid-pointer dereference with discarded-status root cause CWE-754.

sp is NULL-initialized at L17 and assigned by the unchecked conversion at L144 of the request server name (*s, r, attacker-controlled from b->sname/b->realm or the u2u adtkt.cname/crealm). The guard at L138 only requires s != NULL and does not constrain conversion success; on conversion error sp stays NULL and is dereferenced here by krb5_unparse_name. Absent fix: `ret = _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal(context, &sp, *s, r); if (ret) goto out;` at L144. Primary CWE-476, secondary CWE-754.

cp is NULL-initialized at L17 and assigned by the unchecked conversion at L149 of the presented TGT's client name (tgt->cname/tgt->crealm). No guard sits between L149 and L150, so on a conversion error cp remains NULL and is dereferenced here by krb5_unparse_name. Absent fix: `ret = _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal(context, &cp, tgt->cname, tgt->crealm); if (ret) goto out;` at L149. Primary CWE-476, secondary CWE-754.

assumptions: priv->req / priv->req.req_body fields (sname, realm, additional_tickets, etype, kdc_options) are TGS-REQ protocol data parsed from the network and are attacker-controlled (entry-point provenance).

_krb5_principalname2krb5_principal can fail and then leaves its output principal NULL/invalid; the fragment's own checked call sites at the S4U2Self and constrained-delegation conversions demonstrate the return is failure-capable and must be checked.
krb5_unparse_name, by its standard semantics, dereferences the supplied principal to render it.
limitations: The concrete trigger for the conversion failure is an exceptional condition (allocation failure / internal conversion error) rather than one deterministic in-domain value, so the witness is an error-state range; confidence is set to 0.74 accordingly.

For the L93 sink, if the failed conversion leaves *p completely untouched, p is indeterminate stack memory (stronger UB) rather than provably NULL; either outcome dereferences an invalid pointer at L94.

The same discarded-status pattern exists for krb5_make_principal in the capath and need_referral referral branches (unparse_name on a sp forced to NULL at the prior line); these were not added as separate findings because their reachability additionally depends on referral-backend behavior outside the shown code. All other audited operations (additional_tickets->val[0] indexing at L84 and the constrained-delegation val[0] use, the enc_tkt_in_skey etype loop, and the num_capath>0 capath pop) are fully guarded and safe.

verdict.summary: The fragment copies left_width + num_tiles*src_width + right_width bytes through three memcpy sinks (lines 9, 13, 17) using caller-supplied int widths with no in-fragment capacity, non-negativity, or overflow guard. No failure can be demonstrated from shown code alone because neither the source nor destination buffer capacity is declared in the fragment and no width is derived in-fragment to an out-of-domain value; the valgrind memset (line 22) is unreachable for nonnegative widths. Candidates are therefore unconfirmed limitations, not findings.

assumptions: memcpy/memset are evaluated by their standard semantics: exactly the given size argument is copied and no validation of that size occurs (lines 9, 13, 17, 22).
The total destination extent is left_width + num_tiles*src_width + right_width, derived from the shown pointer advances at lines 10, 14, and 19.
limitations: OOB write into dest_strip (sinks at lines 9, 13, 17): the object's capacity is not declared or computed anywhere in the fragment, so rule (a) of the OOB confirmation criteria cannot be met.
OOB read from src_strip (lines 9, 13, 17): source capacity is unshown and no invariant such as left_offset + left_width <= src_width is visible.

Negative or overflowing memcpy sizes (left_width, src_width, right_width, num_tiles*src_width): parameters keep the full signed-int domain, but no in-fragment transformation produces a demonstrably failing value; absence of a caller-visible upper-bound check is not itself a finding.

memset under PACIFY_VALGRIND (line 22): ptr_out_temp is advanced by the full total width, so (dest_strip - ptr_out_temp) <= 0 and ii <= 0 for nonnegative widths, making the ii > 0 branch unreachable; a reaching witness would require unshown negative caller widths.
Integer overflow of num_tiles * src_width or of the cumulative offsets is not demonstrated by the shown code (no constants or derived magnitudes create a wrap in the shown types).

verdict.summary: No security-relevant failure is derivable from the shown statements. The refresh loop (line 10) is bounded by '<' and frees the caller-owned array consistently with a count reset (lines 12-13); the fetch's return status is checked (lines 15-16) so failed output never reaches the stores at lines 18-19; NULL/undersized-array risks depend on unshown caller contract, and the incoming array's capacity is never declared in the fragment.

assumptions: Output parameters mdev_types and nmdev_types are valid non-NULL pointers per the function contract (no NULL producer exists anywhere in the fragment).
The caller maintains the invariant that the incoming *mdev_types array has exactly *nmdev_types elements (the fragment never declares that array's capacity).
virMediatedDeviceGetMdevTypes has the name-implied contract: negative return on failure, and on success a consistent (types, ntypes) pair; the fragment checks the former at line 15.
Locals types (line 5) and ntypes (line 6) are initialized before any use.
limitations: A NULL-dereference scenario (lines 10-13, 18-19) would require an unshown caller passing NULL output pointers or a non-NULL count with a NULL/undersized array; this is caller-contract-dependent and not derivable from the fragment.

An out-of-bounds scenario in the free loop (lines 10-11) would require a caller-supplied count exceeding the caller's actual array size; no capacity is declared in the fragment, so this is an unconfirmable invariant violation.

A failed refresh destroys previously valid capability data (old entries freed at lines 10-13 before the fetch at line 15); this is a fail-closed availability behavior with no memory-safety or security consequence shown.

On a negative return from the fetch, any entries the callee may have partially allocated into the local 'types' would be leaked, but this is inside the unshown callee and not observable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: LogFilePrep passes the attacker-controlled fname parameter directly as the format string to asprintf (line 7), with idstring as the only vararg. A crafted fname containing %n or extra %s/%x specifiers enables arbitrary memory disclosure and arbitrary write, potential code execution. The fragment contains no protective statement converting fname to a data argument (the absent fix is asprintf(&logFileName, "%s", fname)).

evidence.reason: Format-string injection at the sink: fname is attacker-controlled per the fragment's own comment (lines 5-6) and its residual range is unconstrained (any C string), reaching the asprintf format operand at line 7 with no guard, filter, or escaping between entry and the call. Witness fname = "%n" (or repeated %s/%x) is admitted with no preceding guard; the only vararg supplied is idstring, so %n writes the formatted length to an address popped from the stack (arbitrary write) and extra %s/%x read beyond the provided arguments (information disclosure/DoS). The neutralizing protective statement asprintf(&logFileName, "%s", fname) is absent. Primary CWE-134 (use of a non-literal, attacker-influenced format string).

limitations: backup is also used as a format string at line 17 (asprintf(&suffix, backup, idstring)), but no shown caller or in-fragment evidence establishes that it is attacker-controlled, so it is not confirmed as an independent finding.

The comment at lines 5-6 ('should never be called with elevated privileges') is an acknowledgment, not an executable constraint; any assumed caller-side privilege guarantee is outside the fragment and unusable.

verdict.summary: The networkstatus parser contains its protective statements on every dangerous operation: all three ns->cert dereferences are guarded by ns->type != NS_TYPE_CONSENSUS (lines 220, 445, 465) while the certificate is guaranteed non-NULL for non-consensus inputs at line 62; all five base16_decode calls are preceded by exact HEX_DIGEST_LEN length checks (lines 213, 254, 278, 421, 436); the signature-object tor_memdup at line 478 is bounded by the 128..512 range check at line 416 (and line 474); voter/footer smartlist index 0 accesses are covered by lines 267-273 and 360-361; and every token-array index is bounded by asserts at lines 67, 122, 203, 249, 396 and loop conditions. No attacker-controlled value reaches an unprotected sink.

assumptions: ns->type == ns_type is enforced at line 79, so in-fragment guards on ns->type are equivalent to guards on ns_type.
ns->cert is non-NULL exactly when ns_type != NS_TYPE_CONSENSUS: parsed at line 61 and rejected at line 62 otherwise.
Tokenizer-produced directory_token_t args[0..n_args-1] are valid for indices below n_args.
base16_decode with srclen=HEX_DIGEST_LEN writes 20 bytes into the 20-byte DIGEST_LEN buffers used at lines 214, 255, 280, 422, 437.
routerstatus_parse_entry_from_string advances s past each parsed entry, making the line-298 loop terminating on well-formed input.
limitations: Termination of the while loop at line 298 depends on the unshown callee (routerstatus_parse_entry_from_string) advancing s on failure; failure-mode advance semantics are not visible, so a non-termination finding cannot be confirmed.

Arg-count requirements for tokens consumed without an in-fragment assert (K_CONTACT line 246, K_CLIENT_VERSIONS/K_SERVER_VERSIONS lines 149/152, K_LEGACY_DIR_KEY line 278) are enforced by the unshown token tables; no capacity violation is derivable from the shown code.
The object_size upper-bound checks at line 474 are redundant given the 128..512 validation at line 416, leaving no integer-overflow or oversize-copy concern.

If this fragment is the patched counterpart, the decisive fix statement is the added ns->type != NS_TYPE_CONSENSUS guard at line 220 (mirrored at lines 445 and 465) eliminating the NULL ns->cert dereference for consensus inputs.

verdict.summary: udf_expand_file_adinicb() feeds attacker-controlled iinfo->i_lenAlloc into a memset/memcpy against a freshly allocated PAGE_SIZE page without any upper-bound check. verdict.summary: Integer overflow in PresentationContext_new: UINT32 width*height wraps before the 4ULL multiply (line 7), so the INT32_MAX guard (line 8) is bypassed (e.g., width=height=65536 yields s=0), causing BufferPool_Take to allocate a tiny backing buffer (line 33) for a full-size width x height surface (line 40), leading to a heap out-of-bounds write when frames are decoded into surfaceData.

At line 7 the sub-expression 'width * height' is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps modulo 2^32, so s = ((width*height) mod 2^32) * 4. The guard at line 8 tests this already-wrapped s and admits s <= INT32_MAX; witness width=height=65536 gives s=0 and 0 > INT32_MAX is false, so the witness reaches this allocation. The buffer returned here has capacity s (0 or a small pooled chunk), while line 40 binds it to a 65536x65536 surface whose required size 65536*65536*4 = 2^34 bytes is the fragment's own formula at line 7; decoded-frame writes therefore overflow the s-byte buffer. This is CWE-190 integer overflow: the corrupted size is consumed as an allocation size at line 33 and defeats the size check at line 8. The absent fix is a 64-bit-safe computation (e.g., 's = (size_t)width * height * 4ULL;') or a pre-multiply width/height bound check placed before line 8.

assumptions: BufferPool_Take returns a non-NULL buffer of at least s bytes on the success path (name-implied pool semantics; NULL case is handled at line 34).
createSurface (line 40) creates a width x height surface backed by ret->surfaceData whose pixel writes can fill up to width*height*4 bytes — the same size formula the fragment computes at line 7.
width/height are interpreted as attacker-influenced channel data by the (unshown) caller; no bound is derivable from the fragment itself.
limitations: No call site for PresentationContext_new is shown, so the attacker-control of width/height rests on the channel-parser context (rule c), not on an in-fragment statement.
The overflowing write itself occurs inside unshown callees (createSurface/decoder), so a secondary CWE-787 is not independently confirmed in-fragment and is omitted.
On a 32-bit size_t build the wrapped value is additionally truncated mod 2^32, but the bypass (small s with huge surface) holds on any platform; the finding does not depend on this.

OOB read (CWE-125) of the same stack buffer: on the fourth admitted iteration of the same witness (no-whitespace message of length >= 314 with WARN_TEXTWIDTH=79), ptr is at offset 237 and cut is 78, so fwrite reads 79 bytes from ptr at offsets 237..315, beyond the char print_buffer[256] capacity declared at line 7. vsnprintf returns the untruncated would-be length when output exceeds the buffer (standard C semantics applied to line 11), so len's domain includes values larger than sizeof(print_buffer)=256.

limitations: L176 dereference of server->entry.principal->realm on HDB_ERR_WRONG_REALM: a NULL server on that path would require _kdc_db_fetch to return WRONG_REALM without an entry, an unshown internal contract; no in-fragment statement produces NULL here, so this is not confirmable as CWE-476.

L262 ref_realm = strdup(realms[0]) is unchecked (unlike L176 and L224); a NULL result occurs only under OOM and is never dereferenced on that path (only tested at L951 and freed at L1030), so no consumed failure is demonstrated.
