L994 *auth_data passed to tgs_make_reply assumes the AuthorizationData** parameter is non-NULL; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: No confirmed, reachable security flaw. The only dereference of the nullable regs value from get_irq_regs() (L5) is instruction_pointer(regs), which is guarded in-fragment by `regs ? instruction_pointer(regs) : _RET_IP_` (L19) with the admitted set regs != NULL and the excluded set regs == NULL. Every fast_pool->pool index is a literal 0..3 (L17,18,20,21) or the masked expression cycles & 3 (L26), which is bounded to {0,1,2,3} for any cycles_t value including 0. The sizes passed to crng_fast_load and __mix_pool_bytes are sizeof of the exact objects (L30-31, L47, L56). The possibly-NULL regs argument to the unshown get_reg at L14/L22 cannot be confirmed as a dereference without its body, so it is a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: regs from get_irq_regs() (L5) can be NULL, evidenced in-fragment by the ternary at L19 treating NULL as a possible value.
instruction_pointer(regs) dereferences regs, so the `regs ?` test at L19 is the protective statement with admitted set regs != NULL and excluded set regs == NULL.
ip is declared __u64 (L9), so sizeof(ip) == 8 makes `sizeof(ip) > 4` (L21) always true and the L22 get_reg call dead on every target.
cycles & 3 (L26) admits only {0,1,2,3} for every cycles_t value, including the cycles == 0 admitted by L13.
crng_fast_load/__mix_pool_bytes consume exactly the sizeof bounds passed (L30-31, L47, L56), so the size equals the object size.
limitations: get_reg(fast_pool, regs) at L14 (when cycles == 0) and at L22 (dead) can receive a NULL regs, but a NULL dereference would require the unshown get_reg body to dereference regs without a NULL check; the callee is not shown and its NULL-handling is not unambiguously name-implied, so this candidate is demoted and unconfirmed.
The fast_pool struct and pool capacity are not declared inside the fragment, so capacity is inferred; no shown index derivation exceeds 3, so no OOB candidate exists regardless of the exact capacity.

cycles, irq, and jiffies are hardware/kernel-derived values with no attacker-controlled index or size reaching any sink; entropy strength/accounting (credit + 1 at L64) is an intentional design choice, not a confirmed flaw.
Whether get_irq_regs() can actually return NULL at runtime on a given architecture is not observable from the fragment; only the fragment's own NULL-aware handling at L19 is used.

verdict.summary: The heap allocation of `struct cx23888_ir_state` at line 8 is never freed on error paths: `kfifo_alloc` failure returns at line 14 without `kfree(state)` (leak L1), and `v4l2_device_register_subdev` failure frees only the kfifo at line 42 and returns at line 44, also leaking `state` (leak L2). The absent one-statement fix is `kfree(state);` on both error paths.

evidence.reason: Leak L1: `state` is allocated at line 8 (`kzalloc(sizeof(struct cx23888_ir_state), GFP_KERNEL)`) and guard B2 at line 13 admits the failure set `{nonzero}` of `kfifo_alloc`, routing control to this line-14 return with no `kfree(state)` on the path; line 42's `kfifo_free` is unreachable from here. The absent fix statement is `kfree(state);` before this return. Each failed probe permanently leaks one `struct cx23888_ir_state` (with its embedded subdev), a missing-release-of-memory flaw (CWE-401).

Leak L2: on `v4l2_device_register_subdev` returning nonzero (line 25), guard B3 at line 26 admits the failure set, this else-branch statement frees only the rx_kfifo, and `return ret;` at line 44 ends the function with the line-8 `state` allocation still unreleased; since registration failed, no shown framework path (line 20 only stores the pointer) will free it. The absent fix statement is `kfree(state);` alongside this cleanup. Same CWE-401 memory-leak mechanism as the line-14 path.

assumptions: kfifo_alloc returns 0 on success and nonzero on failure, a contract the fragment itself acts on at line 13.

sd is embedded in state (`sd = &state->sd;`, line 17), so `state` is the sole owning allocation, and only an explicit kfree (or successful subdev registration followed by unregister) could release it; neither unregister nor kfree is shown on the failing paths.
v4l2_device_register_subdev returning nonzero means the subdev was not registered, so no later unregister-driven release occurs in the fragment.
limitations: Both confirmed leaks require an allocation or registration failure to trigger; the trigger is environmental and not directly attacker-controlled, and the per-event loss is one small struct, so severity is low (resource leak/robustness on error paths rather than corruption).

No out-of-bounds, use-after-free, NULL-deref, injection, or authz flaw was demonstrated: kzalloc NULL is checked (line 9), snprintf is bounded by sizeof(sd->name) (line 22), and the failed kfifo is never used after line 13's check.
The return values of v4l2_subdev_call (lines 36, 40) are discarded; no security-relevant consumer of that status is shown, so it is demoted to a robustness note.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in mpgviddmx_process: when ctx->bytes_in_header is 1 or 2 (persisted from a prior packet that ended with 1-2 unparsed bytes stored at loop-top, lines 128-131) and the next packet leaves remain at 5-6 (admitted by the `remain<5` guard at line 128), the copy at line 139 reads `8 - bytes_in_header` bytes from `start` — up to 2 bytes past the packet payload whose capacity is `pck_size` from line 31. No clamp or bound check protects this copy.

evidence.reason: Source-overrun sink: line 31 declares the packet payload capacity `pck_size` and lines 34-35 set `start=data; remain=pck_size`, with the invariant `start+remain == data+pck_size` preserved by every advance. `ctx->bytes_in_header` (persisted, never reset at function entry) is 1 when a prior call's loop-top store (lines 128-131, with remain reduced to 1 via lines 381-382/394-395) set it, admitted by `if (remain<5)` at line 128. With the next packet at `remain == 5` (also admitted by line 128), line 139 copies `8 - 1 = 7` bytes from a 5-byte payload, reading 2 bytes past `data + pck_size` (CWE-125 heap OOB read). The fix absent from this fragment is a clamp/bound on the copy, e.g. `if (8 - ctx->bytes_in_header > (u32) remain)` or `memcpy(..., min(8 - bytes_in_header, remain))`, which no shown statement provides.

assumptions: Packet payload capacity is exactly `pck_size` as returned by `gf_filter_pck_get_data(pck, &pck_size)` at line 31.
The invariant `start + remain == data + pck_size` holds on the witness path (fresh-packet case, resume_from == 0), so exactly `remain` bytes are readable at `start`.
`ctx->bytes_in_header` persists across calls (no reset shown at function entry) and takes only values 1..4 (lines 130/199/276/439).
`gf_realloc` at lines 70/306/350 allocates `ctx->hdr_store`, making it non-NULL in flows where the loop-top store at line 129 is written before the demonstrated line-139 overread.
limitations: Write-side capacity of `ctx->hdr_store` for lines 129/217/530 is not declared in-fragment on all paths, so the NULL/small-capacity write to `hdr_store` is not claimed as a separate finding.
Negative `remain` after the resume branch (lines 94-96) requires `!ctx->is_playing` (set at line 399), whose reachability is not shown, so it is not confirmed.
u32 wrap in capacity arithmetic at lines 68-69/304-305/348-349 needs an aggregate of roughly 2^32 bytes of stored data; it is a relational/range concern, not the demonstrated witness.

Whether `gf_m4v_parse_frame` can report `size > remain` on GF_EOS reaching the copies at lines 498/501 (and the `(u32) size` truncation at line 486) depends on unshown callee semantics and is not confirmed.

verdict.summary: ReadCINImage is the hardened/fixed form: every dangerous operation in the fragment is covered by a visible protective statement (magic/count check L68, user_length bound L331, profile NULL check L335, columns*rows/8 file-size bound L350, offset pad check L361, SetImageExtent status L364, full-row equality gate L393, quantum-info/q NULL checks L371/L390, and memset initialization L71). No in-fragment value admitted by every guard exceeds a shown capacity, so no failure is demonstrable.

assumptions: CINInfo.channel has 8 entries, matching the loop bound `i < 8` at line 128 that guards accesses at lines 130-149.
Every `sizeof(src)` passed to CopyMagickString (lines 86-317) is a fixed compile-time struct size smaller than `property[MagickPathExtent]` (line 7); no in-fragment contrary evidence.
On LP64, `image->columns*image->rows` (max (2^32-1)^2) does not overflow size_t.
limitations: `bits_per_pixel` (line 134) allows `image->depth` in [0,255] (line 342), so `length` (lines 376/380) can exceed a 32/64-bit quantum row buffer for depth > 32; however the capacity of `pixels` (line 383) is not declared or computed in the fragment, so an out-of-bounds write in ReadBlobStream (line 392) cannot be confirmed (demoted CWE-787).

The ReadBlob return at line 337 is discarded: with user_length <= GetBlobSize but fewer bytes remaining after the parsed header, a short read would store an uninitialized tail in the 'dpx:user.data' profile; the disclosing writer path is outside the fragment (demoted status-handling/uninitialized-use concern, CWE-754/CWE-908).

AcquireImage (line 55) could return NULL on allocation failure and be dereferenced via OpenBlob/image->endian (line 72); this is an environmental OOM premise with no attacker-derived producer in the fragment (demoted CWE-476).

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart: the CDIC loop bound `while (i < huff_rec_count - 1)` (line 37) exactly matches the allocated symbol capacity `(huff_rec_count - 1) * sizeof(...)` (line 30), so the maximum index `huff_rec_count - 2` stays in bounds on every path. Counts below 2 are rejected at line 15 (preventing `huff_rec_count - 1` underflow), `curr` is NULL-checked at lines 15 and 38, the first record's size is validated at line 19, the malloc result is checked at line 31, and both parse results are checked at lines 24 and 43.

assumptions: Capacity of `huffcdic->symbols` is `huff_rec_count - 1` elements, fixed by the malloc at line 30.

Line 10 bounds `huff_rec_count` to `HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT`, and line 15 guarantees `huff_rec_count >= 2` on the continuing path, so `huff_rec_count - 1` is always in [1, HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT - 1] and never underflows (lines 30, 37).
`mobi_parse_cdic(huffcdic, curr, i)` writes at most one symbol entry at the given index `i`, per the name-implied semantics.
The record linked list supplies at least `huff_rec_count - 1` non-NULL successors; otherwise the function fails closed at lines 38-40.
limitations: Potential `size_t` wrap of `*m->mh->huff_rec_index + offset` (line 8) is not a confirmed finding: no shown magnitude for either addend and no in-fragment capacity for the lookup, whose NULL result is handled at line 15.
Multiplication overflow at the malloc (line 30) cannot be confirmed because `HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT` is not defined in the fragment, so no value that wraps `SIZE_MAX` is demonstrable.
Internals of `mobi_parse_huff`, `mobi_parse_cdic`, and `mobi_get_record_by_seqnumber` beyond their name-implied semantics are not shown and were not assumed.

verdict.summary: No demonstrated failing value reaches any security-relevant sink. The guest-controlled uint16 num_queues/queue_size fields (L37-38) drive an exactly self-consistent uint64 sizing: mmap_size = num_queues * pervq_inflight_size (L50) sizes the mapping (L51), the memset (L57), and the packed init loop (L76-84), and the loop bounds admit only in-range writes. Allocation results are NULL-checked (L29, L52), the exact message-size equality (L13) bounds payload reads, and the inflight_info->fd = -1 init (L34) prevents the zeroed allocation's fd==0 from reaching close(0) via the fd>=0 guard (L64-67). No OOB, NULL, integer, or status flaw is derivable from the shown statements; residual concerns are unconfirmable limitations.

assumptions: get_pervq_shm_size_packed/split(queue_size) (L46/L48, unshown) return per-queue size = header + sizeof(desc)*queue_size, i.e., exactly the footprint the loops write (L79-82) and stride (L83).
inflight_mem_alloc (L51, unshown) maps exactly the requested mmap_size bytes and returns NULL on failure (failure path is handled at L52-56).
ctx->fds has at least one slot (L71 writes ctx->fds[0]) and dev/ctx are valid per the caller contract.
dev->virtqueue[0] is non-NULL whenever dev->nr_vring > 0 (L23-24); no NULL producer for it exists in the fragment.
struct inflight_mem_info is zero-initialized by rte_zmalloc_socket (L27), making the fd=-1 init (L34) and addr==NULL first-call behavior the shown safe state.
limitations: num_queues/queue_size are never validated against negotiated device limits (e.g., nr_vring or the configured ring size), so a malicious guest can request an oversized mmap/memset (up to ~2^36 bytes for max uint16 fields); this is a possible resource-exhaustion concern (CWE-400) but not a confirmed finding because the magnitude depends on unshown sizeof constants in the size helpers and the failure requires the unshown mmap to succeed and the host to exhaust memory.
A possible NULL deref of dev->virtqueue[0] at L24 when nr_vring > 0 is not confirmable under the rules: no statement in the fragment can make dev->virtqueue[0] NULL (framework member pointer).
Discarded return statuses of munmap (L60) and close (L65) are robustness-only; no shown security decision consumes them.
The fds[0] fd is passed to the guest by design; no double-close or stale-fd path was found (L64-67 plus L34 keep the sentinel coherent).

verdict.summary: In the second loop of do_arg_all, the index i (bounded only by count <= opened_len = ARGCOUNT at lines 178-179/196) indexes AARGLIST(alist) at line 252 with no check against alist->al_ga.ga_len, while the fragment's own first-loop guard (line 84) shows ga_len is the valid bound for that container. A window-local arglist shorter than the global count, or an autocommand shrink (acknowledged at lines 48-50 and 176-177), admits i >= alist->al_ga.ga_len and causes a heap out-of-bounds read fed into do_ecmd.

evidence.reason: Index i reaches the sink with residual range 0..opened_len-1 (opened_len = ARGCOUNT at line 43; count clamped to opened_len at lines 178-179; loop bound i < count at line 196), while the valid range of AARGLIST(alist) is 0..alist->al_ga.ga_len-1 as established by the fragment's own guard at line 84 for the identical macro access. No statement between lines 196 and 252 compares i to alist->al_ga.ga_len (line 198 is only an equality test for arg_had_last), and the fragment states the arglist size may change (lines 48-50, 176-177) and that alist may differ from &global_alist (line 198); the clamp at lines 178-179 uses the stale opened_len and does not cover this failure set. Witness: global ARGCOUNT=5 with curwin's w_alist having ga_len=3, so at i=3 all guards pass — line 35 (ARGCOUNT>=1), line 178-179 (count=5), line 196 (3<5), lines 200/228 (opened[3]==0, split_ret==OK) — and line 252 reads AARGLIST(alist)[3] past the 3-element array: heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent protective statement is 'if (i >= alist->al_ga.ga_len) break;' at the top of the second loop body.

assumptions: ARGCOUNT is the global argument-list length (macro over global_alist.al_ga.ga_len, which the fragment references explicitly at line 198) and may differ from the current window's alist length (alist = curwin->w_alist at line 51; the alist == &global_alist test at line 198 shows divergence is possible).
alloc_clear(opened_len) at line 44 supplies opened_len byte slots, giving opened[] valid indices 0..opened_len-1.
The valid index bound for AARGLIST(alist) is alist->al_ga.ga_len, as used to guard the identical access at line 84.
Autocommands triggered by shown calls (win_close line 155, autowrite line 140, goto_tabpage_tp lines 67/173) can change the arglist size, per comments at lines 48-50 and 176-177.
limitations: The concrete magnitude of the divergence (e.g., ga_len=3 vs ARGCOUNT=5) is session state not constructed inside the fragment; only the decoupling between the two sizes and its mutability are shown.
Reaching the sink at line 252 requires win_split at line 237 to return OK on the failing iteration; a FAIL result continues to the next index (lines 239-240) rather than removing the hazard.
The internals of alist_name/do_ecmd are not shown; impact is assessed on the out-of-bounds read of the argentry_T element itself, whose ae_arg pointer is then passed to do_ecmd.
Robustness-level observations (e.g., arg_had_last comparison when ga_len is 0, sentinel w_arg_idx = opened_len) were audited and are not security findings.

verdict.summary: This is the fixed counterpart. The total_slide_infos accumulation is protected by the wrap check at line 18 (ut32 truncation of the size_t sum is always detected because n_slide_infos[i] <= 2^32-1), so the infos allocation at line 29 is exactly sigma(n_slide_infos) and never undersized; k (lines 34, 52, 65) is structurally capped at total_slide_infos, keeping infos[k] writes at lines 60-63 in-bounds. The single-entry branch gates cache->maps[1] behind mappingCount > 1 (line 92), and n_slide_infos[i] writes are bounded by i < MAX_N_HDR (line 12). No confirmed memory-safety, injection, crypto, or authz finding is derivable from the shown statements.

assumptions: RZ_NEW0/RZ_NEWS0 zero-allocate and return NULL on failure; every result is checked in-fragment (lines 3, 30, 77, 94).
rz_buf_read_le32_at and rz_buf_fread_at are bounds-checked reads whose failure return is checked in-fragment (lines 14, 41, 55).
cache->hdr_offset and cache->maps are arrays with at least MAX_N_HDR and mappingCount elements respectively (struct contract outside the fragment).
cache->n_hdr and cache->hdr are non-NULL and internally consistent (caller-side invariant, no NULL producer in the fragment).
limitations: MAX_N_HDR's value is not shown; the fragment only guarantees indices < MAX_N_HDR stay within n_slide_infos (line 9) and by contract within hdr_offset.
get_rebase_info (lines 63, 100) is not shown; its slideInfoOffset/slideInfoSize/fileOffset arguments may be large, but any consuming operations and their validation live outside this fragment.
ut64 wrap in infos[k].end = infos[k].start + entry.size (line 61) and infos[0].end (line 99) has no shown security-relevant consumer, so it is a robustness note, not a finding.
Attacker-controlled n_slide_infos values can request very large allocations; failures are handled gracefully (NULL -> beach), so a DoS is not confirmable within the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment fully sanitizes every attacker-influenced feed field by replacing single quotes with %27 (lines 12-15) before embedding each field in single quotes (line 10), so no field-supplied character can break out of the quoted shell arguments passed to either run_interactively (line 22) or /bin/sh -c via run_program (lines 26-31). The unquoted bookmark_cmd at line 11 is the user-configured command template the feature intentionally executes, not attacker-steerable data.

assumptions: Under POSIX shell semantics, inside a single-quoted string every character except a single quote is literal; lines 12-15 remove all single quotes from url, title, description, and feed_title, so shell metacharacters from those fields cannot act as shell syntax.
bookmark_cmd (line 7) is user configuration: the bookmarking feature is intended to execute the configured command, and the fragment shows no path by which the untrusted feed fields can influence it.
limitations: Newlines from title/description survive the (single-quote-only) replacement and reach the DEBUG log at line 17; a CWE-117 log-injection finding was not confirmed because the fragment shows no security-relevant log consumer or disclosed-recipient impact.
run_interactively's return status is discarded at line 22, but no security decision shown in the fragment depends on it.

The correctness of the non-interactive launcher relies on run_program executing my_argv with /bin/sh semantics implied by argv[0..2]; with the quote sanitization in place, no injection witness was admissible under any such semantics.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the TALOS-CAN-0063 patched counterpart of cookedprint. The only derived-index write path (bv[len] = output_raw; bv[len+1] = '\0'; at L124-125) is protected by the outlen cap sizeof(bv) - 1 at L121-122, which bounds strlen(bv) <= 2*MAXVALLEN - 2, so the two appended bytes stay within char bv[2 * MAXVALLEN] (L22). Fix-Scan finds the neutralizing statement present; no memory, injection, crypto, file/access, or authz finding is confirmable from the shown code.

assumptions: atoascii(in, maxlen, out, outlen) is a bounded ASCII copy: it truncates the input to maxlen characters and writes at most outlen bytes to the destination including the NUL terminator (size-argument semantics implied by the call sites at L119, L121-122, L127-128).
nextvar(&length, &data, &name, &value) at L31 yields NUL-terminated name/value strings.
MAXVARLEN and MAXVALLEN are positive compile-time macros, so 2*MAXVALLEN >= MAXVALLEN + 2 and the append at L124-125 has headroom.
decodearr at L97 fills at most the 8 elements of l_fp lfparr[8] (L19) per the array-size call-site convention.
limitations: The bodies of atoascii, nextvar, decodearr, outputarr, output, and decode* are not shown; their bounds are inferred only from standard/name-implied semantics and the explicit size arguments.

A narr > 8 overflow of lfparr would require decodearr behavior that cannot be derived from the fragment; no in-fragment producer of an out-of-range count exists, so the AR path is a limitation, not a finding.
Byte-level safety of the fprintf %s arguments at L27-28 and L111-112 rests on the unshown NUL-termination contract of nextvar/statustoa-family returns.
The size of MAXVARLEN/MAXVALLEN is not shown; the verdict relies on their relative relationship to the 2* declared buffer sizes, which is visible directly in the declarations at L21-22.

verdict.summary: mcba_usb_start_xmit() guards the transmit path with if (can_dropped_invalid_skb(netdev, skb)) return NETDEV_TX_OK; (lines 14-15) before cf->len is stored into usb_msg.dlc (line 43) and used as the memcpy size (line 45). A false return admits only a valid classic-CAN frame whose len is bounded to 8 (CAN_MAX_DLEN), matching the 8-byte CAN payload of both cf->data and usb_msg.data, so every admitted copy length is safe. The ctx result of mcba_usb_get_free_ctx() is NULL-checked (lines 17-19) and the mcba_usb_xmit() error status is handled (lines 52-54), so no memory-safety, NULL-deref, or status-handling finding is reachable from the shown code.

assumptions: can_dropped_invalid_skb() (lines 14-15) is the CAN-core validator: on true it has already dropped (kfree_skb) the skb and the function returns; on false the skb is a valid CAN/CANFD frame, and for the classic-CAN frames used here (cf is struct can_frame at line 5) its contract bounds len to 8 (CAN_MAX_DLEN), with the helper's cfd aliasing the same skb->data as cf.

cf->data and usb_msg.data are the 8-byte classic-CAN payload arrays; the fragment only uses classic-CAN constants (CAN_EFF_FLAG, CAN_SFF_MASK, CAN_RTR_FLAG) and a packed 8-byte CAN payload copy at line 45.
mcba_usb_get_free_ctx() returns either a valid context pointer or NULL, and the NULL case is handled at line 18-19 before ctx->ndx / ctx are used.
limitations: The exact numeric bound (CAN_MAX_DLEN = 8) and the 8-byte capacities of cf->data / usb_msg.data are not spelled out inside the fragment; they follow from the can_dropped_invalid_skb() helper contract and the classic-CAN frame layout. Analyzed strictly in-fragment without that helper semantics, the memcpy length would be an unconfirmable range, not a finding, in either direction.

The return value of can_put_echo_skb() (line 50) is discarded; on -EBUSY/-ENOMEM the echo bookkeeping fails while the URB is still submitted, but no security-relevant consumer of that failure state is shown, so it is treated as a robustness concern, not a finding.

CAN-FD frames in excess of 8 bytes cannot reach this sink on the admitted path because line 14-15 rejects/drops non-conforming frames; no in-fragment evidence admits a canfd_frame-interpreted payload to the line 45 memcpy.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. huff_rec_count is lower-bounded by the `huff_rec_count < 2` guard (line 15) and upper-bounded by HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT (line 10) before the `(huff_rec_count - 1)` allocation (line 30) and loop bound (line 37), so no underflow, overflow, or out-of-bounds index into huffcdic->symbols is derivable; allocation failure is checked (line 31), curr is checked for NULL on every use (lines 15, 38), and all parsing return statuses are consumed (lines 24, 43).

assumptions: HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT is a small compile-time constant, so `(huff_rec_count - 1) * sizeof(*huffcdic->symbols)` (line 30) cannot overflow.
mobi_parse_cdic addresses huffcdic->symbols only at the index passed as its third argument, which the loop (line 37) confines to 0..huff_rec_count-2 against a capacity of huff_rec_count-1 (line 30).
m and huffcdic are non-NULL per caller contract; no statement in the fragment can produce NULL for them.
limitations: A possible size_t wrap in `*m->mh->huff_rec_index + offset` (line 8) is not demonstrated: magnitudes are unconstrained and the value only feeds mobi_get_record_by_seqnumber, so no wrap-induced failure is visible inside the fragment.
The exact numeric value of HUFF_RECORD_MAXCNT is not shown; the overflow-free reading of line 30 depends on it being a moderately sized constant.
NULL-dereference of the parameters m/huffcdic is not confirmable because the fragment contains no NULL producer for them.

verdict.summary: Off-by-one bounds check in __io_sync_cancel(): the guard at line 11 rejects only fd > ctx->nr_user_files, admitting fd == ctx->nr_user_files; array_index_nospec() at line 13 is a speculation sanitizer, not a bounds check, so io_fixed_file_slot() at line 14 reads one io_fixed_file past the end of the fixed-file table (OOB read). The check must be fd >= ctx->nr_user_files.

evidence.reason: fd is an int parameter whose residual range after the shown guard at line 11 (if (unlikely(fd > ctx->nr_user_files))) is [0, ctx->nr_user_files] because unsigned comparison rejects only fd > nr_user_files and admits the boundary fd == ctx->nr_user_files. array_index_nospec(fd, ctx->nr_user_files) at line 13 is name-implied as a post-bounds-check speculation sanitizer, not a runtime bound, so fd reaches this sink unchanged at the boundary value. ctx->nr_user_files is the fragment's capacity for the file table (it is the size passed to array_index_nospec at line 13), so io_fixed_file_slot(&ctx->file_table, fd) reads element index == nr_user_files, one past the last valid slot 0..nr_user_files-1: an out-of-bounds read of file_ptr (CWE-125). The post-read NULL check at lines 16-17 executes after the read and cannot protect it; the absent single-statement fix is the changed comparison if (unlikely(fd >= ctx->nr_user_files)).

assumptions: ctx->nr_user_files (used as the array_index_nospec size at line 13 and as the guard threshold at line 11) is the element count of ctx->file_table.files, so valid indices are 0..nr_user_files-1.

fd is the io_uring cancel fd supplied through the SQE (IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD / _FD_FIXED), i.e. userspace-controlled; its producer is not shown inside the fragment, so this specific taint link is assumed.
nr_user_files is within the int domain of fd (no unsigned > INT_MAX edge), so the boundary fd == nr_user_files is representable.
array_index_nospec is evaluated by its documented standard semantics (sanitize an index after a correct bounds check); it is not credited as a runtime bounds check.
limitations: The literal declaration/allocation of ctx->file_table.files is outside the fragment; the capacity N is inferred from the fragment's own use of ctx->nr_user_files as the index bound.

On architectures where array_index_mask_nospec masks architecturally, the out-of-range index is clamped to 0, turning the exact OOB read into a wrong-file cancel (fixed slot 0) rather than a memory violation; the off-by-one guard is wrong in either case, but the memory-safety verdict relies on the standard kernel semantics of array_index_nospec as a speculation barrier, not a bound.

A degenerate nr_user_files == 0 with fd == 0 would also pass line 11 and could dereference file_table.files[0] with a NULL/empty table; that sub-case is not separately confirmed because registration gating is not shown.
No NULL producers for cd or tctx are shown in-fragment, so NULL-dereference of those pointers is not assessed.

verdict.summary: sungem_send_packet forwards an unvalidated (buf, size) pair to qemu_receive_packet/qemu_send_packet, but no failing value can be demonstrated from the shown fragment: no buffer capacity is declared, no size-producing statement or call site is shown, and the size parameter retains only its unconstrained declared domain. The line-6 loopback branch is a routing decision that constrains neither argument. Unconfirmed candidates (negative/oversized size OOB read, size_t widening, NULL nc) are relegated to limitations.

assumptions: s, buf, and nc are treated as non-NULL because the fragment contains no statement that can produce a NULL value for them (lines 4, 6, 7, 9).
qemu_receive_packet and qemu_send_packet are packet-transmit helpers whose own internals are not part of the shown code and are not given standard-sink semantics by their names.
limitations: No capacity for buf is declared or computed in the fragment (lines 1-11), so an OOB read via oversized size (CWE-125) at lines 7/9 cannot be confirmed; the size parameter has no shown call site and no failing magnitude is derived inside the fragment (Phase 1 category (c)).
A negative size reaching the sinks would be widened only inside unshown callee internals; no signed-to-unsigned conversion or security-relevant consumer is visible, so CWE-195 is unconfirmed.
No NULL producer for nc is shown (line 4), so a NULL-dereference finding at lines 7/9 relies on an unshown framework contract and is demoted.
The discarded return values of lines 7 and 9 have no subsequent consumer in the fragment; a status-handling flaw (CWE-754) cannot be confirmed.

The fragment lacks any size/buffer protective statement, but a verdict of vulnerable would require a shown capacity and a shown failing derivation, both of which are absent; the safe verdict is the default low-confidence one rather than an audited protective-statement verdict.

verdict.summary: The message-wrapping loop under-decrements the remaining length: line 28 removes only `cut` while lines 25/27 consume and skip `cut + 1` bytes. When a chunk contains no whitespace, `cut == 0`, so `len` never decreases: the while loop at line 15 cannot terminate, while `ptr` keeps advancing at line 27 until the read at line 21 goes past the 256-byte buffer declared at line 7. A caller-supplied whitespace-free string (e.g., a long URL) reaching a warning triggers an infinite-loop DoS and a stack out-of-bounds read. The absent fix statement is `len -= cut + 1;`.

evidence.reason: When the inner scan at lines 21-23 finds no whitespace, `cut == 0`, so this statement subtracts 0 and `len` is unchanged. The outer guard at line 15 (`while(len > 0)`) and the wrap branch at line 18 (`if(len > (int)WARN_TEXTWIDTH)`) both remain true, while line 27 (`ptr += cut+1`) still advances by 1. The loop therefore makes no progress in its state variable and cannot terminate for a message whose W-byte chunk is whitespace-free, giving non-termination (CWE-835). The protective fix absent here is `len -= cut + 1;`, which would consume the actual byte count written at line 25 and skipped at line 27.

On the `cut == 0` path, `ptr` advances by exactly 1 per iteration at line 27 while `len` stays constant at line 28, so the read `ptr[cut]` with `cut = WARN_TEXTWIDTH-1` eventually indexes at or beyond 256, past `char print_buffer[256]` declared at line 7. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the capacity line is 7, the advance is line 27, and the admission of the whitespace-free chunk is not excluded by any guard on the path (lines 15, 18, 21). The absent protective statement is `len -= cut + 1;` (or a clamp of `len` to the buffer size after `vsnprintf` at line 11).

assumptions: WARN_TEXTWIDTH is assumed to be a positive constant (it is used as index `WARN_TEXTWIDTH-1` at lines 19 and 21); its numeric value is not displayed in the fragment.

vsnprintf is assumed to have its standard semantics at line 11: it writes at most 255 chars plus a NUL into the 256-byte buffer and returns the length that would have been written, which may exceed 255.
The triggering text is caller-supplied (e.g., a URL or token interpolated into a warning by an unshown call site); no shown statement constrains the formatted message to contain whitespace.
limitations: The whitespace-free message pattern that drives `cut == 0` comes from unshown callers; within the fragment that residual range is only the absence of an in-fragment whitespace check, not a produced constant.
The duplicate `va_start(ap, fmt)` at lines 9-10 is undefined behavior, but no concrete misread or corruption can be traced to it from the shown statements, so it is not reported as a finding.

For messages longer than 255 characters, `vsnprintf` truncates the buffer while returning the untruncated length; fully hardening the OOB read also requires clamping `len` after line 11, which is beyond the fragment's statements.

Behavior after the out-of-bounds read at line 21 depends on stack contents and is undefined; the confirmed deterministic failure is the OOB read, with non-termination confirmed relative to the shown state variables.

verdict.summary: A crafted archive can write files outside the extraction directory: an AE_IFLNK entry is materialized by g_file_make_symbolic_link (line 220) with an unvalidated, attacker-chosen target (e.g. "../../../../../../etc"), and a later AE_IFREG entry whose relative_path (line 45/50) has that symlink as an intermediate component is opened via g_file_replace (line 202) and written via g_output_stream_write (line 207), following the symlink to an arbitrary path (CWE-59). The fragment contains no symlink-target validation and no NOFOLLOW/symlink-parent check before the write.

evidence.snippet: ostream = (GOutputStream *) g_file_replace (file, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, cancellable, &load_data->error);
evidence.reason: For an AE_IFREG entry the sanitized relative_path (line 45) only guarantees the path string stays below extract_data->destination; it does not constrain the filesystem objects at those components. A previous AE_IFLNK entry created destination/sub -> "../../../../../../etc" (line 220, archive_entry_symlink is passed unvalidated), and g_file_replace (line 202) resolves the intermediate symlink, opening /etc/crontab outside the destination. Every guard on the path admits the witness (lines 35, 39, 46, 54 or 93-98, 108-110, 129, 188, 201: cancellation false, "sub/crontab" non-NULL, parent exists via g_file_query_exists following the symlink, error NULL). The absent one-statement fix is validation of archive_entry_symlink (rejecting absolute/escaping targets, e.g. routing it through _g_path_get_relative_basename_safe) or a G_FILE_QUERY_INFO_NOFOLLOW_SYMLINKS is_symlink check before the replace; primary CWE-59 arbitrary file write/overwrite outside the extraction root.

Attacker-controlled archive data (buffer from archive_read_data_block, line 206) is written through ostream opened at line 202, whose path resolved through the archive-created symlink destination/sub -> /etc to /etc/crontab. buffer_size is a libarchive block size (size_t) and matches the gsize count, so there is no size flaw; the failure is that the write lands outside extract_data->destination because no shown guard rejected the symlinked parent or the unvalidated symlink target (line 220). Primary CWE-59: content controlled by the archive is committed to a path outside the intended extraction tree.

assumptions: extract_data_get_extraction_requested (line 39) admits attacker-chosen archive pathnames (e.g. file_list == NULL means all entries are requested); the fragment only shows it as a skip condition with no shown restriction that blocks a hostile name.

The write witness is admitted under both overwrite outcomes: with overwrite TRUE / skip_older FALSE the block at line 54 is skipped entirely; with overwrite FALSE, a nonexistent target yields G_IO_ERROR_NOT_FOUND at lines 93-98 and extraction proceeds.
Standard GIO/OS semantics: g_file_query_exists / G_FILE_QUERY_INFO_NONE follow symlinks, and g_file_replace opens the full path so the OS resolves intermediate symlink components.
_g_path_get_relative_basename_safe (lines 45/142) admits plain relative paths without ".." such as "sub" and "sub/crontab", which is its name-implied purpose.
limitations: The symlink-following behavior of g_file_replace and g_file_query_exists is taken from standard GIO/file semantics rather than a statement shown in the fragment.
libarchive could in principle return NULL pathname/symlink strings; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so NULL-dereference was not treated as a finding.
The discarded return of archive_read_open (line 21) and the associated error report at line 246 are robustness/status-handling concerns without a demonstrated security consequence.
The path-traversal guards at lines 46 and 143 protect ".."-based escapes for pathnames and hardlink targets; they do not cover the symlink-target surface, which is the confirmed bypass.

verdict.summary: No unguarded security-relevant sink found: file-derived dimensions are validated (L323-326, L381), colormap size is capped and count-verified (L333-334, L401-402, L415-416), and the pixel buffer is allocated with a per-row margin plus exact-full-read verification (L451-452, L459-460) so every row-conversion stride stays in bounds.

assumptions: The width/height guards at L323 and L325 admit only columns >= 1 and rows >= 1 (negative heights become rows=|height|>=1 and are flipped at L909-923), so no empty or negative dimension reaches the row loops.

The per-row bytes_per_line values recomputed at L501, L744, L803, and L843 are numerically equal to, or smaller than, the bytes_per_line used in the allocation at L451-452, so every row stride fits the allocated quantum.
The RLE path (L477-478) passes image->columns*image->rows as the decode length; DecodeImage's internal behavior is not shown, so its safety is taken only insofar as it honors the supplied length.
limitations: The weak pre-check length/8 > GetBlobSize at L446 is safe only because of the exact-count check at L459-460; on its own it would not cap the read, but the check present in the fragment prevents conversion on a short read.
DecodeImage's internal bounds are not visible in the fragment; an overflow inside that unshown callee cannot be confirmed from the shown statements.

Potential size_t overflow in length/bytes_per_line on 32-bit builds cannot be fully excluded from the fragment; the only visible gate is SetImageExtent (L381) whose numeric resource limits are external, so no overflow-to-OOB is derivable here.

The mask-shift loops (L541-546 and siblings) can perform a 32-bit shift count of 32 for all-ones masks (C undefined behavior), but the corrupted value feeds only pixel color arithmetic, not an index, size, or security decision.
Fail-closed robustness items (offset_bits==0 rejected at L436-437, intent switch without default at L287-309, unconditioned partial-row scan at L677) have no reachable security consequence.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the strncasecmp reads at L8/L12 are bounded by len >= url->auth_header_len (L11) and len > url->timelimit_header_len (L14); the trailing-byte probes at L15-16 and L39 are bounded by len >= 2 (L18, L39); the errormsg write at L41-42 is capped at sizeof(url->errormsg) (L35-36) with copy_len = len - 24 + 1 >= 2 guaranteed by len > 24 (L31, L33), and the memcpy read stays within ptr (max end index len - 2). No reachable memory-safety, injection, crypto, file/access, authz, or status flaw is demonstrable from the shown statements alone.

assumptions: ptr references a buffer with exactly len = size*nmemb readable bytes (libcurl callback contract), and every shown access stays within that range.

url->errormsg is a nonempty array whose byte capacity is sizeof(url->errormsg), as used by the cap at L35-36; the exact unseen declaration is irrelevant to safety because the cap enforces the write bound in-fragment.
url->auth_header and url->timelimit_header are non-NULL NUL-terminated C strings (non-NULL checked at L11/L14; strncasecmp stops at a NUL).
auth and url (L8-9) are non-NULL on the shown path: only client is NULL-checked (L7) and no NULL producer for auth->state is shown.
limitations: A theoretical wrap of size * nmemb at L4 is not demonstrable inside the fragment: no shown consumer of a wrapped len against a visible capacity exists.

The sscanf at L21 reads a chunk that libcurl may not NUL-terminate, but the %u digit scan must stop at the in-buffer '\r' verified by L18, so no over-read past the chunk is reachable from shown statements.
time(NULL) + limit at L22 could wrap only for an unshown 32-bit time_t, and the unsigned limit is not consumed by a security decision.
NULL-dereference of auth, url, or client->con has no shown NULL producer and is left unconfirmed.

verdict.summary: decode_errcode_attr computes value.slen = attr->hdr.length - 4 (line 19) from the attacker-controlled 16-bit STUN attribute length set by GETATTRHDR (line 13) with no validation, so a length of 0..3 yields a negative signed pj_ssize_t that pj_strdup (line 22) converts to a huge unsigned size, causing an out-of-bounds read, huge allocation, or abort. The absent fix is a length>=4 guard before line 19.

evidence.reason: value.slen is set at line 19 to attr->hdr.length - 4, where attr->hdr.length is an attacker-controlled STUN attribute length (set from buf[2..3] by GETATTRHDR at line 13) with residual range 0..65535 because the fragment contains no constraint; for length in 0..3 the signed pj_ssize_t slen is -4..-1. pj_strdup uses src->slen as the raw allocation/copy size (standard name-implied semantics), implicitly converting the negative signed width to pj_size_t (~SIZE_MAX), so the copy at line 22 reads out of bounds from value.ptr = buf+8 (line 18) or aborts on the huge allocation. There are no conditionals in the fragment (lines 5-28), so the exact witness length=3 (slen=-1) is admitted on the only path; the absent protective fix is a check such as 'if (attr->hdr.length < 4) return PJ_ETOOSMALL;' before line 19. Primary CWE-195 (signed-to-unsigned negative-size conversion), secondary CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read).

assumptions: GETATTRHDR (line 13) reads the 4-byte STUN attribute header and stores the network-order 16-bit length in attr->hdr.length (pj_uint16_t, domain 0..65535).
value.slen is a signed pj_ssize_t, so attr->hdr.length - 4 can be negative.
pj_strdup(pool, dst, src) uses src->slen as the raw size for allocation and copy (standard name-implied semantics).
limitations: The buf[6]/buf[7] reads at line 15 can exceed the attribute when length < 4, but are not separately confirmed as OOB because the enclosing message-buffer capacity is not shown in the fragment; the same absent length>=4 check would cover them.
The unchecked PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T result at line 12 is not a NULL-deref finding because PJLIB's allocator treats OOM as fatal in standard builds and no NULL producer is shown.

The caller-side check that the attribute fits inside the message is outside the fragment and was not relied upon in either direction; positive lengths (>= 4) up to 65531 were not confirmed as OOB here.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is demonstrable within the shown fragment. The only failure-prone consumption is `limit` at line 17 after `sscanf`'s return is discarded at line 16; the initialization `unsigned int limit = 0;` at line 15 pins `limit` to 0 whenever `sscanf` fails to match, covering the entire failure set and yielding fail-closed behavior (`discon_time = time(NULL)`). Every admitted `limit` (0..UINT_MAX) keeps `time(NULL) + limit` representable on 64-bit time_t, and the candidate hazards (NULL derefs of `client->auth`/`auth->state`/`client->con`, OOB reads via `strncasecmp`/`%s`, `size*nmemb` overflow) lack an in-fragment NULL producer or shown buffer capacity.

assumptions: `time_t` is 64-bit, so `time(NULL) + limit` for any admitted `limit` in [0, UINT_MAX] (lines 15-17) cannot overflow (max ≈ +136 years).

libcurl invokes this HEADERFUNCTION with each header line NUL-terminated, so `strncasecmp` at lines 11/13, `sscanf` at line 16, and `%s` at line 22 stop at the header's terminator; the equality guards at lines 11, 13, and 19 additionally prove the line holds at least `auth_header_len`, `timelimit_header_len`, and 22 bytes before the `ptr + len` offsets are used.
`url->auth_header_len`, `url->timelimit_header_len`, and the header strings are admin-configured values; no shown statement derives them from input.
`client->auth`, `auth->state`, and `client->con` are treated as non-NULL because no statement in the fragment can produce NULL for them.
limitations: The discarded `sscanf` return at line 16 is a status-handling gap (CWE-754-style) but is fail-closed: on no-match/EOF, `limit` stays 0 and `discon_time` becomes `time(NULL)`. Had the `= 0` initialization at line 15 been absent, an indeterminate `limit` would be consumed at line 17; that initialization is the protective statement present in this (fixed) fragment.

Out-of-bounds reads via `strncasecmp(ptr, ..., auth_header_len)` (line 11), `strncasecmp(ptr, ..., timelimit_header_len)` (line 13), `sscanf` at `ptr + timelimit_header_len` (line 16), and `%s` from `ptr+22` (line 22) are unconfirmed: no capacity for the header buffer is shown, each successful prefix match guarantees at least the compared number of bytes, and the reads terminate at the header's NUL under libcurl semantics.
NULL-dereference candidates at lines 9, 10, and 17 (`client->auth`, `auth->state`, `client->con`) lack an in-fragment NULL producer; only `client` (line 7) has a shown NULL guard.

`size * nmemb` (line 4) could theoretically overflow, but `bytes` is only returned at line 31 with no in-fragment security consumer; a short callback return is aborted by curl (robustness, not a shown exploit).

A crafted timelimit value only moves `discon_time` within [now, now + UINT_MAX seconds]; on 32-bit time_t platforms the addition could wrap and force an early disconnect, a platform-dependent robustness concern rather than a demonstrated breach.

verdict.summary: The fragment applies no constraint to the int size passed to the receive()/qemu_send_packet() sinks (lines 7, 9) and no NULL check to nc from qemu_get_queue() (line 4), but it also declares no capacity for buf, derives no failing size value, and shows no NULL producer, so no failure can be demonstrated from the shown statements alone; all candidates rest on unshown caller/device-setup premises and are demoted to limitations.

assumptions: MAC_XIFCFG >> 2 in the line-6 condition is a compile-time constant register index, so the macregs[] read is not attacker-indexed by anything shown in the fragment.
Line 6 is a neutral loopback/normal dispatch rather than a security decision; both branches pass the same buf and size to a receive/send sink.
limitations: size (int, line 2) is unconstrained in the fragment; a negative or capacity-exceeding value reaching nc->info->receive() (line 7) or qemu_send_packet() (line 9) cannot be demonstrated because no bad-size derivation and no capacity for buf are shown (would-be CWE-125/787 demoted).

nc from qemu_get_queue(s->nic) (line 4) is dereferenced at lines 7 without a NULL/nullability check, but a NULL-producing condition (e.g., s->nic == NULL or missing queues) is not visible in the fragment (would-be CWE-476/754 demoted).
The capacity of s->macregs is not shown, so even the constant-index read at line 6 cannot be bounds-verified in-fragment, though the index is not attacker-controlled.
Whether the size reached here originates from guest-controlled TX descriptor lengths is determined in unshown callers, which the analysis is not permitted to assume.

verdict.summary: In the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA write path (line 115-124), the block length data->block[0] is unvalidated (u8, 0..255). With data->block[0]==255, line 119 assigns dma_size = 256 which truncates to 0 in the u8 declared at line 8; at line 124 the memcpy count dma_size-1 becomes -1 -> SIZE_MAX, causing a massive out-of-bounds write/read from dma_buffer and data->block. The length clamp present at lines 150-154 protects only the I2C_BLOCK_DATA case and is absent on this path.

evidence.reason: data->block[0] is an entry-point SMBus block-length field with residual range 0..255 (u8): no constraint exists on the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA path (lines 115-124); the only clamp in the fragment (lines 150-154) guards case I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA only. For data->block[0]==255, line 119 stores 256 into u8 dma_size (declared line 8), truncating to 0; at line 124, dma_size-1 evaluates to -1 (int) and converts to SIZE_MAX as the size_t copy count, so memcpy overruns the dma_buffer (heap member of struct ismt_priv, capacity unshown in-fragment, exceeded by the SIZE_MAX count) from &dma_buffer[1] and reads past &data->block[1] — CWE-787 OOB write with CWE-190 u8 truncation as the root arithmetic. The guards on the path (line 37 dispatch, line 116 read_write==I2C_SMBUS_WRITE) admit the witness; the absent fix is a data->block[0] > I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX clamp before line 119, mirroring lines 153-154.

assumptions: data->block[0] is the block-length byte of caller-supplied SMBus transaction data (entry-point input) per the union i2c_smbus_data usage at lines 119, 140, 145, 150-154, 159, 164, 168.
dma_size is an 8-bit unsigned type as declared at line 8, so the assignment at line 119 truncates 256 to 0.
I2C_SMBUS_WRITE selects the write branch at line 116 for the confirmed witness.
limitations: The exact out-of-bounds extent beyond dma_buffer depends on the byte capacity of priv->buffer, which is not declared in the fragment; the SIZE_MAX copy count makes overflow certain regardless, so this does not affect the verdict.

The memcpy at line 145 (I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL) also uses unvalidated data->block[0] (0..255) as its length, but its demonstrated overrun requires the unshown capacities of dma_buffer/priv->buffer and of the union's block field, so it is demoted to a limitation rather than a separate finding.
No caller-side validation (e.g., i2c-dev) is assumed in either direction; the fragment's own clamp at lines 150-154 demonstrates the driver is responsible for validating block lengths.

verdict.summary: Fragment is the patched variant of r_core_anal_esil. The dangerous operation (r_anal_op reading from buf at offset i with length iend - i, line 212) is protected by the bound check `if (i > iend) { goto repeat; }` (line 209) placed BEFORE the call, admitting only i in [0, iend]; together with the iend+2 allocation (line 79), the iend+1-byte fill (line 85), the op.size>=1 guard (line 222) and the loop-exit `if (i >= iend) break;` (line 448), no shown derivation can drive buf+i or iend-i out of bounds. No memory-safety, NULL-deref, integer, injection, or logic/status flaw is confirmable from the shown statements.

assumptions: buf capacity is iend+2 bytes and initialized region is indices 0..iend (lines 79 and 85).
iend is non-negative (line 72) and capped by MAX_SCAN_SIZE (line 75), so (size_t)iend + 2 does not overflow.
r_anal_op is analyzed by its name-implied semantics: it reads at most the passed length; the (buf+iend, 0) boundary case is a zero-length read at an allocated, initialized byte.
The loop index i is size_t, starting at addr - start (line 152), and every path that reaches the sink passes the line 209 guard.
limitations: Potential strdup NULL for spname/pcname (lines 101, 124) is not a confirmed finding: neither pointer is dereferenced in the fragment (only passed as register-name arguments and freed).

If end < start, `iend = end - start` (line 71) truncates a wrapped ut64 to int; the resulting small window stays within the shown capacities and is validated by the io-offset check, so no out-of-bounds is derivable in-fragment.
get_next_i (line 451) behavior is unshown, but its re-entry is bounded by the loop-exit check at line 448 and the pre-sink guard at line 209.

The historical counterpart confirms this is the post-fix layout (radare2 PR #18846 moved the `i > iend` guard before the r_anal_op call and tightened the loop exit to `i >= iend`); that is corroborating, not required, evidence.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no confirmed vulnerability. The memcpy size is capped by min(max_data, write_pos - read_pos) (lines 3-4), and every in-fragment mutation (lines 8, 12) preserves read_pos <= write_pos, so the unsigned underflow that would permit an out-of-bounds read at line 7 requires an entry state (read_pos > write_pos) and a buffer capacity that no shown statement produces or declares. The NULL-buffer and destination-overflow candidates are likewise unconfirmable within the fragment.

assumptions: min is the conventional two-operand minimum macro returning the smaller value.
The caller supplies a destination `data` able to hold at least `max_data` bytes; the visible bound `count <= max_data` (lines 3-4) is the only in-fragment guarantee for the destination write.
gs_free_object is the standard allocator free; its return value, if any, is not consumed.
limitations: Unsigned underflow hazard: if pcs->status.read_pos > pcs->status.write_pos on entry, the subtraction at line 4 wraps to a huge value, count becomes max_data, and line 7 could read beyond the status buffer (CWE-125 pattern). No statement in the fragment can produce read_pos > write_pos — line 8 only advances read_pos toward write_pos and line 12 resets both to 0 together — so the failing state requires an unshown producer (e.g., an external status writer resetting write_pos), and the buffer's allocated capacity is never declared in the fragment. Demoted per Phase 3.

NULL source/free: the only NULL producer is line 11, immediately neutralized by the line 12 reset (read_pos == write_pos == 0) and the line 6 count guard, so a memcpy with a NULL source or gs_free_object(NULL) would require an entry state (buffer NULL with read_pos != write_pos) that the shown code cannot create.

Destination overflow of `data` beyond max_data is not derivable: count = min(...) <= max_data always, so exceeding the destination depends on an unshown caller contract where the destination buffer is smaller than max_data.

verdict.summary: In ismt_access(), the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA write path sets u8 dma_size = data->block[0] + 1 without validating data->block[0]. With block[0] == 0xFF the u8 arithmetic wraps dma_size to 0, and memcpy(&dma_buffer[1], &data->block[1], dma_size - 1) converts -1 to SIZE_MAX, causing an enormous out-of-bounds write/read and kernel memory corruption. The protective bound check present in other cases (BLOCK_PROC_CALL and I2C_BLOCK_DATA) is missing on this path.

evidence.reason: On the BLOCK_DATA write path (size==I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA at line 115, read_write==I2C_SMBUS_WRITE at line 116), data->block[0] retains its full entry-point residual range 0..255 because the only bounds visible on block[0] (lines 138-139 and 153-157) belong to other switch cases. For data->block[0] == 0xFF, line 119 computes data->block[0] + 1 = 256 into u8 dma_size (declared line 8), wrapping to 0; the memcpy length argument dma_size - 1 then promotes to int -1 and converts to SIZE_MAX as size_t, so the copy at this sink writes/reads past every finite object — the destination DMA buffer backed by priv->buffer (line 13) and the source data->block. The post-sink guard if (dma_size != 0) at line 193 is evaluated after this copy and is bypassed (dma_size==0). The absent one-statement fix is a bound check on data->block[0] before line 119 in the BLOCK_DATA write branch (e.g., 'if (data->block[0] > I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX) return -EINVAL;'), i.e., the same protection shown for BLOCK_PROC_CALL at lines 138-139. Primary mechanism: out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); the independently shown u8 wrap at line 119 is CWE-190.

assumptions: data->block[0] is an 8-bit length byte per standard kernel union i2c_smbus_data semantics (not declared in the fragment), so 0xFF (255) is in its value domain.
The DMA buffer (priv->buffer, referenced at line 13) and data->block are finite objects, so a copy length of SIZE_MAX overruns them regardless of exact capacity.
limitations: Exact capacities of priv->buffer and union i2c_smbus_data are not declared in the fragment; the OOB conclusion rests on the in-fragment derivation of a SIZE_MAX copy length rather than a quoted capacity line.
No caller-side validation in the i2c core/i2c-dev (unshown) is relied upon either way; if such validation existed it could bound block[0], but none is visible in the fragment.
Exploitation requires local access to the SMBus/i2c device node (usually privileged); precise severity is deployment-dependent.

Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the io_setup_async_rw failure set is excluded by the ret2 status check (L62-63) before the rw/iter dereference (L66-68, L72); iovec ownership after transfer is cleared by `iovec = NULL` (L65) and NULL-guarded at the free (L95-96), preventing a double-free; and the retry loop's `io_size -= ret` (L71) cannot underflow because L55 admits only ret > 0 with ret != io_size and L90 re-admits only ret < io_size. No attacker-controlled value can reach a memory, injection, crypto, file, or auth sink through the shown statements.

assumptions: io_import_iovec (L14) on success fills *iovec with import-owned memory and iter; failure returns ret < 0 (checked L15-16).

io_setup_async_rw (L29, L61) returns 0 on success after storing req->async_data when iovec is non-NULL, and returns non-zero on failure; when req->async_data is already non-NULL it returns 0 without replacing it.
rw_verify_area (L33) rejects negative/oversized access size with an error, so io_size reaching L39 is non-negative.
io_iter_do_read (L39, L85) returns at most the remaining iov_iter count and reports -EAGAIN/-EIOCBQUEUED per the shown dispatch (L41, L53, L86).
inline_vecs[UIO_FASTIOV] (L3) is never indexed inside the fragment; it is only passed by pointer.
limitations: NULL-deref of rw at L68/L72 would be a real flaw if io_setup_async_rw could return 0 without setting req->async_data, but no shown statement or entry invariant produces that state (L6/L10-12 plus L62-63), so the premise is unconfirmable from the fragment.

kfree(iovec) at L35 on the rw_verify_area error path assumes io_import_iovec leaves an import-owned (kmalloc) pointer; if it could leave the stack inline_vecs (L3), that free would be invalid. That behavior is inside an unshown callee, so it is recorded here rather than as a finding.
iov_iter_reexpand/revert (L50-51) arithmetic depends on iter->truncated state produced by unshown code; iov_iter_revert itself is unshown, so any degenerate revert amount is out of scope.

Fall-through from the -EAGAIN branch with ret == 0 (L52) re-issues the read; any duplicate-IO or timing behavior is a semantics concern, not a memory/injection/auth flaw.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of the BMP 1-/4-bpp scanline decoder: the conversion loops already cap their index bounds (x < columns-7 at line 630; x < columns-1 at line 674), excluding the odd-width overrun witnesses, and the post-loop guard at 691-692 plus the pixel-buffer allocation at 464-465/485-486 (>= bytes_per_line*rows at 458) keep every SetPixelIndex/SetPixel* write and *p read inside capacities derived in-fragment. The pixel buffer's per-row capacity is MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) (lines 464-465 and 485-486), which is >= bytes_per_line used for row addressing and >= columns+256UL for the RLE override at line 713.
GetAuthenticIndexQueue(image) returns a row index queue of image->columns entries matching QueueAuthenticPixels(image,0,y,image->columns,1,...) per standard ImageMagick semantics.
limitations: DecodeImage (line 490) is not shown, so the RLE decoder's own internal bounds are out of scope.

The bitfield mask shift loops (lines 554-614) can perform shifts >= 32 (UB) for pathological masks, but the corrupted values only feed color computation with no security-relevant consumer in the shown fragment; demoted, no CWE.
The guard at lines 691-692 never triggers for any width admitted by line 333 (it is a dead safety net), so it is not relied upon as the decisive barrier.
Index-queue length, SetImageExtent, and FlipImage behavior in unshown callees are assumed sane per standard semantics.

verdict.summary: disable_priv_mode logs setresuid/setresgid failures but proceeds as if the privilege drop succeeded: lines 25-26 unconditionally record current_user.euid/egid as dropped even when the credential syscalls failed (e.g., errno=EPERM, which bypasses the EAGAIN-only exit at lines 13-16), and the void function has no return-on-failure, so callers and downstream authorization logic observe false 'privileges dropped' state (CWE-273).

evidence.reason: Sink is the unconditional privilege-state write reached after setresuid/setuid returned -1 (line 6 `< 0` branch admits the failure) with errno != EAGAIN (line 14 guard admits only EAGAIN and is further gated by the EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE macro at line 13; EPERM bypasses it); the failure branch (lines 10-17) contains no return, so control flows to line 25. The absent fix is a success-conditional or return-on-failure statement (e.g., assign only when setresuid(...) == 0); without it, current_user.euid is set to current_user.uid while the real effective uid is unchanged, so consumers trust false dropped-privilege state — CWE-273.

Same unconditional state-write sink for the gid drop: after setresgid/setgid returns -1 (lines 19/21 `< 0`), the failure is only logged at line 23 and line 26 still records egid as dropped with no success check and no return, corrupting the privilege-state cache on a failed gid drop — CWE-273.

assumptions: setresuid/setuid/setresgid/setgid follow the standard contract implied by the shown `< 0` checks (lines 6, 8, 19, 21): 0 on success, -1 on failure with errno set.
The function returns void (lines 1/27) and contains no return statement on any failure path, so a normal return is the only completion signal visible in the fragment.
limitations: Whether EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE is defined at build time is not shown; if it is defined, only the errno==EAGAIN case is fail-closed, and the demonstrated EPERM witness still reaches lines 25-26.
The downstream security consequence depends on an unshown consumer of current_user.euid/egid; the in-fragment confirmed failure is the recording of false dropped-privilege state after a failed drop.
Any non-EAGAIN errno (EPERM, EINVAL, etc.) admits the same witness; the failure mode is anticipated by the fragment itself, which reports it at lines 11-12.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. count is clamped by min(max_data, write_pos - read_pos) (lines 3-4), the memcpy at line 7 is guarded by if (count) (line 6) and stays within the pending window [read_pos, write_pos) whenever the entry state satisfies read_pos <= write_pos, which the fragment's own arithmetic (lines 8, 11) preserves. The candidate failures (unsigned underflow of write_pos - read_pos when read_pos > write_pos, over-read of pcs->status.buffer, and use-after-free of the buffer freed at line 10) all require either an unshown caller-maintained state or an unshown buffer capacity, so they are limitations, not findings.

assumptions: uint is an unsigned 32-bit type, so `pcs->status.write_pos - pcs->status.read_pos` (line 4) wraps modulo 2^32 only when read_pos > write_pos, a state no shown statement produces.
The fragment's own updates maintain read_pos <= write_pos on every in-fragment path: the min clamp (lines 3-4), `read_pos += count` (line 8), and the combined reset of both positions to 0 (line 11).
gs_free_object follows standard Ghostscript semantics and tolerates a NULL buffer, so the free at line 10 is safe even when pcs->status.buffer is NULL (initial state).
`min(max_data, write_pos - read_pos)` (lines 3-4) guarantees count <= max_data, matching the ordinary read-up-to-max contract for the destination `data`; that capacity is not visible in the fragment.
limitations: Source over-read of pcs->status.buffer at line 7 cannot be confirmed: the buffer's capacity is not declared anywhere in the fragment, and the `write_pos <= capacity` invariant is established only by the unshown status-write path.

The unsigned underflow at line 4 (count ballooning to max_data when read_pos > write_pos) is not a finding because no shown statement can produce read_pos > write_pos; it would require an unshown caller state, so the degenerate witness is rejected.

Use-after-free of the dangling pcs->status.buffer after gs_free_object (line 10) is not confirmed: the fragment resets both positions to 0 (line 11) so no later in-fragment invocation dereferences the freed pointer (count would be 0, keeping line 7 unreachable); reuse of the stale pointer would require the unshown write path.

The destination write into `data` (line 7) is bounded by count <= max_data (lines 3-4), but the actual size of the caller's `data` buffer is not visible, so no write-side failure can be established from the fragment alone.
The discarded return status of gs_free_object (line 10) has no shown consumer of a failure state; at most a robustness concern.

verdict.summary: In cookedprint(), when a decoded variable fails and output_raw is set to '?' (e.g., line 42), value is ASCII-escaped into bv (capacity 2*MAXVALLEN, line 22) which can be filled to the last byte, and the unconditional append at lines 121-123 writes bv[len+1]='\0' one element past the array.

evidence.reason: bv is declared char bv[2 * MAXVALLEN] at line 22. Attacker-controlled value from nextvar (line 31) flows to atoascii(value, MAXVALLEN, bv, sizeof(bv)) at line 119 after a decode failure sets output_raw='?' at line 42 (admitted by guard line 117 'output_raw != 0' and line 120 'output_raw != '*''). When atoascii fills bv to its maximum NUL-terminated length, len=strlen(bv)=2*MAXVALLEN-1 (line 121) and this statement writes index 2*MAXVALLEN, one byte past the capacity declared at line 22. No length guard exists between line 120 and this write; the absent protective fix is a one-larger capacity (2*MAXVALLEN+1) or an 'if (len < sizeof(bv) - 2)' check before the append. Primary CWE-787: stack out-of-bounds write.

assumptions: value and name returned by nextvar (line 31) are entry-point-derived: arbitrary length and byte content from the response buffer, with no shown length cap.
atoascii (lines 118-119) is a bounded converter honoring its outsize argument, so strlen(bv) can reach 2*MAXVALLEN-1; its exact expansion behavior is not shown in the fragment.
MAXVALLEN >= 1 so the boundary value 2*MAXVALLEN-1 is representable.
limitations: atoascii's internal expansion rules are not shown; if it were to cap output at MAXVALLEN characters with no expansion, the append would fit and the overflow would not occur. This single assumed magnitude link keeps confidence at 0.74 rather than higher.
decodearr/outputarr (lines 97-100) and output() call sites (lines 44, 52, 54, 62, 64, 66, 83, 92, 107, 125) are unshown consumers whose internal bounds could not be audited from this fragment.
The RF-case raw output (lines 65-66) is restricted to strlen(value) <= 4 and shows no memory-safety issue in the fragment.

verdict.summary: In Image::printIFDStructure, `long long allocate = (long long) (size*count + pad+20)` (line 68) evaluates `size*count` in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before the cast. A crafted IFD entry (e.g., type=12/tiffDouble, count=0xFFFFFFFF) wraps allocate to 12, so the Error(57) guard (line 69) compares the tiny wrapped value against io.size() and admits the entry for any ordinary file; DataBuf buf(allocate) (line 72) then holds only 12 bytes, while io.read(buf.pData_, count*size) (line 79) writes up to 4294967288 file bytes into it, causing a heap buffer overflow. The same wrap also leaves a 20-byte buffer indexed to 36..39 in the isRationalType print loop (line 106), an out-of-bounds heap read.

evidence.reason: count (line 37) is entry-point uint32 with residual range 0..2^32-1, uncapped by any shown guard. With type=12 (size=8, line 61) and count=4294967295, line 68 computes size*count in uint32: 8*4294967295 ≡ 4294967288 (mod 2^32), plus pad+20 wraps again to allocate=12. The guard at line 69 compares this wrapped 12 against io.size(), so every file of at least 12 bytes passes; the absent fix is a 64-bit product (e.g., (long long)size*count + pad + 20) applied before the multiply. DataBuf buf(allocate) at line 72 is a 12-byte heap buffer, bOffsetIsPointer (line 74) is true (4294967288 > 4), and io.read at line 79 writes all available file bytes after offset (attacker-controlled, far exceeding 12) into it: heap buffer overflow (CWE-122), root integer overflow (CWE-190).

Same uint32 wrap at line 68: type=5 (is8ByteType, size=8, line 61) with count=0x20000000 gives size*count = 2^32 ≡ 0, so allocate=20; guard line 69 admits it (20 <= io.size() for a >=20-byte file), DataBuf buf(20) at line 72 has capacity 20, and count*size=0 makes bOffsetIsPointer false (line 74) so the buffer is never filled beyond the 4-byte memcpy at line 73. With bPrint true (line 83) and isRationalType(5) (line 103), kount=5 (line 54) drives k=4 and byteSwap4(buf, 4*8+4) reads indices 36..39 past the 20-byte capacity: out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125).

assumptions: dir buffer capacity is 32 bytes (lines 7-8); the reads into dir at lines 14, 34, 167 are 2/12/4 bytes and stay in-bounds.
dirLength is bounded to 0..500 by the tooBig throw at lines 17-18, bounding the entry loop at line 26.
count/type/tag/offset decoded at lines 35-38 are entry-point (file) data; count and offset keep the full uint32 domain.
buf capacity equals the (possibly wrapped) allocate value from line 72.
limitations: io.read return values are discarded (lines 14, 34, 79, 128, 139, 144, 167); short reads would decode stale dir bytes, but no memory-safety failure from that alone is demonstrated in the fragment.
The same wrap could overrun the XMP/ICC outputs (lines 159, 163), but those paths are gated by unshown isPrintXMP/isPrintICC option semantics, so they are not confirmed.

The IPTCNAA branch (line 127) and MakerNote branch (line 143) allocate count / count-10 bytes with io.read fills of the same length; those show no overrun, only possible allocation pressure capped by file size — not confirmed as memory-safety findings.

is4ByteType/is8ByteType, io.read, DataBuf, and typeValid semantics are taken from their standard Exiv2 meaning (type 4=long/4-byte; type 5,12=8-byte; read writes available bytes into the destination buffer; typeValid accepts standard types 1..13).

verdict.summary: Command injection: title, description, and feed_title are interpolated into a shell command line without shell quoting and executed via /bin/sh -c (or run_interactively). A feed-controlled value such as 'x; touch /tmp/pwned' survives stfl::quote/quote_empty unchanged and is executed as a separate shell command with the user's privileges.

evidence.reason: title/description/feed_title (lines 3-5) retain their full string domain: the only transforms (stfl::quote, quote_empty, lines 13-15) do STFL-level escaping and empty-handling, not shell quoting, so ';' survives into cmdline (lines 10-15). Line 29 assigns cmdline as the -c argument to /bin/sh and line 31 executes the argv, so a title of 'x; touch /tmp/pwned' runs touch after the bookmark command. The single-quote wrapper and replace_all at lines 10-12 protect only the url slot; the absent fix is shell-quoting (single-quote wrapping with ' escaping, e.g. utils::shell_quote) for title/description/feed_title. Primary CWE-78 (command injection).

On the is_interactive branch (line 19 true), the same unsanitized cmdline built at lines 10-15 is executed as a shell command; a title containing ';' or '$()' (unconstrained by lines 13-15) is interpreted by the shell, giving the same CWE-78 command injection as the non-interactive path. No guard on this path excludes the witness; the missing protective statement is shell-quoting of the three feed-derived arguments.

assumptions: my_argv (line 26) is a 4-element array fully initialized at lines 27-30, so the pointer array itself has no out-of-bounds issue.
bookmark_cmd (line 7) is admin-controlled configuration treated as the intended command template; injection targets are the three feed-derived fields.
stfl::quote and quote_empty (lines 13-15) implement STFL-markup escaping and empty-argument substitution by name-implied semantics; neither performs shell quoting.
limitations: Log injection at line 17 (cmdline may contain newlines from title/description/feed_title, CWE-117 candidate) is demoted because the LOG(level::DEBUG, ...) write is gated by unshown logger-level configuration.
The discarded return of run_interactively at line 22 is a robustness/UX concern only, with no security-relevant state impact.
Exploitation requires bookmark-cmd to be configured (line 9), an administrative prerequisite.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in get_lisp_indent(): when the opening '(' or '[' is the last character of a line and is preceded by a multibyte character (e.g. line "\tü("), the column loop (lines 97-101) advances `that` to the line's NUL terminator, then the unconditional `that++;` at line 114 moves it one byte past the NUL-terminated line returned by ml_get_curline() (line 88), and `while (VIM_ISWHITE(*that))` at line 118 dereferences out of bounds. The missing guard is `if (*that != NUL)` around `that++;` (Vim patch 8.2.5151).

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125). `that` is the ml_get_curline() pointer (line 88); with line `\tü(` and pos->col = 3 (line 86), the loop at 97-101 advances `that` by one full character per lbr_chartabsize_adv() call while `col--` decrements by one byte, so after 3 iterations `that` points at the line's NUL (idx 4). Branch 109 (NUL != '(' or '[') routes into the else at 112, and the unconditional `that++;` at line 114 moves the pointer one byte past the NUL terminator of the line buffer. This dereference at line 118 reads heap memory beyond the NUL-terminated line; if that byte is white, lines 120-121 read even further. No protective statement between lines 97 and 118 checks `*that != NUL`; the absent fix (Vim 8.2.5151) is `if (*that != NUL) { that++; amount++; }`.

assumptions: ml_get_curline() at line 88 returns a NUL-terminated line buffer; the NUL sentinel is the accessible-object boundary, established in-fragment by the loop condition `*that != NUL` at line 37.
pos->col (line 86) is a byte offset and findmatch positions `pos` at an existing `(`/`[`, so when the paren is the last character col equals the line's byte count.

lbr_chartabsize_adv() (line 99) advances `that` past one full character per call, including a multibyte character; this is standard Vim semantics and is corroborated by the upstream 8.2.5151 regression test using the line `\tü(`.
The witness path requires vi_lisp == FALSE (default 'cpoptions', line 12) so branch 90 takes the else at 92.
limitations: The overread is one byte past the NUL (plus any contiguous run of space/tab bytes); if the byte after the terminator is neither ' ' nor '\t', only a single-byte OOB read occurs at line 118 before the loop exits.

Sinks in the first scan loop (comment/backslash/quote skips, lines 41-69) were audited and are covered by visible NUL sentinel checks, including the `if (*that == NUL) break;` at lines 67-68; no finding there.
The earlier UAF fix (`paren = *pos;`, line 21, Vim 8.2.4146) is already present in this fragment and was not a finding.

No attacker-controlled input, degenerating producer, or in-fragment numeric derivation can reach any dangerous operation, so no failing value is demonstrated.

The only in-fragment array-index sink, tccp->prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns[rlvlno] (lines 287-288), is bounded by the maxrlvls guard at line 167 (rejects maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS), so the fill loop at line 286 indexes only 0..JPC_MAXRLVLS-1. verdict.summary: Fail-open privilege-drop handling in disable_priv_mode: setuid failures are only fatal for errno==EAGAIN (and only when EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE is defined), setgid failures are never fatal, yet lines 17-18 unconditionally record the process as unprivileged. A setuid failure with any other errno (e.g., EPERM) or any setgid failure leaves the original effective UID/GID in force while current_user.euid/egid claim the drop succeeded, enabling later authorization decisions to fail open.

evidence.reason: These unconditional state writes execute on every path, including the failure paths admitted by line 5 (setuid returns -1; e=errno at line 7) and line 14 (setgid returns -1). The only protective statement on the path, exit(e) at line 11, is gated by line 10 (e == EAGAIN) and line 9 (#if defined(EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE)), so it excludes only the single errno EAGAIN and only under that macro; a setuid failure with errno==EPERM (or any non-EAGAIN errno, and EAGAIN itself if the macro is undefined) passes lines 10 and 14-15 and reaches line 17, while every setgid failure reaches line 18 with no guard at all. The write records euid/egid as dropped although the kernel still holds the original effective IDs, so the failure state is consumed as success — CWE-754 fail-open privilege-drop / status-handling flaw. The absent fix is unconditional fatal handling of any setuid/setgid failure, or assigning euid/egid only inside the success paths.

assumptions: setuid/setgid can return -1 on failure, since the fragment itself branches on those returns at lines 5 and 14.
Errno constants other than EAGAIN (e.g., EPERM, EINVAL, ENOSYS) are within setuid's documented failure domain and are not excluded by any shown statement.
current_user.euid/egid are the program's authorization-relevant privilege-state fields, written at lines 17-18 and read elsewhere in the program.
limitations: The precise non-EAGAIN errno is environment-dependent (e.g., a process with effective UID privileged but CAP_SETUID removed, such as a capability-restricted container); no in-fragment producer forces a specific errno value.
Whether EXIT_ON_SETUID_FAILURE is defined at build time is not shown; if it is undefined, even EAGAIN failures continue.

Downstream exploitation (a later privilege check consulting the falsified current_user.euid/egid) is outside the fragment; the confirmed impact is retained effective IDs combined with falsified privilege state.
