verdict.summary: The line 19 guard computes hdr.nSubrects * (4 + (BPP/8)) in unsigned 32-bit arithmetic, so a server-supplied nSubrects of 0x20000001 with BPP=32 wraps the product to 8 <= RFB_BUFFER_SIZE and passes the check; the line 24 loop then runs 536,870,913 iterations, reading 8 bytes per iteration from client->buffer (lines 25-30) far beyond its RFB_BUFFER_SIZE capacity — a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) enabled by the integer overflow (CWE-190), with an unbounded-loop resource-exhaustion aspect.

evidence.reason: ptr is initialized from client->buffer at line 22 and advances by 4+BPP/8 = 8 bytes per iteration (lines 25-30) under the loop bound hdr.nSubrects (line 24). hdr.nSubrects is a server-supplied CARD32 read at lines 9-12, residual range 0..2^32-1. The guard at line 19 ('hdr.nSubrects * (4 + (BPP / 8)) > RFB_BUFFER_SIZE') multiplies in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic: for the exact witness nSubrects = 0x20000001 and BPP = 32, 0x20000001 * 8 = 0x100000008 wraps to 8, which is <= RFB_BUFFER_SIZE, so the guard admits the value (and the 8-byte ReadFromRFBServer succeeds); the loop then executes 536,870,913 iterations, and at iteration i = 8192 line 25 reads 4 bytes at offset 65536, one byte past the RFB_BUFFER_SIZE-sized client->buffer, continuing to offset ~4.29e9. The absent fix is a non-wrapping bound, e.g. 'hdr.nSubrects > RFB_BUFFER_SIZE / (4 + (BPP / 8))' or a 64-bit product; the confirmed mechanism is an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125) driven by the 32-bit overflow (CWE-190).

assumptions: hdr.nSubrects is a CARD32 (unsigned 32-bit) field of rfbRREHeader, consistent with the 32-bit byte swap at line 12 and the RFB RRE protocol; the struct declaration itself is in an unshown header.
client->buffer has capacity RFB_BUFFER_SIZE — the constant the guard at line 19 itself uses as the transfer limit.
The function is macro-instantiated per pixel depth, so BPP = 32 (CARDBPP = uint32_t) is a valid instance giving stride 4 + BPP/8 = 8.
ReadFromRFBServer returns TRUE exactly when it reads the requested n bytes and FALSE on failure (standard helper semantics).
limitations: The literal value of RFB_BUFFER_SIZE is not shown; the witness only requires RFB_BUFFER_SIZE >= 8 and < 2^32 (it is 65536 in libvncclient), so the wrapped product 8 always passes the guard.
If nSubrects were signed (int) instead of CARD32, values >= 2^31 would produce a negative product and be rejected by the guard; the RFB RRE header defines the field as unsigned, so the wrap stands.

Other wrap witnesses require an iteration count beyond 2^31, which would rest on practical two's-complement wraparound of the signed loop index (UB); the chosen witness keeps i below 2^31, so its loop count is fully well-defined.
The ~5.4e8-iteration/GotFillRect-call resource-exhaustion aspect is a CWE-400/835-class concern noted but not added as an additional CWE.
The GotFillRect callback and framebuffer handling are unshown; only the reads from client->buffer (lines 25-30) are treated as confirmed sinks.

verdict.summary: simplestring_addn's overflow guard underflows when add_len == SIZE_MAX: the second clause (SIZE_MAX - add_len - 1) wraps to SIZE_MAX and never fires, and the first clause fires only when target->len > 0. With target->len == 0 and add_len == SIZE_MAX, memcpy copies SIZE_MAX bytes into a buffer whose capacity is target->size (lines 11, 24), and target->str[target->len] afterward writes at index SIZE_MAX — a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: add_len's residual range after the line 7 guard still contains SIZE_MAX: with target->len == 0, (SIZE_MAX - add_len) < 0 is false and (SIZE_MAX - add_len - 1) underflows to SIZE_MAX, so SIZE_MAX < 0 is false and the guard at lines 7-9 returns nothing. Line 11 wraps 0 + SIZE_MAX + 1 to 0, which is not > target->size, so the realloc branch is skipped, and line 27 admits SIZE_MAX. The memcpy at line 28 then writes SIZE_MAX bytes into a buffer whose capacity is target->size (the capacity used at line 11 and recorded at line 24), an out-of-bounds heap write. No statement rejects add_len == SIZE_MAX; the absent fix is an explicit check such as add_len > SIZE_MAX - target->len - 1 or add_len == SIZE_MAX.

On the same witness (target->len == 0, add_len == SIZE_MAX) admitted by the line 7 guard, line 30 sets target->len = SIZE_MAX, and line 31 writes the NUL terminator at index SIZE_MAX into the buffer whose capacity is target->size (lines 11, 24) — a second heap out-of-bounds write caused by the same absent rejection of add_len == SIZE_MAX.

assumptions: The buffer capacity is target->size, which the fragment itself uses as capacity at line 11 and updates from the realloc result at line 24.
The exploit path requires target->str to be non-NULL with target->size >= 1 (e.g., a freshly initialized string); simplestring_init_str's body is not shown and its failure behavior is unknown.
add_len is treated as an unbounded size_t length (e.g., attacker-controlled protocol/file length); no call site is shown.
limitations: Line 2 dereferences target before the line 3 NULL check, but no NULL producer is shown in-fragment, so a NULL-deref finding was not confirmed.

The witness requires the degenerate state target->len == 0, which is not derived by any shown statement; if callers guarantee len > 0, the guard returns safely and the bug is unreachable (kept as a boundary-fragile finding, hence confidence 0.67).
If simplestring_init_str leaves target->str NULL or target->size == 0 on the path, the memcpy at line 28 is skipped (line 26), blocking the exploit.
In practice memcpy with a SIZE_MAX length will fault or be optimized per platform limits; the static out-of-bounds write condition is confirmed independently of that.

verdict.summary: In jp2_decode, the CDEF channel-definition loop iterates i over dec->numchans (attacker-controlled via cmap.numchans at L233) and reads dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents[i] without bounding i against the CDEF box's own entry count (cdef.numchans). A malicious archive containing (1) a symlink entry "evil" -> /tmp/out (created at line 206 with the unvalidated archive_entry_symlink target) and (2) a regular-file entry "evil/pwned" causes line 188's g_file_replace (G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION) to resolve the symlinked parent and create/overwrite /tmp/out/pwned outside extract_data->destination. The only parent guard (lines 102-104) tests existence with g_file_query_exists (which follows symlinks) and skips its block for an existing parent, so no protective statement covers the write.

evidence.snippet: ostream = (GOutputStream *) g_file_replace (file, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, cancellable, &load_data->error);
evidence.reason: CWE-59 link-following write. Taint: entry 2's pathname "evil/pwned" (line 37) is normalized into file = dest/evil/pwned at line 44; the intermediate component dest/evil is a symlink created earlier (line 206) from the attacker-controlled archive_entry_symlink target /tmp/out. Guards admitted: line 38 (requested), lines 102-104 (parent exists -> g_file_query_exists returns TRUE, so the mkdir block is skipped and the only ancestor check never evaluates a symlink condition), line 174 (load_data->error == NULL), line 121 (filetype AE_IFREG). Sink line 188 then opens dest/evil/pwned, and OS path resolution follows dest/evil outside extract_data->destination; with REPLACE_DESTINATION an existing target is overwritten (e.g., evil -> $HOME plus entry evil/.bashrc). Absent fix: a per-entry check that no ancestor of file is a symlink (NOFOLLOW IS_SYMLINK query / recorded-symlink skip, as in the historical _g_path_is_external_to_destination fix), or validation of the line-206 symlink target.

assumptions: extract_data_get_extraction_requested (line 38) returns TRUE for the witness entries (extract-all path); the skip branch at lines 38-41 is not taken.

extract_data->overwrite is TRUE and skip_older is FALSE (defaults), so the query block at lines 48-94 does not run for the witness; even if it did, g_file_query_info on the not-yet-existing child returns NOT_FOUND and continues.

GIO's g_file_replace and g_file_query_exists resolve intermediate symlink components via ordinary OS path semantics.
_g_path_get_relative_basename leaves the witness names 'evil' and 'evil/pwned' unchanged (they contain no '..').

status->errormsg at line 78 could be NULL only if parse_status_msg returned a status with a NULL errormsg; no shown statement can produce that, so it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: The attacker-controlled TIFF IFD count field (uint32_t, decoded at line 37, unconstrained by any shown check) drives the 32-bit buffer-size computation size*count at line 66. With type RATIONAL (size=8) and count=2^29 the product wraps to 0, allocating a 20-byte DataBuf, after which line 153 executes buf.pData_[count]=0 — a heap buffer overflow write at index 2^29. The same wrap also enables out-of-bounds reads in the rational print loop (lines 99-100) and the XMP/ICC output blocks (lines 154, 157). No protective bound, clamp, or overflow check exists between the count read and the sink; the commented-out check at line 65 is inactive.

evidence.reason: count (uint32_t) is read directly from the file at line 37 with residual range [0, 2^32-1]; dirLength<=500 (line 17) bounds only the entry count and typeValid (line 41) only the type. For type RATIONAL (size=8 via line 61, pad=0 via line 57), count=2^29 makes size*count=2^32 wrap to 0 in unsigned 32-bit arithmetic, so DataBuf buf(size*count+pad+20) at line 66 allocates only 20 bytes. bOffsetIsPointer (line 68: count*size=0>4=false) does not constrain this path, and isPrintXMP(tag==0x02bc,option) at line 152 is true, so line 153 writes byte 0 at heap offset 2^29 — a heap buffer overflow WRITE (CWE-787) far beyond the named 20-byte capacity. The absent fix is a bound/overflow validation of size*count before the line 66 allocation or a cap on count before line 153.

assumptions: DataBuf(size_t) allocates exactly the named byte count (new byte[size])
typeValid() admits RATIONAL (TIFF type 5), making is8ByteType true and size=8; RATIONAL is the standard 8-byte outside type, consistent with the shown is8ByteType/isRationalType branch structure
isPrintXMP(tag,option) is true for the XMP tag (0x02bc) with the XMP/recursive print option, per the branch structure the fragment itself uses
limitations: The same size*count wrap also produces out-of-bounds heap READS in the rational print loop (lines 99-100: k=4 reads buf[32..39] from the 20-byte buffer) and in the XMP C-string write (line 154) / ICC bulk read (line 157); these are secondary manifestations of the same unsanitized product
Discarded BasicIo::read/seek return statuses imply short reads leave partially initialized buffers — a robustness concern, not needed for the confirmed finding
Unbounded recursive printIFDStructure/printTiffStructure calls (lines 115, 140, 145) enable stack exhaustion on crafted cyclic offsets; treated as a DoS concern, not part of the primary verdict

verdict.summary: ZIP entry filenames are turned into output paths with no containment check, so `..` segments escape `targetDirectory` and the decompressed payload is written to an arbitrary location (zip-slip / path traversal).

evidence.reason: entryPath = zei->entry.filename (lines 6/8) is an attacker-controlled ZIP protocol field whose residual range after guards L11 (non-empty only) and L16 (non-separator-suffixed only) still contains `../../escaped.txt`; line 14 `targetDirectory.getChildFile (entryPath)` builds a path that the OS resolves above the extraction root because `File::getChildFile` concatenates without normalizing `..`; `FileOutputStream out (targetFile)` at line 46 opens it and line 51 `out << *in;` writes arbitrary entry content outside `targetDirectory`; no containment/isAChildOf-style validation exists between line 14 and this sink; the absent fix is an added check such as `if (! targetFile.isAChildOf (targetDirectory)) return Result::fail(...)` after line 14; mechanism is path traversal leading to arbitrary file write (CWE-22).

assumptions: zei->entry.filename is populated from ZIP entry headers by the ZipFile parser, i.e., it is attacker-controlled protocol data.
File::getChildFile concatenates the child path without normalizing `..` segments; `..` is resolved by the OS when the file is opened at line 46.
createStreamForEntry(index) returns a non-null stream for a valid crafted file entry; line 21 handles only the failure case.
Extraction runs in a context where the escaped destination (e.g., the parent of the extraction root) is writable.
limitations: entries.getUnchecked(index) at line 3: no capacity of `entries` and no producer of an out-of-range index are shown in the fragment, so an OOB read cannot be confirmed.

File::createSymbolicLink (line 41) uses the entry payload as the link target without validating it, but the main write-through impact requires a subsequent uncompressEntry call that writes through the created link, which lies outside this single-call fragment.
Directory-entry creation (line 17) and deleteFile (line 29) are the same traversal with different sinks; reported once at the primary file-write sink.

verdict.summary: ha_maria::drop_table discards the return status of ha_close() (line 4) and of maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME) (line 5) with (void) casts, so a failed close is never detected before the destructive table-file deletion proceeds unconditionally, and a failed deletion is silently swallowed without being reported; error conditions on an exceptional path are unhandled (CWE-754) and a detected deletion failure triggers no action, leaving the handler/catalog in an inconsistent state (CWE-390).

evidence.reason: The return status of ha_close() (line 4) is discarded via (void); its residual range is fully unconstrained (nothing compares, stores, or propagates it), and the only guard in the fragment, the DBUG_ASSERT(!file || file->s->temporary) at line 3, constrains only the file state and cannot make the close succeed. On any execution where ha_close() returns nonzero (an unchecked environment/close failure), the destructive deletion at line 5 runs regardless, in an undefined post-failure state, with the error invisible to the caller of this void function — an improper check for an exceptional condition, primary CWE-754. The absent fix statement is a return-status check on ha_close() (e.g., if (ha_close()) return;) before the deletion.

The return status of maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME) (line 5) is discarded via (void) along the unconditional sequence from line 4; a nonzero deletion result (e.g., locked, missing, or permission-denied files) is never checked or propagated, so the engine behaves as if the drop succeeded while the table files remain or are partially removed — error status detected by the callee but no action is taken, secondary CWE-390. The absent fix statement is capturing/propagating this error (e.g., returning or checking the maria_delete_table_files result).

assumptions: ha_close() and maria_delete_table_files() return status codes with nonzero-on-failure semantics, per the standard meaning of their names as engine close/delete operations.
file is engine-internal handler state whose setter/producer is outside this fragment; the DBUG_ASSERT at line 3 is a debug-build-only check.
limitations: A non-NULL, non-temporary file state that would violate the line-3 invariant has no producer shown inside the fragment, so the assertion-violation / wrong-table-file-deletion scenario is unconfirmable from the shown code.

The name parameter (line 1) is not validated in-fragment, but no in-fragment producer of a path-traversal or symlink-hostile value exists, so CWE-22/CWE-59 via name is unconfirmable and is not reported.

The severity of the status-handling flaw depends on an error-path (environmental) trigger rather than a directly attacker-chosen input; the confidence reflects that the failure-trigger premise is assumed from callee semantics, not shown as a literal.

verdict.summary: ZipFile::uncompressEntry lets an archive write outside the target directory through a symlink at the final path component: the symlink-entry payload (originalFilePath, L44-L45) is never validated before File::createSymbolicLink (L47), and the extraction guard checks only the parent chain (hasSymbolicPart(targetDirectory, targetFile.getParentDirectory()), L36). A dangling symlink makes targetFile.exists() (L27) false, so the delete-at-L32 protection never runs, and FileOutputStream (L52) follows the link at L52, so out << *in (L57) creates/writes an attacker-chosen file outside the extraction root.

evidence.reason: FileOutputStream opens targetFile with O_CREAT/O_TRUNC semantics implied by the name, following a dangling symlink placed at the final path component by a prior invocation of this same function (File::createSymbolicLink with the unvalidated, attacker-controlled originalFilePath from L44-L45). The witness: archive entry 'link' (symlink) with payload '/OUT' creates targetDirectory/link -> /OUT because L16 (isAChildOf, lexical only) admits it, L27 exists() is false for the dangling link so the L32 delete is skipped, and L36 hasSymbolicPart(targetDirectory, targetFile.getParentDirectory()) inspects only the parent directory, not targetFile itself; a second entry 'link' (regular file) passes the same guards and reaches this open, which resolves outside the extraction root, after which L54 failedToOpen() reports no failure and L57 writes payload bytes to /OUT. The absent protective statement is a final-component symlink check (e.g., adding || targetFile.isSymbolicLink() to the L36 guard, or validating originalFilePath before L47); primary CWE-59 improper link resolution before file access.

assumptions: File::exists() follows symlinks and returns false for a dangling symlink (standard stat semantics implied by the call names)
FileOutputStream opens via open(O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) without O_NOFOLLOW, so a dangling symlink at targetFile creates the link destination (standard POSIX open semantics)
hasSymbolicPart(targetDirectory, targetFile.getParentDirectory()) examines only the path chain above the file, since the final component is passed as getParentDirectory()
entries stores the parsed ZIP central-directory records, so zei->entry.filename/isSymbolicLink are archive-controlled
limitations: entries.getUnchecked(index) at L3 has no shown bounds check and no shown capacity, so an out-of-range index (negative or >= entries.size()) cannot be confirmed from the fragment
The out-of-tree write requires two sequential invocations of uncompressEntry (a symlink entry followed by a same-named regular entry); the per-entry extraction loop is not shown in the fragment

The overwrite impact is limited to creating a file at a currently non-existing destination; if the destination already exists, L27 exists() is true and L32 deleteFile() unlinks the final-component symlink, closing this path
readEntireStreamAsString() on a very large symlink entry is an unbounded allocation (resource exhaustion) and was not assessed as a memory-safety finding
Windows symlink creation may require elevated privileges, so the confirmed chain primarily applies on POSIX platforms

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled maxrlvls (line 166, atoi on the OPT_MAXRLVLS value, no upper-bound validation) drives the loop at line 282 writing tccp->prcwidthexpns[rlvlno] and prcwidthexpns[rlvlno] for rlvlno in [0, maxrlvls). Capacity JPC_MAXRLVLS=33 is a fixed array bound of jpc_enc_tccp_t not shown in the fragment. Absent fix: pre-loop upper-bound validation of maxrlvls. CWE-787.

assumptions: tccp->prcwidthexpns and tccp->prcheightexpns are fixed-size arrays in jpc_enc_tccp_t with capacity JPC_MAXRLVLS (33) per the JasPer definition; the declaration is outside the shown fragment.

Unsigned arithmetic on imgareatlx/hsteplcm/refgrdwidth (lines 234, 242, 244-245, 313-317) can wrap, but no memory sink inside the fragment consumes those wrapped values, so no confirmed integer-overflow finding.

verdict.summary: simplestring_addn passes the int add_len directly as the memcpy byte count (line 20) with no sign or capacity validation: a negative add_len, admitted by the only guard on the parameter (line 19 `if(add_len)`), is converted to SIZE_MAX and copied into the target->str heap buffer past its tracked capacity (lines 6, 15), causing heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) and out-of-bounds read of source (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: add_len has residual range INT_MIN..INT_MAX minus {0}: the only guard on it in the fragment is line 19 `if(add_len)`, which excludes 0 but admits every negative value. For add_len = -1, C semantics convert the count to size_t SIZE_MAX; the guard chain line 2 (non-NULL), line 6 (`target->len + (-1) + 1 = target->len` is not > target->size, so realloc is skipped and the capacity remains the target->size tracked at lines 6 and 15), line 18 (str non-NULL), line 19 (admitted) all pass, and memcpy writes SIZE_MAX bytes from target->str + target->len, exceeding the buffer capacity by orders of magnitude for any int-representable size. The absent protective statement is a negative-length or capacity validation (e.g., `if (add_len < 0) return;` or `if (add_len > 0)`), which the vulnerable fragment does not contain. Primary CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write; the identical over-length read of source is secondary CWE-125.

assumptions: target->size is the allocation capacity of target->str: the fragment sets it to the realloc size at line 15 and compares needed space against it at line 6.
simplestring_init_str (line 4) succeeds and leaves target->str non-NULL, since no failure semantics are shown.
The int-to-size_t conversion of a negative add_len in memcpy's third argument follows C standard semantics (yielding SIZE_MAX).
limitations: No call site for simplestring_addn is shown, so the negative add_len input is an assumed value drawn from the unconstrained int parameter domain (helper category (c)) rather than from an in-fragment producer.

An alternative witness with add_len = INT_MAX relies on signed overflow of target->len + add_len + 1 (undefined behavior) to bypass the line 6 realloc gate; it is secondary to the -1 witness and not needed for the verdict.

The initial target->size before any shown realloc is established by the unshown simplestring_init_str; however the memcpy length SIZE_MAX exceeds any int-representable capacity, so the overrun does not depend on that specific value.

Division by zero at line 12 (incr == 0 from target->size == 0) is not reachable from a shown producer: after a failed realloc, target->str is NULL and line 18 blocks the copy; left as a hardening note.

verdict.summary: LZWDecodeCompat is the fixed counterpart: the code-table write pointer is bounds-checked (lines 105-106) to the array range [0, CSIZE-1] before the write at line 112, the stored next pointer is re-checked (113-114) before dereference, undefined table entries are rejected by the length==0 check (135), and every output copy is capped by residue/length-vs-occ guards (30, 142, 161) so no failing value reaches any sink; no in-fragment witness survives the guards.

assumptions: dec_codetab has CSIZE elements; capacity is evidenced inside the fragment by the memset range (CSIZE - CODE_FIRST) at lines 80-81 and the same &sp->dec_codetab[CSIZE] bound used in guards at lines 106 and 114.
LZW constant conventions: CODE_FIRST=257, CSIZE=4096, BITS_MIN=9, BITS_MAX=12, MAXCODE(n)=(1<<n)-1, so code is masked to [0, 4095] and codep = dec_codetab + code stays in-bounds.
Output buffer capacity equals occ0 bytes at op0; every emit path decrements occ by exactly the number of bytes written, so writes stay within [op0, op0+occ0).
code_t.next chains are NULL-terminated and each entry's length equals its chain size, maintained in-fragment by free_entp->next = oldcodep and length = next->length+1 (lines 112, 119-120).
dec_restart < dec_codep->length on entry to the restart branch; the only in-fragment producer of dec_restart sets it to occ with 1 <= occ < codep->length (lines 149-153).
limitations: Upstream comparison was unavailable (GitHub connector returned 404 for libtiff/libtiff), so the analysis is fully internal to the shown fragment.

Degenerate inputs (occ0 == 0 with a pending dec_restart, or occ0 < 0) have no producer inside the fragment; they reach no emitter because of the while (occ > 0) loop guard at line 73, and were demoted under degenerate-input discipline.

The initial values of sp->lzw_nbits, sp->dec_oldcodep, and sp->dec_free_entp are assumed to satisfy the invariants the fragment itself maintains (nbits capped at BITS_MAX, code < CSIZE, free_entp within the table); no statement in the fragment can push them outside those ranges.
No sink was found to have a non-empty admitted failure set, so no CWE is assigned; concerning-looking chains (long decoded strings, large code values) are all bounded by the guards enumerated above.

verdict.summary: LoaderXM::load reads attacker-controlled XM pattern/instrument data past the bounds of its buffers: the pattern RLE decompressor indexes buffer[pc] (heap, sized by the file field patdata) with an unbounded pc, and the instrument sample-number table indexes smpReloc[nbu[sc]] with a raw file byte. Both are confirmed out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125) reachable from a crafted file.

evidence.reason: buffer is allocated as new mp_ubyte[phead[y].patdata] (line 286) and filled with exactly patdata attacker-controlled bytes (line 294), but pc is only incremented (lines 308, 313, 318, 323, 328, 333, 340) and never compared against patdata. With patdata=1 (admitted by the guard at line 285) and buffer[0]=0x90, the compressed path advances pc to 1 and reads buffer[1] (lines 307/312/317/322/327/332) past the 1-element buffer; line 339 memcpy(slot,buffer+pc,5) likewise overruns. No bound check on pc exists on any path, so the required protective statement (a pc >= patdata check) is absent. Out-of-bounds heap read, CWE-125.

nbu is filled from attacker-controlled file bytes via memcpy(nbu, insDataPtr, MP_MAXINSSAMPS) (line 109), so nbu[sc] is an unconstrained mp_ubyte (0-255), while smpReloc is declared as mp_sint32 smpReloc[MP_MAXINSSAMPS] (line 4). The loop at line 225 (sc < MP_MAXINSSAMPS) imposes no constraint on the value of nbu[sc]; for nbu[0] >= MP_MAXINSSAMPS (e.g. 255), smpReloc[nbu[sc]] (line 226, also line 229) indexes beyond the array. The guards on this path (lines 83, 87, 101, 106) only bound the sample count, not the sample-number values, so the required protective bound check on nbu[sc] is absent. Out-of-bounds read, CWE-125.

assumptions: MP_MAXINSSAMPS (capacity of smpReloc and nbu, and loop bound at line 225) is a small per-instrument sample count well below 256, so a raw mp_ubyte nbu[sc] can exceed it.
patternData allocation capacity rows*channum*6 (line 275) is exactly matched by the bc writes (lines 370-376), so the pattern output writes are in-bounds and not a finding.
limitations: The exact numeric value of the MP_MAXINSSAMPS macro is not shown in the fragment; the smpReloc OOB conclusion relies on MP_MAXINSSAMPS < 256, which is certain from its use but not a literal shown constant.
The old-version branch (lines 225-230) also reads uninitialized smpReloc entries when nbu[sc] points past the initialized prefix; this is subsumed by the OOB read finding.

Severity is high for the unbounded pattern read; if the environment treats reads as crash-only it could be rated medium, but the attacker-controlled unbounded index in an untrusted-file parser warrants high.

The missing return-status checks on wddx_stack_top at lines 22, 66, and 137 are robustness concerns only; the empty-stack failure mode they would catch is already excluded by the guard at lines 13-15, so they are not independently exploitable in this fragment.

Invoking __wakeup (line 55) and add_property_zval with attacker-controlled varname (line 118) is deserialization-by-design WDDX object surface with no shown memory-safety consequence; not a confirmed finding.

strlen(ent1->varname)+1 (line 121) and Z_STRLEN_P(ent1->data)+1 (line 86) assume NUL-terminated/int-bounded C strings from the unshown push side; no in-fragment producer contradicts this, and no in-fragment capacity is shown that these lengths can exceed.

verdict.summary: ReadTIFFImage is the protected counterpart: samples_per_pixel is capped at MaxPixelChannels (32) before any channel-driven sizing/loops, scanline_size is rejected when <= 0 and when it exceeds 1.5x the geometry-derived buffer estimate, rows_per_strip is clamped to image->rows, and every pixel/strip/tile/generic buffer allocation is NULL-checked with capacities that match the subsequent read/write byte counts. assumptions: AcquireVirtualMemory and AcquireQuantumMemory are checked allocators returning NULL on allocation/overflow failure (used to justify that extent-product overflow converts to a NULL check, lines 600-602, 730-733, 824-829, 918-923).

libtiff size functions (TIFFScanlineSize, TIFFStripSize, TIFFVStripSize, TIFFTileSize, TIFFTileRowSize) return sizes consistent with their names and are monotonic in row count, so rows*stride <= TIFFStripSize and rows*TIFFTileRowSize <= TIFFTileSize within a single strip/tile.

GetAuthenticIndexQueue(image) may return NULL on the YCCK path (line 681) and is dereferenced via SetPixelBlack(indexes+x,...) at line 692 without a NULL check; the NULL producer depends on unshown pixel-cache/image state, so it is a limitation.

32-bit size_t builds could truncate 64-bit number_pixels or wrap image->columns*image->rows (lines 594-596, 920, 932); only 64-bit behavior is analyzed.
TIFFGetEXIFProperties/TIFFGetGPSProperties return values are discarded (lines 308, 312); no security-relevant failed-resource use is shown, so this is noted for completeness.

On the meta-branch path (line 676) the globfree(&dirs) calls at lines 734 and 748 would touch a dirs object initialized only by the recursion's line 32-36; reaching them additionally requires realloc/strdup allocation failure, an OOM-only error path not attacker-demonstrable from the shown code.

The getpwnam_r/getlogin_r interplay (lines 345-367) could not be fully resolved from the shown code; no failing value was demonstrated, so it is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

verdict.summary: In the GLOB_TILDE specific-user handling, the unescaping loop and the plain-copy branch write past a buffer whose capacity is only `end_name - dirname` (allocated at L470/L474). A multi-slash pattern such as "~u...u\\/x...x/z" with GLOB_TILDE admits an interior '/' in dirname (L187, L237-238, L268-270), so the sentinel loop `while (*q != '\0')` (L487) copies the entire tail past the slash (L502) into the undersized buffer — a 1000-byte OOB write — and the else branch (L507) performs a 1-byte OOB write.

evidence.reason: Heap/stack OOB write (CWE-787). Input: entry-point `pattern` (L1, only L16 non-NULL/flag guard) admits "~" + 'u'*5000 + "\\/" + 'x'*1000 + "/z" with GLOB_TILDE. Shown chain: strrchr last '/' (L187), dirname copy up to last '/' (L237-238, L268-270) yields interior '/' at end_name (L449), backslash at unescape before it (L463), buffer capacity `end_name - dirname` = 5002 (L470/L474). The sentinel loop L487 only stops at the string NUL — nothing compares q to end_name — so L502 copies the '\/', the 1000 'x's and the tail, writing 6002 bytes into the 5002-byte buffer (writes reach newp[6001]). Fix-Scan: no protective statement bounds the loop or sizes the buffer from strlen(dirname)+1; the L460 guard only protects the end_name==NULL case (L456); L496 only suppresses one final-byte write. Absent fix: loop bound against end_name (e.g. `while (q < end_name)`) or capacity `strlen(dirname)+1`.

1-byte OOB write (CWE-787). Input: entry-point `pattern` = "~ab/cd/z" with GLOB_TILDE; shown chain: dirname = "~ab/cd" (L187, L237-238, L268-270), end_name = interior '/' (L449), unescape NULL → else branch, capacity `end_name - dirname` = 3 (L470/L474). The mempcpy length is also `end_name - dirname` = 3, so the terminating NUL is written at newp[3], one past the 3-byte buffer (writes 4 bytes into 3). Fix-Scan: no `-1` on the length and no `+1` on either allocation; absent fix: copy length `end_name - dirname - 1` or capacity `end_name - dirname + 1`.

assumptions: pattern and flags are entry-point inputs to glob(3); GLOB_TILDE is a valid flag bit admitted by the L16 check.
dirname may contain an interior '/' because it is derived from the portion of pattern up to the LAST slash (L187, L237-238, L268-270) and pattern content is unconstrained.
glob_use_alloca (L470) may select alloca or malloc for the identical `end_name - dirname` size; the OOB write occurs on either branch.
The overflow completes before getpwnam_r (L520), so the lookup result does not affect reachability.
limitations: The `home_len + dirlen` (L416/L421) and `home_drive_len + home_path_len + 1` (L336) summation-overflow candidates are demoted: no shown producer can yield strlen values summing to >= SIZE_MAX.
GLOB_BRACE `pattern_len = strlen(pattern) - 1` (L91) underflow is unreachable because `begin != NULL` requires a '{' (L58-L78).
The exact `glob_use_alloca` threshold is not shown; it only changes whether the confirmed overflow lands on the stack or the heap.

verdict.summary: In unlzw, the LZW prefix-decode loop writes characters onto the de_stack via '*--stackp' (L142) without any bound check against de_stack. A crafted input can build a prefix chain as long as maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) (with maxbits up to BITS, L31/L33), overflowing de_stack by writing before the array. The protective bound check present in the fixed version (gzip 1.12, CVE-2022-1271) is absent here.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled code from input(inbuf,posbits,code,n_bits,bitmask) (L93) follows a strictly-decreasing prefix chain via tab_prefixof(code) (L143); each iteration decrements stackp (initialized to de_stack at L112) and writes one byte, with the loop condition (L140) terminating only at code < 256 and never bounding stackp against de_stack. With maxbits up to BITS (L33) giving maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) (L31), the chain can be as long as maxmaxcode, exceeding de_stack's STACK_SIZE capacity, so the write at L142 lands before de_stack (CWE-787 out-of-bounds write). No protective bound check (the absent fix 'if (stackp == de_stack) gzip_error(...)') exists on any path to this sink.

assumptions: de_stack is a fixed-capacity buffer whose capacity (gzip STACK_SIZE = (1<<BITS) - BITS - 1) is smaller than the maximum possible prefix-chain length maxmaxcode = (1<<maxbits); this capacity constant is not declared inside the shown fragment.
maxbits is bounded to [0, BITS] by the shown check at L33-39, so maxmaxcode can reach MAXCODE(BITS).

Each new table entry (L176-177) points to a strictly older/smaller code, so prefix chains strictly decrease and terminate at code < 256, bounding loop length by the code count rather than by stack capacity.
limitations: The exact numeric capacity of de_stack is not visible in the fragment; the overflow magnitude relies on the well-established gzip buffer layout, which lowers confidence below the exact-witness band.

Line 145 ('*--stackp = (char_type)(finchar = tab_suffixof(code))') and line 136 ('*--stackp = (char_type)finchar') are the same de_stack underflow mechanism and share the primary finding; they were not given separate evidence items.
The outbuf writes (L99, L156, L169) and table writes (L176-177) are adequately guarded by shown checks (L97-98, L151-167, L174) and were not treated as findings.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of gzip unlzw(): the attacker-controlled maxbits byte (line 24) is capped by the guard at lines 33-39 (admitted range 0..BITS; > BITS returns ERROR before any LZW state is used), bounding maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) to MAXCODE(BITS) at line 31, and therefore bounding every dictionary index (free_ent/oldcode/code < free_ent <= maxmaxcode) used at lines 143/146/177/178. The additional first-code guard (lines 98-99, reject code >= 256) and the KwKwK guard (line 116, reject code > free_ent) cover the remaining degenerate inputs. outbuf writes (lines 100/157/170) are bounded by the OUTBUFSIZ split at lines 152-172 and by outpos==0 on the only first-code path. No demonstrated failure value reaches any sink.

assumptions: The guard at lines 33-39 admits maxbits in [0, BITS] and excludes all values > BITS on every path, because it returns ERROR before any dictionary/output state is initialized or used.

maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) at line 31 is therefore <= MAXCODE(BITS), and dictionary write indices are bounded by the gate at line 175 (`(code = free_ent) < maxmaxcode`) to [0, MAXCODE(BITS)-1]; read indices at lines 143/146 are < free_ent via the guards at lines 115-116.

read_buffer's -1 return is fully handled by read_error() at lines 72-74; partial/full reads advance insize at line 75 without discarding failure status.
limitations: The numeric values of BITS, BIT_MASK, MAXCODE, CLEAR, FIRST, INBUFSIZ, INBUF_EXTRA, OUTBUFSIZ, and the declared sizes of tab_prefix/tab_suffix/de_stack/inbuf/outbuf are not shown in this fragment, so the absolute capacities could not be independently re-derived; safety relies on the standard BITS-bit LZW table sizing semantics.

The de_stack chain bound (lines 137/143/146) is inferred from the maxbits cap and the shown chain-termination-at-a-literal structure, not from a visible de_stack declaration; no overrun is derivable from the shown statements alone.
The inbuf shift/read arithmetic (lines 64-77) is treated as safe-by-construction; buffer padding (INBUF_EXTRA) is not visible, so no standalone upper-bound proof was possible in-fragment.

verdict.summary: Stack-based buffer overflow in GmfOpenMesh's ASCII read path: tokens are read with unbounded fscanf("%s") into the fixed-size stack buffer str[GmfStrSiz] (line 5); a mesh file containing a token of length >= GmfStrSiz overflows the buffer.

evidence.reason: The file token is entry-point input (file contents) with no shown length constraint: line 39 bounds only strlen(FilNam), and the loop condition at line 128 plus the EOF check at lines 130-131 execute after this write. The '%s' conversion has no width specifier, so a token of length L >= GmfStrSiz (capacity declared at line 5, "char str[ GmfStrSiz ];" ) writes L+1 bytes into a GmfStrSiz-byte stack array via the path 63 -> 77(false) -> 122 -> 127, bypassing guards 39, 53, 63, 77, 122. The absent fix is a width-limited format such as fscanf(msh->hdl, "%127s", str); overflow occurs during the conversion, before strcmp at line 128, so no later guard helps. Primary CWE-121, unbounded copy into a visible-size stack object.

Second unbounded '%s' conversion in the same ASCII-read branch. After the first keyword loop terminates (lines 130-131 admit res != EOF) and the version check at lines 135-136 admits ver == 1, loop 138-141 reads another token; a token of length L >= GmfStrSiz overflows str (capacity declared at line 5) on the first iteration. No pre-sink statement constrains token length; the loop condition at line 141 and EOF check at lines 143-144 run only after the write. The absent fix is the same width-limited conversion. Primary CWE-121, stack-based buffer overflow of a visible-size stack array.

assumptions: Capacity of the stack object sink: "char str[ GmfStrSiz ];" (line 5) sizes the buffer to GmfStrSiz bytes as declared in the fragment.
msh->FilNam is GmfStrSiz bytes (implied by the constant name and the protective check at line 39); under that reading the strcpy at line 42 is fully protected by line 39 and is not a finding.
GmfRead vs. GmfWrite and the extension typing are as shown in the fragment; a ".mesh" name sets Asc|MshFil with the Bin bit clear, taking the ASCII branch (lines 119-147).
limitations: The literal numeric value of GmfStrSiz is not shown; it is not needed since an attacker can choose a token longer than the array regardless of its size.

The varargs-based output pointers PtrVer/PtrDim (lines 71-72, 152-153) and write-mode version/dimension (lines 181-183) contain no in-fragment NULL/absence check; a caller omitting them would be undefined behavior, but no failure can be derived from the shown statements.

Callees ScaWrd, GetPos, safe_fread, safe_fscanf, and ScaKwdTab are not shown; their arguments as supplied here are covered by the in-fragment range checks (lines 100, 105, 108, 113, 135, 149), so no additional finding is confirmed from them.

If this fragment were intended to be read as the patched counterpart, the protective statement at line 39 covers only the strcpy sink; it provides no protection for the fscanf("%s") writes at lines 127 and 140.

cq_size <= 0 makes roundup_pow_of_two/ilog2 (lines 15-16) undefined; no shown caller derives such a value, and any consequence would materialize only in unshown callees (no in-fragment capacity exceeded), so it is not a confirmed finding.

The CQE write is bounded by the '<' loop guard (line 26); the kvzalloc result is NULL-checked (lines 34-37); every helper return is checked (lines 23-24, 40-43, 59-60); and the PAS fill (line 54) is exactly sized by the allocation formula (lines 31-33). assumptions: The loop guard at line 26 (`i < mlx5_cqwq_get_size(&conn->cq.wq)`) admits i in [0, size-1] and excludes the off-by-one value i == size, so the CQE write at line 28 indexes only CQEs of the WQ produced by mlx5_cqwq_create at lines 21-22 via the same helper pair.

Writes through set_ci_db/arm_db at lines 65-66 alias the doorbell db.db created by mlx5_cqwq_create (lines 63-64) and are only reached after all status checks (lines 23-24, 40-43, 59-60) admit success.

verdict.summary: In the L_SENDB send path of mrb_vm_exec, the local mrb_value blk (declared line 421) is never assigned on any path before it is consumed at line 452 (mrb_proc_p(blk)) and dereferenced at line 453 (mrb_proc_ptr(blk)) inside the CFUNC branch; an indeterminate value is read and, if its tag matches MRB_TT_PROC, an invalid pointer is dereferenced, giving an untrusted-bytecode-reachable memory-safety failure. evidence.reason: blk is declared at line 421 ('mrb_value recv, blk;') and no statement between line 421 and line 452 assigns it; ARGUMENT_NORMALIZE (line 423), cipush (line 434) and the C function call (lines 437-447) never write blk. On the reachable path OP_SEND -> L_SENDB (lines 404-416) with a defined CFUNC target (guard line 436 taken) and no pending exception (guard line 450 passed), line 452 reads the indeterminate value and branches on it; a garbage tag equal to MRB_TT_PROC makes line 453 mrb_proc_ptr(blk) dereference an invalid RProc pointer (p->flags, MRB_PROC_ENV(p), line 454), an untrusted-bytecode-reachable out-of-bounds read/crash. All guards on the path (lines 428, 436, 450) admit this witness and none protects blk; the absent fix is a one-statement initialization (e.g., blk = regs[mrb_ci_bidx(ci)]; after line 451) before the orphan-marking check. Primary CWE-457 (use of uninitialized variable).

assumptions: Bytecode (the mrb_code stream and its operands) is treated as entry-point input, so any validly-decoded instruction sequence may execute; register/pool/sym/jump-target bounds are assumed constrained only by the unshown bytecode loader/verifier.
A send whose resolved method is a C function (MRB_METHOD_CFUNC_P true) with no pending exception is a normal, always-available path in the fragment (lines 436-451).
limitations: OP_ARGARY/OP_BLKPUSH env-stack reads: the guard 'MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1' (e.g., line 647) covers the non-keyword accesses; a kd=1 access one slot deeper would require MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2 exactly, an env-length equality not produced by any shown statement, so it is demoted.
Register, pool, syms, and OP_JMPUW/OP_EXT1-3 targets are not provably out of bounds from shown statements; such claims would rest on unshown nregs/ilen/pool-count capacities, so they are demoted.
prepare_missing (line 429) also receives the indeterminate blk by value, but its behavior is in an unshown callee and is not independently confirmed.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of mruby's gen_assignment. Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the NULL arg-list dereferences are guarded by `if (tree)` at line 104, the count `n` is pinned to [1..15] by the checks at lines 107, 113, 120, 140, 142, and 147 so no pop_n/pop can underflow and no SEND/ARRAY operand can escape the fragment's own bounds, `skip` is initialized at line 83 before `dispatch`, and the retval-slot push is guarded by `if (val || sp == cursp())` at line 87. No failing witness passes every guard, and no buffer/register capacity exists in the fragment that any shown derivation could exceed; all deeper memory effects are inside unshown emitter helpers with in-range arguments.

assumptions: Name-implied helper semantics used for the guard audit: push()/pop()/pop_n() adjust s->sp by the named amount; cursp() returns s->sp; codegen(..., VAL) leaves one additional value on the codegen stack; gen_values returns the count of compiled positional args (0..14) or a negative value for a splat and pushes that many values; gen_hash pushes one hash value; lv_idx returns -1 when a local is not visible.
The AST shape produced by the unshown parser can yield a NULL arg-list node for a no-argument setter lvalue (e.g. `obj.attr = v`), which is exactly the case the line 104 `if (tree)` guard excludes.
15 is treated as the splat/"pack all remaining" encoding for OP_ARRAY/OP_SEND, consistent with the fragment's own `n == 15`/`n < 15` handling at lines 140-149.
limitations: Actual out-of-bounds memory writes, if any, would occur inside unshown emitter helpers (genop_*, gen_move, codegen) whose irep/iseq/register-file capacities are not declared anywhere in the fragment, so an OOB finding cannot be confirmed from the shown statements; the fragment's own derivations (n <= 15, idx > 0, sp = cursp() >= 0) remain inside its established ranges.

The precise micro-spelling of the one-line historical fix (whether it is the line 104 NULL guard, the line 87 `sp == cursp()` equality clause, or the count caps) cannot be uniquely identified from the fragment alone; the audit establishes that all candidate fix forms are present, which is sufficient for the not-vulnerable verdict.

The full VM register semantics of OP_SEND/OP_SETIDX/OP_ARRAY operand packing are name-implied; a residual doubt about operand-order conventions is noted but no shown value violates the visible bounds.

verdict.summary: The chunk-offset bounds at line 94 (`offsets[tile_idx] + sizeof(int)*5 > size`) and line 184 (`offsets[y_idx] + sizeof(int)*2 > size`) add 20/8 to an unconstrained uint64 offset. An in-domain offset in [2^64-19, 2^64-1] (tiled) or [2^64-7, 2^64-1] (scanline) wraps the addition past size, is admitted by the guard, and drives `head + offsets[i]` ~2^64 bytes past the size-byte buffer, so the memcpy reads at lines 106/121 and 195/197 perform an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125, root cause CWE-190).

evidence.reason: offsets[tile_idx] is uint64 (declared line 2) with no shown upper bound; the only guard on this path, line 94 (`offsets[tile_idx] + sizeof(int) * 5 > size`), evaluates the sum in wrapping uint64, so the in-domain value o = 2^64-19 satisfies (o+20) mod 2^64 = 1 <= size for any size >= 1 and is admitted. Line 103 then sets data_ptr = head + o, and this 16-byte memcpy reads far past the size-byte buffer whose capacity is declared at line 3 (`head`/`size`). No statement between line 94 and line 106 constrains offsets[tile_idx]; the absent fix is a wrap-free bound such as `offsets[tile_idx] >= size || size - offsets[tile_idx] < sizeof(int)*5`. Confirmed OOB read, CWE-125, root cause unsigned-overflow defeat of the guard, CWE-190.

On the scanline path the only guard before this read, line 184 (`offsets[y_idx] + sizeof(int) * 2 > size`), also sums in wrapping uint64: for offsets[y_idx] = 2^64-1 the sum wraps to 7, so `7 > size` is false for size >= 7 and the else-branch is taken. Line 192 forms data_ptr = head + offsets[y_idx], and this 4-byte memcpy (and the identical 4-byte read at data_ptr+4, line 197) reads out of bounds of the size-byte buffer declared at line 3. The absent fix is a wrap-free offset bound (e.g., `offsets[y_idx] >= size || size - offsets[y_idx] < sizeof(int)*2`) evaluated before the reads. Confirmed OOB read, CWE-125, root cause CWE-190.

assumptions: `tinyexr::tinyexr_uint64` is a 64-bit unsigned integer type, so the additions at lines 94 and 184 wrap modulo 2^64 (defined behavior).
`sizeof(int) == 4`, consistent with the in-fragment use of `swap4` (lines 107-110, 123, 198-199) and 4-byte memcpys.
`head`/`size` (line 3) denote a readable buffer of exactly `size` bytes; this is the capacity the fragment's own guards use for the reads at lines 106, 121, 195, 197.
The 20-byte tiled block header (16-byte coordinates + 4-byte data_len) and 8-byte scanline block header are confirmed by the code's own comments at lines 91-93, 132, and 187-189.
limitations: The extreme offset values (2^64-19 / 2^64-1) have no shown producer inside the fragment; their provenance is the unshown caller (provenance class (c)), which is why confidence is 0.74 rather than higher.

The `calloc` at line 83 is unchecked and would be dereferenced at line 87 if it returned NULL, but a NULL result requires an environmental allocation failure and an unshown huge `offsets.size()`; not confirmed as a demonstrated failure in-fragment.

Signed overflow in `line_no + num_scanline_blocks` (line 209) or `data_window[3] + 1` (line 210) only drives `end_line_no` negative, forcing `num_lines <= 0` (line 214) to reject; no admitting-path security consequence is demonstrable.
If `num_blocks > INT_MAX`, the cast at line 181 is implementation-defined and the scanline loop body does not run; no in-fragment memory consequence.

The fragment already contains protective statements for the data_len/line-argument sinks (`data_len < 4`, line 125; `data_len == 0`, line 203; int64 `lno` check, lines 223-230; `total_data_len_overflown`, lines 162-163), which fully cover those sinks and are not findings; none of them covers the offset-guard wrap.
Sibling reads at lines 121 and 197 are affected by the same wrap mechanism as the reported sinks and are discussed within the corresponding evidence reasons.

verdict.summary: In OP_ARGARY (line 671) and OP_BLKPUSH (lines 1170/1174) the environment-length guard `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1` omits the `kd` term, so when the bytecode operand sets kd=1 and the environment has exactly m1+r+m2+2 slots, the code reads one `mrb_value` past the environment stack (e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]). The fix absent in this fragment is extending the guard to `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1+kd`.

evidence.reason: CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. Operand b (entry-point bytecode) decodes to m1=0,r=0,m2=0,kd=1,lv=1 (lines 619-623); the guard at lines 638-639 admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e)=2 (rejects only <= m1+r+m2+1=1), and line 640 makes stack=e->stack+1, so line 671 reads e->stack[2] while valid indexes are 0..1. Guard lacks the `+kd` term (absent fix: `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1+kd`), which would reject this witness; the kd=1 read therefore overruns the environment stack by one element.

CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. With operand m1=0,r=0,m2=0,kd=1,lv=1 (lines 1153-1157) and MRB_ENV_LEN(e)=2, the guard at line 1164 (reject only if len <= m1+r+m2+1) passes, line 1168 sets stack=e->stack+1, and the read at line 1174 (same index already fetched at line 1170) accesses e->stack[2], one past the valid 0..1 range. The guard omits the `kd` term; the absent fix `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1+kd` would exclude this witness.

assumptions: Bytecode operands (a, b, c, insn) are treated as untrusted entry-point input; their decoded sub-fields m1/r/m2/kd/lv are unconstrained beyond the shown masks (lines 619-623, 1153-1157).
uvenv(mrb, lv-1) returns a non-NULL REnv for the witness (line 636 / line 1162), and for OP_BLKPUSH the env is on-stack or has mid != 0 so the guard term at line 1163 does not reject.

MRB_ENV_LEN(e) is the capacity bound of the environment stack; the fragment derives the failing value from its own guard (line 638/1164) plus the kd=1 operand, with no in-fragment producer guaranteeing a larger minimum.
limitations: The exact failing capacity MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2 is produced by the (unshown) closure/env creation, not inside this fragment, so the witness is an edge value at the guard's admitted boundary (confidence 0.67 rather than 0.8+).

Operand-indexed accesses into irep->pool / irep->syms / irep->reps (OP_LOADL, OP_LOADSYM, OP_LAMBDA, OP_ERR, etc.) lack visible bounds checks, but the corresponding capacity fields are not declared in the fragment, so no OOB can be confirmed for them.

OP_JMPUW's jump target is bounded only by a debug-time mrb_assert (line 321) and OP_STOP indexes regs[irep->nlocals]; demonstrating concrete overruns there requires unshown irep size/stack-size invariants, so those were not counted as findings.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the protected counterpart of mrb_vm_exec: every env-stack sink is preceded by a bounds check on the shown paths (OP_GETUPVAR line 252 and OP_SETUPVAR line 267 admit only b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e); OP_ARGARY line 639 and OP_BLKPUSH lines 1165-1166 admit only MRB_ENV_LEN(e) > m1+r+m2+1 before the demonstrated arg reads; OP_ENTER line 761/785 guard the possibly-NULL argv). No shown statement derives a failing value that reaches any sink, so no vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone.

assumptions: MRB_ENV_LEN(e) denotes the number of valid mrb_value slots of e->stack, so stack = e->stack + 1 (lines 641, 1170) shifts every access by one — assumed only to translate guard bounds into element addresses.
In OP_GETUPVAR/OP_SETUPVAR, `b` (uint16_t) is promoted for the signed comparison `b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)`, so the admitted range is exactly [0, len-1].
uvenv() may return NULL (the fragment tests for it), and its returned environment's length is taken as the capacity compared by the guards.
For non-kd OP_ARGARY/OP_BLKPUSH lanes, the maximum accessed env-stack element is e->stack[m1+r+m2+1], fully covered by the guards at lines 639 and 1165-1166.
limitations: kd=1 boundary: OP_ARGARY lines 671-672 and OP_BLKPUSH lines 1172/1176 read e->stack[m1+r+m2+2] when kd=1; the guards at lines 639 and 1165-1166 admit the boundary length MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, leaving that element one past the end. This is demoted because the exact boundary length comes from the environment produced by uvenv() (lines 637, 1164), whose producer and sizing are not shown in the fragment; the in-fragment code only compares, never derives, that length.

OP_JMPUW main path (lines 301-324) recomputes target a at line 302 and sets pc = irep->iseq + a at line 322 with only the debug-only mrb_assert(a >= 0 && a < irep->ilen) at line 308; a runtime violation cannot be derived from shown statements because irep->ilen is never produced in-fragment.

regs[]/pool[b]/syms[b]/irep->reps[b] indexing with bytecode-derived indices (e.g., lines 47, 189, 222, 244, 417, 704, 717, 762, 769, 53, 120, 145, 227, 238, 407) has no shown capacity or guard; confirmation would require the loader/frame-layout invariants, which are outside the fragment.
Frame sizing and irb register counts guaranteed by the mruby compiler/loader are assumed neither safe nor unsafe; only the guarded env-stack operations are resolved.

verdict.summary: unix_expandpath() shows no confirmable vulnerability: every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement. The STRCPY family (L150, L157-158, L164) writes into buf sized STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5 (L32), and no in-fragment derivation produces a length exceeding that capacity; the name-length bound (NAME_MAX) that would be required to demonstrate an overflow is not shown. The only unbounded structures, the recursive "**" expansions (L125, L160, L169), are capped by stardepth < 100 at L120 and L153 (admitting depth 0..99). NULL producers (alloc L32/check L33, file_pat_to_reg_pat L93/check L94, vim_regcomp L107/check L112 with regprog!=NULL guard L145, opendir L131/check L134, readdir L138/check L139) are all checked before use.

assumptions: buf capacity is declared at L32 as STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5; BASENAMELEN is a macro whose value is not shown and is treated as opaque, which is why copy safety is audit-grade rather than a named-bound verdict.
gap is a valid garray_T and addfile() (L194) maintains a non-NULL ga_data used by qsort at L207-209.
vim_regfree(NULL) is a no-op, making the EW_NOTWILD/NULL-regprog path (L112, L145, L204) safe.
The d_name upper bound (NAME_MAX) is an OS invariant not visible in the fragment; with canonical values (NAME_MAX <= BASENAMELEN), the L32 allocation leaves margin for all STRCPY operations.
limitations: No OOB (CWE-787) could be confirmed: demonstrating an overflow of L150/L157-158/L164 requires d_name longer than BASENAMELEN + (e - s) + 2, a magnitude only provable from the unshown NAME_MAX constant; per the OOB rules that is an assumed magnitude, relegated here to a limitation.

The MACOS_CONVERT block (L183-193) copies via mch_memmove with precomp_len from mac_precompose_path; MACOS_CONVERT is not enabled in this fragment and the precompose length invariant is unshown, so no failure is demonstrated.

If NAME_MAX exceeded the L32 capacity slack on an exotic filesystem, the STRCPY operations at L150/L157-158/L164 would be a heap overflow and the absent fix would be an explicit length check before them; this is the unconfirmable residual concern.

verdict.summary: suggest_trie_walk writes tword[sp->ts_twordlen++] = c (lines 699, 930) and tword[sp->ts_twordlen] = NUL (line 182) with no visible bound on sp->ts_twordlen, which starts at 0 (line 50) and grows by one per trie descent. A crafted spell trie word and long fword admitted by every shown guard (lines 653, 678-682, 919-920) drive ts_twordlen to MAXWLEN, producing an out-of-bounds stack write past tword[MAXWLEN] (declared line 7). The neutralising statement 'if (sp->ts_twordlen + 1 < MAXWLEN)' is absent.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds stack write (CWE-121/787): tword is declared char_u tword[MAXWLEN] (line 7), capacity MAXWLEN elements; ts_twordlen is 0 from CLEAR_POINTER (line 50) and increments strictly by 1 per accepted STATE_PLAIN append (line 699) inside the while loop (line 98). A trie path and fword of length >= MAXWLEN+1 (both attacker-supplied entry-point data; no shown length cap) is admitted by every guard on the path: line 653 (ts_curi <= byts[arridx]), line 673/678-682 (newscore == 0 because c == fword[ts_fidx]), leaving TRY_DEEPER as the only unshown element, which cannot supply the missing bound. After MAXWLEN+1 appends, ts_twordlen == MAXWLEN and line 699 writes tword[MAXWLEN], one past the array; the absent fix 'if (sp->ts_twordlen + 1 < MAXWLEN)' is not present anywhere before the sink.

Second instance of the same unguarded OOB write (CWE-121/787): STATE_INS reaches line 930 after ++depth (line 928) with no check on sp->ts_twordlen; the guards on the path (line 899 sp->ts_curi > byts[n] node-exhaustion, line 919 c != fword[ts_fidx] && TRY_DEEPER) bound only node bytes and score, not word length. Reaching the same ts_twordlen == MAXWLEN state as the line 699 sink writes tword[MAXWLEN] past the line-7 capacity; the required bound statement is absent.

Same overflow mechanism on the word-end path (CWE-121/787): when a node's current byte is the end-of-word NUL (line 160 false branch) and ts_twordlen has reached MAXWLEN via the line 699/930 appends, line 182 writes the terminating NUL at tword[MAXWLEN], past the MAXWLEN-element array declared at line 7. No visible guard on ts_twordlen precedes the write; the fix 'if (sp->ts_twordlen < MAXWLEN)' is absent.

assumptions: tword[MAXWLEN] (line 7), stack[MAXWLEN] (line 8) and compflags[MAXWLEN] (line 14) declare capacities of exactly MAXWLEN elements (valid indices 0..MAXWLEN-1).
sp->ts_twordlen is initialised to 0 by CLEAR_POINTER(sp) at line 50 and is incremented by exactly one per appended byte via the shown writes at lines 699 and 930.
fword (line 4) and the trie arrays byts/idxs (lines 56-57, 67-70) are entry-point data whose lengths the fragment leaves unconstrained.
The prefix-branch guard 'depth < MAXWLEN - 1' (line 126) is the only in-fragment depth cap and applies solely to the prefix go_deeper path, not to the STATE_PLAIN/STATE_INS descents.
limitations: The definitions of TRY_DEEPER and go_deeper are outside the fragment; if they internally capped depth at MAXWLEN-1 the demonstrated overflow would not occur, but no such bound is derivable from the shown statements and an unshown callee cannot be credited with the missing guard.

su->su_maxscore and fword/su->su_badlen come from unshown callers; the witness only requires a score of 0 or a small substitution score, consistent with any non-trivial su_maxscore, but the value itself is not shown.

stack[] (lines 100/696/929) and compflags[] (lines 270-271/480-481) overflows share the same unbounded-walk root cause but are not given separate evidence items because their index derivation relies partly on unshown go_deeper/compound configuration semantics.

The DEBUG_TRIEWALK sprintf calls (e.g. lines 139, 538-542, 687-693, 827-829, 924-926) use fixed '%.*s' precision against tword and are compiled out in normal builds; not treated as format-string findings.

verdict.summary: OP_BLKPUSH (and identically OP_ARGARY) check the upvalue environment length as MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1, omitting the keyword-dictionary term kd. With kd=1 and an REnv whose length is exactly m1+r+m2+2, the guard admits the frame but the sinks read stack[m1+r+m2+kd] (= e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]), one mrb_value past the end of e->stack, causing a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The missing protective statement is counting kd in the bound (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+kd+1).

evidence.reason: OP_BLKPUSH: operand b decoded at lines 1160-1164 gives kd=(b>>4)&1 and lv=(b>>0)&0xf; the lv>0 path takes stack = e->stack + 1 (line 1175), so this read (and the identical read in the nil-check at line 1177) accesses e->stack[m1+r+m2+kd+1]. Guard line 1171 (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1 -> raise) admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, while the sink needs MRB_ENV_LEN(e) >= m1+r+m2+kd+2; with kd=1 and an env of length m1+r+m2+2 (e.g. m1=r=m2=0, lv=1, b=0x11) the guard passes and e->stack[m1+r+m2+2] == e->stack[MRB_ENV_LEN(e)] is read one slot past the capacity named in line 1171 - heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent fix is counting the keyword slot in the bound: MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+kd+1 (upstream commit 1348daa68).

OP_ARGARY: with kd=1 (byte b decoded at lines 625-629) and stack = e->stack + 1 (line 646), this read accesses e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]. Guard line 644 (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1 -> goto L_NOSUPER) admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, but the sink requires MRB_ENV_LEN(e) >= m1+r+m2+3, so the last slot read is e->stack[MRB_ENV_LEN(e)], one element past the env capacity stated by the guard - heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), same missing +kd protective statement as OP_BLKPUSH (upstream commit 735369a).

assumptions: MRB_ENV_LEN(e) is the slot count of e->stack, the capacity the guards at lines 644 and 1171 compare against.
The VM executes irep bytecode supplied as entry-point input (compiled/loaded .mrb code or hand-built irep), so the decoded operand bits m1/r/m2/kd/lv are attacker-controlled.

For the lv>0 path (lines 1167-1176 / 640-647) the REnv is reachable with a length equal to the guard's admitted boundary, which the upstream fix message confirms is the case the check is meant to catch ('irep built by hand or damaged in transit').
limitations: OP_JMPUW (line 330, pc = irep->iseq + a) has no in-fragment main-path bound against irep->ilen (only the assert at line 316 on the CHECKPOINT_RESTORE path); upstream has never added such a check, so it is not treated as the benchmark's one-statement fix and is demoted.
Register/stack indexing in OP_APOST, OP_HASH, OP_HASHADD, OP_ENTER and the various regs[a]/regs[b] accesses cannot be confirmed: the VM-stack capacity irep->nregs is not shown in the fragment.

OP_EXT1/2/3 unknown-opcode fallthrough (pc--; NEXT;) and unvalidated typed-opcode casts (e.g. mrb_class_ptr, mrb_proc_ptr) are robustness/typing concerns without an in-fragment demonstrated memory-safety failure.
OP_GETUPVAR/OP_SETUPVAR are safe: guards at lines 260 and 275 (b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)) fully cover the operand domain.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in find_pattern_in_path() during insert-mode include/define completion: p (= startp, inside the LSIZE line buffer allocated at line 51) is advanced by the unconstrained helper return ins_compl_len() at line 409, and vim_iswordp(p) at line 410 dereferences past the allocation whenever ins_compl_len() exceeds the remaining buffer room. The condition at line 407 lacks the protective length check '(int)STRLEN(p) >= ins_compl_len()' (upstream patch 9.1.1751), so the vulnerable (pre-fix) counterpart is shown.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125): p is set to startp at line 406 and advanced by p += ins_compl_len() at line 409; startp derives from regmatch.startp[0] (line 350) or skipwhite(p) (line 338) and lies inside the line buffer allocated at line 51 (file_line = alloc(LSIZE); line content read via get_line_and_copy at line 100 and vim_fgets at line 432). ins_compl_len() is a helper return with no in-fragment bound, so its residual domain is the full non-negative int range; the only guard on the path, line 407 (if (compl_status_adding())), admits that full range. For any ins_compl_len() > LSIZE - (startp - line), p lands beyond the LSIZE allocation and vim_iswordp(p) at line 410 reads out of bounds (find_word_start/find_word_end at lines 412-414 follow the same corrupted pointer). The absent fix is the length check '(int)STRLEN(p) >= ins_compl_len()' that the vulnerable condition at line 407 is missing (upstream patch 9.1.1751); guards at lines 395, 397, and 403 are all satisfied/avoidable as quoted.

assumptions: line and startp always point inside the file_line allocation of capacity LSIZE (alloc at line 51; line assigned only at lines 100, 430, 432).
startp is non-NULL whenever matched is TRUE, since it is assigned at line 338 or 350 before use at line 406.
ins_compl_len() returns a non-negative int with no in-fragment constraint (residual = full declared domain).
On non-OOM paths the file-stack invariant depth+1 <= old_files <= max_path_depth holds (init at lines 89-93, resize at lines 248-269, pop at the EOF loop), keeping files[] indexing in bounds.
limitations: If ALLOC_MULT at line 250 returns NULL while depth+1 == old_files == max_path_depth, lines 270-286 (files[depth+1].fp write, vim_free(files[old_files].name) at line 281, ++old_files at line 282, files[depth] writes at lines 284-286) address files[max_path_depth], one past the allocation — a heap OOB on an OOM-only path; demoted because it is gated on an environment failure and is not the one-statement fix target.

An OOB write via STRNCPY(IObuff, aux, i) at line 420 would require the OOB pointer walk at lines 410-414 to make find_word_end(p) - startp exactly equal ins_compl_len(), which is not determinable from the shown statements.
IObuff[i-2] reads at lines 449-453 require i == ins_compl_len() with i < 2; no shown statement establishes such a small completion length.
startp[len] at line 343 was rejected as a sink: a match at lines 339/341 implies STRLEN(startp) >= len, so the read stays inside the string.

verdict.summary: No demonstrated failure reaches a security-relevant sink. The only configuration where a runtime character can exceed the UCD table geometry (32-bit non-UTF) is protected by the visible clamp at lines 222-224 (CMP SLJIT_LESS vs MAX_UTF_CODE_POINT+1 with UNASSIGNED_UTF_CHAR substitution), and both 32-byte map lookups are guarded by the CMP GREATER 255 jumps at lines 160 and 190-194. The always-false condition at line 61 and the OR-mask inconsistency at line 618 are correctness issues whose security impact is not demonstrable within the fragment.

assumptions: The XCL byte stream at `cc` is produced by the unshown pattern compiler and is well-formed with an `XCL_END` terminator (the sentinel loops at lines 32 and 458 rely on it).

The UCD tables (`PRIV(ucd_stage1)`, `PRIV(ucd_stage2)`, `PRIV(ucd_records)`, `PRIV(ucd_boolprop_sets)`, `PRIV(ucd_script_sets)`, `PRIV(ucp_typerange)`, `PRIV(ucd_caseless_sets)`) are sized to cover character codes 0..MAX_UTF_CODE_POINT (0x10FFFF), which makes the clamp at lines 222-224 sufficient for the indexing emitted at lines 228-238.
In UTF-32 mode the character decoder caps code points at 0x10FFFF, so the clamp's `#if PCRE2_CODE_UNIT_WIDTH == 32` scope covers the only width whose raw code-unit value can exceed the UCD tables.
PT_CLIST caseless sets contain at least three entries followed by the NOTACHAR terminator (asserted at lines 594-595), bounding the `other_cases[0..3]` reads and the NOTACHAR loop at lines 634-638.
